nodes.name: Quasi-compact space
nodes.description: A topological space (not necessarily Hausdorff) in which every open cover has a finite subcover; Bourbaki reserves 'compact' for Hausdorff.

nodes.name: Finite intersection property characterization of compactness
nodes.description: A space is compact iff every collection of closed sets with the finite intersection property has nonempty intersection.

nodes.name: Continuous image of compact is compact
nodes.description: The continuous image of a compact space is compact.

nodes.name: Closed subsets of compact spaces are compact
nodes.description: Every closed subset of a compact space is compact; every compact subset of a Hausdorff space is closed.

nodes.name: Compact Hausdorff implies normal
nodes.description: Every compact Hausdorff space is normal (T4).

nodes.name: Continuous bijection from compact to Hausdorff is homeomorphism
nodes.description: A continuous bijection from a compact space to a Hausdorff space is automatically a homeomorphism.

nodes.name: Proper map
nodes.description: A continuous map f : X -> Y such that preimages of compact sets are compact (equivalently, f x id_Z is closed for every Z).

nodes.name: Locally finite family
nodes.description: A family of subsets such that every point has a neighborhood meeting only finitely many members.

nodes.name: Refinement of a cover
nodes.description: A cover {V_j} refines {U_i} if every V_j is contained in some U_i.

nodes.name: Paracompactness of metrizable spaces (Stone's theorem)
nodes.description: Every metrizable space is paracompact; every open cover has a sigma-discrete open refinement.

nodes.name: Nowhere dense set
nodes.description: A set whose closure has empty interior.

nodes.name: Meager set (first category)
nodes.description: A countable union of nowhere dense sets; by Baire's theorem, a complete metric space is not meager in itself.

nodes.name: Characterization of semicontinuity via liminf/limsup
nodes.description: f is lower semicontinuous at x iff f(x) <= lim inf_{y->x} f(y); upper iff f(x) >= lim sup_{y->x} f(y).

nodes.name: Supremum of lower semicontinuous functions
nodes.description: The pointwise supremum of any family of lower semicontinuous functions is lower semicontinuous.

nodes.name: Paracompactness and partitions of unity
nodes.description: A Hausdorff space is paracompact iff every open cover admits a subordinate partition of unity.

nodes.name: Lindelof space
nodes.description: A topological space in which every open cover has a countable subcover.

nodes.name: Second-countable implies Lindelof
nodes.description: Every second-countable space is Lindelof, separable, and hereditarily Lindelof.

nodes.name: Compact-open topology
nodes.description: The topology on C(X,Y) generated by subbasic sets {f : f(K) subset U} where K compact and U open.

nodes.name: Topology of uniform convergence
nodes.description: The topology on function spaces defined by the uniformity: f and g are V-close if (f(x),g(x)) in V for all x.

nodes.name: Topology of compact convergence
nodes.description: The topology on C(X,Y) defined by uniform convergence on each compact subset of X.

nodes.name: Pointwise convergence topology
nodes.description: The topology on Y^X induced by the product topology; convergence means convergence at each point.

nodes.name: Evaluation map
nodes.description: The map ev : C(X,Y) x X -> Y defined by ev(f,x) = f(x); continuous when C(X,Y) has the compact-open topology and X is locally compact.

nodes.name: Exponential law for function spaces
nodes.description: For locally compact Hausdorff X, C(X x Y, Z) -> C(Y, C(X,Z)) by currying is a homeomorphism under compact-open topology.

nodes.name: Uniform limit of continuous functions is continuous
nodes.description: C(X,Y) is closed in Y^X under the topology of uniform convergence when Y is Hausdorff.

nodes.name: Completeness of function spaces
nodes.description: If Y is a complete uniform space, the space of bounded uniformly continuous functions X -> Y is complete under uniform convergence.

nodes.name: Filter generated by a base
nodes.description: The unique smallest filter containing a given filter base, consisting of all supersets of members of the base.

nodes.name: Finer and coarser topologies
nodes.description: Topology T1 is finer than T2 if T2 subset T1; the identity (X,T1) -> (X,T2) is then continuous.

nodes.name: Discrete and indiscrete topologies
nodes.description: The finest topology (every subset open) and the coarsest topology ({empty, X} only) on a set X.

nodes.name: Clopen set
nodes.description: A set that is simultaneously open and closed; a space is connected iff its only clopen sets are empty and X.

nodes.name: Sigma-compact space
nodes.description: A topological space that is a countable union of compact subsets.

nodes.name: Cauchy sequence
nodes.description: A sequence (x_n) in a metric/uniform space such that for every entourage V, there exists N with (x_m, x_n) in V for all m, n >= N.

nodes.name: Pseudometric uniformity
nodes.description: A pseudometric (allowing d(x,y)=0 for x != y) generates a uniformity; the associated topology need not be Hausdorff.

nodes.name: Continuity via filters
nodes.description: A map f : X -> Y is continuous at x iff the image filter of the neighborhood filter of x converges to f(x).

nodes.name: Universal property of completion
nodes.description: Every uniformly continuous map from X to a complete Hausdorff uniform space extends uniquely through X -> X-hat.

nodes.name: Compactness equals complete and totally bounded
nodes.description: A uniform space is compact iff it is complete and totally bounded.

nodes.name: Lebesgue covering lemma
nodes.description: For every open cover of a compact metric space, there exists delta > 0 such that every subset of diameter < delta lies in some member.

nodes.name: Topological embedding
nodes.description: An injective continuous map f : X -> Y that is a homeomorphism onto its image f(X) with the subspace topology.

nodes.name: Monoid
nodes.description: A set equipped with an associative binary operation possessing an identity element.

nodes.name: Group
nodes.description: A monoid in which every element is invertible.

nodes.name: Characteristic of a ring
nodes.description: The nonnegative generator of the kernel of the unique ring homomorphism Z -> A.

nodes.name: Opposite ring
nodes.description: For a ring A, the ring A^op with the same additive group but reversed multiplication a *' b = ba.

nodes.name: Left module / right module
nodes.description: A module where scalars act on the left (resp. right), with axiom (ab)x = a(bx) for left modules and x(ab) = (xa)b for right modules.

nodes.name: Basis of a module
nodes.description: A family of elements such that every element of the module can be written uniquely as a finite linear combination of them.

nodes.name: Rank of a linear map
nodes.description: The dimension of the image of a linear map between vector spaces.

nodes.name: Direct sum decomposition
nodes.description: A module M is a direct sum of submodules M_1,...,M_n if the canonical map M_1 + ... + M_n -> M is an isomorphism.

nodes.name: Noetherian module
nodes.description: A module satisfying the ascending chain condition on submodules, equivalently every submodule is finitely generated.

nodes.name: Artinian module
nodes.description: A module satisfying the descending chain condition on submodules.

nodes.name: Annihilator
nodes.description: For a submodule N of M, the ideal Ann(N) = {a in A : aN = 0}; dually for an ideal I, Ann_M(I) = {x in M : Ix = 0}.

nodes.name: Multilinear map
nodes.description: A map f: M_1 x ... x M_n -> N that is linear in each variable when the others are held fixed.

nodes.name: Right exactness of tensor product
nodes.description: The functor M tensor_A (-) is right exact: it preserves cokernels and direct sums but not injections in general.

nodes.name: Tensor algebra
nodes.description: The graded algebra T(M) = direct_sum_{n>=0} M^{tensor n} with concatenation multiplication, universal for linear maps from M to associative algebras.

nodes.name: Exterior product (wedge product)
nodes.description: The product in the exterior algebra, denoted x wedge y, satisfying x wedge x = 0 and x wedge y = -y wedge x.

nodes.name: Exterior power
nodes.description: The p-th component Lambda^p(M) of the exterior algebra, the quotient of M^{tensor p} by tensors with a repeated factor.

nodes.name: Symmetric algebra
nodes.description: The quotient S(M) = T(M)/<x tensor y - y tensor x>, a graded commutative algebra universal for linear maps from M to commutative algebras.

nodes.name: Symmetric power
nodes.description: The p-th component S^p(M) of the symmetric algebra, the quotient of M^{tensor p} by differences of permuted tensors.

nodes.name: Graded algebra
nodes.description: An algebra A with a direct sum decomposition A = direct_sum_{n>=0} A_n such that A_m * A_n subset A_{m+n}.

nodes.name: Extension of scalars
nodes.function_signature: (A-module M, ring hom A -> B) -> B-module M tensor_A B
nodes.description: Constructs a B-module from an A-module M and a ring homomorphism A -> B via the tensor product M tensor_A B.

nodes.name: Polynomial ring in several variables
nodes.description: The ring A[X_1,...,X_n] defined inductively as A[X_1,...,X_{n-1}][X_n], or as formal sums over multi-indices.

nodes.name: Euclidean division for polynomials
nodes.description: For f, g in K[X] with g nonzero and K a field, there exist unique q, r with f = qg + r and deg(r) < deg(g).

nodes.name: Root of a polynomial
nodes.description: An element alpha in an extension of the coefficient ring such that f(alpha) = 0.

nodes.name: Factor theorem
nodes.description: An element alpha is a root of f in K[X] if and only if (X - alpha) divides f.

nodes.name: Irreducible polynomial
nodes.description: A nonconstant polynomial that cannot be written as a product of two polynomials of lower degree.

nodes.name: Unique factorization in K[X]
nodes.description: The polynomial ring K[X] over a field K is a UFD: every nonconstant polynomial factors uniquely into irreducibles up to units.

nodes.name: Greatest common divisor of polynomials
nodes.description: The monic polynomial of greatest degree dividing two given polynomials, computable by the Euclidean algorithm.

nodes.name: Partial fraction decomposition
nodes.function_signature: (rational fraction in K(X)) -> polynomial + sum of a_ij/(X - alpha_i)^j
nodes.description: Expresses a rational fraction as a polynomial plus a sum of terms with prime-power denominators via the Chinese remainder theorem.

nodes.name: Algebraic element
nodes.description: An element alpha in L that is a root of some nonzero polynomial in K[X].

nodes.name: Transcendental element
nodes.description: An element alpha in L that is not algebraic over K.

nodes.name: Simple algebraic extension
nodes.description: An extension K(alpha)/K generated by a single algebraic element alpha, isomorphic to K[X]/(minimal polynomial of alpha).

nodes.name: Tower law (multiplicativity of degrees)
nodes.description: If K subset L subset M are field extensions, then [M:K] = [M:L]*[L:K].

nodes.name: Existence and uniqueness of algebraic closure
nodes.description: Every field admits an algebraic closure, and any two algebraic closures are isomorphic (though not canonically).

nodes.name: Separable polynomial
nodes.description: A polynomial whose roots in an algebraic closure are all distinct, equivalently gcd(f, f') = 1.

nodes.name: Inseparable extension / purely inseparable extension
nodes.description: An algebraic extension that is not separable; purely inseparable if every element has minimal polynomial X^{p^n} - a in characteristic p.

nodes.name: Perfect field
nodes.description: A field of characteristic 0, or of characteristic p in which the Frobenius endomorphism x -> x^p is surjective.

nodes.name: Normal extension
nodes.description: An algebraic extension L/K such that every irreducible polynomial in K[X] with a root in L splits completely in L.

nodes.name: Transcendence basis
nodes.description: A maximal algebraically independent subset of L over K, such that L is algebraic over K(B).

nodes.name: Norm and trace of a field extension
nodes.description: For a finite extension L/K and alpha in L, N_{L/K}(alpha) = det(mult. by alpha) and Tr_{L/K}(alpha) = trace(mult. by alpha) as K-linear endomorphisms.

nodes.name: Artin's theorem on characters
nodes.description: Distinct characters (homomorphisms) from a group to the multiplicative group of a field are linearly independent over that field.

nodes.name: Totally ordered group
nodes.description: A group equipped with a total order compatible with the group operation: x <= y implies xz <= yz and zx <= zy.

nodes.name: Archimedean ordered group
nodes.description: A totally ordered group in which for any positive a, b there exists n in Z with na > b, equivalently embeddable in (R,+).

nodes.name: Valuation (Krull valuation)
nodes.description: A map v: K* -> Gamma to a totally ordered abelian group satisfying v(xy) = v(x) + v(y) and v(x+y) >= min(v(x),v(y)).

nodes.name: Absolute value on a field
nodes.description: A map |*|: K -> R_{>=0} satisfying |x| = 0 iff x = 0, |xy| = |x||y|, and |x+y| <= |x|+|y|.

nodes.name: Convex subgroup
nodes.description: A subgroup H of a totally ordered group G such that if a <= x <= b with a,b in H then x in H.

nodes.name: Elementary divisors
nodes.description: The prime power factors in the primary decomposition of a finitely generated module over a PID, determining its isomorphism class.

nodes.name: Characteristic polynomial
nodes.description: For a matrix A or endomorphism u, the polynomial chi(X) = det(XI - A) whose roots are the eigenvalues with algebraic multiplicities.

nodes.name: Minimal polynomial of an endomorphism
nodes.description: The monic generator of the annihilator ideal of the K[X]-module defined by the endomorphism, dividing the characteristic polynomial.

nodes.name: Torsion submodule
nodes.description: For a module M over an integral domain A, the submodule Tors(M) = {m in M : am = 0 for some nonzero a in A}.

nodes.name: Torsion-free module
nodes.description: A module M over an integral domain such that Tors(M) = 0, i.e., am = 0 with a nonzero implies m = 0.

nodes.name: Semisimple module
nodes.description: A module that is a direct sum of simple modules, equivalently every submodule is a direct summand.

nodes.name: Semisimple ring
nodes.description: A ring that is semisimple as a module over itself, equivalently an Artinian ring with zero Jacobson radical.

nodes.name: Simple ring
nodes.description: A ring with no two-sided ideals other than 0 and itself (and with R^2 nonzero).

nodes.name: Symmetric bilinear form
nodes.description: A bilinear form Phi with Phi(x,y) = Phi(y,x) for all x,y.

nodes.name: Alternating bilinear form
nodes.description: A bilinear form Phi with Phi(x,x) = 0 for all x, hence Phi(x,y) = -Phi(y,x).

nodes.name: Sesquilinear form
nodes.description: A map Phi: M x M -> K that is linear in one variable and conjugate-linear with respect to an involution in the other.

nodes.name: Hermitian form
nodes.description: A sesquilinear form Phi satisfying Phi(y,x) = sigma(Phi(x,y)) where sigma is the given involution.

nodes.name: Non-degenerate form
nodes.description: A bilinear or quadratic form for which the canonical map M -> M* is injective, equivalently the radical is zero.

nodes.name: Radical of a form
nodes.description: The submodule rad(Phi) = {x in M : Phi(x,y) = 0 for all y in M}, the kernel of the map M -> M* induced by the form.

nodes.name: Orthogonal complement
nodes.description: For a subset S of M with bilinear form, the submodule S^perp = {y in M : Phi(x,y) = 0 for all x in S}.

nodes.name: Witt's theorem
nodes.description: An isometry between non-degenerate subspaces of a regular quadratic space extends to an isometry of the whole space.

nodes.name: Witt group
nodes.description: The group W(K) of isometry classes of non-degenerate quadratic forms over K modulo hyperbolic forms, with orthogonal sum.

nodes.name: Hyperbolic plane (quadratic forms)
nodes.description: A non-degenerate quadratic module of dimension 2 with basis {e,f} satisfying q(e) = q(f) = 0 and Phi(e,f) = 1.

nodes.name: Symplectic group
nodes.description: The group Sp(M,Phi) of linear maps preserving a non-degenerate alternating bilinear form.

nodes.name: Spin group
nodes.description: The double cover Spin(n) of SO(n) constructed inside the even part of the Clifford algebra, kernel of the spinor norm on the special Clifford group.

nodes.name: Spinor norm
nodes.description: A homomorphism from the orthogonal group to K*/K*^2 defined via the Clifford algebra, measuring the signed length of reflections composing an isometry.

nodes.name: Associative algebra
nodes.description: A ring A that is also a module over a commutative ring K, with K acting centrally: k(ab) = (ka)b = a(kb).

nodes.name: Lie subalgebra
nodes.description: A submodule of a Lie algebra closed under the Lie bracket.

nodes.name: Ideal of a Lie algebra
nodes.description: A Lie subalgebra h of g such that [g,h] subset h.

nodes.name: Commutator Lie algebra
nodes.description: For an associative algebra A, the Lie algebra A^- with bracket [a,b] = ab - ba.

nodes.name: Poincare-Birkhoff-Witt theorem
nodes.description: The canonical map g -> U(g) is injective, and ordered monomials of a basis form a basis of the universal enveloping algebra.

nodes.name: Free Lie algebra
nodes.description: The Lie algebra L(X) on a set X satisfying the universal property that every map X -> g extends uniquely to a homomorphism L(X) -> g.

nodes.name: Nilpotent Lie algebra
nodes.description: A Lie algebra whose lower central series g supset [g,g] supset [g,[g,g]] supset ... terminates at 0 in finitely many steps.

nodes.name: Solvable Lie algebra
nodes.description: A Lie algebra whose derived series g supset [g,g] supset [[g,g],[g,g]] supset ... terminates at 0 in finitely many steps.

nodes.name: Abelian Lie algebra
nodes.description: A Lie algebra in which [x,y] = 0 for all x,y.

nodes.name: Faithfully flat module
nodes.description: A flat A-module M such that M tensor_A N = 0 implies N = 0, equivalently M tensor_A (-) reflects exactness.

nodes.name: Faithfully flat descent
nodes.function_signature: (Module or algebra over A, faithfully flat A -> B) -> descended properties over A
nodes.description: Deduces properties of modules or algebras over A from their base change to a faithfully flat extension B.

nodes.name: Local-global principle
nodes.function_signature: (Property of module M) -> (Property holds iff it holds at all localizations M_p)
nodes.description: A property of modules holds globally iff it holds after localization at every prime ideal.

nodes.name: Support of a module
nodes.description: The set Supp(M) = {p in Spec(A) : M_p nonzero}, a closed subset of Spec(A) when M is finitely generated.

nodes.name: Associated graded ring/module
nodes.description: For a filtered ring A, the graded ring gr(A) = direct_sum_n A_n/A_{n+1}, capturing the leading term structure.

nodes.name: Filtered ring
nodes.description: A ring equipped with a decreasing sequence of ideals ... supset F_n supset F_{n+1} supset ... compatible with multiplication: F_m * F_n subset F_{m+n}.

nodes.name: I-adic filtration
nodes.description: The filtration of a ring A by powers of an ideal I: F_n = I^n.

nodes.name: I-adic topology
nodes.description: The linear topology on a ring or module defined by powers of an ideal I, where {I^n} forms a neighborhood base of 0.

nodes.name: Hilbert function / Hilbert-Samuel function
nodes.description: For a graded module M, H(n) = dim_k(M_n); for I-adic filtrations, H_I(n) = length(M/I^{n+1}M), both eventually polynomial.

nodes.name: Primary ideal
nodes.description: An ideal q such that if ab in q and a not in q then b^n in q for some n, equivalently A/q has every zero-divisor nilpotent.

nodes.name: Uniqueness theorems for primary decomposition
nodes.description: The associated primes and primary components for minimal primes are uniquely determined; embedded components may not be unique.

nodes.name: Integral element
nodes.description: An element b of a ring extension B supset A is integral over A if it satisfies a monic polynomial with coefficients in A.

nodes.name: Lying-over theorem
nodes.description: If A subset B is an integral extension, then for every prime ideal p of A there exists a prime ideal q of B with q intersect A = p.

nodes.name: Valuation ring
nodes.description: An integral domain A such that for every nonzero element x of its fraction field, either x in A or x^{-1} in A.

nodes.name: Place
nodes.description: An equivalence class of valuations on a field, or a homomorphism from a valuation ring to a field together with infinity.

nodes.name: Uniformizer
nodes.description: A generator of the maximal ideal of a DVR, equivalently an element of valuation 1.

nodes.name: Rank of a valuation
nodes.description: The Krull dimension of the associated valuation ring, equivalently the order type of convex subgroups of the value group.

nodes.name: Henselian ring
nodes.description: A local ring satisfying the conclusion of Hensel's lemma, equivalently every finite algebra over it is a product of local algebras.

nodes.name: Ramification index and residue degree
nodes.description: For a valued field extension L/K, e = [v(L*):v(K*)] and f = [kappa_L:kappa_K]; the fundamental inequality gives ef <= [L:K].

nodes.name: Extension of valuations
nodes.description: Every valuation on a field K extends to any algebraic extension L of K, with at most [L:K] extensions.

nodes.name: Principal divisor
nodes.description: The divisor div(f) associated to a nonzero element f of the fraction field, defined as sum_v v(f)*[v] over height-1 primes.

nodes.name: Factorial ring (UFD)
nodes.description: An integral domain with unique factorization into irreducibles; equivalently a Noetherian integrally closed domain with trivial divisor class group.

nodes.name: Invertible ideal
nodes.description: A fractional ideal I such that I*I^{-1} = A where I^{-1} = {x in K : xI subset A}; equivalently a locally principal fractional ideal.

nodes.name: Unique factorization of ideals in Dedekind domains
nodes.description: In a Dedekind domain, every nonzero ideal factors uniquely as a product of prime ideals.

nodes.name: Approximation theorem for valuations
nodes.description: Given finitely many independent valuations and target elements, one can find x simultaneously approximating each target.

nodes.name: System of parameters
nodes.description: In a Noetherian local ring of dimension d, a sequence of d elements whose generated ideal is m-primary.

nodes.name: Dimension theorem for Noetherian local rings
nodes.description: The Krull dimension equals the degree of the Hilbert-Samuel polynomial, equals the minimum number of generators of an m-primary ideal.

nodes.name: Dimension of polynomial rings
nodes.description: If A is a Noetherian ring, then dim(A[X]) = dim(A) + 1.

nodes.name: Catenary ring
nodes.description: A Noetherian ring in which all maximal chains of primes between any pair p subset q have the same length.

nodes.name: Universally catenary ring
nodes.description: A Noetherian ring A such that every finitely generated A-algebra is catenary.

nodes.name: Unmixedness theorem
nodes.description: In a Cohen-Macaulay ring, every ideal generated by height-many elements is unmixed (all associated primes are minimal of equal height).

nodes.name: Multiplicity of a local ring
nodes.description: The normalized leading coefficient of the Hilbert-Samuel polynomial, measuring algebraic multiplicity; equals 1 for regular local rings.

nodes.name: Coefficient field / coefficient ring
nodes.description: A subfield or complete DVR of a complete local ring mapping isomorphically to the residue field, guaranteed by the Cohen structure theorem.

nodes.name: Weierstrass division theorem
nodes.description: Division with remainder by a Weierstrass polynomial in k[[X_1,...,X_n]]: unique q and r with deg_{X_n}(r) < d.

nodes.name: Nagata ring (Japanese ring)
nodes.description: A Noetherian domain whose integral closure in any finite extension of its fraction field is a finite module.

nodes.name: Excellent ring
nodes.description: A universally catenary Noetherian ring with geometrically regular formal fibers and open regular locus; complete local rings are excellent.

nodes.name: Depth
nodes.description: The length of a maximal regular sequence in m on a finitely generated module over a Noetherian local ring, equivalently the smallest i with Ext^i(k,M) nonzero.

nodes.name: Regular sequence
nodes.description: A sequence x_1,...,x_n such that x_i is a non-zero-divisor on M/(x_1,...,x_{i-1})M for each i, and the quotient is nonzero.

nodes.name: Depth lemma
nodes.description: For a short exact sequence 0 -> M' -> M -> M'' -> 0, depth(M) >= min(depth(M'), depth(M'') + 1).

nodes.name: Injective hull (injective envelope)
nodes.description: The minimal injective module containing M as an essential submodule, unique up to isomorphism.

nodes.name: Matlis duality
nodes.description: Over a complete Noetherian local ring, Hom(-,E(k)) gives an anti-equivalence between finitely generated and Artinian modules.

nodes.name: Dualizing module (canonical module)
nodes.description: A finitely generated module over a Cohen-Macaulay local ring satisfying local duality via Ext and local cohomology.

nodes.name: Local duality theorem
nodes.description: For a complete Noetherian local ring of dimension d with dualizing module omega, H^i_m(M)^v isomorphic to Ext^{d-i}(M, omega).

nodes.name: Regular rings have finite global dimension
nodes.description: A Noetherian local ring is regular iff it has finite global dimension, and then gl.dim(A) = dim(A).

nodes.name: Bass's theorem
nodes.description: A Noetherian local ring is Gorenstein iff it has finite injective dimension, and then inj.dim(A) = dim(A).

nodes.name: Derivative of a vector-valued function
nodes.description: For a function f mapping an interval of R into a normed vector space E, the derivative at a point x₀ is the limit of (f(x) - f(x₀))/(x - x₀) as x → x₀, when this limit exists in E.

nodes.name: Differentiability
nodes.description: A function f is differentiable at x₀ if there exists a continuous linear map L such that f(x₀ + h) = f(x₀) + L(h) + o(h) as h → 0.

nodes.name: Linearity of differentiation
nodes.description: The derivative operator is linear: (αf + βg)' = αf' + βg' for differentiable functions f, g and scalars α, β.

nodes.name: Product rule (Leibniz rule)
nodes.description: If f and g are differentiable real-valued functions, then (fg)' = f'g + fg'.

nodes.name: Chain rule
nodes.description: If g is differentiable at x₀ and f is differentiable at g(x₀), then f ∘ g is differentiable at x₀ with derivative f'(g(x₀)) · g'(x₀).

nodes.name: Derivative of the inverse function
nodes.description: If f is a continuous bijection differentiable at x₀ with f'(x₀) ≠ 0, then f⁻¹ is differentiable at f(x₀) with derivative 1/f'(x₀).

nodes.name: Monotonicity criterion via derivative
nodes.description: A differentiable function f on an interval is non-decreasing if and only if f'(x) ≥ 0 for all x in the interval.

nodes.name: Convexity criterion via second derivative
nodes.description: A twice-differentiable function f on an interval is convex if and only if f''(x) ≥ 0 for all x in the interval.

nodes.name: Higher-order derivative
nodes.description: The n-th derivative f⁽ⁿ⁾ is defined inductively as the derivative of f⁽ⁿ⁻¹⁾, when it exists.

nodes.name: Leibniz formula for n-th derivative of a product
nodes.description: The n-th derivative of a product fg equals Σₖ₌₀ⁿ C(n,k) f⁽ᵏ⁾g⁽ⁿ⁻ᵏ⁾.

nodes.name: Regulated function
nodes.description: A function f from an interval I into a Banach space E is regulated if it has a left limit and a right limit at every point of I, equivalently if it is a uniform limit of step functions.

nodes.name: Step function
nodes.description: A function on an interval that takes only finitely many values, each on a sub-interval of a finite partition.

nodes.name: Integral of a regulated function
nodes.description: The integral of a regulated function f is defined as the limit of integrals of step functions converging uniformly to f, and this limit is independent of the approximating sequence.

nodes.name: Primitive (antiderivative)
nodes.description: A primitive of a function f on an interval I is a function F such that F' = f on I.

nodes.name: Integration by parts
nodes.description: If f and g are continuously differentiable on [a,b], then ∫ₐᵇ f'(t)g(t) dt = f(b)g(b) - f(a)g(a) - ∫ₐᵇ f(t)g'(t) dt.

nodes.name: Change of variables in integrals
nodes.description: If φ is a C¹ diffeomorphism and f is regulated, then ∫_{φ(a)}^{φ(b)} f(t) dt = ∫ₐᵇ f(φ(u)) φ'(u) du.

nodes.name: Integral remainder for Taylor's formula
nodes.description: If f is of class Cⁿ⁺¹, the remainder in the n-th order Taylor expansion equals (1/n!) ∫₀ʰ (h-t)ⁿ f⁽ⁿ⁺¹⁾(x₀+t) dt.

nodes.name: Uniform convergence and integration
nodes.description: If a sequence of regulated functions converges uniformly to f, then f is regulated and the integral of the limit equals the limit of the integrals.

nodes.name: Improper integral (convergent integral on unbounded interval)
nodes.description: The integral ∫ₐ^∞ f(t) dt is defined as limₓ→∞ ∫ₐˣ f(t) dt when this limit exists.

nodes.name: Absolute convergence of improper integrals
nodes.description: If ∫ₐ^∞ ‖f(t)‖ dt converges, then ∫ₐ^∞ f(t) dt converges and ‖∫ₐ^∞ f(t) dt‖ ≤ ∫ₐ^∞ ‖f(t)‖ dt.

nodes.name: Power function x^α
nodes.description: For x > 0 and α ∈ R, defined as x^α = exp(α log x), extending integer powers to all real exponents.

nodes.name: Number π
nodes.description: Defined as twice the smallest positive zero of cosine, establishing the period 2π of the trigonometric functions.

nodes.name: Inverse trigonometric functions (arcsin, arccos, arctan)
nodes.description: The inverse functions of sin, cos, tan restricted to appropriate intervals where they are bijective, with derivatives 1/√(1-x²), -1/√(1-x²), 1/(1+x²) respectively.

nodes.name: Hyperbolic functions (sinh, cosh, tanh)
nodes.description: Defined as sinh(x) = (eˣ - e⁻ˣ)/2, cosh(x) = (eˣ + e⁻ˣ)/2, tanh(x) = sinh(x)/cosh(x), satisfying the identity cosh²(x) - sinh²(x) = 1.

nodes.name: Inverse hyperbolic functions
nodes.description: The inverses of sinh, cosh|[0,∞), tanh, expressible in terms of logarithm: arsinh(x) = log(x + √(x²+1)).

nodes.name: Analyticity of elementary functions
nodes.description: The functions exp, log, sin, cos, and their inverses are all real-analytic on their domains of definition, represented by convergent power series.

nodes.name: Growth comparison of elementary functions
nodes.description: As x → +∞, for any α > 0 and β > 0: (log x)^α = o(x^β) and x^β = o(e^{αx}), establishing the asymptotic hierarchy log ≪ polynomial ≪ exponential.

nodes.name: Lipschitz condition
nodes.description: A function f(t, y) satisfies a Lipschitz condition in y if ‖f(t, y₁) - f(t, y₂)‖ ≤ K‖y₁ - y₂‖ for some constant K and all (t, yᵢ) in the domain.

nodes.name: Integral equation formulation of ODE
nodes.description: The initial value problem y' = f(t,y), y(t₀) = y₀ is equivalent to the integral equation y(t) = y₀ + ∫_{t₀}^t f(s, y(s)) ds.

nodes.name: Maximal solution of an ODE
nodes.description: A solution defined on a maximal interval of existence that cannot be extended to a larger interval, whose existence is guaranteed by Zorn's lemma from local solutions.

nodes.name: Blow-up criterion (escape to boundary)
nodes.description: If the maximal interval of existence of a solution is bounded, then the solution leaves every compact subset of the domain of f, i.e., ‖y(t)‖ → ∞ or the solution approaches the boundary.

nodes.name: Linear ordinary differential equation
nodes.description: An ODE of the form y' = A(t)y + b(t), where A(t) is a continuous matrix-valued function and b(t) is continuous, whose solutions form an affine subspace.

nodes.name: Homogeneous linear ODE
nodes.description: A linear ODE of the form y' = A(t)y (with b = 0) whose solutions form a vector space of dimension equal to the order of the system.

nodes.name: Fundamental matrix (resolvent)
nodes.description: A matrix-valued function Φ(t) whose columns form a basis of solutions of y' = A(t)y, satisfying Φ' = A(t)Φ with Φ(t₀) = I.

nodes.name: Variation of constants (variation of parameters)
nodes.description: A method to solve the non-homogeneous equation y' = A(t)y + b(t) by writing y(t) = Φ(t)c(t) where Φ is the fundamental matrix, leading to c'(t) = Φ(t)⁻¹b(t).
nodes.function_signature: (Non-homogeneous linear ODE, Fundamental matrix) → (Particular solution)

nodes.name: Linear ODE with constant coefficients
nodes.description: The system y' = Ay with A constant has the explicit solution y(t) = e^{tA}y₀, reducible via Jordan normal form to exponential-polynomial expressions.

nodes.name: Differentiable dependence on parameters
nodes.description: If f(t, y, λ) is Cᵏ in all variables, then the solution y(t, λ) of y' = f(t, y, λ) is Cᵏ in the parameter λ.

nodes.name: Lagrange remainder
nodes.description: For f of class Cⁿ⁺¹, the remainder Rₙ(h) = f⁽ⁿ⁺¹⁾(x₀ + θh) hⁿ⁺¹/(n+1)! for some θ ∈ (0,1).

nodes.name: Asymptotic expansion
nodes.description: A formal series Σ aₙφₙ(x) is an asymptotic expansion of f(x) as x → x₀ if f(x) - Σₖ₌₀ⁿ aₖφₖ(x) = o(φₙ(x)) for each n, where (φₙ) is an asymptotic scale.

nodes.name: Asymptotic scale
nodes.description: A sequence of functions (φₙ) such that φₙ₊₁(x) = o(φₙ(x)) as x → x₀, providing a graded comparison framework for the growth or decay of functions.

nodes.name: Little-o and big-O notation
nodes.description: f = o(g) means f/g → 0 and f = O(g) means |f/g| is bounded, as x approaches a specified limit, providing a calculus of asymptotic comparison.

nodes.name: Asymptotic comparison of functions
nodes.description: The systematic use of asymptotic expansions and asymptotic scales to compare functions' growth rates, compute limits of indeterminate forms, and approximate functions near singular points.
nodes.function_signature: (Functions near a point) → (Asymptotic ordering and expansions)

nodes.name: Bernoulli numbers
nodes.description: The sequence of rational numbers Bₙ defined by the generating function t/(eᵗ - 1) = Σₙ₌₀^∞ Bₙ tⁿ/n!, with B₀ = 1, B₁ = -1/2, and B₂ₖ₊₁ = 0 for k ≥ 1.

nodes.name: Bernoulli polynomials
nodes.description: Polynomials Bₙ(x) defined by the generating function te^{xt}/(eᵗ - 1) = Σₙ₌₀^∞ Bₙ(x) tⁿ/n!, satisfying Bₙ'(x) = nBₙ₋₁(x) and Bₙ(0) = Bₙ.

nodes.name: Euler-Maclaurin summation formula
nodes.description: Relates a sum Σₖ₌ₐᵇ f(k) to the integral ∫ₐᵇ f(t) dt plus correction terms involving Bernoulli numbers and derivatives of f at the endpoints, with a remainder expressible as an integral involving Bernoulli polynomials.

nodes.name: Summation of divergent series by Euler-Maclaurin
nodes.description: Using the Euler-Maclaurin formula to assign finite values to formally divergent sums by analytic continuation, yielding values for ζ(-n) in terms of Bernoulli numbers.
nodes.function_signature: (Divergent series, Euler-Maclaurin formula) → (Regularized finite value)

nodes.name: Asymptotic expansion of the gamma function
nodes.description: The Stirling series Γ(x) ~ √(2π) x^{x-1/2} e^{-x} (1 + Σₖ₌₁^∞ cₖ/x^k), an asymptotic expansion for x → +∞ with coefficients expressible via Bernoulli numbers.

nodes.name: Beta function
nodes.description: Defined as B(p,q) = ∫₀¹ t^{p-1}(1-t)^{q-1} dt for p, q > 0, related to the gamma function by B(p,q) = Γ(p)Γ(q)/Γ(p+q).

nodes.name: Digamma function
nodes.description: The logarithmic derivative ψ(x) = Γ'(x)/Γ(x) = (d/dx) log Γ(x), whose asymptotic expansion involves Bernoulli numbers: ψ(x) ~ log x - 1/(2x) - Σₖ₌₁^∞ B₂ₖ/(2k·x²ᵏ).

nodes.name: Abscissa of convergence
nodes.description: The infimum σ₀ of real numbers σ such that the Laplace integral ∫₀^∞ e^{-σt} f(t) dt converges, establishing a half-plane Re(s) > σ₀ of convergence.

nodes.name: Abscissa of absolute convergence
nodes.description: The infimum σₐ of real numbers σ such that ∫₀^∞ e^{-σt} |f(t)| dt converges, always satisfying σ₀ ≤ σₐ ≤ σ₀ + 1 for locally integrable f.

nodes.name: Laplace transform of derivatives
nodes.description: L{f'}(s) = sL{f}(s) - f(0⁺), and more generally L{f⁽ⁿ⁾}(s) = sⁿL{f}(s) - Σₖ₌₀ⁿ⁻¹ sⁿ⁻¹⁻ᵏ f⁽ᵏ⁾(0⁺), converting differential equations to algebraic equations.

nodes.name: Laplace transform of convolutions
nodes.description: L{f * g}(s) = L{f}(s) · L{g}(s), where (f * g)(t) = ∫₀ᵗ f(t-u) g(u) du, converting convolution to pointwise multiplication.

nodes.name: Inversion formula for Laplace transform
nodes.description: Under suitable conditions, f(t) = (1/2πi) ∫_{c-i∞}^{c+i∞} e^{st} L{f}(s) ds for c > σ₀, recovering f from its Laplace transform via a Bromwich contour integral.

nodes.name: Uniqueness theorem for Laplace transform
nodes.description: If L{f}(s) = L{g}(s) for all s in a half-plane and f, g are continuous, then f = g, establishing injectivity of the Laplace transform on continuous functions.

nodes.name: Application of Laplace transform to linear ODE
nodes.description: Converting a linear ODE with constant coefficients and initial conditions to an algebraic equation via Laplace transform, solving algebraically, then inverting to obtain the solution.
nodes.function_signature: (Linear ODE with initial conditions) → (Algebraic equation → Solution via inversion)

nodes.name: Valued field
nodes.description: A field K equipped with an absolute value |·|: K → R₊ satisfying |xy| = |x||y| and the triangle inequality, inducing a metric topology on K.

nodes.name: Neighborhood of zero (fundamental system)
nodes.description: In a TVS, the topology is entirely determined by a fundamental system of neighborhoods of the origin, which must be absorbing, balanced sets; translations then give the full topology.

nodes.name: Absorbing set
nodes.description: A subset A of a vector space E such that for every x ∈ E there exists λ₀ > 0 with x ∈ λA for all |λ| ≥ λ₀.

nodes.name: Balanced set
nodes.description: A subset B of a vector space E such that λB ⊆ B for all scalars λ with |λ| ≤ 1.

nodes.name: Bounded set in a TVS
nodes.description: A subset B of a TVS E is bounded if for every neighborhood V of 0, there exists λ > 0 such that B ⊆ λV, equivalently if B is absorbed by every neighborhood of zero.

nodes.name: Metrizable TVS
nodes.description: A TVS whose topology is metrizable, which occurs if and only if it has a countable fundamental system of neighborhoods of zero, in which case it can be metrized by a translation-invariant metric.

nodes.name: Normable TVS
nodes.description: A TVS whose topology can be defined by a single norm, characterized by having a bounded convex neighborhood of zero.

nodes.name: Completeness of a TVS
nodes.description: A TVS is complete if every Cauchy net (or Cauchy filter) converges; a complete metrizable locally convex space is a Fréchet space.

nodes.name: Topological direct sum of TVS
nodes.description: A TVS E is a topological direct sum of subspaces E₁ and E₂ if the map (x₁, x₂) ↦ x₁ + x₂ is a topological isomorphism from E₁ × E₂ to E.

nodes.name: Quotient TVS
nodes.description: For a closed subspace F of a TVS E, the quotient E/F with the quotient topology is again a TVS, and E/F is Hausdorff if and only if F is closed.

nodes.name: Product of TVS
nodes.description: The Cartesian product Πᵢ Eᵢ of TVS equipped with the product topology is again a TVS, and it is locally convex (resp. complete) if each factor is.

nodes.name: Minkowski functional (gauge)
nodes.description: For a convex absorbing set C containing 0, the Minkowski functional is p_C(x) = inf{λ > 0 : x ∈ λC}, which is a sublinear function and a seminorm when C is balanced.

nodes.name: Strict separation theorem
nodes.description: If A is a closed convex set and B is a compact convex set in a locally convex space with A ∩ B = ∅, then there exists a continuous linear functional strictly separating them: sup_{a∈A} f(a) < inf_{b∈B} f(b).

nodes.name: Supporting hyperplane theorem
nodes.description: At every boundary point of a closed convex set in a locally convex space, there exists a closed hyperplane containing the point and having the convex set on one side.

nodes.name: Bipolar theorem
nodes.description: For a subset A of a locally convex space, the bipolar A°° equals the closed convex balanced hull of A.

nodes.name: Space of continuous linear maps L(E, F)
nodes.description: The vector space of all continuous linear maps from a TVS E to a TVS F, which can be given various topologies depending on the notion of convergence desired.

nodes.name: Topology of bounded convergence (strong topology on L(E,F))
nodes.description: The topology on L(E,F) of uniform convergence on bounded subsets of E, making L(E,F) into a locally convex space when F is locally convex.

nodes.name: Topology of pointwise convergence (weak topology on L(E,F))
nodes.description: The coarsest topology on L(E,F) making all evaluation maps u ↦ u(x) continuous, also called the simple topology.

nodes.name: Barrelled space
nodes.description: A locally convex space in which every barrel (closed, convex, balanced, absorbing set) is a neighborhood of zero; every Fréchet space and every Baire locally convex space is barrelled.

nodes.name: Barrel
nodes.description: A subset of a TVS that is closed, convex, balanced, and absorbing.

nodes.name: Weak-* topology σ(E', E)
nodes.description: The weak topology on the dual E' of a TVS E induced by the duality ⟨E', E⟩, under which E' is a locally convex space and E embeds canonically into (E')'.

nodes.name: Mackey topology τ(E, F)
nodes.description: The finest locally convex topology on E consistent with the duality ⟨E, F⟩, defined as the topology of uniform convergence on σ(F, E)-compact convex balanced subsets of F.

nodes.name: Semi-reflexive space
nodes.description: A locally convex space E is semi-reflexive if the canonical map J: E → E'' is surjective (algebraic isomorphism), without requiring it to be a homeomorphism.

nodes.name: Strong topology β(E', E)
nodes.description: The topology on E' of uniform convergence on all bounded subsets of E, making E' a locally convex space called the strong dual.

nodes.name: Grothendieck completion theorem
nodes.description: Every Hausdorff locally convex space has a completion that is unique up to topological isomorphism, constructed as a subspace of the algebraic dual of E' with the topology of uniform convergence on equicontinuous sets.

nodes.name: Transpose (adjoint) of a continuous linear map
nodes.description: For u: E → F continuous linear, the transpose ᵗu: F' → E' is defined by ⟨ᵗu(f), x⟩ = ⟨f, u(x)⟩, and ᵗu is continuous for the weak-* and strong topologies.

nodes.name: Weak compactness and completeness
nodes.description: In a complete locally convex space, a closed bounded set is weakly compact if and only if every bounded sequence has a weakly convergent subsequence.

nodes.name: Parallelogram law
nodes.description: In an inner product space, ‖x+y‖² + ‖x-y‖² = 2(‖x‖² + ‖y‖²), and a normed space satisfying this identity is an inner product space (Jordan-von Neumann theorem).

nodes.name: Orthogonality
nodes.description: Two elements x, y of an inner product space are orthogonal (x ⊥ y) if ⟨x,y⟩ = 0; a set S is orthogonal if its elements are pairwise orthogonal.

nodes.name: Orthogonal projection theorem
nodes.description: For every closed subspace M of a Hilbert space H, each x ∈ H has a unique decomposition x = m + m⊥ with m ∈ M and m⊥ ∈ M⊥, and m is the unique best approximation of x from M.

nodes.name: Orthonormal system
nodes.description: A family (eᵢ) in a Hilbert space such that ⟨eᵢ, eⱼ⟩ = δᵢⱼ (Kronecker delta), i.e., pairwise orthogonal unit vectors.

nodes.name: Normal operator
nodes.description: A bounded linear operator T on a Hilbert space satisfying T*T = TT*, implying the spectral theorem applies.

nodes.name: Direct sum of Hilbert spaces
nodes.description: The Hilbert space direct sum ⊕ᵢ Hᵢ consists of families (xᵢ) with xᵢ ∈ Hᵢ and Σᵢ ‖xᵢ‖² < ∞, equipped with the inner product ⟨(xᵢ),(yᵢ)⟩ = Σᵢ ⟨xᵢ,yᵢ⟩.

nodes.name: Young's inequality for products
nodes.description: For a, b >= 0 and conjugate exponents p, q (1/p + 1/q = 1): ab <= a^p/p + b^q/q, with equality iff a^p = b^q.

nodes.name: Conjugate exponents
nodes.description: A pair (p, q) with 1 <= p, q <= infinity satisfying 1/p + 1/q = 1, fundamental to Lp space duality and Holder's inequality.

nodes.name: Log-convexity of Lp norms (Riesz interpolation inequality)
nodes.description: For 1 <= p1 <= p <= p2 <= infinity, if f in Lp1 cap Lp2, then f in Lp and ||f||_p <= ||f||_{p1}^theta ||f||_{p2}^{1-theta} where 1/p = theta/p1 + (1-theta)/p2.

nodes.name: Bounded Radon measure
nodes.description: A Radon measure mu on X that extends to a continuous linear form on C_0(X), equivalently one with finite total variation |mu|(X) < infinity.

nodes.name: Support of a measure
nodes.description: The smallest closed set F such that mu(f) = 0 for every continuous function f with compact support contained in X \ F.

nodes.name: Total variation measure
nodes.description: For a complex Radon measure mu, the positive measure |mu| defined by |mu|(f) = sup{|mu(g)| : |g| <= f, g in K(X)} for f >= 0, making bounded measures a Banach space under ||mu|| = |mu|(X).

nodes.name: Vague topology on measures
nodes.description: The weak-* topology sigma(M(X), K(X)) on the space of Radon measures, where mu_n -> mu vaguely iff mu_n(f) -> mu(f) for all f in K(X).

nodes.name: Dirac measure
nodes.description: The measure delta_x defined by delta_x(f) = f(x) for a point x in X, the atomic probability measure concentrated at a single point.

nodes.name: Image measure (pushforward measure)
nodes.description: For a proper continuous map phi: X -> Y and a measure mu on X, the image measure phi_*(mu) on Y defined by phi_*(mu)(f) = mu(f o phi).

nodes.name: Regularity of Radon measures
nodes.description: Every Radon measure on a locally compact space is inner regular (approximable from below by compact sets) and outer regular (approximable from above by open sets) on sigma-finite measurable sets.

nodes.name: Upper integral
nodes.description: For a positive measure mu and a lower semicontinuous function f >= 0, defined as mu*(f) = sup{mu(g) : g in K(X), 0 <= g <= f}, extending integration beyond continuous functions.

nodes.name: Measurable function (Bourbaki, mu-measurable)
nodes.description: A function f: X -> R is mu-measurable if for every compact K and epsilon > 0, there exists compact K' subset K with mu(K \ K') < epsilon such that f|_{K'} is continuous (Lusin characterization).

nodes.name: Integrable function (Lebesgue integrable)
nodes.description: A measurable function f is mu-integrable if integral |f| dmu < infinity, where the integral is defined via the Daniell construction extending from continuous functions with compact support.

nodes.name: Negligible set (mu-null set)
nodes.description: A set N subset X is mu-negligible if mu*(chi_N) = 0, equivalently if it is contained in an open set of arbitrarily small measure.

nodes.name: Lp space (1 <= p < infinity)
nodes.description: The Banach space of equivalence classes of measurable functions f with integral |f|^p dmu < infinity, modulo equality a.e., with norm ||f||_p = (integral |f|^p dmu)^{1/p}.

nodes.name: L-infinity space
nodes.description: The Banach space of equivalence classes of essentially bounded measurable functions, with norm ||f||_infinity = ess sup |f| = inf{M : |f| <= M a.e.}.

nodes.name: Dense subspaces of Lp
nodes.description: For 1 <= p < infinity, the space K(X) of continuous functions with compact support is dense in Lp(mu), as is the space of simple functions.

nodes.name: Essential supremum
nodes.description: The essential supremum of a measurable function f is ess sup f = inf{M in R : f <= M a.e.}, the smallest a.e. upper bound.

nodes.name: Convergence in measure
nodes.description: A sequence (f_n) converges to f in measure if for every epsilon > 0, mu({x : |f_n(x) - f(x)| > epsilon}) -> 0; Lp convergence implies convergence in measure.

nodes.name: Product measure
nodes.description: For sigma-finite measures mu on X and nu on Y, the unique measure mu tensor nu on X x Y satisfying (mu tensor nu)(A x B) = mu(A) nu(B) for measurable rectangles.

nodes.name: Tonelli's theorem
nodes.description: If f is a non-negative measurable function on X x Y, then integral f d(mu tensor nu) = integral integral f(x,y) dmu(x) dnu(y), with iterated integrals equal without assuming integrability.

nodes.name: Change of variables formula (integration on Rn)
nodes.description: If phi: U -> V is a C1 diffeomorphism between open sets in Rn, then integral_V f(y) dy = integral_U f(phi(x)) |det J_phi(x)| dx for integrable f.

nodes.name: Bochner integral
nodes.description: The integral of a strongly measurable function f: X -> E (E a Banach space) with integral ||f|| dmu < infinity, defined as the limit of integrals of simple functions; f is Bochner integrable iff ||f|| is Lebesgue integrable.

nodes.name: Strongly measurable function
nodes.description: A function f: X -> E (E separable Banach space) is strongly measurable if it is the a.e. limit of a sequence of simple (measurable, finitely-valued) functions.

nodes.name: Vector-valued measure (vector measure)
nodes.description: A countably additive map mu: Sigma -> E from a sigma-algebra into a Banach space, generalizing scalar measures.

nodes.name: Radon-Nikodym derivative (density)
nodes.description: The a.e. unique measurable function dnu/dmu satisfying nu(A) = integral_A (dnu/dmu) dmu for all measurable sets A, existing when nu << mu and both are sigma-finite.

nodes.name: Left invariance of Haar measure
nodes.description: A measure mu on a topological group G is left-invariant if mu(gA) = mu(A) for all g in G and all measurable A, equivalently integral f(g^{-1}x) dmu(x) = integral f(x) dmu(x).

nodes.name: Right Haar measure
nodes.description: A right-invariant positive Radon measure on G, related to left Haar measure via the modular function: d mu_r(x) = Delta(x^{-1}) d mu_l(x).

nodes.name: Modular function
nodes.description: The continuous homomorphism Delta: G -> R_+* defined by mu(Ag) = Delta(g) mu(A) for left Haar measure mu, measuring the failure of left Haar measure to be right-invariant.

nodes.name: Unimodular group
nodes.description: A locally compact group whose modular function is identically 1, so left and right Haar measures coincide; includes all compact groups, abelian groups, and semisimple Lie groups.

nodes.name: Haar measure on compact groups
nodes.description: On a compact group, the Haar measure is both left- and right-invariant (unimodular) and can be normalized to a probability measure with mu(G) = 1.

nodes.name: Integration formula for quotient groups
nodes.description: If H is a closed subgroup of G with Haar measures mu_G, mu_H, and G/H admits an invariant measure, then integral_G f dmu_G = integral_{G/H} (integral_H f(xh) dmu_H(h)) dmu_{G/H}(xH).

nodes.name: Weil's formula (quotient integral formula)
nodes.description: A G-invariant measure on the quotient space G/H exists if and only if Delta_G|_H = Delta_H, and when it exists it is unique up to a positive scalar.

nodes.name: Convolution of measures
nodes.description: For bounded Radon measures mu and nu on a locally compact group G, the convolution (mu * nu)(f) = integral integral f(xy) dmu(x) dnu(y), making bounded measures a Banach algebra.

nodes.name: Convolution of functions on a group
nodes.description: For f, g in L1(G), the convolution (f * g)(x) = integral_G f(xy^{-1}) g(y) dmu(y) with respect to left Haar measure, making L1(G) a Banach algebra.

nodes.name: Approximate identity in L1(G)
nodes.description: A net (e_i) in L1(G) with integral e_i dmu = 1 and support shrinking to {e} such that e_i * f -> f in L1 norm for all f, replacing the absent unit element.

nodes.name: Character of a representation
nodes.description: The character of a finite-dimensional representation pi is the function chi_pi(g) = tr(pi(g)), a continuous class function that determines the representation up to equivalence.

nodes.name: Convolution algebra of measures M(G)
nodes.description: The Banach space of bounded Radon measures on G with convolution as multiplication and total variation as norm, forming a unital Banach algebra with unit delta_e.

nodes.name: Integrated representation
nodes.description: For a unitary representation pi of G on H, the integrated form pi~: L1(G) -> B(H) defined by pi~(f) = integral_G f(g) pi(g) dmu(g) is a non-degenerate *-representation of the group algebra.

nodes.name: Fourier transform on locally compact abelian groups
nodes.description: For f in L1(G), the Fourier transform f_hat(chi) = integral_G f(g) overline{chi(g)} dmu(g) for chi in G_hat, mapping L1(G) to C_0(G_hat) and satisfying (f * g)^ = f_hat g_hat.

nodes.name: Fourier inversion formula (LCA groups)
nodes.description: Under appropriate normalization of Haar measures, if f in L1(G) and f_hat in L1(G_hat), then f(g) = integral_{G_hat} f_hat(chi) chi(g) d mu_hat(chi) for a.e. g.

nodes.name: Tight measure
nodes.description: A Borel measure mu on a topological space X is tight if for every epsilon > 0, there exists a compact set K with mu(X \ K) < epsilon.

nodes.name: Weak convergence of measures (narrow convergence)
nodes.description: A sequence of measures mu_n converges weakly to mu if integral f dmu_n -> integral f dmu for all bounded continuous functions f.

nodes.name: Regular Borel measure
nodes.description: A Borel measure that is both inner regular (mu(A) = sup{mu(K) : K subset A compact}) and outer regular (mu(A) = inf{mu(U) : U supset A open}) on all measurable sets.

nodes.name: Inner regularity
nodes.description: A measure mu is inner regular on a measurable set A if mu(A) = sup{mu(K) : K subset A, K compact}.

nodes.name: Outer regularity
nodes.description: A measure mu is outer regular on a measurable set A if mu(A) = inf{mu(U) : A subset U, U open}.

nodes.name: Suslin space (analytic space)
nodes.description: A Hausdorff topological space that is the continuous image of a Polish space; every Borel subset of a Polish space is Suslin, and measures on Suslin spaces have strong regularity properties.

nodes.name: Choquet capacitability theorem
nodes.description: In a Suslin space, every analytic set is capacitable, meaning its outer measure equals the supremum of measures of compact subsets, extending inner regularity to analytic sets.

nodes.name: Daniell integral approach
nodes.function_signature: (Positive linear functional on lattice of functions) -> (Complete measure and integration theory)
nodes.description: Bourbaki's method of defining integration starting from a positive linear functional on a lattice of functions, then extending via upper integrals and completion, rather than from a measure on sets.

nodes.name: Approximation by continuous functions
nodes.function_signature: (Measurable or integrable function, epsilon > 0) -> (Continuous function with compact support within epsilon)
nodes.description: The systematic use of Urysohn's lemma and partitions of unity to approximate measurable or integrable functions by continuous functions with compact support.

nodes.name: Inductive limit topology
nodes.description: The finest locally convex topology on K(X) = union_K C(K) making all inclusion maps C(K) -> K(X) continuous, used in Bourbaki's definition of Radon measures.

nodes.name: Abel-Liouville formula (Wronskian formula)
nodes.description: The Wronskian of solutions of y' = A(t)y satisfies W(t) = W(t_0) exp(integral_{t_0}^t tr A(s) ds), showing it is either identically zero or never zero.

nodes.name: Pontryagin dual group
nodes.description: For a locally compact abelian group G, the dual group G_hat = Hom(G, T) is the group of continuous homomorphisms from G to the circle group T, equipped with the compact-open topology.

nodes.name: Spectral radius formula
nodes.description: For a bounded linear operator T on a Banach space, the spectral radius r(T) = lim ||T^n||^{1/n} = inf ||T^n||^{1/n}.

nodes.name: Resolvent of an operator
nodes.description: For lambda not in sigma(T), the resolvent R(lambda,T) = (lambda I - T)^{-1} is a bounded operator depending analytically on lambda, satisfying the resolvent identity R(lambda) - R(mu) = (mu - lambda)R(lambda)R(mu).

nodes.name: Pettis integral (weak integral)
nodes.description: A vector x in E is the Pettis integral of f: X -> E if <x, x'> = integral <f, x'> dmu for all x' in E'; weaker than Bochner, requiring only scalar measurability.

nodes.name: Convolution semigroup
nodes.description: A family (mu_t)_{t>=0} of probability measures on a locally compact group satisfying mu_s * mu_t = mu_{s+t} and mu_0 = delta_e, modeling diffusion and Markov processes on groups.

nodes.name: Lie algebra homomorphism
nodes.description: A linear map φ: g → h between Lie algebras satisfying φ([x,y]) = [φ(x),φ(y)] for all x,y in g.

nodes.name: Quotient Lie algebra
nodes.description: For an ideal a of g, the vector space g/a equipped with the bracket [x+a, y+a] = [x,y]+a, yielding a well-defined Lie algebra structure.

nodes.name: Center of a Lie algebra
nodes.description: The ideal z(g) = {x ∈ g : [x,y] = 0 for all y ∈ g}, consisting of elements that bracket trivially with all of g.

nodes.name: Derived subalgebra (commutator subalgebra)
nodes.description: The ideal [g,g] = D(g) spanned by all brackets [x,y], measuring the failure of g to be abelian.

nodes.name: Derived series
nodes.description: The descending sequence D⁰(g) = g, Dⁿ⁺¹(g) = [Dⁿ(g), Dⁿ(g)] obtained by iterating the derived subalgebra construction.

nodes.name: Radical of a Lie algebra
nodes.description: The unique maximal solvable ideal rad(g) of a finite-dimensional Lie algebra g, which contains every solvable ideal.

nodes.name: Simple Lie algebra
nodes.description: A non-abelian Lie algebra whose only ideals are 0 and itself, serving as the irreducible building blocks of semisimple Lie algebras.

nodes.name: Lie's theorem
nodes.description: If g is a solvable Lie algebra over an algebraically closed field of characteristic zero and V is a finite-dimensional g-module, then there exists a common eigenvector for all elements of g acting on V.

nodes.name: Cartan's criterion for solvability
nodes.description: A finite-dimensional Lie algebra g over a field of characteristic zero is solvable if and only if B(x,y) = 0 for all x ∈ g and y ∈ [g,g], where B is the Killing form.

nodes.name: Cartan's criterion for semisimplicity
nodes.description: A finite-dimensional Lie algebra g over a field of characteristic zero is semisimple if and only if its Killing form is non-degenerate.

nodes.name: Levi decomposition
nodes.description: Every finite-dimensional Lie algebra g over a field of characteristic zero is a semidirect product g = rad(g) ⋊ s where s is a semisimple subalgebra (called a Levi factor), and any two Levi factors are conjugate.

nodes.name: Poincaré-Birkhoff-Witt theorem
nodes.description: If {x₁,...,xₙ} is an ordered basis of g, then the monomials x₁^{a₁}···xₙ^{aₙ} form a basis of U(g), proving the canonical map g → U(g) is injective.

nodes.name: Normalizer of a subalgebra
nodes.description: For a subalgebra h of g, the subalgebra N_g(h) = {x ∈ g : [x,h] ⊆ h}, the largest subalgebra of g in which h is an ideal.

nodes.name: Centralizer in a Lie algebra
nodes.description: For a subset S of g, the subalgebra C_g(S) = {x ∈ g : [x,s] = 0 for all s ∈ S}, consisting of elements commuting with all of S.

nodes.name: Semidirect product of Lie algebras
nodes.description: Given Lie algebras h and a with a representation ρ: h → der(a), the vector space h ⊕ a with bracket [(h₁,a₁),(h₂,a₂)] = ([h₁,h₂], [a₁,a₂]+ρ(h₁)a₂−ρ(h₂)a₁).

nodes.name: Derivation of a Lie algebra
nodes.description: A linear map D: g → g satisfying D([x,y]) = [D(x),y] + [x,D(y)], with inner derivations being those of the form ad(x).

nodes.name: Whitehead's lemma (first)
nodes.description: For a semisimple Lie algebra g over a field of characteristic zero and a finite-dimensional g-module V, every derivation from g to V is inner, i.e., H¹(g,V) = 0.

nodes.name: Whitehead's lemma (second)
nodes.description: For a semisimple Lie algebra g over characteristic zero and a finite-dimensional g-module V, every extension of g by V splits, i.e., H²(g,V) = 0.

nodes.name: Jordan decomposition in a Lie algebra
nodes.description: In a semisimple Lie algebra g over a perfect field, each element x has a unique decomposition x = xₛ + xₙ with xₛ semisimple, xₙ nilpotent, and [xₛ,xₙ] = 0, compatible with any faithful representation.

nodes.name: Invariant bilinear form
nodes.description: A bilinear form B on g satisfying B([x,y],z) = B(x,[y,z]) for all x,y,z ∈ g, with the Killing form being the canonical example.

nodes.name: Witt formula
nodes.description: The dimension of the degree-n homogeneous component of the free Lie algebra on q generators is (1/n)∑_{d|n} μ(d)q^{n/d}, where μ is the Möbius function.

nodes.name: Baker-Campbell-Hausdorff formula
nodes.description: For elements x,y in a complete filtered Lie algebra (or in a neighborhood of identity in a Lie group), log(eˣeʸ) = x + y + ½[x,y] + 1/12([x,[x,y]]+[y,[y,x]]) + ···, expressing the group product in terms of iterated Lie brackets.

nodes.name: Lie group homomorphism
nodes.description: A smooth group homomorphism between Lie groups, whose differential at the identity is a Lie algebra homomorphism.

nodes.name: Lie algebra of a Lie group
nodes.description: The tangent space at the identity g = T_eG equipped with the Lie bracket inherited from left-invariant vector fields, functorially associated to the Lie group G.

nodes.name: Lie subgroup
nodes.description: A subgroup H of a Lie group G that is an immersed submanifold (or, in the closed case, an embedded submanifold) carrying an induced Lie group structure.

nodes.name: Closed subgroup theorem (Cartan's theorem)
nodes.description: Every closed subgroup of a Lie group is an embedded Lie subgroup, i.e., it automatically inherits a smooth manifold structure making it a Lie group in the subspace topology.

nodes.name: Quotient of a Lie group
nodes.description: For a closed normal subgroup N of G, the quotient G/N carries a unique Lie group structure making the projection G → G/N a smooth surjective homomorphism with Lie algebra g/n.

nodes.name: Lie functor
nodes.description: The functor Lie: LieGrp → LieAlg sending each Lie group to its Lie algebra and each homomorphism to its differential at the identity, providing the algebraic linearization of group theory.
nodes.function_signature: (Input) → (Output)

nodes.name: Integration of Lie algebra homomorphisms
nodes.description: The process of lifting a Lie algebra homomorphism g → h to a Lie group homomorphism G → H when G is simply connected, by using the exponential map and path-lifting.
nodes.function_signature: (Input) → (Output)

nodes.name: Coxeter group
nodes.description: A group W with a presentation ⟨s₁,...,sₙ | (sᵢsⱼ)^{mᵢⱼ} = 1⟩ where mᵢᵢ = 1 and mᵢⱼ = mⱼᵢ ≥ 2 (or ∞), abstracting the structure of reflection groups.

nodes.name: Coxeter matrix
nodes.description: A symmetric matrix M = (mᵢⱼ) with mᵢᵢ = 1 and mᵢⱼ ∈ {2,3,...,∞} for i≠j, encoding the orders of products of pairs of generators in a Coxeter group.

nodes.name: Coxeter graph
nodes.description: A labeled graph with vertices indexed by generators of a Coxeter group, edges connecting pairs with mᵢⱼ ≥ 3, and edge labels mᵢⱼ when mᵢⱼ ≥ 4, encoding the Coxeter matrix.

nodes.name: Exchange property
nodes.description: In a Coxeter group, if ℓ(sw) < ℓ(w) for a simple reflection s, then there exists an index i such that sw = s₁···ŝᵢ···sₖ (omitting sᵢ) for any reduced expression w = s₁···sₖ.

nodes.name: Deletion property
nodes.description: In a Coxeter group, any non-reduced expression s₁···sₖ can be shortened by deleting an even number of factors to obtain a reduced expression for the same element.

nodes.name: Tits system (BN-pair)
nodes.description: A group G with subgroups B and N such that B ∩ N = T is normal in N, W = N/T is a Coxeter group with generators S, and the axioms BwB·BsB ⊆ BwsB ∪ BwB and sBs⁻¹ ⊄ B hold for all w ∈ W, s ∈ S.

nodes.name: Parabolic subgroup of a Coxeter group
nodes.description: For a subset J ⊆ S of simple reflections, the subgroup W_J generated by J, which is itself a Coxeter group with Coxeter matrix restricted to J.

nodes.name: Coxeter complex
nodes.description: The simplicial complex associated to a Coxeter group W whose simplices are cosets of parabolic subgroups of W, serving as the building block (apartment) of a Tits building.

nodes.name: Matsumoto's theorem
nodes.description: Any two reduced expressions for the same element of a Coxeter group are related by a sequence of braid relations sᵢsⱼsᵢ··· = sⱼsᵢsⱼ··· (mᵢⱼ factors each side), without requiring insertion/deletion.

nodes.name: Strong exchange property
nodes.description: In a Coxeter group, if ℓ(tw) < ℓ(w) for a reflection t (not necessarily simple), then t can replace one of the factors in any reduced expression for w.

nodes.name: Classification of finite Coxeter groups
nodes.description: The irreducible finite Coxeter groups are exactly the types Aₙ, Bₙ, Dₙ, E₆, E₇, E₈, F₄, G₂ (crystallographic, i.e., Weyl groups) together with H₃, H₄, and I₂(m) (non-crystallographic).

nodes.name: Coroot
nodes.description: For a root α, the coroot α∨ = 2α/⟨α,α⟩, such that the reflection s_α(β) = β − ⟨β,α∨⟩α, and the coroots form the dual root system.

nodes.name: Cartan matrix
nodes.description: The n×n integer matrix A = (aᵢⱼ) where aᵢⱼ = ⟨αᵢ,αⱼ∨⟩ for simple roots αᵢ,αⱼ, satisfying aᵢᵢ = 2, aᵢⱼ ≤ 0 for i≠j, and aᵢⱼ = 0 iff aⱼᵢ = 0, determining the root system up to isomorphism.

nodes.name: Classification of irreducible root systems
nodes.description: The connected Dynkin diagrams (equivalently irreducible root systems) are exactly Aₙ (n≥1), Bₙ (n≥2), Cₙ (n≥3), Dₙ (n≥4), E₆, E₇, E₈, F₄, and G₂.

nodes.name: Weyl chamber
nodes.description: A connected component of E \ ∪_{α∈Φ} H_α where H_α = ker(α), forming a fundamental domain for the W-action; the dominant chamber is the one defined by ⟨·,αᵢ∨⟩ > 0 for all simple αᵢ.

nodes.name: Root lattice
nodes.description: The Z-span Q = ZΦ of the root system in E, a sublattice of the weight lattice, with the quotient P/Q being a finite group isomorphic to the center of the simply connected group.

nodes.name: Fundamental weights
nodes.description: The basis {ω₁,...,ωₙ} of the weight lattice P dual to the simple coroots, defined by ⟨ωᵢ,αⱼ∨⟩ = δᵢⱼ, indexing the vertices of the fundamental Weyl chamber.

nodes.name: Extended (affine) Dynkin diagram
nodes.description: The Dynkin diagram augmented by an additional node corresponding to the negative of the highest root −θ, classifying affine root systems and appearing in the theory of loop algebras.

nodes.name: Affine root system
nodes.description: An infinite root system on an affine space obtained by adding integer translates α + nδ of roots of a finite root system, whose Weyl group is the affine Weyl group acting by reflections in affine hyperplanes.

nodes.name: Affine Weyl group
nodes.description: The infinite Coxeter group generated by reflections in affine hyperplanes H_{α,n} = {x : ⟨x,α⟩ = n}, isomorphic to the semidirect product W ⋉ Q∨ of the Weyl group with the coroot lattice.

nodes.name: Alcove
nodes.description: A connected component of the complement of all affine reflecting hyperplanes, forming a fundamental domain for the affine Weyl group; the fundamental alcove is a simplex.

nodes.name: Root space decomposition
nodes.description: For a semisimple Lie algebra g with Cartan subalgebra h, the decomposition g = h ⊕ (⊕_{α∈Φ} g_α) where g_α = {x ∈ g : [h,x] = α(h)x for all h ∈ h} and Φ ⊂ h* is the root system.

nodes.name: Chevalley basis
nodes.description: A basis {hᵢ, e_α} of a semisimple Lie algebra with integer structure constants, consisting of coroots hᵢ = αᵢ∨ in h and root vectors e_α ∈ g_α satisfying [e_α, e_{-α}] = α∨ and specific sign conventions.

nodes.name: Conjugacy of Cartan subalgebras
nodes.description: Any two Cartan subalgebras of a finite-dimensional Lie algebra over an algebraically closed field of characteristic zero are conjugate by an inner automorphism of g.

nodes.name: sl₂-triple
nodes.description: A triple (e,h,f) in a Lie algebra satisfying [h,e] = 2e, [h,f] = −2f, [e,f] = h, spanning a subalgebra isomorphic to sl(2), with one such triple for each root.

nodes.name: Jacobson-Morozov theorem
nodes.description: In a semisimple Lie algebra over a field of characteristic zero, every nilpotent element e can be embedded in an sl₂-triple (e,h,f), and the sl₂-triples for a given nilpotent orbit are conjugate.

nodes.name: Split semisimple Lie algebra
nodes.description: A semisimple Lie algebra g over a field k possessing a splitting Cartan subalgebra h such that all roots are in k (not just in the algebraic closure), equivalently g is an inner form.

nodes.name: Parabolic subalgebra
nodes.description: A subalgebra p of g containing a Borel subalgebra, classified by subsets of simple roots and corresponding to parabolic subgroups in the group setting.

nodes.name: Kostant multiplicity formula
nodes.description: The multiplicity of weight μ in L(λ) is dim L(λ)_μ = ∑_{w∈W} ε(w) P(w(λ+ρ) − (μ+ρ)) where P is the Kostant partition function counting expressions as sums of positive roots.

nodes.name: Kostant partition function
nodes.description: The function P(ν) counting the number of ways to write ν as an unordered sum of positive roots (with repetition), appearing in weight multiplicity formulas.

nodes.name: Freudenthal's formula
nodes.description: A recursive formula computing the multiplicity of a weight μ in L(λ) using the inner product of weights and the multiplicities of higher weights, derived from the Casimir operator.

nodes.name: Existence theorem for semisimple Lie algebras
nodes.description: For every Cartan matrix (equivalently every Dynkin diagram), there exists a unique (up to isomorphism) semisimple Lie algebra over an algebraically closed field of characteristic zero having that Cartan matrix.

nodes.name: Serre's presentation (Serre relations)
nodes.description: A semisimple Lie algebra is the quotient of the free Lie algebra on generators {eᵢ, fᵢ, hᵢ} by the relations [hᵢ,hⱼ]=0, [hᵢ,eⱼ]=aᵢⱼeⱼ, [hᵢ,fⱼ]=−aᵢⱼfⱼ, [eᵢ,fⱼ]=δᵢⱼhᵢ, and (ad eᵢ)^{1−aᵢⱼ}(eⱼ)=0 (and similarly for f).

nodes.name: Maximal torus
nodes.description: A maximal connected abelian subgroup T of a compact Lie group G, isomorphic to (S¹)ʳ where r = rank(G); every element of G is conjugate to an element of T.

nodes.name: Conjugacy of maximal tori
nodes.description: Any two maximal tori in a compact Lie group are conjugate by an inner automorphism, so the rank and the Weyl group N_G(T)/T are well-defined invariants.

nodes.name: Compact real form
nodes.description: A compact real Lie subalgebra g_u of a complex semisimple Lie algebra g_C such that g_C = g_u ⊗_R C, unique up to conjugacy; its Killing form is negative definite.

nodes.name: Weyl's unitary trick
nodes.description: The technique of proving results for a complex semisimple Lie algebra by passing to its compact real form, where integration over the compact group via Haar measure and averaging yields complete reducibility and other results.
nodes.function_signature: (Input) → (Output)

nodes.name: Banach algebra
nodes.description: A complete normed algebra A over C (or R) satisfying ‖xy‖ ≤ ‖x‖·‖y‖, providing the analytic framework for spectral theory and operator algebras.

nodes.name: Resolvent identity
nodes.description: For λ,μ in the resolvent set, R(λ,a) − R(μ,a) = (μ−λ)R(λ,a)R(μ,a), and the resolvent is an analytic function of λ vanishing at infinity.

nodes.name: Character (multiplicative linear functional)
nodes.description: A nonzero algebra homomorphism χ: A → C from a commutative Banach algebra A, necessarily continuous with ‖χ‖ = 1 and χ(1) = 1, forming the points of the Gelfand spectrum.

nodes.name: Gelfand spectrum (maximal ideal space)
nodes.description: The set Ω(A) of all characters of a commutative unital Banach algebra A, equipped with the weak-* topology making it a compact Hausdorff space; maximal ideals correspond bijectively to characters via ker(χ).

nodes.name: C*-identity
nodes.description: The norm condition ‖a*a‖ = ‖a‖² characterizing C*-algebras, from which it follows that ‖a*‖ = ‖a‖ and the norm is uniquely determined by the algebraic structure.

nodes.name: State on a C*-algebra
nodes.description: A positive linear functional φ: A → C with ‖φ‖ = 1 (or φ(1) = 1 in the unital case), serving as a noncommutative probability measure and providing the input for the GNS construction.

nodes.name: Cyclic vector
nodes.description: A vector ξ in a Hilbert space H such that π(A)ξ is dense in H for a representation π of A, ensuring the representation is determined by the state φ(a) = ⟨π(a)ξ,ξ⟩.

nodes.name: Spectral mapping theorem
nodes.description: For a continuous function f and a normal element a of a C*-algebra, σ(f(a)) = f(σ(a)), so the spectrum of f(a) is the image of the spectrum of a under f.

nodes.name: Unitization of a C*-algebra
nodes.description: For a non-unital C*-algebra A, the C*-algebra Ã = A ⊕ C with multiplication (a,λ)(b,μ) = (ab+λb+μa, λμ) and a suitable norm making it a unital C*-algebra containing A as a maximal ideal.

nodes.name: Locally compact group
nodes.description: A topological group whose underlying topology is locally compact and Hausdorff, providing the natural setting for abstract harmonic analysis with the existence of Haar measure.

nodes.name: Convolution product
nodes.description: The binary operation (f*g)(x) = ∫_G f(y)g(y⁻¹x)dy on L¹(G), making it a Banach algebra; for abelian groups, the Gelfand transform of L¹(G) is the Fourier transform.

nodes.name: Group C*-algebra C*(G)
nodes.description: The completion of L¹(G) with respect to the norm ‖f‖_{C*} = sup_π ‖π(f)‖ where the supremum is over all *-representations of L¹(G), whose representations correspond bijectively to unitary representations of G.

nodes.name: Spectral theorem for bounded normal operators
nodes.description: For a bounded normal operator T on a Hilbert space, there exists a unique spectral measure E on σ(T) such that T = ∫_{σ(T)} λ dE(λ), establishing a bijection between normal operators and spectral measures on compact subsets of C.

nodes.name: Spectral theorem for commuting normal operators
nodes.description: A finite family of pairwise commuting bounded normal operators on a Hilbert space has a joint spectral measure E on the product of their spectra, simultaneously diagonalizing all operators as T_k = ∫ λ_k dE(λ₁,...,λₙ).

nodes.name: SNAG theorem (Stone-Naimark-Ambrose-Godement)
nodes.description: Every strongly continuous unitary representation of a locally compact abelian group G on a Hilbert space is of the form π(g) = ∫_Ĝ χ(g) dE(χ) for a unique spectral measure E on the Pontryagin dual Ĝ.

nodes.name: Type decomposition of von Neumann algebras
nodes.description: Every von Neumann algebra decomposes uniquely as a direct sum of type I, type II₁, type II_∞, and type III factors, classified by the structure of their projection lattices.

nodes.name: Holomorphic functional calculus
nodes.description: For an element a of a unital Banach algebra and f holomorphic on a neighborhood of σ(a), f(a) = (1/2πi)∮_Γ f(λ)(λ−a)⁻¹dλ defines an algebra homomorphism from the algebra of germs of holomorphic functions on σ(a) to A.

nodes.name: Fell topology
nodes.description: The topology on the set of irreducible representations of a C*-algebra (or locally compact group) defined by convergence of states, making the unitary dual a (generally non-Hausdorff) topological space.

nodes.name: Spectral permanence
nodes.description: If B is a closed *-subalgebra of a C*-algebra A and a ∈ B, then σ_B(a) = σ_A(a); the spectrum of an element does not change when computed in a C*-subalgebra.

nodes.name: Mellin Transform
nodes.description: The integral transform M{f}(s) = integral_0^infty x^{s-1} f(x) dx, analytic in a vertical strip.

nodes.name: Faa di Bruno's Formula
nodes.description: Explicit formula for the n-th derivative of a composite function f(g(x)) as a sum over partitions involving Bell polynomials.

nodes.name: Leibniz Integral Rule (Differentiation Under the Sign)
nodes.description: d/dx integral_{a(x)}^{b(x)} f(x,t) dt = f(x,b)b' - f(x,a)a' + integral partial_x f dt under suitable regularity.

nodes.name: Poincare Asymptotic Expansion
nodes.description: A formal series f(z) ~ sum a_n z^{-n} as z -> infty, where for each N the remainder is O(z^{-N}) in a given sector.

nodes.name: Watson's Lemma
nodes.description: If f(t) has an asymptotic expansion at t=0, then its Laplace-type integral admits term-by-term asymptotic integration as z -> infty.

nodes.name: Stokes Phenomenon
nodes.description: The discontinuous change in asymptotic expansion form as the argument crosses Stokes lines in the complex plane, where subdominant exponentials switch on or off.

nodes.name: Abel-Plana Summation Formula
nodes.description: Relates sum f(n) to integral f(t) dt plus a correction term involving f(it)-f(-it), converting sums to integrals without requiring derivatives.

nodes.name: Laplace's Method
nodes.function_signature: (Integral of e^{-z p(t)} q(t) dt, z -> infty) -> (Asymptotic expansion)
nodes.description: Obtains asymptotic expansions of Laplace-type integrals for large z by expanding about the minimum of the exponent.

nodes.name: Method of Steepest Descents
nodes.function_signature: (Contour integral with large parameter) -> (Asymptotic expansion via saddle-point deformation)
nodes.description: Deforms a contour integral through saddle points along paths of steepest descent to obtain asymptotic expansions.

nodes.name: Bleistein's Method
nodes.function_signature: (Integral with coalescing critical points) -> (Uniform asymptotic expansion in Airy functions)
nodes.description: Obtains uniform asymptotic expansions when two stationary points coalesce, expressing results in terms of Airy functions.

nodes.name: Mellin Transform Asymptotics
nodes.function_signature: (Mellin-Barnes integral) -> (Asymptotic expansion by contour shifting)
nodes.description: Derives asymptotic expansions by shifting contours in Mellin-Barnes integrals and collecting residues.

nodes.name: Liouville-Green (WKB) Approximation
nodes.function_signature: (Second-order ODE with large parameter) -> (Approximate exponential-integral solutions)
nodes.description: Constructs approximate solutions to d^2w/dz^2 = u^2 f(z) w for large u as f^{-1/4} exp(+/-u integral sqrt{f} dz).

nodes.name: Fuchs-Frobenius Theory
nodes.function_signature: (ODE with regular singular point) -> (Generalized power series solutions via indicial equation)
nodes.description: Constructs solutions of linear ODEs near regular singular points as z^r sum a_n z^n where r satisfies the indicial equation.

nodes.name: Darboux's Method
nodes.function_signature: (Generating function singularity) -> (Asymptotic formula for Taylor coefficients)
nodes.description: Extracts asymptotic behavior of Taylor coefficients from the singularity structure on the circle of convergence.

nodes.name: Exponentially Improved Asymptotics
nodes.function_signature: (Optimally truncated Poincare series) -> (Re-expansion with exponentially small error)
