nodes.description: Re-expands the remainder after optimal truncation to capture exponentially small terms beyond all algebraic orders.

nodes.name: Hyperasymptotics
nodes.function_signature: (Exponentially improved remainder) -> (Iterated re-expansion with super-exponential accuracy)
nodes.description: Iterates exponentially improved asymptotics to achieve successively more accurate approximations.

nodes.name: Borel Summation
nodes.description: Method assigning a value to a divergent series via Borel transform and Laplace integral: sum a_n z^n -> integral_0^infty e^{-t} (sum a_n (tz)^n/n!) dt.

nodes.name: Clenshaw-Curtis Quadrature
nodes.function_signature: (Integrand on [-1,1]) -> (Numerical integral via Chebyshev-point interpolation)
nodes.description: Approximates definite integrals by interpolating at Chebyshev points and integrating the polynomial exactly.

nodes.name: Romberg Integration
nodes.function_signature: (Integrand, interval) -> (High-order numerical integral via Richardson extrapolation)
nodes.description: Accelerates the trapezoidal rule by systematic Richardson extrapolation on halved step sizes.

nodes.name: Pade Approximation
nodes.function_signature: (Power series) -> (Rational function matching maximum coefficients)
nodes.description: Approximates a function by a rational function whose Taylor expansion matches the given series to maximum order.

nodes.name: Chebyshev Expansion
nodes.function_signature: (Function on [-1,1]) -> (Near-minimax polynomial in Chebyshev basis)
nodes.description: Expands a function in Chebyshev polynomials T_n(x) yielding near-optimal uniform polynomial approximations.

nodes.name: Minimax Rational Approximation
nodes.function_signature: (Function, degree bounds) -> (Rational function minimizing sup-norm error)
nodes.description: Constructs the rational approximation minimizing maximum absolute error, characterized by equioscillation.

nodes.name: Aitken's Delta-Squared Process
nodes.function_signature: (Linearly convergent sequence) -> (Accelerated sequence)
nodes.description: Transforms a linearly convergent sequence via s'_n = s_n - (Delta s_n)^2/(Delta^2 s_n) to achieve faster convergence.

nodes.name: Wynn's Epsilon Algorithm
nodes.function_signature: (Partial sums) -> (Pade-like accelerated approximations)
nodes.description: Computes sequence transformations equivalent to diagonal Pade approximants via a recursive triangular array.

nodes.name: Levin's Transformation
nodes.function_signature: (Slowly convergent series) -> (Accelerated sequence using remainder estimates)
nodes.description: A nonlinear sequence transformation accelerating convergence by using estimates of the general term's behavior.

nodes.name: Gauss-Legendre Quadrature
nodes.function_signature: (Integrand on [-1,1]) -> (Optimal n-point numerical integral)
nodes.description: Evaluates integral with optimal polynomial degree accuracy 2n-1 using zeros of Legendre polynomials as nodes.

nodes.name: Gauss-Laguerre Quadrature
nodes.function_signature: (Integrand on [0,infty) with weight x^alpha e^{-x}) -> (Numerical integral)
nodes.description: Optimal quadrature for integrands with Laguerre weight using zeros of Laguerre polynomials.

nodes.name: Gauss-Hermite Quadrature
nodes.function_signature: (Integrand on R with weight e^{-x^2}) -> (Numerical integral)
nodes.description: Optimal quadrature for Gaussian-weighted integrals using zeros of Hermite polynomials.

nodes.name: Lambert W-Function
nodes.description: The multivalued inverse of f(w) = we^w, with principal branch W_0 real-valued for x >= -1/e.

nodes.name: Gudermannian Function gd(x)
nodes.description: gd(x) = 2 arctan(tanh(x/2)), connecting circular and hyperbolic functions without complex numbers.

nodes.name: Euler-Mascheroni Constant
nodes.description: The constant gamma = lim(sum 1/k - ln n) approx 0.5772, appearing in the digamma function psi(1) = -gamma.

nodes.name: Pochhammer Symbol (Rising Factorial)
nodes.description: The rising factorial (a)_n = a(a+1)...(a+n-1) = Gamma(a+n)/Gamma(a), fundamental to hypergeometric series.

nodes.name: Gamma Function Recurrence Relation
nodes.description: The functional equation Gamma(z+1) = z Gamma(z), generalizing n! = n(n-1)!.

nodes.name: Euler's Reflection Formula
nodes.description: Gamma(z) Gamma(1-z) = pi/sin(pi z), connecting Gamma at complementary arguments.

nodes.name: Legendre Duplication Formula
nodes.description: Gamma(z) Gamma(z+1/2) = sqrt(pi) 2^{1-2z} Gamma(2z), relating Gamma at z and 2z.

nodes.name: Gauss Multiplication Formula
nodes.description: Product of Gamma(z+k/n) for k=0..n-1 equals (2pi)^{(n-1)/2} n^{1/2-nz} Gamma(nz).

nodes.name: Bohr-Mollerup Theorem
nodes.description: Gamma is the unique log-convex function on (0,infty) with f(1)=1 and f(x+1)=xf(x).

nodes.name: Hankel's Contour Integral for 1/Gamma(z)
nodes.description: 1/Gamma(z) = (1/2pi i) oint (-t)^{-z} e^{-t} dt over a Hankel contour, showing 1/Gamma is entire.

nodes.name: Binet's Formula for ln Gamma
nodes.description: Integral representation expressing the Stirling remainder of ln Gamma(z) as an explicit arctangent integral.

nodes.name: Polygamma Functions
nodes.description: The functions psi^{(n)}(z) = d^{n+1}/dz^{n+1} ln Gamma(z), with psi^{(0)} the digamma function.

nodes.name: Polygamma Recurrence Relation
nodes.description: psi^{(n)}(z+1) = psi^{(n)}(z) + (-1)^n n!/z^{n+1}, reducing polygamma evaluation to a strip.

nodes.name: Barnes G-Function
nodes.description: Entire function satisfying G(z+1) = Gamma(z) G(z) with G(1)=1, a double gamma function.

nodes.name: q-Gamma Function
nodes.description: q-analog of Gamma defined via Gamma_q(z) = (q;q)_infty/(q^z;q)_infty (1-q)^{1-z}, reducing to Gamma(z) as q->1.

nodes.name: Reciprocal Gamma as Entire Function
nodes.description: 1/Gamma(z) is an entire function of order 1 with zeros at z = 0, -1, -2, ... and Weierstrass product representation.

nodes.name: Beta Function Integral Representation
nodes.description: B(a,b) = integral_0^1 t^{a-1}(1-t)^{b-1} dt = Gamma(a)Gamma(b)/Gamma(a+b) for Re a, Re b > 0.

nodes.name: Exponential Integral E_1(z)
nodes.description: E_1(z) = integral_z^infty e^{-t}/t dt, the principal exponential integral with logarithmic singularity at z=0.

nodes.name: Exponential Integral Ei(x)
nodes.description: Ei(x) = P.V. integral_{-infty}^x e^t/t dt for real x, related to E_1 by Ei(x) = -E_1(-x) +/- i pi.

nodes.name: Sine Integral Si(z)
nodes.description: Si(z) = integral_0^z sin(t)/t dt, an entire odd function with Si(+infty) = pi/2.

nodes.name: Cosine Integral Ci(z)
nodes.description: Ci(z) = -integral_z^infty cos(t)/t dt = gamma + ln z + integral_0^z (cos t -1)/t dt with branch point at origin.

nodes.name: Error Function erf(z)
nodes.description: erf(z) = (2/sqrt(pi)) integral_0^z e^{-t^2} dt, the normalized incomplete Gaussian integral.

nodes.name: Complementary Error Function erfc(z)
nodes.description: erfc(z) = 1 - erf(z) = (2/sqrt(pi)) integral_z^infty e^{-t^2} dt, preferred for large arguments.

nodes.name: Faddeeva Function w(z)
nodes.description: w(z) = e^{-z^2} erfc(-iz), central to Voigt profile computation and plasma dispersion.

nodes.name: Dawson's Integral F(z)
nodes.description: F(z) = e^{-z^2} integral_0^z e^{t^2} dt, a one-sided Fourier-Laplace transform of the Gaussian.

nodes.name: Fresnel Cosine Integral C(z)
nodes.description: C(z) = integral_0^z cos(pi t^2/2) dt, an entire function whose plot forms the Cornu spiral.

nodes.name: Fresnel Sine Integral S(z)
nodes.description: S(z) = integral_0^z sin(pi t^2/2) dt, companion to C(z) in the Cornu spiral.

nodes.name: Voigt Profile
nodes.description: Convolution of Gaussian and Lorentzian line shapes V(x;sigma,gamma) = Re[w(z)]/(sigma sqrt(2pi)), central to spectroscopy.

nodes.name: Lower Incomplete Gamma Function gamma(a,z)
nodes.description: gamma(a,z) = integral_0^z t^{a-1} e^{-t} dt, satisfying gamma(a,z) + Gamma(a,z) = Gamma(a).

nodes.name: Upper Incomplete Gamma Function Gamma(a,z)
nodes.description: Gamma(a,z) = integral_z^infty t^{a-1} e^{-t} dt, related to E_n(z) = z^{n-1} Gamma(1-n,z).

nodes.name: Regularized Incomplete Gamma P(a,z) and Q(a,z)
nodes.description: P = gamma(a,z)/Gamma(a) and Q = Gamma(a,z)/Gamma(a) with P+Q=1, giving the chi-squared CDF.

nodes.name: Incomplete Beta Function B_x(a,b)
nodes.description: B_x(a,b) = integral_0^x t^{a-1}(1-t)^{b-1} dt, whose regularized form I_x gives the Beta CDF.

nodes.name: Generalized Exponential Integral E_p(z)
nodes.description: E_p(z) = integral_1^infty e^{-zt}/t^p dt, extending E_1 to complex order via E_p(z) = z^{p-1} Gamma(1-p,z).

nodes.name: Airy Differential Equation
nodes.description: The ODE w'' - zw = 0, exhibiting a transition from oscillatory to exponential behavior at z=0.

nodes.name: Airy Function Ai(z)
nodes.description: The recessive solution of w'' = zw, defined by Ai(z) = (1/pi) integral_0^infty cos(t^3/3 + zt) dt.

nodes.name: Airy Function Bi(z)
nodes.description: The dominant solution of w'' = zw, exponentially growing as z -> +infty and linearly independent from Ai.

nodes.name: Scorer Function Gi(z)
nodes.description: Particular solution of w'' - zw = 1/pi via Gi(z) = (1/pi) integral_0^infty sin(t^3/3 + zt) dt.

nodes.name: Scorer Function Hi(z)
nodes.description: Particular solution of w'' - zw = 1/pi complementary to Gi, with Hi(z) - Gi(z) = Bi(z).

nodes.name: Airy Integral Representation
nodes.description: Ai(z) = (1/2pi i) integral exp(t^3/3 - zt) dt along a contour from infty e^{-pi i/3} to infty e^{pi i/3}.

nodes.name: Bessel Differential Equation
nodes.description: The ODE z^2 w'' + z w' + (z^2 - nu^2) w = 0 with regular singularity at z=0 and irregular at infinity.

nodes.name: Bessel Function J_nu(z)
nodes.description: Bessel function of the first kind, the solution regular at the origin defined by (z/2)^nu sum (-z^2/4)^k/(k! Gamma(nu+k+1)).

nodes.name: Bessel Function Y_nu(z)
nodes.description: Bessel function of the second kind (Neumann function), singular at the origin, linearly independent from J_nu.

nodes.name: Hankel Functions H_nu^{(1)}(z) and H_nu^{(2)}(z)
nodes.description: H_nu^{(1)} = J_nu + iY_nu and H_nu^{(2)} = J_nu - iY_nu, representing outgoing and incoming cylindrical waves.

nodes.name: Modified Bessel Function I_nu(z)
nodes.description: Modified Bessel function of the first kind, exponentially growing solution of z^2w'' + zw' - (z^2+nu^2)w = 0.

nodes.name: Modified Bessel Function K_nu(z)
nodes.description: Modified Bessel function of the second kind, exponentially decaying for large real positive z.

nodes.name: Spherical Bessel Functions
nodes.description: Solutions j_n, y_n, h_n of the radial Helmholtz equation, related to Bessel functions by j_n(z) = sqrt(pi/(2z)) J_{n+1/2}(z).

nodes.name: Kelvin Functions ber, bei, ker, kei
nodes.description: Real and imaginary parts of Bessel functions at complex arguments xe^{3pi i/4}, used in electromagnetic skin-effect calculations.

nodes.name: Mittag-Leffler Function E_{a,b}(z)
nodes.description: The entire function sum z^k/Gamma(ak+b) generalizing the exponential, fundamental in fractional calculus.

nodes.name: Hankel Transform
nodes.function_signature: (f(r), order nu) -> F(k) = integral_0^infty f(r) J_nu(kr) r dr
nodes.description: Integral transform with Bessel function kernel, the radial part of the 2D Fourier transform.

nodes.name: Bessel Addition Theorem
nodes.description: Expresses J_0(R) in terms of J_n at component distances: J_0(|r-r'|) = sum epsilon_n J_n(r) J_n(r') cos n(theta-theta').

nodes.name: Nicholson's Integral
nodes.description: J_nu(z)^2 + Y_nu(z)^2 = (8/pi^2) integral_0^infty K_0(2z sinh t) cosh(2nu t) dt.

nodes.name: Poisson Integral for Bessel Functions
nodes.description: J_nu(z) = (z/2)^nu/(sqrt(pi) Gamma(nu+1/2)) integral_0^pi cos(z cos theta) sin^{2nu}(theta) d theta for Re nu > -1/2.

nodes.name: Struve Function H_nu(z)
nodes.description: Solution of the inhomogeneous Bessel equation with right-hand side (z/2)^{nu-1}/(sqrt(pi) Gamma(nu+1/2)).

nodes.name: Modified Struve Function L_nu(z)
nodes.description: L_nu(z) = -ie^{-inu pi/2} H_nu(iz), solving the inhomogeneous modified Bessel equation.

nodes.name: Lommel Functions s_{mu,nu} and S_{mu,nu}
nodes.description: Particular solutions of the inhomogeneous Bessel equation z^2y'' + zy' + (z^2 - nu^2)y = z^{mu+1}.

nodes.name: Anger Function
nodes.description: (1/pi) integral_0^pi cos(nu theta - z sin theta) d theta, generalizing J_nu to non-integer order.

nodes.name: Weber Function E_nu(z)
nodes.description: (1/pi) integral_0^pi sin(nu theta - z sin theta) d theta, companion to the Anger function.

nodes.name: Parabolic Cylinder Differential Equation
nodes.description: The ODE w'' + (nu + 1/2 - z^2/4)w = 0 from separation in parabolic coordinates.

nodes.name: Parabolic Cylinder Function U(a,z)
nodes.description: Standard solution decaying as z -> +infty, expressible via confluent hypergeometric functions.

nodes.name: Parabolic Cylinder Function V(a,z)
nodes.description: Companion solution growing as z -> +infty, linearly independent from U(a,z).

nodes.name: Weber Parabolic Cylinder Function D_nu(z)
nodes.description: Classical notation D_nu(z) = U(-nu-1/2, z) for parabolic cylinder functions.

nodes.name: Kummer's Confluent Hypergeometric Equation
nodes.description: The ODE zw'' + (b-z)w' - aw = 0 with regular singularity at z=0 and irregular singularity at infinity.

nodes.name: Kummer Function M(a,b,z)
nodes.description: Confluent hypergeometric function 1F1(a;b;z) = sum (a)_k z^k/((b)_k k!), entire in z for b not a non-positive integer.

nodes.name: Tricomi Function U(a,b,z)
nodes.description: Second confluent hypergeometric function with U(a,b,z) ~ z^{-a} as z -> infty, unique with this decay.

nodes.name: Kummer Transformation
nodes.description: M(a,b,z) = e^z M(b-a,b,-z), the fundamental symmetry of confluent hypergeometric functions.

nodes.name: Whittaker Differential Equation
nodes.description: W'' + (-1/4 + kappa/z + (1/4-mu^2)/z^2)W = 0, alternative form of Kummer's equation.

nodes.name: Whittaker Function M_{kappa,mu}(z)
nodes.description: Whittaker function related to Kummer M by M_{kappa,mu} = e^{-z/2} z^{mu+1/2} M(mu-kappa+1/2, 2mu+1, z).

nodes.name: Whittaker Function W_{kappa,mu}(z)
nodes.description: Whittaker function related to Tricomi U, the recessive solution decaying as z -> infty.

nodes.name: Confluent Hypergeometric Limit
nodes.description: 1F1(a;b;z/b) -> 0F1(;a;z) as b -> infty, the confluence process merging regular singularities.

nodes.name: Associated Legendre Differential Equation
nodes.description: (1-x^2)y'' - 2xy' + [nu(nu+1) - mu^2/(1-x^2)]y = 0, generalizing Legendre's equation with order mu.

nodes.name: Ferrers Function P_nu^mu(x)
nodes.description: Associated Legendre function of the first kind on (-1,1), defined via the hypergeometric function.

nodes.name: Toroidal (Ring) Functions
nodes.description: Associated Legendre functions with half-integer degree P_{n-1/2}^m(cosh eta) for potential theory in toroidal geometry.

nodes.name: Conical (Mehler) Functions
nodes.description: Associated Legendre functions P_{-1/2+itau}^mu(x) with complex degree, arising in conical boundary problems.

nodes.name: Mehler-Fock Transform
nodes.function_signature: (f(x) on (1,infty)) -> F(tau) = integral f(x) P_{-1/2+itau}(x) dx
nodes.description: Integral transform with conical function kernel for axially symmetric potential problems.

nodes.name: Legendre Function of the Second Kind Q_nu(z)
nodes.description: Q_nu(z) = (pi/2)(cos nu pi P_nu(z) - P_{-nu-1}(z))/sin nu pi, singular at z = +/- 1.

nodes.name: Addition Theorem for Legendre Functions
nodes.description: P_n(cos gamma) = sum_{m} epsilon_m P_n^m(cos theta) P_n^m(cos theta') cos m(phi-phi') connecting P_n at composed angles.

nodes.name: Gauss Hypergeometric Function 2F1(a,b;c;z)
nodes.description: sum (a)_k(b)_k z^k/((c)_k k!) analytic in |z|<1, satisfying a Fuchsian ODE with 3 regular singular points.

nodes.name: Hypergeometric Differential Equation
nodes.description: z(1-z)w'' + [c-(a+b+1)z]w' - ab w = 0, the Fuchsian equation with regular singularities at 0, 1, infty.

nodes.name: Riemann Differential Equation and P-symbol
nodes.description: Most general second-order Fuchsian ODE with three regular singularities, encoded by the Riemann P-symbol.

nodes.name: Euler Integral Representation for 2F1
nodes.description: 2F1(a,b;c;z) = B(b,c-b)^{-1} integral_0^1 t^{b-1}(1-t)^{c-b-1}(1-zt)^{-a} dt for Re c > Re b > 0.

nodes.name: Kummer's 24 Solutions
nodes.description: The 24 solutions of the hypergeometric ODE obtained by transforming z -> z, 1-z, 1/z, 1/(1-z), z/(z-1), (z-1)/z and choosing exponents.

nodes.name: Pfaff-Saalschutz Summation Theorem
nodes.description: Evaluates terminating balanced 3F2 at z=1 as a ratio of Pochhammer symbols.

nodes.name: Dixon's Summation Theorem
nodes.description: Evaluates well-poised 3F2(a,b,c;1+a-b,1+a-c;1) as a ratio of Gamma functions.

nodes.name: Dougall Summation Theorem
nodes.description: Evaluates terminating very-well-poised 7F6(1) as a product of Pochhammer symbols.

nodes.name: Meijer G-Function
nodes.description: Mellin-Barnes contour integral unifying hypergeometric, Bessel, and other special functions as special cases.

nodes.name: Appell Function F_1
nodes.description: Two-variable hypergeometric function F_1(a;b,b';c;x,y) with coupled rising factorials.

nodes.name: Appell Functions F_2, F_3, F_4
nodes.description: The remaining three Appell two-variable hypergeometric functions with distinct convergence regions.

nodes.name: Fox H-Function
nodes.description: Generalization of the Meijer G-function with arbitrary powers in the Gamma factors, used in fractional calculus and statistics.

nodes.name: Bilateral Hypergeometric Series
nodes.description: pHq: sum from n=-infty to infty of (a_1)_n...(a_p)_n z^n/((b_1)_n...(b_q)_n), generalizing one-sided series.

nodes.name: Whipple's Transformation
nodes.description: Relates a well-poised 7F6(1) to a balanced 4F3(1), connecting different types of hypergeometric series.

nodes.name: q-Binomial Coefficient (Gaussian Binomial)
nodes.description: [n choose k]_q = (q;q)_n/((q;q)_k(q;q)_{n-k}), counting subspaces of F_q^n.

nodes.name: q-Derivative Operator D_q
nodes.description: D_q f(z) = (f(z)-f(qz))/((1-q)z), the q-analog of differentiation reducing to f'(z) as q->1.

nodes.name: q-Integral (Jackson Integral)
nodes.description: integral_0^a f(x) d_q x = a(1-q) sum f(aq^k) q^k, the inverse of the q-derivative.

nodes.name: q-Binomial Theorem
nodes.description: sum (a;q)_k z^k/(q;q)_k = (az;q)_infty/(z;q)_infty, the q-analog of the binomial series.

nodes.name: Basic Hypergeometric Function r+1-phi-s
nodes.description: q-analog of pFq with q-shifted factorials, converging for all z when s>r and |z|<1 when s=r.

nodes.name: Ramanujan's 1-psi-1 Bilateral Summation
nodes.description: Evaluates the bilateral q-series sum (a;q)_n z^n/(b;q)_n as an infinite product of q-Pochhammer symbols.

nodes.name: Bailey Pairs and Bailey Chain
nodes.function_signature: (Bailey pair (alpha_n, beta_n)) -> (Infinitely many new q-series identities)
nodes.description: Iterative mechanism: the Bailey lemma produces new q-hypergeometric identities from existing Bailey pairs.

nodes.name: q-Exponential Functions e_q and E_q
nodes.description: q-analogs of exp: e_q(z) = sum z^n/(q;q)_n = 1/(z;q)_infty and E_q(z) = sum q^{n(n-1)/2} z^n/(q;q)_n = (-z;q)_infty.

nodes.name: Jacobi Polynomial P_n^{alpha,beta}(x)
nodes.description: Orthogonal polynomials on [-1,1] with weight (1-x)^alpha(1+x)^beta, the most general classical family on a finite interval.

nodes.name: Gegenbauer (Ultraspherical) Polynomial C_n^lambda(x)
nodes.description: Jacobi polynomials with alpha=beta=lambda-1/2, orthogonal with weight (1-x^2)^{lambda-1/2}.

nodes.name: Laguerre Polynomial L_n^alpha(x)
nodes.description: Orthogonal polynomials on [0,infty) with weight x^alpha e^{-x}, arising as hydrogen atom radial wavefunctions.

nodes.name: Christoffel-Darboux Formula
nodes.description: Closed form for the reproducing kernel sum p_k(x)p_k(y)/h_k as a ratio of consecutive polynomials.

nodes.name: Favard's Theorem
nodes.description: Any polynomial sequence satisfying a three-term recurrence with positive coefficients is orthogonal with respect to some positive measure.

nodes.name: Hahn Polynomial
nodes.description: Discrete orthogonal polynomials on {0,...,N} with hypergeometric weight, the discrete analog of Jacobi polynomials.

nodes.name: Wilson Polynomial
nodes.description: The most general hypergeometric orthogonal polynomials (continuous variable), expressed as 4F3 series atop the Askey scheme.

nodes.name: Racah Polynomial
nodes.description: The most general discrete hypergeometric orthogonal polynomials, the discrete companion of Wilson polynomials.

nodes.name: Askey Scheme
nodes.description: Hierarchical classification of hypergeometric orthogonal polynomials by limit relations, with Wilson and Racah at the top.

nodes.name: Askey-Wilson Polynomial
nodes.description: Most general q-hypergeometric orthogonal polynomial family defined as a 4_phi_3, atop the q-Askey scheme.

nodes.name: Krawtchouk Polynomial
nodes.description: Discrete orthogonal polynomials on {0,...,N} with binomial weight, characters of the Hamming scheme.

nodes.name: Meixner Polynomial
nodes.description: Discrete orthogonal polynomials on non-negative integers with negative binomial weight.

nodes.name: Charlier Polynomial
nodes.description: Discrete orthogonal polynomials on non-negative integers with Poisson weight.

nodes.name: Chebyshev Polynomial of the First Kind T_n(x)
nodes.description: T_n(cos theta) = cos(n theta), orthogonal on [-1,1] with weight (1-x^2)^{-1/2}, optimal for minimax approximation.

nodes.name: Chebyshev Polynomial of the Second Kind U_n(x)
nodes.description: U_n(cos theta) = sin((n+1)theta)/sin(theta), orthogonal on [-1,1] with weight (1-x^2)^{1/2}.

nodes.name: Meixner-Pollaczek Polynomial P_n^lambda(x;phi)
nodes.description: Continuous orthogonal polynomials on R with weight |Gamma(lambda+ix)|^2 e^{(2phi-pi)x}, in the Askey scheme.

nodes.name: Continuous Hahn Polynomial
nodes.description: Orthogonal polynomials on R with weight |Gamma(a+ix)Gamma(b+ix)|^2, between Wilson and Meixner-Pollaczek.

nodes.name: Continuous Dual Hahn Polynomial
nodes.description: Orthogonal polynomials on [0,infty) as a 3F2 at z=-1, dual to continuous Hahn polynomials.

nodes.name: Dual Hahn Polynomial
nodes.description: Discrete orthogonal polynomials dual to Hahn, related to 6j symbols in angular momentum theory.

nodes.name: Rodrigues Formula (General)
nodes.description: p_n(x) = (1/(k_n w(x))) (d/dx)^n [w(x) sigma(x)^n], generating classical orthogonal polynomials from weight and classification.

nodes.name: Three-Term Recurrence Relation
nodes.description: x p_n(x) = a_n p_{n+1}(x) + b_n p_n(x) + c_n p_{n-1}(x), the fundamental structure theorem for orthogonal polynomials.

nodes.name: Complete Elliptic Integral K(k)
nodes.description: K(k) = integral_0^{pi/2} d theta/sqrt(1-k^2 sin^2 theta), the quarter-period of Jacobian elliptic functions.

nodes.name: Complete Elliptic Integral E(k)
nodes.description: E(k) = integral_0^{pi/2} sqrt(1-k^2 sin^2 theta) d theta, giving the arc length of an ellipse.

nodes.name: Complete Elliptic Integral Pi(n,k)
nodes.description: Pi(n,k) = integral_0^{pi/2} d theta/((1-n sin^2 theta) sqrt(1-k^2 sin^2 theta)), the third-kind integral.

nodes.name: Carlson Symmetric R_F(x,y,z)
nodes.description: R_F = (1/2) integral_0^infty [(t+x)(t+y)(t+z)]^{-1/2} dt, symmetric elliptic integral of the first kind.

nodes.name: Carlson Symmetric R_J(x,y,z,p)
nodes.description: R_J = (3/2) integral_0^infty [(t+x)(t+y)(t+z)]^{-1/2}(t+p)^{-1} dt, symmetric third-kind integral.

nodes.name: Carlson Symmetric R_D(x,y,z)
nodes.description: R_D = R_J(x,y,z,z), special case of R_J with E(k) = R_F(0,k'^2,1) - (k^2/3) R_D(0,k'^2,1).

nodes.name: Carlson Symmetric R_C(x,y)
nodes.description: R_C(x,y) = R_F(x,y,y), degenerate symmetric integral reducing to inverse trig/hyperbolic functions.

nodes.name: Arithmetic-Geometric Mean M(a,g)
nodes.function_signature: (a_0, g_0) -> AGM limit M with K(k) = pi/(2M(1,k'))
nodes.description: Iterates a_{n+1}=(a_n+g_n)/2, g_{n+1}=sqrt(a_n g_n) with quadratic convergence to compute elliptic integrals.

nodes.name: Landen Transformation
nodes.function_signature: (Elliptic integral at modulus k) -> (Same value at reduced/increased modulus)
nodes.description: Modulus-changing substitution preserving elliptic integral values, enabling iterative computation.

nodes.name: Legendre's Relation for Elliptic Integrals
nodes.description: E(k)K'(k) + E'(k)K(k) - K(k)K'(k) = pi/2, the fundamental relation between complete elliptic integrals.

nodes.name: Jacobi Theta Function theta_1(z,q)
nodes.description: The odd Jacobi theta function theta_1 = 2 sum (-1)^n q^{(n+1/2)^2} sin((2n+1)z), vanishing at z=0.

nodes.name: Jacobi Theta Function theta_2(z,q)
nodes.description: The even Jacobi theta function theta_2 = 2 sum q^{(n+1/2)^2} cos((2n+1)z).

nodes.name: Jacobi Theta Function theta_3(z,q)
nodes.description: theta_3 = 1 + 2 sum q^{n^2} cos(2nz), the basic Jacobi theta function.

nodes.name: Jacobi Theta Function theta_4(z,q)
nodes.description: theta_4 = 1 + 2 sum (-1)^n q^{n^2} cos(2nz), related to theta_3 by a half-period shift.

nodes.name: Theta Function Heat Equation
nodes.description: Jacobi theta functions satisfy 4pi i partial_tau theta = partial_z^2 theta, connecting them to heat kernels.

nodes.name: Jacobi Imaginary Transformation
nodes.description: theta_3(z|tau) = (-i tau)^{-1/2} exp(z^2/(pi i tau)) theta_3(z/tau | -1/tau), the modular transformation.

nodes.name: Riemann Theta Function
nodes.description: Theta(z|Omega) = sum_{n in Z^g} exp(pi i n^T Omega n + 2pi i n^T z) for g-dimensional z and g x g Riemann matrix Omega.

nodes.name: Siegel Modular Group Sp(2g,Z)
nodes.description: The group of transformations of genus-g Riemann matrices under which Riemann theta functions transform covariantly.

nodes.name: Jacobian Elliptic Function sn(z,k)
nodes.description: The sine-amplitude function inverting F(phi,k), doubly periodic with periods 4K and 2iK'.

nodes.name: Jacobian Elliptic Function cn(z,k)
nodes.description: The cosine-amplitude function satisfying sn^2 + cn^2 = 1, doubly periodic with periods 4K and 2K+2iK'.

nodes.name: Jacobian Elliptic Function dn(z,k)
nodes.description: The delta-amplitude function satisfying dn^2 + k^2 sn^2 = 1, doubly periodic with periods 2K and 4iK'.

nodes.name: Jacobi Amplitude Function am(u,k)
nodes.description: am(u,k) = phi where u = F(phi,k), the inverse of the incomplete elliptic integral of the first kind.

nodes.name: Twelve Jacobian Elliptic Functions
nodes.description: The twelve pq(z,k) functions (p,q in {s,c,d,n}) defined as ratios of any two of H, H_1, Theta, Theta_1 theta functions.

nodes.name: Jacobi Elliptic Addition Theorems
nodes.description: sn(u+v) = (sn u cn v dn v + sn v cn u dn u)/(1-k^2 sn^2 u sn^2 v) and analogues for cn, dn.

nodes.name: Weierstrass Elliptic Function wp(z)
nodes.description: wp(z;omega_1,omega_2) = 1/z^2 + sum'_{m,n} [1/(z-Omega_{m,n})^2 - 1/Omega_{m,n}^2], the canonical elliptic function of order 2.

nodes.name: Weierstrass Sigma Function sigma(z)
nodes.description: Entire function with simple zeros at lattice points: sigma(z) = z prod' (1-z/Omega) exp(z/Omega + z^2/(2Omega^2)).

nodes.name: Weierstrass Zeta Function zeta(z)
nodes.description: zeta(z) = sigma'(z)/sigma(z) = 1/z + sum' [1/(z-Omega) + 1/Omega + z/Omega^2], a quasi-periodic meromorphic function.

nodes.name: Weierstrass Differential Equation
nodes.description: (wp')^2 = 4 wp^3 - g_2 wp - g_3, the ODE defining wp in terms of invariants g_2, g_3.

nodes.name: Modular Discriminant Delta(tau)
nodes.description: Delta = g_2^3 - 27 g_3^2 = (2pi)^{12} eta(tau)^{24}, a weight-12 cusp form vanishing iff the lattice degenerates.

nodes.name: Klein j-Invariant j(tau)
nodes.description: j = 1728 g_2^3/Delta, the unique modular function for SL(2,Z) classifying isomorphism classes of elliptic curves.

nodes.name: Eisenstein Series E_{2k}(tau)
nodes.description: E_{2k}(tau) = 1 - (4k/B_{2k}) sum sigma_{2k-1}(n) q^n, modular forms of weight 2k for k >= 2.

nodes.name: Elliptic Modular Function lambda(tau)
nodes.description: lambda(tau) = theta_2(0,q)^4/theta_3(0,q)^4 = k^2, a modular function for Gamma(2) mapping H to C\{0,1}.

nodes.name: Bernoulli Polynomial B_n(x)
nodes.description: Defined by te^{xt}/(e^t-1) = sum B_n(x) t^n/n!, with B_n(0) = B_n the Bernoulli numbers.

nodes.name: Euler Polynomial E_n(x)
nodes.description: Defined by 2e^{xt}/(e^t+1) = sum E_n(x) t^n/n!, with E_n(1/2) related to Euler numbers.

nodes.name: Genocchi Numbers
nodes.description: G_n = 2(1-2^n)B_n, integers related to Bernoulli numbers with generating function 2t/(e^t+1).

nodes.name: Bernoulli-Euler Complement Formula
nodes.description: B_n(1-x) = (-1)^n B_n(x) and E_n(1-x) = (-1)^n E_n(x), reflection symmetries.

nodes.name: Euler-Maclaurin Summation Formula
nodes.description: sum f(k) = integral f(x)dx + f(a)/2 + f(b)/2 + sum B_{2k}/(2k)! (f^{(2k-1)}(b)-f^{(2k-1)}(a)) + R, bridging sums and integrals via Bernoulli numbers.

nodes.name: Hurwitz Zeta Function zeta(s,a)
nodes.description: zeta(s,a) = sum_{n=0}^infty (n+a)^{-s} for Re s > 1, generalizing Riemann zeta with zeta(s,1) = zeta(s).

nodes.name: Polylogarithm Li_s(z)
nodes.description: Li_s(z) = sum z^n/n^s for |z|<=1, generalizing -log(1-z)=Li_1(z) and extending to all s by analytic continuation.

nodes.name: Lerch Transcendent Phi(z,s,a)
nodes.description: Phi(z,s,a) = sum z^n/(n+a)^s unifying Hurwitz zeta (z=1), polylogarithm (a=1), and Riemann zeta (z=1,a=1).

nodes.name: Fermi-Dirac Integral
nodes.description: F_s(x) = -Li_{s+1}(-e^x), standard integral for fermion energy distributions in quantum statistics.

nodes.name: Bose-Einstein Integral
nodes.description: G_s(x) = Li_{s+1}(e^x), the bosonic counterpart to the Fermi-Dirac integral.

nodes.name: Stieltjes Constants
nodes.description: Coefficients gamma_n in the Laurent expansion zeta(s) = 1/(s-1) + sum (-1)^n gamma_n (s-1)^n/n! near s=1.

nodes.name: Dirichlet Beta Function beta(s)
nodes.description: beta(s) = sum (-1)^n/(2n+1)^s = (1/4^s)(zeta(s,1/4) - zeta(s,3/4)), with beta(1) = pi/4.

nodes.name: Clausen Function Cl_2(theta)
nodes.description: Cl_2(theta) = -integral_0^theta ln|2 sin(t/2)| dt = sum sin(n theta)/n^2, related to the dilogarithm.

nodes.name: Bell Number B_n
nodes.description: Number of partitions of {1,...,n}: B_n = sum S(n,k), with e.g.f. exp(e^x-1).

nodes.name: Bell Polynomial B_{n,k}
nodes.description: Partial Bell polynomials B_{n,k}(x_1,...,x_{n-k+1}) appearing in Faa di Bruno's formula for composite derivatives.

nodes.name: Plane Partition
nodes.description: A 2D array of nonneg integers weakly decreasing along rows and columns, with MacMahon generating function prod(1-q^k)^{-k}.

nodes.name: MacMahon Box Formula
nodes.description: Number of plane partitions in an a x b x c box = prod_{i,j,k} (i+j+k-1)/(i+j+k-2).

nodes.name: Twelvefold Way
nodes.function_signature: (n objects, k boxes, constraint) -> Count
nodes.description: Classification of 12 counting problems by distinguishability of objects/boxes and mapping type.

nodes.name: Derangement Number D_n
nodes.description: Number of permutations with no fixed points: D_n = n! sum_{k=0}^n (-1)^k/k!, with D_n/n! -> 1/e.

nodes.name: Narayana Number N(n,k)
nodes.description: N(n,k) = (1/n) C(n,k) C(n,k-1), refining Catalan numbers by counting paths by number of peaks.

nodes.name: Jordan's Totient Function J_k(n)
nodes.description: J_k(n) = n^k prod_{p|n}(1-p^{-k}), counting k-tuples coprime to n; J_1 = Euler totient phi.

nodes.name: Ramanujan Tau Function
nodes.description: tau(n) defined by Delta(q) = q prod(1-q^n)^{24} = sum tau(n)q^n, a multiplicative function.

nodes.name: Lambert Series
nodes.function_signature: (Arithmetic function f) -> sum f(n) q^n/(1-q^n) = sum (sum_{d|n} f(d)) q^n
nodes.description: Converts between arithmetic functions and their summatory transforms via divisor sums.

nodes.name: Liouville Lambda Function lambda(n)
nodes.description: lambda(n) = (-1)^{Omega(n)} where Omega counts prime factors with multiplicity; Dirichlet series zeta(2s)/zeta(s).

nodes.name: Dedekind Sum s(h,k)
nodes.description: s(h,k) = sum_{r=1}^{k-1} ((r/k))((hr/k)) with sawtooth function ((x)), appearing in the transformation of log eta(tau).

nodes.name: Mathieu Equation
nodes.description: The ODE w'' + (a - 2q cos 2z)w = 0 arising from the wave equation in elliptic cylinder coordinates.

nodes.name: Mathieu Characteristic Values a_n(q), b_n(q)
nodes.description: Eigenvalues of Mathieu's equation for which periodic solutions of period pi or 2pi exist.

nodes.name: Mathieu Function ce_n(z,q)
nodes.description: Even periodic Mathieu eigenfunction with eigenvalue a_n(q), reducing to cos(nz) when q=0.

nodes.name: Mathieu Function se_n(z,q)
nodes.description: Odd periodic Mathieu eigenfunction with eigenvalue b_n(q), reducing to sin(nz) when q=0.

nodes.name: Modified Mathieu Equation
nodes.description: w'' - (a - 2q cosh 2z)w = 0 from Mathieu's equation by z -> iz, for radial separation.

nodes.name: Hill's Equation
nodes.description: The ODE w'' + Q(z)w = 0 with periodic Q, generalizing Mathieu's equation to arbitrary periodic potentials.

nodes.name: Hill Discriminant
nodes.description: Delta(lambda) = w_1(pi) + w_2'(pi), whose values +/-2 locate stability band edges of Hill's equation.

nodes.name: Mathieu-Floquet Solution
nodes.description: Solution of Mathieu's equation of the form e^{i nu z} P(z) with P periodic, where nu is the Floquet exponent.

nodes.name: Lame Equation
nodes.description: d^2w/dz^2 + (h - nu(nu+1)k^2 sn^2(z,k))w = 0, a doubly-periodic potential eigenvalue problem.

nodes.name: Lame Polynomials
nodes.description: Polynomial solutions of the Lame equation for integer nu, classified into eight types by parity structure.

nodes.name: Ellipsoidal Harmonics
nodes.description: Products of Lame functions in confocal ellipsoidal coordinates, generalizing spherical harmonics.

nodes.name: Lame Eigenvalues
nodes.description: The 2nu+1 eigenvalues h of Lame's equation for integer nu, organized by parity and node structure.

nodes.name: Spheroidal Differential Equation
nodes.description: d/dz[(1-z^2)dw/dz] + [lambda + gamma^2(1-z^2) - mu^2/(1-z^2)]w = 0 from Helmholtz in spheroidal coords.

nodes.name: Angular Spheroidal Wave Function Ps_n^m
nodes.description: Eigenfunction on [-1,1] reducing to Ferrers P_n^m when gamma=0, used in antenna and scattering theory.

nodes.name: Radial Spheroidal Wave Functions
nodes.description: Four kinds of radial solutions analogous to spherical Bessel functions, for the exterior region.

nodes.name: Spheroidal Eigenvalues lambda_n^m(gamma^2)
nodes.description: Eigenvalues of the angular spheroidal equation, reducing to n(n+1) when gamma=0.

nodes.name: Prolate Spheroidal Wave Function
nodes.description: Angular spheroidal function with gamma^2 > 0, bandlimited functions with maximal spatial concentration (Slepian).

nodes.name: Heun's Equation
nodes.description: Most general second-order Fuchsian ODE with four regular singular points at {0, 1, a, infty}.

nodes.name: Heun Function Hl
nodes.description: Local Frobenius solution Hl(a,q;alpha,beta,gamma,delta;z) analytic at z=0 with accessory parameter q.

nodes.name: Accessory Parameter
nodes.description: The parameter q in Heun's equation not determined by exponents, controlling global connection behavior.

nodes.name: Confluent Heun Equation
nodes.description: Heun equation with two regular singularities merged into one irregular, having three singularities total.

nodes.name: Biconfluent Heun Equation
nodes.description: Heun equation with three regular singularities merged into one irregular of rank 2 plus one regular.

nodes.name: Triconfluent Heun Equation
nodes.description: Maximally confluent Heun equation with one irregular singularity at infinity.

nodes.name: Heun's 192 Local Solutions
nodes.description: The 192 = 4 x 48 local Frobenius solutions of Heun's equation at its four singular points, generalizing Kummer's 24.

nodes.name: First Painleve Equation P_I
nodes.description: y'' = 6y^2 + z, the simplest Painleve transcendent with no free parameters.

nodes.name: Second Painleve Equation P_II
nodes.description: y'' = 2y^3 + zy + alpha, with Airy function solutions when alpha = n + 1/2.

nodes.name: Third Painleve Equation P_III
nodes.description: y'' = (y')^2/y - y'/z + (alpha y^2 + beta)/z + gamma y^3 + delta/y, with Bessel function solutions.

nodes.name: Fifth Painleve Equation P_V
nodes.description: Most complex Painleve equation with four parameters, with Whittaker/confluent hypergeometric solutions.

nodes.name: Sixth Painleve Equation P_VI
nodes.description: Most general Painleve equation with four parameters, containing P_I-P_V as coalescence limits.

nodes.name: Painleve Coalescence Cascade
nodes.description: Limiting process P_VI->P_V->P_IV->P_II->P_I and P_V->P_III->P_II relating all six Painleve equations.

nodes.name: Backlund Transformations for Painleve
nodes.function_signature: (Solution y(z; params)) -> (Solution y~(z; shifted params))
nodes.description: Rational transformations mapping Painleve solutions to solutions with shifted parameter values.

nodes.name: Isomonodromic Deformation Connection
nodes.description: Each Painleve equation is the compatibility condition for isomonodromic deformation of an associated linear system.

nodes.name: Painleve Property
nodes.description: An ODE has the Painleve property if all movable singularities of all solutions are poles (no movable branch points or essential singularities).

nodes.name: Coulomb Wave Equation
nodes.description: d^2w/drho^2 + (1 - 2eta/rho - l(l+1)/rho^2)w = 0 for scattering in a Coulomb field.

nodes.name: Regular Coulomb Function F_l(eta,rho)
nodes.description: Regular solution vanishing at origin, normalized by the Gamow factor C_l(eta).

nodes.name: Irregular Coulomb Functions G_l, H_l^{+/-}
nodes.description: Irregular solution G_l and Coulomb-Hankel functions H_l^{+/-} = G_l +/- iF_l for scattering theory.

nodes.name: Gamow-Sommerfeld Factor
nodes.description: C_0^2(eta) = 2pi eta/(e^{2pi eta}-1), the Coulomb barrier penetration probability for nuclear reactions.

nodes.name: Coulomb Phase Shift sigma_l(eta)
nodes.description: sigma_l(eta) = arg Gamma(l+1+i eta), the phase shift from the long-range Coulomb potential.

nodes.name: Wigner 3j Symbol
nodes.description: Coupling coefficient (j1 j2 j3; m1 m2 m3) for three angular momenta summing to zero total.

nodes.name: 6j Symbol (Racah Coefficient)
nodes.description: Recoupling coefficient {j1 j2 j3; l1 l2 l3} for three angular momenta, expressible as a 4F3 series.

nodes.name: 9j Symbol
nodes.description: Recoupling coefficient for four angular momenta, a sum of products of three 6j symbols.

nodes.name: Gaunt Coefficient
nodes.description: Integral of three spherical harmonics over the sphere, equal to a product of two 3j symbols.

nodes.name: Biedenharn-Elliott Identity
nodes.description: Pentagon identity: sum of product of three 6j symbols over intermediate j equals a product of two 6j symbols.

nodes.name: Clebsch-Gordan Coefficient
nodes.description: C^{j,m}_{j_1,m_1,j_2,m_2} coupling two angular momenta j_1+j_2 to resultant j, related to 3j by phase and sqrt factor.

nodes.name: Wigner D-Matrix D^j_{m'm}(alpha,beta,gamma)
nodes.description: Matrix elements of rotation operators in angular momentum basis, D^j_{m'm} = e^{-im'alpha} d^j_{m'm}(beta) e^{-im gamma}.

nodes.name: Multivariate Gamma Function Gamma_m(a)
nodes.description: Gamma_m(a) = pi^{m(m-1)/4} prod Gamma(a-(j-1)/2), arising in matrix variate distributions.

nodes.name: Zonal Polynomials Z_kappa(T)
nodes.description: Symmetric polynomials in eigenvalues of symmetric matrix T, the spherical functions of GL(m)/O(m).

nodes.name: Hypergeometric Function of Matrix Argument
nodes.description: pF_q with matrix argument via sum over partitions of zonal polynomial expansions.

nodes.name: Wishart Distribution
nodes.description: Distribution of S = X^T X for Gaussian X, with density involving |S|^{(n-p-1)/2} exp(-tr Sigma^{-1}S/2) / (Gamma_p(n/2) |Sigma|^{n/2}).

nodes.name: Jack Polynomial P_kappa^{(alpha)}
nodes.description: Symmetric polynomials generalizing Schur polynomials (alpha=1) and zonal polynomials (alpha=2), indexed by partitions.

nodes.name: Cuspoid Canonical Integral Psi_K
nodes.description: Psi_K(x) = integral exp(i(t^{K+2} + x_K t^K + ... + x_1 t)) dt, the K-th cuspoid diffraction integral.

nodes.name: Pearcey Integral
nodes.description: The K=2 cuspoid integral integral exp(i(t^4 + x_2 t^2 + x_1 t)) dt, governing cusp diffraction.

nodes.name: Swallowtail Canonical Integral
nodes.description: The K=3 cuspoid integral integral exp(i(t^5 + zt^3 + yt^2 + xt)) dt for swallowtail diffraction.

nodes.name: Elliptic Umbilic Catastrophe
nodes.description: Catastrophe with phase s^3 - 3st^2 + z(s^2+t^2) + ys + xt, possessing three-fold rotational symmetry.

nodes.name: Hyperbolic Umbilic Catastrophe
nodes.description: Catastrophe with phase s^3 + t^3 + zst + ys + xt, dual to the elliptic umbilic.

nodes.name: Butterfly Canonical Integral
nodes.description: The K=4 cuspoid integral with phase t^6 + x_4 t^4 + x_3 t^3 + x_2 t^2 + x_1 t, the butterfly catastrophe.

nodes.name: Hilbert Transform
nodes.function_signature: (f(x)) -> H[f](x) = P.V. (1/pi) integral f(t)/(t-x) dt
nodes.description: Singular integral transform producing the analytic signal; maps cos to sin and connects real/imaginary parts of boundary values.

nodes.name: Abel Transform
nodes.function_signature: (f(r)) -> F(y) = 2 integral_y^infty f(r) r dr/sqrt(r^2-y^2)
nodes.description: Integral transform for recovering radial profiles from projected data, inverse via Abel inversion formula.

nodes.name: Hankel Contour Method
nodes.function_signature: (Meromorphic integrand) -> (Sum of residues via keyhole contour)
nodes.description: Evaluates integrals and sums using a contour wrapping the negative real axis, fundamental for Gamma and 1/Gamma representations.

nodes.name: Bateman's Function k_nu(x)
nodes.description: k_nu(x) = (2/pi) integral_0^{pi/2} cos(x tan theta - nu theta) d theta, related to Bessel functions.

nodes.name: Wright Function W_{lambda,mu}(z)
nodes.description: W_{lambda,mu}(z) = sum z^n/(n! Gamma(lambda n + mu)), generalizing Airy functions (lambda = +/-1/3) and Mittag-Leffler.

nodes.name: Fox-Wright Psi Function
nodes.description: p_Psi_q: generalized hypergeometric series with Gamma ratios allowing non-unit increments, interpolating between pFq and H-function.

nodes.name: Dedekind Eta Function eta(tau)
nodes.description: eta(tau) = q^{1/24} prod_{n=1}^infty (1-q^n) for q=e^{2pi i tau}, a weight-1/2 modular form with multiplier system.

nodes.name: Weber Modular Functions f, f_1, f_2
nodes.description: f(tau) = e^{-pi i/24} eta((tau+1)/2)/eta(tau), algebraic at CM points and used in class field theory.

nodes.name: Darboux-Christoffel Kernel
nodes.description: K_n(x,y) = sum_{k=0}^n p_k(x) p_k(y)/h_k, the reproducing kernel whose diagonal gives the density of states.

nodes.name: Turan Inequality for Orthogonal Polynomials
nodes.description: P_n(x)^2 - P_{n-1}(x) P_{n+1}(x) >= 0 for x in [-1,1], a universal positivity result for Legendre polynomials.

nodes.name: Dirichlet Character chi mod q
nodes.description: A completely multiplicative function chi: Z -> C with period q and chi(n) = 0 when gcd(n,q) > 1.

nodes.name: Gauss Sum g(chi)
nodes.description: g(chi) = sum_{a=1}^q chi(a) e^{2pi ia/q}, with |g(chi)| = sqrt(q) for primitive chi.

nodes.name: Jacobi Sum J(chi_1, chi_2)
nodes.description: J(chi_1,chi_2) = sum_{a+b=1} chi_1(a) chi_2(b) = g(chi_1)g(chi_2)/g(chi_1 chi_2), product of Gauss sums.

nodes.name: Riemann Xi Function xi(s)
nodes.description: xi(s) = (1/2)s(s-1) pi^{-s/2} Gamma(s/2) zeta(s), entire and satisfying xi(s) = xi(1-s).

nodes.name: Functional Equation for Hurwitz Zeta
nodes.description: zeta(1-s,a) = Gamma(s)/(2pi)^s [e^{-pi is/2} F(a,s) + e^{pi is/2} F(-a,s)] with F the periodic zeta function.

nodes.name: Partition Function (Statistical Mechanics) Z
nodes.description: Z = sum_states exp(-E/kT), the normalizing factor in Boltzmann statistics from which thermodynamic quantities derive.

nodes.name: Painleve Hamiltonians
nodes.description: Each Painleve equation admits a Hamiltonian formulation y' = dH/dq, q' = -dH/dy with polynomial Hamiltonian H.

nodes.name: Painleve Tau Function
nodes.description: tau(z) defined by d/dz ln tau = H(z), entire function whose zeros encode the poles of the Painleve transcendent.

nodes.name: Separation of Variables in Coordinate Systems
nodes.function_signature: (PDE in orthogonal coordinates) -> (System of ODEs for each coordinate)
nodes.description: Decomposes PDEs into ODEs by exploiting coordinate symmetry; 11 coordinate systems separate the Helmholtz equation.

nodes.name: Connection Formulas for 2F1
nodes.description: Express solutions at one singularity as linear combinations of solutions at another, with coefficients involving Gamma functions.

nodes.name: Lipschitz Summation Formula
nodes.description: sum_{n=0}^infty (n+a)^{-s} e^{2pi in z} = Gamma(s)^{-1} sum_{n=-infty}^infty 1/(z-n+a)^s for Im z > 0, connecting Hurwitz zeta to periodic sums.

nodes.name: Ramanujan's Master Theorem
nodes.description: If f(x) = sum (-1)^n phi(n) x^n/n!, then integral_0^infty x^{s-1} f(x) dx = Gamma(s) phi(-s), a Mellin transform result.

nodes.name: Big q-Jacobi Polynomial
nodes.description: q-analog of Jacobi polynomials on a q-linear lattice, in the q-Askey scheme between Askey-Wilson and q-Hahn.

nodes.name: Little q-Jacobi Polynomial
nodes.description: Simpler q-analog of Jacobi polynomials on {q^k}, a limiting case of big q-Jacobi polynomials.

nodes.name: Al-Salam-Chihara Polynomial
nodes.description: q-orthogonal polynomials on [-1,1] defined as 3_phi_2, in the q-Askey scheme below Askey-Wilson.

nodes.name: q-Racah Polynomial
nodes.description: q-analog of Racah polynomials atop the discrete branch of the q-Askey scheme.

nodes.name: q-Hahn Polynomial
nodes.description: q-analog of Hahn polynomials, discrete orthogonal on {1, q, ..., q^N}.

nodes.name: Volterra Integral Equation
nodes.description: f(x) = g(x) + lambda integral_a^x K(x,t) f(t) dt, with variable upper limit making it uniquely solvable.

nodes.name: Fredholm Integral Equation
nodes.description: f(x) = g(x) + lambda integral_a^b K(x,t) f(t) dt, with fixed limits; solvability governed by Fredholm theory.

nodes.name: Appell Sequence
nodes.description: A polynomial sequence {p_n} with d/dx p_n = n p_{n-1}, including Bernoulli, Euler, and Hermite polynomials.

nodes.name: Sheffer Sequence
nodes.description: Polynomial sequence defined by generating function A(t) exp(x B(t)) = sum p_n(x) t^n/n!, generalizing Appell sequences.

nodes.name: Zeros of Bessel Functions
nodes.description: The positive zeros j_{nu,s} of J_nu(z) are real, simple, and interlace with zeros of J_{nu+1}; asymptotically j_{nu,s} ~ (s+nu/2-1/4)pi.

nodes.name: Debye Asymptotic Expansion for Bessel Functions
nodes.description: Uniform large-order expansion J_nu(nu z) ~ (phi/sqrt(1-z^2))^{1/2} [Ai(nu^{2/3}phi)/(nu^{1/3})] sum, valid through the transition region.

nodes.name: Olver Uniform Asymptotic Expansion
nodes.description: Uniform expansion of J_nu(nu z) valid for all z including the turning point, involving Airy functions and their derivatives.

nodes.name: Weierstrass Addition Theorem
nodes.description: wp(u+v) = -wp(u) - wp(v) + (1/4)((wp'(u)-wp'(v))/(wp(u)-wp(v)))^2, the algebraic addition law.

nodes.name: Abel's Theorem for Elliptic Functions
nodes.description: For an elliptic function f of order n, the sum of zeros minus sum of poles in a period parallelogram is a lattice point.

nodes.name: Method of Stationary Phase
nodes.function_signature: (Oscillatory integral integral e^{i lambda phi(x)} A(x) dx, lambda -> infty) -> (Asymptotic expansion)
nodes.description: Asymptotic evaluation of oscillatory integrals via contributions from critical points of the phase phi(x).

nodes.name: Watson Transformation
nodes.function_signature: (Slowly convergent partial-wave series) -> (Contour integral in complex angular momentum)
nodes.description: Converts a sum over angular momentum into a contour integral, enabling asymptotic evaluation of scattering amplitudes.

nodes.name: Perron's Formula
nodes.description: sum_{n<=x} a_n = (1/2pi i) integral_{c-iT}^{c+iT} F(s) x^s/s ds + error, recovering partial sums from Dirichlet series.

nodes.name: Marchenko-Pastur Distribution
nodes.description: Limiting spectral distribution of Wishart matrices X^TX/n as p/n -> gamma, with density on [(1-sqrt(gamma))^2, (1+sqrt(gamma))^2].

nodes.name: Motzkin Number M_n
nodes.description: Number of paths from (0,0) to (n,0) with steps (1,1), (1,-1), (1,0) staying nonneg; M_n = sum C(n,2k) C_k.

nodes.name: Schroder Number
nodes.description: Number of lattice paths from (0,0) to (n,n) with steps (1,0), (0,1), (1,1) not crossing the diagonal.

nodes.name: Greatest common divisor
nodes.description: The greatest common divisor gcd(a,b) is the largest positive integer dividing both a and b, defined for any pair of integers not both zero.

nodes.name: Least common multiple
nodes.description: The least common multiple lcm(a,b) is the smallest positive integer divisible by both a and b.

nodes.name: GCD–LCM product relation
nodes.description: For positive integers a and b, gcd(a,b) · lcm(a,b) = ab.

nodes.name: Prime number
nodes.description: A natural number p > 1 whose only positive divisors are 1 and p.

nodes.name: Composite number
nodes.description: A natural number n > 1 that is not prime, equivalently n = ab for some integers 1 < a, b < n.

nodes.name: Canonical prime factorization
nodes.description: The standard-form representation n = p₁^{a₁} p₂^{a₂} ··· pₖ^{aₖ} with p₁ < p₂ < ··· < pₖ prime and each aᵢ ≥ 1.

nodes.name: Divisor characterization via prime factorization
nodes.description: If n = ∏ pᵢ^{aᵢ}, then d | n iff d = ∏ pᵢ^{bᵢ} with 0 ≤ bᵢ ≤ aᵢ for all i.

nodes.name: GCD and LCM via prime factorization
nodes.description: For n = ∏ pᵢ^{aᵢ} and m = ∏ pᵢ^{bᵢ}, gcd(n,m) = ∏ pᵢ^{min(aᵢ,bᵢ)} and lcm(n,m) = ∏ pᵢ^{max(aᵢ,bᵢ)}.

nodes.name: Integrality of binomial coefficients
nodes.description: The binomial coefficient C(n,k) = n!/(k!(n−k)!) is an integer for all 0 ≤ k ≤ n.

nodes.name: Prime divisibility of binomial coefficients
nodes.description: For prime p and 1 ≤ k ≤ p−1, the prime p divides C(p,k).

nodes.name: Completely multiplicative function
nodes.description: An arithmetic function f with f(1) = 1 and f(mn) = f(m)f(n) for all positive integers m, n without any coprimality restriction.

nodes.name: Multiplicative function determination by prime powers
nodes.description: A multiplicative function f is completely determined by its values f(pᵃ) at prime powers, since f(n) = ∏ f(pᵢ^{aᵢ}).

nodes.name: Möbius function sum identity
nodes.description: For all positive integers n, ∑_{d|n} μ(d) = [n = 1], equaling 1 if n = 1 and 0 otherwise.

nodes.name: Euler totient divisor sum
nodes.description: For all positive integers n, ∑_{d|n} φ(d) = n.

nodes.name: Euler totient product formula
nodes.description: φ(n) = n ∏_{p|n} (1 − 1/p), expressing the totient as a product over the distinct prime divisors of n.

nodes.name: Dirichlet identity function ε
nodes.description: The function ε(n) = [n = 1], serving as the multiplicative identity for Dirichlet convolution.

nodes.name: Dirichlet inverse existence
nodes.description: An arithmetic function f has a unique Dirichlet inverse f⁻¹ (with f ∗ f⁻¹ = ε) if and only if f(1) ≠ 0.

nodes.name: Abelian group of arithmetic functions under Dirichlet product
nodes.description: The set of arithmetic functions f with f(1) ≠ 0 forms an abelian group under Dirichlet convolution, with identity ε.

nodes.name: Unit function u(n) = 1
nodes.description: The arithmetic function u(n) = 1 for all positive integers n, a completely multiplicative function.

nodes.name: Number-theoretic identity function N(n) = n
nodes.description: The arithmetic function N(n) = n, a completely multiplicative function.

nodes.name: Möbius function is Dirichlet inverse of unit function
nodes.description: μ = u⁻¹ under Dirichlet convolution, equivalently μ ∗ u = ε.

nodes.name: Von Mangoldt divisor sum identity
nodes.description: For all n ≥ 1, ∑_{d|n} Λ(d) = log n, equivalently Λ = μ ∗ log as Dirichlet convolution.

nodes.name: Liouville function is completely multiplicative
nodes.description: The Liouville function λ(n) = (−1)^{Ω(n)} satisfies λ(mn) = λ(m)λ(n) for all positive integers m, n.

nodes.name: Liouville function divisor sum
nodes.description: ∑_{d|n} λ(d) = [n is a perfect square], equaling 1 if n is a perfect square and 0 otherwise.

nodes.name: Generalized divisor function σ_α
nodes.description: The function σ_α(n) = ∑_{d|n} d^α, a family of arithmetic functions parametrized by α ∈ ℂ.

nodes.name: Number of divisors function d(n)
nodes.description: The function d(n) = σ₀(n) = |{d > 0 : d | n}|, counting the number of positive divisors of n.

nodes.name: Sum of divisors function σ(n)
nodes.description: The function σ(n) = σ₁(n) = ∑_{d|n} d, giving the sum of all positive divisors of n.

nodes.name: Divisor function multiplicativity
nodes.description: The generalized divisor function σ_α is multiplicative for every α.

nodes.name: Divisor function prime power formula
nodes.description: For prime p and α ≠ 0, σ_α(pᵃ) = (p^{α(a+1)} − 1)/(p^α − 1); for α = 0, d(pᵃ) = a + 1.

nodes.name: Dirichlet product of multiplicative functions is multiplicative
nodes.description: If f and g are multiplicative, their Dirichlet product f ∗ g is also multiplicative.

nodes.name: Dirichlet inverse of multiplicative function is multiplicative
nodes.description: If f is multiplicative, its Dirichlet inverse f⁻¹ is also multiplicative.

nodes.name: Bell series
nodes.description: The Bell series of an arithmetic function f at a prime p is the formal power series f_p(x) = ∑_{n=0}^{∞} f(pⁿ) xⁿ.

nodes.name: Bell series multiplication theorem
nodes.description: If h = f ∗ g (Dirichlet product) and all three are multiplicative, then h_p(x) = f_p(x) · g_p(x) for every prime p.

nodes.name: Euler totient via Möbius inversion
nodes.description: φ = μ ∗ N under Dirichlet convolution, equivalently φ(n) = ∑_{d|n} μ(d)(n/d).

nodes.name: Euler totient multiplicativity
nodes.description: Euler's totient function φ is multiplicative: φ(mn) = φ(m)φ(n) whenever gcd(m,n) = 1.

nodes.name: Dirichlet ring of arithmetic functions
nodes.description: The commutative ring of all arithmetic functions under pointwise addition and Dirichlet convolution, with identity ε.

nodes.name: Generalized Möbius inversion
nodes.description: If F(x) = ∑_{n≤x} f(x/n) for all x ≥ 1, then f(x) = ∑_{n≤x} μ(n)F(x/n), and conversely.

nodes.name: Completely multiplicative Dirichlet inverse formula
nodes.description: If f is completely multiplicative, then f⁻¹(n) = μ(n)f(n) for all n.

nodes.name: Asymptotic equality
nodes.description: f ∼ g means f(x)/g(x) → 1 as x → ∞.

nodes.name: Average order of an arithmetic function
nodes.description: A function g(n) is an average order of f(n) if ∑_{n≤x} f(n) ∼ ∑_{n≤x} g(n).

nodes.name: Euler summation formula
nodes.description: ∑_{a<n≤b} f(n) = ∫_a^b f(t)dt + ∫_a^b (t − [t])f′(t)dt + f(x)([x] − x) − f(y)([y] − y), for f with continuous derivative.

nodes.name: Average order of d(n)
nodes.description: ∑_{n≤x} d(n) = x log x + (2γ − 1)x + O(√x), where γ is the Euler–Mascheroni constant.

nodes.name: Dirichlet hyperbola method
nodes.function_signature: (Dirichlet convolution sum ∑_{n≤x} (f∗g)(n)) → (Improved asymptotic estimate)
nodes.description: Splits the sum over the region {(a,b) : ab ≤ x} into three parts along a hyperbola to improve error terms in divisor-sum estimates.

nodes.name: Harmonic sum estimate
nodes.description: ∑_{n≤x} 1/n = log x + γ + O(1/x), where γ is the Euler–Mascheroni constant.

nodes.name: Average order of μ(n) is zero
nodes.description: M(x) = ∑_{n≤x} μ(n) = o(x), equivalently the Möbius function has mean value zero.

nodes.name: Mertens function
nodes.description: M(x) = ∑_{n≤x} μ(n), the summatory function of the Möbius function.

nodes.name: Lattice point counting
nodes.function_signature: (Arithmetic sum) → (Geometric count of lattice points)
nodes.description: Estimates arithmetic sums by counting integer lattice points in planar regions, e.g., under the hyperbola ab = x.

nodes.name: Prime counting function π(x)
nodes.description: π(x) = |{p ≤ x : p prime}|, counting the number of primes not exceeding x.

nodes.name: Relation between Chebyshev θ and ψ
nodes.description: ψ(x) = θ(x) + O(√x log² x), so θ(x) ∼ x if and only if ψ(x) ∼ x.

nodes.name: Abel summation relating π(x) and θ(x)
nodes.description: θ(x) = π(x) log x − ∫₂ˣ π(t)/t dt, obtained by partial summation.

nodes.name: Equivalence of PNT forms
nodes.description: The statements π(x) ∼ x/log x, θ(x) ∼ x, ψ(x) ∼ x, and π(x) ∼ Li(x) are mutually equivalent.

nodes.name: Shapiro's Tauberian theorem
nodes.description: If aₙ ≥ 0 and ∑_{n≤x} aₙ [x/n] = x log x + O(x), then ∑_{n≤x} aₙ/n = log x + O(1).

nodes.name: Selberg's identity
nodes.description: Λ(n) log n + ∑_{d|n} Λ(d)Λ(n/d) = ∑_{d|n} μ(d) log²(n/d), an exact identity for the von Mangoldt function.

nodes.name: Asymptotic formula for the n-th prime
nodes.description: The n-th prime satisfies pₙ ∼ n log n as n → ∞.

nodes.name: Divergence of the sum of prime reciprocals
nodes.description: ∑_{p prime} 1/p = ∞; more precisely ∑_{p≤x} 1/p = log log x + M + O(1/log x) where M is the Meissel–Mertens constant.

nodes.name: Residue class
nodes.description: The residue class of a modulo m is the equivalence class a + mℤ = {a + km : k ∈ ℤ}.

nodes.name: Complete residue system
nodes.description: A set of m integers containing exactly one representative from each residue class modulo m.

nodes.name: Reduced residue system
nodes.description: A set of φ(m) integers, one from each residue class coprime to m.

nodes.name: Linear congruence
nodes.description: An equation ax ≡ b (mod m) seeking integer solutions x.

nodes.name: Linear congruence solvability
nodes.description: The congruence ax ≡ b (mod m) has a solution iff gcd(a,m) | b, in which case there are exactly gcd(a,m) incongruent solutions.

nodes.name: Multiplicative inverse modulo m
nodes.description: An integer a has a multiplicative inverse modulo m if and only if gcd(a,m) = 1.

nodes.name: Polynomial congruence
nodes.description: An equation f(x) ≡ 0 (mod m) where f is a polynomial with integer coefficients.

nodes.name: Lagrange's theorem on polynomial congruences mod p
nodes.description: A polynomial of degree n with integer coefficients has at most n incongruent roots modulo a prime p.

nodes.name: Order of a group element
nodes.description: The smallest positive integer n such that gⁿ = e, for an element g in a finite group G.

nodes.name: Order of element divides group order
nodes.description: In a finite group G, the order of every element divides |G|.

nodes.name: Cyclic group
nodes.description: A group generated by a single element, isomorphic to ℤ/nℤ for some positive integer n.

nodes.name: Subgroups of cyclic groups are cyclic
nodes.description: Every subgroup of a cyclic group is cyclic, and for each divisor d of |G| there is exactly one subgroup of order d.

nodes.name: Direct product of groups
nodes.description: The direct product G × H of two groups is the set of pairs (g,h) with componentwise multiplication.

nodes.name: Group character (finite abelian)
nodes.description: A homomorphism χ: G → ℂ* from a finite abelian group G to the multiplicative group of nonzero complex numbers.

nodes.name: Character group is isomorphic to G
nodes.description: For a finite abelian group G, its character group Ĝ is (non-canonically) isomorphic to G, so |Ĝ| = |G|.

nodes.name: Orthogonality relations for Dirichlet characters
nodes.description: ∑_{χ mod m} χ(a)χ̄(b) = φ(m) if a ≡ b (mod m) with gcd(a,m) = 1, and 0 otherwise.

nodes.name: Extraction of arithmetic progressions via characters
nodes.function_signature: (Dirichlet characters mod m, residue class l) → (Indicator function for n ≡ l mod m)
nodes.description: Isolates a single residue class using the orthogonality relation: 𝟙_{n≡l} = (1/φ(m)) ∑_χ χ̄(l) χ(n).

nodes.name: Euler product for L(s,χ)
nodes.description: For Re(s) > 1, L(s,χ) = ∏_p (1 − χ(p)p⁻ˢ)⁻¹, expressing the Dirichlet L-function as a product over primes.

nodes.name: L(s,χ₀) relation to Riemann zeta
nodes.description: L(s,χ₀) = ζ(s) ∏_{p|m} (1 − p⁻ˢ) for the principal character χ₀ mod m.

nodes.name: Logarithm of L(s,χ) series
nodes.description: −log L(s,χ) = ∑_p ∑_{k≥1} χ(pᵏ)/(kpᵏˢ) for Re(s) > 1, from the Euler product.

nodes.name: Dirichlet series for primes in arithmetic progressions
nodes.description: ∑_{p≡l(m)} p⁻ˢ = (1/φ(m)) ∑_χ χ̄(l) log L(s,χ) + bounded terms for Re(s) > 1.

nodes.name: Pole of L(s,χ₀) at s = 1
nodes.description: L(s,χ₀) has a simple pole at s = 1 with residue ∏_{p|m}(1 − 1/p), inherited from the pole of ζ(s).

nodes.name: Product of all L-functions mod m
nodes.function_signature: (All Dirichlet characters mod m) → (Dirichlet series with nonnegative coefficients)
nodes.description: The product ∏_χ L(s,χ) yields a Dirichlet series with nonnegative coefficients, used to prove L(1,χ) ≠ 0 for complex χ.

nodes.name: Nonvanishing of L(1,χ) for real χ via Landau's theorem
nodes.function_signature: (L(s,χ) with real χ, Landau's theorem) → (L(1,χ) ≠ 0)
nodes.description: Proves L(1,χ) ≠ 0 for real χ using Landau's theorem that a Dirichlet series with nonneg coefficients has a singularity at its abscissa of convergence.

nodes.name: Equidistribution of primes in residue classes
nodes.description: The primes are equidistributed among the φ(m) reduced residue classes mod m: ∑_{p≤x, p≡l(m)} 1/p ∼ (1/φ(m)) log log x.

nodes.name: Convergence of L(s,χ) for nonprincipal χ at s > 0
nodes.description: For nonprincipal χ, the series L(s,χ) converges (conditionally) for all s with Re(s) > 0.

nodes.name: Periodic arithmetical function
nodes.description: An arithmetical function f satisfying f(n + q) = f(n) for all integers n and some fixed positive integer q.

nodes.name: Finite Fourier expansion of periodic functions
nodes.description: Every arithmetical function with period q can be written as f(n) = ∑_{k=1}^q a(k) e^{2πikn/q} with a(k) = (1/q) ∑_{r=1}^q f(r) e^{-2πikr/q}.

nodes.name: Ramanujan sum via Möbius function
nodes.description: c_q(n) = ∑_{d|gcd(n,q)} μ(q/d) d, expressing the Ramanujan sum as a divisor sum involving μ.

nodes.name: Multiplicativity of Ramanujan sums
nodes.description: For fixed n, the function q ↦ c_q(n) is multiplicative: c_{q₁q₂}(n) = c_{q₁}(n) c_{q₂}(n) when gcd(q₁,q₂) = 1.

nodes.name: Ramanujan expansion of arithmetical functions
nodes.function_signature: (ArithmeticFunction f) → (Series ∑ aₖ cₖ(n) in Ramanujan sums)
nodes.description: Expresses an arithmetical function as a pointwise convergent series in Ramanujan sums, analogous to Fourier expansion.

nodes.name: Separability of Gauss sums
nodes.description: A character χ mod m is separable if G(n,χ) = χ̄(n) G(1,χ) holds for all integers n.

nodes.name: Primitive characters are separable
nodes.description: Every primitive Dirichlet character mod m is separable: G(n,χ) = χ̄(n) G(1,χ) for all n.

nodes.name: Modulus of Gauss sum for primitive characters
nodes.description: For a primitive character χ mod m, |G(1,χ)|² = m, equivalently |G(1,χ)| = √m.

nodes.name: Quadratic Gauss sum
nodes.description: The sum G = ∑_{a=0}^{p−1} (a/p) e^{2πia/p} associated to the Legendre symbol, satisfying G² = (−1)^{(p−1)/2} p.

nodes.name: Sign of the quadratic Gauss sum
nodes.description: The quadratic Gauss sum equals √p if p ≡ 1 (mod 4) and i√p if p ≡ 3 (mod 4).

nodes.name: Representation of χ(n) via Gauss sums
nodes.description: For primitive χ mod m, χ(n) = (1/G(1,χ̄)) ∑_{a=1}^m χ̄(a) e^{2πian/m}, recovering χ from its Gauss sum.

nodes.name: Gauss sum product identity G(1,χ)G(1,χ̄) = χ(−1)m
nodes.description: For primitive χ mod m, G(1,χ)G(1,χ̄) = χ(−1) · m.

nodes.name: Von Sterneck's formula for Ramanujan sums
nodes.description: c_q(n) = μ(q/gcd(n,q)) φ(q)/φ(q/gcd(n,q)) when q/gcd(n,q) is squarefree, and 0 otherwise.

nodes.name: Half of reduced residues are quadratic residues
nodes.description: Among 1, 2, …, p−1, exactly (p−1)/2 are quadratic residues mod p and (p−1)/2 are nonresidues.

nodes.name: Euler's criterion
nodes.description: For odd prime p and gcd(a,p) = 1, the Legendre symbol (a/p) ≡ a^{(p−1)/2} (mod p).

nodes.name: Legendre symbol is completely multiplicative
nodes.description: The Legendre symbol satisfies (ab/p) = (a/p)(b/p) for all integers a, b.

nodes.name: First supplement to quadratic reciprocity
nodes.description: (−1/p) = (−1)^{(p−1)/2}, so −1 is a quadratic residue mod p iff p ≡ 1 (mod 4).

nodes.name: Gauss's lemma for the Legendre symbol
nodes.description: (a/p) = (−1)ⁿ where n counts the least positive residues of a, 2a, …, ((p−1)/2)a exceeding p/2.

nodes.name: Second supplement to quadratic reciprocity
nodes.description: (2/p) = (−1)^{(p²−1)/8}, so 2 is a quadratic residue mod p iff p ≡ ±1 (mod 8).

nodes.name: Jacobi symbol
nodes.description: For odd n = p₁^{a₁}···pₖ^{aₖ}, the Jacobi symbol (a/n) = ∏ (a/pᵢ)^{aᵢ} extends the Legendre symbol.

nodes.name: Quadratic reciprocity for Jacobi symbol
nodes.description: For coprime odd positive m, n: (m/n)(n/m) = (−1)^{((m−1)/2)((n−1)/2)}.

nodes.name: First supplement for Jacobi symbol
nodes.description: (−1/n) = (−1)^{(n−1)/2} for every odd positive integer n.

nodes.name: Second supplement for Jacobi symbol
nodes.description: (2/n) = (−1)^{(n²−1)/8} for every odd positive integer n.

nodes.name: Eisenstein's lemma
nodes.description: (a/p) = (−1)^{∑_{k=1}^{(p−1)/2} ⌊ka/p⌋}, expressing the Legendre symbol via a sum of floor functions.

nodes.name: Proof of quadratic reciprocity via Gauss sums
nodes.function_signature: (Quadratic Gauss sum G, G² = (−1)^{(p−1)/2}p) → (Quadratic reciprocity law)
nodes.description: Raises the quadratic Gauss sum to the q-th power and reduces mod q to derive (p/q)(q/p) = (−1)^{((p−1)/2)((q−1)/2)}.

nodes.name: Lattice point counting proof of quadratic reciprocity
nodes.function_signature: (Eisenstein's lemma, lattice points in rectangle) → (Quadratic reciprocity law)
nodes.description: Counts lattice points in the rectangle [1,(p−1)/2] × [1,(q−1)/2] above and below the diagonal to prove reciprocity.

nodes.name: Number of solutions of x² ≡ a (mod p)
nodes.description: The number of solutions of x² ≡ a (mod p) is 1 + (a/p): two if a is a nonzero QR, zero if a is a QNR, one if p | a.

nodes.name: Order of an integer modulo m
nodes.description: For gcd(a,m) = 1, the order ord_m(a) is the smallest positive integer k such that aᵏ ≡ 1 (mod m).

nodes.name: Order divides exponent iff congruence holds
nodes.description: aⁿ ≡ 1 (mod m) if and only if ord_m(a) | n.

nodes.name: Order of a power of an element
Number of primitive roots modulo m
nodes.description: If primitive roots exist modulo m, there are exactly φ(φ(m)) incongruent primitive roots.

nodes.name: Existence of primitive roots modulo p^k
nodes.description: For odd prime p and k ≥ 1, the group (ℤ/pᵏℤ)* is cyclic, i.e., primitive roots exist modulo pᵏ.

nodes.name: Existence of primitive roots modulo 2p^k
nodes.description: For odd prime p and k ≥ 1, the group (ℤ/2pᵏℤ)* is cyclic.

nodes.name: Nonexistence of primitive roots modulo 2^k for k ≥ 3
nodes.description: For k ≥ 3, (ℤ/2ᵏℤ)* ≅ ℤ/2 × ℤ/2^{k−2} is not cyclic, so no primitive root exists.

nodes.name: Classification of moduli having primitive roots
nodes.description: Primitive roots exist modulo m iff m ∈ {1, 2, 4, pᵏ, 2pᵏ} for an odd prime p and k ≥ 1.

nodes.name: Index (discrete logarithm) modulo m
nodes.description: For primitive root g mod m, ind_g(a) is the unique integer r mod φ(m) with gʳ ≡ a (mod m).

nodes.name: Homomorphism properties of the index function
nodes.description: ind_g(ab) ≡ ind_g(a) + ind_g(b) (mod φ(m)) and ind_g(aⁿ) ≡ n·ind_g(a) (mod φ(m)), giving (ℤ/mℤ)* ≅ ℤ/φ(m)ℤ.

nodes.name: Solving polynomial congruences via indices
nodes.function_signature: (Polynomial congruence mod m with primitive root g) → (Linear congruence in index variable)
nodes.description: Reduces xⁿ ≡ a (mod m) to the linear congruence n·ind_g(x) ≡ ind_g(a) (mod φ(m)).

nodes.name: Power residue criterion via indices
nodes.description: xⁿ ≡ a (mod p) is solvable iff a^{(p−1)/d} ≡ 1 (mod p) where d = gcd(n, p−1), with exactly d solutions.

nodes.name: Characters mod p via primitive roots
nodes.description: Every Dirichlet character mod p is χⱼ(gᵏ) = e^{2πijk/(p−1)} for unique j ∈ {0,…,p−2}, where g is a primitive root.

nodes.name: Abscissa of convergence vs absolute convergence relation
nodes.description: For a Dirichlet series ∑ f(n)/nˢ, σ_c ≤ σ_a ≤ σ_c + 1, bounding the gap between conditional and absolute convergence.

nodes.name: Analyticity of Dirichlet series
nodes.description: A Dirichlet series ∑ aₙ n⁻ˢ represents a holomorphic function in its half-plane of convergence Re(s) > σ_c, differentiable term by term.

nodes.name: Uniqueness theorem for Dirichlet series
nodes.description: If ∑ aₙ/nˢ = ∑ bₙ/nˢ in some half-plane, then aₙ = bₙ for all n.

nodes.name: Euler product for multiplicative functions
nodes.description: If f is multiplicative and ∑ f(n)/nˢ converges absolutely, then ∑ f(n)/nˢ = ∏_p (1 + f(p)/pˢ + f(p²)/p²ˢ + ···).

nodes.name: Euler product for completely multiplicative functions
nodes.description: If f is completely multiplicative with absolutely convergent Dirichlet series, then ∑ f(n)/nˢ = ∏_p (1 − f(p)/pˢ)⁻¹.

nodes.name: Dirichlet series for 1/ζ(s)
nodes.description: 1/ζ(s) = ∑ μ(n)/nˢ for Re(s) > 1, expressing the reciprocal of zeta via the Möbius function.

nodes.name: Dirichlet series for −ζ′(s)/ζ(s)
nodes.description: −ζ′(s)/ζ(s) = ∑ Λ(n)/nˢ for Re(s) > 1, the logarithmic derivative of zeta via the von Mangoldt function.

nodes.name: L(s,χ) as linear combination of Hurwitz zeta functions
nodes.description: L(s,χ) = k⁻ˢ ∑_{r=1}^k χ(r) ζ(s, r/k) for a character χ mod k.

nodes.name: Analytic continuation of ζ(s) to Re(s) > 0
nodes.description: ζ(s) extends to a meromorphic function on Re(s) > 0 with a simple pole at s = 1 with residue 1.

nodes.name: Analytic continuation of L(s,χ) to Re(s) > 0
nodes.description: For nonprincipal χ, L(s,χ) extends to an analytic function on Re(s) > 0 via partial summation.

nodes.name: Analytic continuation of Γ to meromorphic function on ℂ
nodes.description: Γ(s) extends to a meromorphic function on all of ℂ with simple poles at s = 0, −1, −2, … and residue (−1)ⁿ/n! at s = −n.

nodes.name: Difference equation for Bernoulli polynomials
nodes.description: Bₙ(x+1) − Bₙ(x) = nxⁿ⁻¹, characterizing Bernoulli polynomials via their first difference.

nodes.name: Contour integral representation of Hurwitz zeta
nodes.description: ζ(s,a) = −Γ(1−s)/(2πi) ∮_C (−z)^{s−1} e^{−az}/(1−e^{−z}) dz over a Hankel contour, valid for all s ≠ 1.

nodes.name: Analytic continuation of Hurwitz zeta to all of ℂ
nodes.description: Via the contour integral, ζ(s,a) extends to a meromorphic function on all of ℂ with only a simple pole at s = 1.

nodes.name: Values of ζ(s,a) at negative integers
nodes.description: ζ(−n, a) = −B_{n+1}(a)/(n+1) for n ≥ 0, expressing Hurwitz zeta at nonpositive integers via Bernoulli polynomials.

nodes.name: Values of ζ(s) at negative integers
nodes.description: ζ(−n) = −B_{n+1}/(n+1) for n ≥ 0, giving ζ(0) = −1/2 and ζ(−2k) = 0 for k ≥ 1.

nodes.name: Evaluation of ζ(2n) via Bernoulli numbers
Functional equation of L(s,χ) for primitive characters
nodes.description: For primitive χ mod k with a = (1−χ(−1))/2, the completed L-function Λ(s,χ) = (k/π)^{(s+a)/2} Γ((s+a)/2) L(s,χ) satisfies Λ(s,χ) = ε(χ) Λ(1−s,χ̄).

nodes.name: Analytic continuation of L(s,χ) to all of ℂ
nodes.description: For primitive nonprincipal χ, L(s,χ) extends to an entire function on ℂ via the functional equation.

nodes.name: Integral representation Γ(s)ζ(s) via Mellin transform
Periodic zeta function F(a,s)
nodes.description: F(a,s) = ∑_{n=1}^∞ e^{2πina}/nˢ for Re(s) > 1 and 0 < a < 1, appearing in the functional equation of Hurwitz zeta.

nodes.name: Simple pole of ζ(s) at s = 1
nodes.description: ζ(s) has a simple pole at s = 1 with residue 1, equivalently lim_{s→1} (s−1)ζ(s) = 1.

nodes.name: Mertens 3-4-1 inequality
nodes.function_signature: (Euler product of ζ(s)) → (ζ(1+it) ≠ 0 for all real t)
nodes.description: Uses 3 + 4cos θ + cos 2θ ≥ 0 to show |ζ(σ)³ ζ(σ+it)⁴ ζ(σ+2it)| ≥ 1, proving nonvanishing of ζ on Re(s) = 1.

nodes.name: Meromorphic structure of ζ′(s)/ζ(s)
nodes.description: −ζ′(s)/ζ(s) is meromorphic with a simple pole at s = 1 (residue 1) and poles at zeros ρ of ζ(s).

nodes.name: Derivation of PNT from Wiener–Ikehara theorem
nodes.function_signature: (Wiener–Ikehara theorem, −ζ′/ζ properties) → (ψ(x) ∼ x)
nodes.description: Applies the Wiener–Ikehara Tauberian theorem to −ζ′(s)/ζ(s) with its simple pole at s = 1 to deduce ψ(x) ∼ x.

nodes.name: Newman's short Tauberian proof of PNT
nodes.function_signature: (Analytic properties of ζ) → (ψ(x) ∼ x)
nodes.description: Newman's simplified analytic proof of PNT using a direct contour-integral argument avoiding the full Wiener–Ikehara machinery.

nodes.name: Integral representation of ψ(x) via ζ′/ζ
nodes.description: ψ(x) = (1/2πi) ∫_{c−i∞}^{c+i∞} (−ζ′(s)/ζ(s)) xˢ/s ds for c > 1, via Perron's formula.

nodes.name: Contour integration method for PNT
nodes.function_signature: (Integral for ψ(x), zero-free region) → (ψ(x) = x + error)
nodes.description: Shifts the Perron-type contour leftward past Re(s) = 1, extracting the main term x from the pole and bounding the remainder.

nodes.name: PNT with error term (de la Vallée-Poussin)
nodes.description: ψ(x) = x + O(x exp(−c√(log x))) for some c > 0, the quantitative prime number theorem.

nodes.name: PNT equivalent to nonvanishing of ζ on Re(s) = 1
nodes.description: ψ(x) ∼ x is logically equivalent to ζ(1+it) ≠ 0 for all real t.

nodes.name: Convexity bound for ζ(s) in the critical strip
nodes.description: ζ(σ+it) = O(|t|^{(1−σ)/2+ε}) for 0 ≤ σ ≤ 1 and |t| ≥ 1, by the Phragmén–Lindelöf principle.

nodes.name: Dirichlet eta function relation to ζ(s)
nodes.description: ζ(s) = (1 − 2^{1−s})⁻¹ η(s) where η(s) = ∑ (−1)^{n−1}/nˢ converges for Re(s) > 0.

nodes.name: ζ(s)² = ∑ d(n)/nˢ
nodes.description: ζ(s)² = ∑ d(n)/nˢ for Re(s) > 1, since d = 1 ∗ 1 under Dirichlet convolution.

nodes.name: ζ(s)ζ(s−1) = ∑ σ(n)/nˢ
nodes.description: ζ(s)ζ(s−1) = ∑ σ(n)/nˢ for Re(s) > 2, from the Dirichlet convolution of N and u.

nodes.name: Landau's theorem on Dirichlet series with nonneg coefficients
nodes.description: If aₙ ≥ 0 and ∑ aₙ/nˢ has finite abscissa of convergence σ_c, then s = σ_c is a singularity of the function.

nodes.name: Relation between ψ(x) and π(x) via Abel summation
nodes.description: π(x) = ψ(x)/log x + ∫₂ˣ ψ(t)/(t log² t) dt, so ψ(x) ∼ x implies π(x) ∼ x/log x.

nodes.name: Euler totient function φ(n)
nodes.description: φ(n) = |{1 ≤ k ≤ n : gcd(k,n) = 1}|, counting the integers up to n that are coprime to n.

nodes.name: Asymptotic for the summatory Euler totient
nodes.description: ∑_{n≤x} φ(n) = (3/π²)x² + O(x log x), following from Möbius inversion and the hyperbola method.

nodes.name: Density of squarefree integers
nodes.description: The proportion of squarefree integers up to x tends to 6/π² = 1/ζ(2); equivalently ∑_{n≤x} |μ(n)| = (6/π²)x + O(√x).

nodes.name: Big-omega function Ω(n)
nodes.description: Ω(n) = ∑_{p^a‖n} a, the number of prime factors of n counted with multiplicity; a completely additive function.

nodes.name: Mean value of ω(n)
nodes.description: ∑_{n≤x} ω(n) = x log log x + Mx + o(x) where M is the Meissel–Mertens constant; similarly for Ω(n).

nodes.name: Hardy–Ramanujan theorem on normal order of ω(n)
nodes.description: The normal order of ω(n) is log log n: for every ε > 0, the set of n with |ω(n) − log log n| > ε√(log log n) has density zero.

nodes.name: Turán's inequality for ω(n)
nodes.description: ∑_{n≤x} (ω(n) − log log x)² = O(x log log x), giving the variance bound that implies the Hardy–Ramanujan normal order result.

nodes.name: Legendre sieve formula
nodes.description: S(A,z) = ∑_{d|P(z)} μ(d)|A_d|, the inclusion-exclusion identity counting elements of A not divisible by primes below z, where P(z) = ∏_{p<z} p.

nodes.name: Twin prime sieve estimate
nodes.description: |{n ≤ x : n and n+2 both prime}| ≪ x/(log x)² by Selberg's or Brun's sieve, consistent with the Hardy–Littlewood conjecture up to the constant.

nodes.name: Additive character mod q
nodes.description: The function e_q(a) = e^{2πia/q} for a ∈ ℤ/qℤ, forming the character group of (ℤ/qℤ, +).

nodes.name: Orthogonality of additive characters
nodes.description: ∑_{a=0}^{q−1} e_q(na) = q if q|n and 0 otherwise, the discrete Fourier orthogonality for ℤ/qℤ.

nodes.name: Truncated Perron formula
nodes.description: ∑_{n≤x} aₙ = (1/2πi) ∫_{c−iT}^{c+iT} F(s)xˢ/s ds + O(xᶜ/(T·min(1,‖x‖))), the effective version of Perron's formula with explicit error from truncation.

nodes.name: Cesàro summability and Riesz means
nodes.description: The Riesz mean of order δ of a Dirichlet series: (1/Γ(δ+1)) ∑_{n≤x} aₙ(1−n/x)^δ, a smoothed partial sum that improves convergence properties.

nodes.name: Landau's formula for Dirichlet series coefficients
nodes.description: ∑_{n≤x} aₙ = (1/2πi) ∮ F(s)xˢ/s ds with the sum over residues giving the main terms, relating singularities of F(s) to the average behavior of aₙ.

nodes.name: 3-4-1 trigonometric inequality
nodes.description: 3 + 4cos θ + cos 2θ ≥ 0 for all real θ, the key inequality used to prove ζ(1+it) ≠ 0 via |ζ(σ)³ ζ(σ+it)⁴ ζ(σ+2it)| ≥ 1.

nodes.name: y-smooth integer (friable number)
nodes.description: A positive integer n is y-smooth if all its prime factors satisfy p ≤ y; Ψ(x,y) = |{n ≤ x : P⁺(n) ≤ y}| counts them.

nodes.name: Dickman rho function ρ(u)
nodes.description: The continuous function satisfying ρ(u) = 1 for 0 ≤ u ≤ 1 and uρ′(u) = −ρ(u−1) for u > 1, governing the density of smooth numbers: Ψ(x, x^{1/u}) ∼ ρ(u)x.

nodes.name: Smooth number asymptotic (de Bruijn / Hildebrand–Tenenbaum)
nodes.description: Ψ(x,y) ∼ xρ(u) uniformly for u = log x/log y in a wide range, with Hildebrand's refinement extending this to exp((log y)^{3/5−ε}) ≤ y ≤ x.

nodes.name: Buchstab function ω(u)
nodes.description: The continuous function with ω(u) = 1/u for 1 ≤ u ≤ 2 and (uω(u))′ = ω(u−1) for u > 2, arising in the Buchstab identity for Φ(x,y) = |{n ≤ x : P⁻(n) > y}|.

nodes.name: Primes in short intervals
nodes.description: π(x+h) − π(x) ∼ h/log x for h = x^θ with θ > 7/12 (Huxley), showing primes exist in intervals [x, x + x^θ].

nodes.name: Sathe–Selberg theorem on integers with k prime factors
nodes.description: |{n ≤ x : ω(n) = k}| ∼ (x/log x)(log log x)^{k−1}/((k−1)!) uniformly for 1 ≤ k ≤ (2−ε)log log x.

nodes.name: Beurling generalized primes
nodes.description: A sequence 1 < p₁ ≤ p₂ ≤ ⋯ of reals (generalized primes) generating by multiplicative closure a set of generalized integers; the framework for studying PNT-type results axiomatically.

nodes.name: Beurling PNT for generalized primes
nodes.description: If N(x) = Ax + O(x/(log x)^γ) with γ > 3/2 for the counting function of Beurling integers, then π_P(x) ∼ x/log x.

nodes.name: Induced Dirichlet character
