nodes.description: A power series F(X,Y) ∈ O[[X,Y]] satisfying the axioms of a commutative group law (associativity, commutativity, identity at 0, existence of inverses).

nodes.name: Lubin–Tate polynomial
nodes.description: A polynomial f(X) ∈ O_K[X] with f(X) ≡ πX (mod X²) and f(X) ≡ X^q (mod π), serving as the endomorphism [π] of the associated Lubin–Tate formal group.

nodes.name: Lubin–Tate extension
nodes.description: The totally ramified abelian extension K_{π,n} = K(λ) where λ ranges over πⁿ-torsion of the Lubin–Tate group, with Gal(K_{π,n}/K) ≅ (O_K/πⁿO_K)×.

nodes.name: Maximal abelian extension of a local field
nodes.description: The compositum K^{ab} = K^{ur}·K_π, independent of the choice of uniformizer π, where K^{ur} is the maximal unramified extension and K_π = ∪ K_{π,n}.

nodes.name: Local reciprocity law
nodes.description: For every finite abelian extension L/K of local fields, the local Artin map induces an isomorphism K×/N_{L/K}(L×) → Gal(L/K).

nodes.name: Local existence theorem
nodes.description: Every open subgroup of finite index in K× is the norm group N_{L/K}(L×) for a unique finite abelian extension L/K of local fields.

nodes.name: Hilbert symbol
nodes.description: For a local field K with n-th roots of unity, the pairing (a,b)_n: K×/K×ⁿ × K×/K×ⁿ → μ_n satisfying bimultiplicativity and (a,1−a)_n = 1.

nodes.name: Ramification filtration (upper numbering)
nodes.description: The filtration Gal(L/K)^s (s ∈ ℝ, s ≥ −1) of the Galois group by higher ramification groups in upper numbering, compatible with quotients via the Herbrand function.

nodes.name: Herbrand function
nodes.description: The function φ_{L/K}(s) = ∫₀ˢ dt/[G₀:G_t] converting lower numbering to upper numbering of ramification groups, with inverse ψ_{L/K}.

nodes.name: Maximal unramified extension
nodes.description: The extension K^{ur} = ∪ K(ζ_{q^n−1}) of a local field K, with Gal(K^{ur}/K) ≅ Ẑ via the Frobenius automorphism.

nodes.name: Local norm residue symbol (local Artin map)
nodes.description: The continuous homomorphism r_K: K× → Gal(K^{ab}/K) sending a uniformizer to Frobenius on K^{ur} and acting on torsion points via [a⁻¹].

nodes.name: Local Kronecker–Weber theorem
nodes.description: Every finite abelian extension of ℚ_p is contained in a cyclotomic field ℚ_p(ζ_n) for some n.

nodes.name: Strong approximation theorem
nodes.description: For a number field K and a place v₀, the image of K in ∏_{v≠v₀} K_v is dense; equivalently J_K = K×·J_K^{v₀}.

nodes.name: Global Artin map
nodes.description: The surjective continuous homomorphism r_K: C_K → Gal(K^{ab}/K) whose restriction to each local factor K_v× is the local Artin map.

nodes.name: Artin reciprocity law (global)
nodes.description: For every finite abelian extension L/K, the global Artin map induces an isomorphism C_K/N_{L/K}(C_L) → Gal(L/K).

nodes.name: Global existence theorem
nodes.description: Every open subgroup of finite index in C_K is the norm group N_{L/K}(C_L) for a unique finite abelian extension L/K.

nodes.name: Ray class field
nodes.description: The unique abelian extension K(𝔪)/K corresponding to the ray class group Cl_𝔪(K), with Gal(K(𝔪)/K) ≅ Cl_𝔪(K); a prime is unramified iff it does not divide 𝔪.

nodes.name: Modulus (cycle)
nodes.description: A formal product 𝔪 = ∏_v 𝔭_v^{n_v} over places with n_v ≥ 0 for finite places and n_v ∈ {0,1} for real places, defining congruence conditions for ray class groups.

nodes.name: Conductor of an abelian extension
nodes.description: The smallest modulus 𝔣 = 𝔣(L/K) such that the Artin map factors through Cl_𝔣(K), equal to the product of local conductors over all places.

nodes.name: Principal ideal theorem (Hauptidealsatz, class field theory)
nodes.description: Every fractional ideal of K becomes principal in the Hilbert class field H, proved via the triviality of the transfer map Gal(K₂/K) → Gal(K₂/H).

nodes.name: Hasse norm theorem
nodes.description: An element a ∈ K× is a norm from a cyclic extension L/K if and only if a is a local norm at every place v.

nodes.name: Grunwald–Wang theorem
nodes.description: Given local conditions at finitely many places compatible with a global degree, there exists a cyclic extension realizing them, subject to a specific exception for 2-powers.

nodes.name: Class field tower
nodes.description: The tower K = K₀ ⊂ K₁ ⊂ K₂ ⊂ ··· where Kᵢ₊₁ is the Hilbert class field of Kᵢ; by Golod–Shafarevich, infinite towers exist.

nodes.name: Norm limitation theorem
nodes.description: For a finite Galois extension L/K, N_{L/K}(C_L) = N_{M/K}(C_M) where M/K is the maximal abelian sub-extension; the norm group depends only on the abelian part.

nodes.name: Artin symbol (Frobenius at unramified primes)
nodes.description: For an abelian extension L/K unramified at 𝔭, the element (L/K, 𝔭) ∈ Gal(L/K) acting as x ↦ x^{N𝔭} on the residue field.

nodes.name: Idelic norm map
nodes.description: For L/K, the map N_{L/K}: J_L → J_K defined component-wise by local norms, continuous and inducing C_L → C_K on idèle class groups.

nodes.name: Conductor–discriminant formula
nodes.description: For a finite abelian extension L/K, d_{L/K} = ∏_χ 𝔣(χ) where χ ranges over characters of Gal(L/K) and 𝔣(χ) is the Artin conductor.

nodes.name: Decomposition law in abelian extensions
nodes.description: For an abelian extension L/K, a prime 𝔭 with Artin symbol of order f splits into g = [L:K]/ef primes of residue degree f and ramification index e.

nodes.name: Content (idèle norm)
nodes.description: The continuous homomorphism ‖·‖: J_K → ℝ_{>0} defined by ‖a‖ = ∏_v |a_v|_v, trivial on K× by the product formula, factoring through C_K.

nodes.name: Analytic continuation of the Dedekind zeta function
nodes.description: ζ_K(s) extends to a meromorphic function on ℂ with a simple pole at s = 1 of residue (2^{r₁}(2π)^{r₂}h_K R_K)/(w_K√|d_K|).

nodes.name: Functional equation for the Dedekind zeta function
nodes.description: The completed zeta function ξ_K(s) = |d_K|^{s/2}·Γ_ℝ(s)^{r₁}·Γ_ℂ(s)^{r₂}·ζ_K(s) satisfies ξ_K(s) = ξ_K(1−s).

nodes.name: Hecke character (Größencharakter)
nodes.description: A continuous homomorphism χ: C_K = J_K/K× → ℂ×, unifying Dirichlet characters and characters at infinity into a single adelic framework.

nodes.name: Artin conductor
nodes.description: For a representation ρ of Gal(L/K), the ideal 𝔣(ρ) = ∏_𝔭 𝔭^{f_𝔭(ρ)} where f_𝔭 = Σᵢ (|Gᵢ|/|G₀|)·codim(V^{Gᵢ}), measuring ramification.

nodes.name: Artin conjecture
nodes.description: Every nontrivial irreducible Artin L-function L(s,ρ,L/K) is entire; known for 1-dimensional representations via class field theory, open in general.

nodes.name: Meromorphic continuation of Artin L-functions
nodes.description: By Brauer's theorem, every Artin L-function admits meromorphic continuation to ℂ, being expressible as a quotient of products of Hecke L-functions.

nodes.name: L-function non-vanishing at s = 1
nodes.description: For any nontrivial character χ of a ray class group, L(1,χ) ≠ 0; the key analytic input for the Chebotarev density theorem and the existence theorem.

nodes.name: Schwartz–Bruhat function
nodes.description: On a local field K_v: a Schwartz function for archimedean v, a locally constant compactly supported function for non-archimedean v; the test functions for adelic analysis.

nodes.name: Local zeta integral (Tate)
nodes.description: Z_v(f_v, χ_v, s) = ∫_{K_v×} f_v(x)χ_v(x)|x|_v^s d×x for a local Schwartz–Bruhat function f_v, whose ratio with the local L-factor gives the epsilon factor.

nodes.name: Local epsilon factor
nodes.description: The local constant ε(s, χ_v, ψ_v) appearing in the local functional equation, depending on the character χ_v and additive character ψ_v, whose product gives the root number.

nodes.name: Adelic Poisson summation
nodes.description: For a Schwartz–Bruhat function f on 𝔸_K: Σ_{α∈K} f(α) = Σ_{α∈K} f̂(α), with Fourier transform via the self-dual Haar measure on 𝔸_K/K.

nodes.name: Self-duality of 𝔸_K/K
nodes.description: The compact group 𝔸_K/K is Pontryagin self-dual via the pairing (x,y) ↦ ψ(xy) for a nontrivial additive character ψ, the key ingredient for adelic Poisson summation.

nodes.name: Abelian Artin L-function equals Hecke L-function
nodes.description: For a one-dimensional Artin representation χ of Gal(L/K) with L/K abelian, L(s,χ,L/K) = L(s,χ') where χ' is the Hecke character via the Artin map.

nodes.name: Inductivity of Artin L-functions
nodes.description: L(s, Ind_H^G σ) = L(s, σ, L/F) for induced representations, meaning Artin L-functions are invariant under induction from subgroups.

nodes.name: Factorization of the Dedekind zeta function
nodes.description: For a Galois extension L/K, ζ_L(s) = ∏_ρ L(s,ρ)^{dim(ρ)} over irreducible representations ρ of Gal(L/K); for abelian extensions, ζ_L = ∏_χ L(s,χ).

nodes.name: Functional equation for Hecke L-functions
nodes.description: Λ(s,χ) = (|d_K|·N𝔣(χ))^{s/2}·∏_{v|∞} γ_v(s,χ_v)·L(s,χ) satisfies Λ(s,χ) = W(χ)·Λ(1−s,χ̄), proved via Tate's thesis.

nodes.name: Functional equation for Artin L-functions
nodes.description: Λ(s,ρ) = (|d_K|^{dim ρ}·N𝔣(ρ))^{s/2}·∏_{v|∞} L_v(s,ρ)·L(s,ρ) satisfies Λ(s,ρ) = W(ρ)·Λ(1−s,ρ̌), via Brauer's theorem.

nodes.name: Analytic continuation of Hecke L-functions
nodes.description: Every Hecke L-function for a nontrivial character extends to an entire function on ℂ; for the trivial character it has a simple pole at s = 1.

nodes.name: Haar measure on idèles
nodes.description: The product measure d×x = ∏_v d×x_v on J_K with vol(O_v×) = 1 for almost all v and d×x_v = dx_v/|x_v|_v, giving J_K a locally compact group structure.

nodes.name: Inertia-invariant subspace V^{I_𝔭}
nodes.description: For a Galois representation ρ and prime 𝔭 with inertia group I_𝔭, the subspace of V fixed by I_𝔭, on which Frobenius acts to define the local Euler factor at ramified primes.

nodes.name: Dirichlet's theorem on primes in number fields
nodes.description: For any nontrivial class c in Cl_𝔪(K), there are infinitely many primes in c, with Dirichlet density 1/|Cl_𝔪(K)|.

nodes.name: Logarithmic embedding (Dirichlet map)
nodes.description: Maps a unit u to (log|σ₁(u)|,...,log|σ_{r₁+r₂}(u)|), whose image is a lattice of rank r₁+r₂−1 in the trace-zero hyperplane.

nodes.name: Minkowski's lattice point argument
nodes.function_signature: (Ideal, Canonical embedding) → (Algebraic integer with bounded norm)
nodes.description: Embeds an ideal as a lattice via the canonical embedding then applies the convex body theorem to find algebraic integers of bounded norm.

nodes.name: Ideal norm reduction
nodes.function_signature: (Ideal class) → (Representative ideal of bounded norm)
nodes.description: Shows every ideal class contains an ideal of norm at most the Minkowski bound by applying the convex body theorem to the ideal lattice.

nodes.name: Hensel lifting
nodes.function_signature: (Approximate root mod 𝔪ⁿ) → (Exact root in complete field)
nodes.description: Iterative Newton-like procedure lifting approximate roots modulo higher powers of the maximal ideal, converging in the complete valued field.

nodes.name: Dimension shifting in group cohomology
nodes.function_signature: (Hⁿ(G,A)) → (Hⁿ⁻¹(G,A') or Hⁿ⁺¹(G,A''))
nodes.description: Embeds A into an induced module I and uses the long exact sequence to relate Hⁿ(G,A) to Hⁿ⁻¹(G,I/A), reducing higher cohomology to lower.

nodes.name: Herbrand quotient computation
nodes.function_signature: (Short exact sequences of G-modules) → (Herbrand quotient of middle term)
nodes.description: Exploits multiplicativity of Herbrand quotients on short exact sequences and h(G,A) = 1 for finite A, reducing computations via filtrations.

nodes.name: Cup product pairing technique
nodes.function_signature: (Ĥᵖ(G,A) × Ĥ⁻ᵖ⁻¹(G,A*)) → (ℚ/ℤ)
nodes.description: Uses cup product to establish dualities and periodicity in Tate cohomology, notably cupping with a class in H² to produce periodicity isomorphisms.

nodes.name: Reduction to Sylow subgroups in cohomology
nodes.function_signature: (Cohomological statement for G) → (Statement for each Sylow p-subgroup G_p)
nodes.description: Reduces cohomological statements to Sylow subgroups via injectivity of restriction on p-primary parts and cor ∘ res = [G:G_p].

nodes.name: Lubin–Tate formal group construction
nodes.function_signature: (Uniformizer π, Local field K) → (Totally ramified abelian extensions, Local Artin map)
nodes.description: Constructs explicit abelian extensions of a local field by adjoining torsion of a formal group, providing a non-cohomological construction of the local Artin map.

nodes.name: Brauer induction
nodes.function_signature: (Artin L-function L(s,ρ)) → (Product/quotient of Hecke L-functions)
nodes.description: Expresses an arbitrary Galois representation as a virtual sum of induced 1-dimensional characters, reducing Artin L-function properties to abelian L-functions.

nodes.name: Tate's thesis (adelic zeta integrals)
nodes.function_signature: (Schwartz–Bruhat function, Hecke character) → (L-function with functional equation)
nodes.description: Computes L-functions as integrals ζ(f,χ,s) = ∫_{J_K} f(x)χ(x)|x|^s d×x, with the functional equation arising from adelic Poisson summation.

nodes.name: Transfer (Verlagerung) homomorphism
nodes.description: The group-theoretic transfer map Ver: G^{ab} → H^{ab} for H ≤ G, used in proving the principal ideal theorem by reducing to a group-theoretic triviality statement.

nodes.name: Poisson summation in number field setting
nodes.function_signature: (Theta function on ideal lattice) → (Functional equation of ζ_K(s))
nodes.description: Applies Σ_{x∈Λ} f(x) = (1/vol)Σ_{y∈Λ*} f̂(y) over ideal lattices to derive the functional equation of Dedekind zeta functions.

nodes.name: Pro-p group
nodes.description: A profinite group that is an inverse limit of finite p-groups for a fixed prime p.
nodes.source: Cassels & Fröhlich, Algebraic Number Theory (1967), Ch. V

nodes.name: Complex multiplication (CM) field
nodes.description: A totally imaginary quadratic extension of a totally real number field; the endomorphism algebra of a CM abelian variety.
nodes.source: Cassels & Fröhlich, Algebraic Number Theory (1967), Ch. XIII

nodes.name: Linear algebraic group
nodes.description: An algebraic variety G equipped with a group structure such that multiplication and inversion are morphisms of varieties.
nodes.source: Cassels & Fröhlich, Algebraic Number Theory (1967), Ch. X

nodes.name: Semi-simple algebraic group
nodes.description: A connected linear algebraic group with no nontrivial connected solvable normal subgroup (trivial radical).
nodes.source: Cassels & Fröhlich, Algebraic Number Theory (1967), Ch. X

nodes.name: Simply connected algebraic group
nodes.description: A semi-simple algebraic group that admits no nontrivial central isogeny from another semi-simple group; its own universal cover.
nodes.source: Cassels & Fröhlich, Algebraic Number Theory (1967), Ch. X

nodes.name: Restricted topological product (restricted direct product)
nodes.description: Given locally compact groups {G_v} with compact open subgroups {H_v} for almost all v, the subgroup of the direct product consisting of tuples (g_v) with g_v ∈ H_v for almost all v.
nodes.source: Cassels & Fröhlich, Algebraic Number Theory (1967), Ch. II

nodes.name: Group homology H_n(G, M)
nodes.description: The left derived functors of the G-coinvariants functor M ↦ M_G = M/I_G·M, where I_G is the augmentation ideal of ℤ[G].
nodes.source: Cassels & Fröhlich, Algebraic Number Theory (1967), Ch. IV

nodes.name: Absolute Galois group Gal(K^sep/K)
nodes.description: The Galois group of the separable closure of K over K, equipped with the Krull topology as an inverse limit of finite Galois groups.
nodes.source: Cassels & Fröhlich, Algebraic Number Theory (1967), Ch. V

nodes.name: Supernatural number
nodes.description: A formal product ∏ p^{n_p} over all primes with exponents n_p ∈ {0, 1, 2, …, ∞}; the order of a profinite group is a supernatural number.
nodes.source: Cassels & Fröhlich, Algebraic Number Theory (1967), Ch. V

nodes.name: Free profinite group
nodes.description: A profinite group F such that every continuous map from a basis set to a profinite group G extends uniquely to a continuous homomorphism F → G.
nodes.source: Cassels & Fröhlich, Algebraic Number Theory (1967), Ch. V

nodes.name: Continuous cohomology of profinite groups
nodes.description: H^n(G, M) = lim_U H^n(G/U, M^U) over open normal subgroups U, the cohomology theory for profinite groups with discrete coefficient modules.
nodes.source: Cassels & Fröhlich, Algebraic Number Theory (1967), Ch. V

nodes.name: CM type
nodes.description: For a CM field E of degree 2g over ℚ, a set Φ = {φ_1, …, φ_g} of embeddings E ↪ ℂ choosing one from each complex-conjugate pair; determines the complex structure of the associated abelian variety.
nodes.source: Cassels & Fröhlich, Algebraic Number Theory (1967), Ch. XIII

nodes.name: Abelian variety with complex multiplication
nodes.description: An abelian variety A of dimension g whose endomorphism algebra End(A) ⊗ ℚ contains a CM field of degree 2g; the richest class of abelian varieties for arithmetic applications.
nodes.source: Cassels & Fröhlich, Algebraic Number Theory (1967), Ch. XIII

nodes.name: Reflex field (reflex CM type)
nodes.description: For a CM type (E, Φ), the subfield E* of ℂ generated over ℚ by {∑_{φ ∈ Φ} φ(a) : a ∈ E}; the field of definition of the CM type up to isogeny.
nodes.source: Cassels & Fröhlich, Algebraic Number Theory (1967), Ch. XIII

nodes.name: Algebraic Hecke character (Grössencharakter of type A₀)
nodes.description: A Hecke character χ: I_K → ℂ* whose infinity-type is algebraic, given by a product of embeddings raised to integer powers; naturally associated to CM abelian varieties via their ℓ-adic representations.
nodes.source: Cassels & Fröhlich, Algebraic Number Theory (1967), Ch. XIII

nodes.name: ℓ-extension
nodes.description: A Galois extension whose Galois group is a pro-ℓ group for a fixed prime ℓ; the study of the ℓ-part of class field theory.
nodes.source: Cassels & Fröhlich, Algebraic Number Theory (1967), Ch. XIV

nodes.name: ℤ_ℓ-extension
nodes.description: A Galois extension with Galois group isomorphic to ℤ_ℓ (the ℓ-adic integers); the cyclotomic ℤ_p-extension ℚ(μ_{p^∞})/ℚ is the prototypical example.
nodes.source: Cassels & Fröhlich, Algebraic Number Theory (1967), Ch. XIV

nodes.name: Global zeta integral (Tate)
nodes.description: Z(f, χ, s) = ∫_{I_K} f(x)χ(x)|x|^s d*x where f is a Schwartz–Bruhat function on 𝔸_K and χ is a Hecke character; a single integral computing all Hecke L-functions.
nodes.source: Cassels & Fröhlich, Algebraic Number Theory (1967), Ch. XV (Tate's Thesis)

nodes.name: Quasi-character of K_v*
nodes.description: A continuous homomorphism χ: K_v* → ℂ*; of the form χ(x) = χ₀(x)|x|^s where χ₀ is a unitary character and s ∈ ℂ.
nodes.source: Cassels & Fröhlich, Algebraic Number Theory (1967), Ch. XV (Tate's Thesis)

nodes.name: Self-dual Haar measure
nodes.description: The unique Haar measure on 𝔸_K (relative to an additive character ψ) such that the Fourier transform is an isometry; equivalently, vol(𝔸_K/K) = 1 with standard normalization.
nodes.source: Cassels & Fröhlich, Algebraic Number Theory (1967), Ch. XV (Tate's Thesis)

nodes.name: Kronecker's Jugendtraum
nodes.description: The program (partially realized by CM theory) to generate all abelian extensions of imaginary quadratic fields via special values of elliptic functions and modular functions.
nodes.source: Cassels & Fröhlich, Algebraic Number Theory (1967), Ch. XI

nodes.name: Kneser–Tits conjecture
nodes.description: The conjecture that for an isotropic simply connected simple algebraic group G over a field K, the Whitehead group G(K)/G(K)⁺ is trivial, where G(K)⁺ is generated by unipotent elements.
nodes.source: Cassels & Fröhlich, Algebraic Number Theory (1967), Ch. X

nodes.name: Golod–Shafarevich theorem
nodes.description: If G is a finite p-group with d minimal generators and r relations, then r > d²/4; consequently, certain pro-p groups with enough generators relative to relations must be infinite.
nodes.source: Cassels & Fröhlich, Algebraic Number Theory (1967), Ch. IX

nodes.name: Existence of infinite class field towers
nodes.description: There exist number fields whose p-class field tower K ⊂ K₁ ⊂ K₂ ⊂ ⋯ does not terminate, answering negatively a question of Furtwängler; proved via the Golod–Shafarevich theorem.
nodes.source: Cassels & Fröhlich, Algebraic Number Theory (1967), Ch. IX

nodes.name: Hasse principle for algebraic groups (Kneser–Harder)
nodes.description: For simply connected semi-simple groups G over a number field K, the map H¹(K, G) → ∏_v H¹(K_v, G) is injective; the local-global principle holds for principal homogeneous spaces.
nodes.source: Cassels & Fröhlich, Algebraic Number Theory (1967), Ch. X

nodes.name: Strong approximation for algebraic groups
nodes.description: For a simply connected semi-simple group G over a number field K and a place v with G(K_v) non-compact, G(K) is dense in ∏'_{w≠v} G(K_w).
nodes.source: Cassels & Fröhlich, Algebraic Number Theory (1967), Ch. X

nodes.name: Main theorem of complex multiplication
nodes.description: For an abelian variety A with CM type (E, Φ) and σ ∈ Aut(ℂ/E*), the conjugate σ(A) is isogenous to A via an isogeny controlled by the reflex norm and the Artin map of the reflex field E*.
nodes.source: Cassels & Fröhlich, Algebraic Number Theory (1967), Ch. XIII

nodes.name: Serre–Tate theorem (good reduction of CM abelian varieties)
nodes.description: An abelian variety with sufficiently many complex multiplications has potentially good reduction at every finite place; it acquires good reduction over a finite extension of the base field.
nodes.source: Cassels & Fröhlich, Algebraic Number Theory (1967), Ch. XIII

nodes.name: Iwasawa's theorem on class numbers in ℤ_p-extensions
nodes.description: For a ℤ_p-extension K_∞/K with intermediate fields K_n, the p-part of the class number satisfies v_p(h_n) = μp^n + λn + ν for sufficiently large n, with Iwasawa invariants μ, λ, ν.
nodes.source: Cassels & Fröhlich, Algebraic Number Theory (1967), Ch. XIV

nodes.name: Local functional equation (Tate)
nodes.description: The local zeta integral satisfies Z(f̂, χ⁻¹, 1−s) = ε(χ, s, ψ)·Z(f, χ, s) where f̂ is the Fourier transform, ψ is an additive character, and ε is the local epsilon factor.
nodes.source: Cassels & Fröhlich, Algebraic Number Theory (1967), Ch. XV (Tate's Thesis)

nodes.name: Global functional equation (Tate's thesis)
nodes.description: The global zeta integral Z(f, χ, s) has meromorphic continuation to all s ∈ ℂ and satisfies Z(f̂, χ⁻¹, 1−s) = Z(f, χ, s); implies the functional equation and analytic continuation of all Hecke L-functions.
nodes.source: Cassels & Fröhlich, Algebraic Number Theory (1967), Ch. XV (Tate's Thesis)

nodes.name: Decomposition of L-functions into local zeta integrals
nodes.description: For factorizable Schwartz–Bruhat functions f = ∏_v f_v, the global zeta integral decomposes as Z(f, χ, s) = ∏_v Z(f_v, χ_v, s); with standard choices, this recovers the Euler product of the Hecke L-function.
nodes.source: Cassels & Fröhlich, Algebraic Number Theory (1967), Ch. XV (Tate's Thesis)

nodes.name: Global–local compatibility of reciprocity maps
nodes.description: The global Artin map r_K restricted to K_v* (via the natural embedding K_v* → I_K → C_K) equals the local Artin map φ_{K_v} for each place v.
aliases: compatibility of local and global Artin maps
nodes.source: Cassels & Fröhlich, Algebraic Number Theory (1967), Ch. VII

nodes.name: Hilbert's different formula
nodes.description: For a Galois extension of local fields with ramification groups G_i, the different exponent equals ∑_{i=0}^∞ (|G_i| − 1), linking the different ideal to the higher ramification filtration.
nodes.source: Cassels & Fröhlich, Algebraic Number Theory (1967), Ch. I

nodes.name: First inequality (global class field theory)
nodes.description: For L/K cyclic of degree n, [C_K : N_{L/K}C_L] ≥ n; proved analytically using the non-vanishing of L(1, χ) for nontrivial characters.
nodes.source: Cassels & Fröhlich, Algebraic Number Theory (1967), Ch. VII

nodes.name: Second inequality (global class field theory)
nodes.description: For L/K cyclic of degree n, |H²(Gal(L/K), C_L)| ≤ n; combined with the first inequality yields |Ĥ⁰| = n and |Ĥ⁻¹| = 1 for the Tate cohomology of C_L.
nodes.source: Cassels & Fröhlich, Algebraic Number Theory (1967), Ch. VII

nodes.name: Krull's theorem (infinite Galois theory)
nodes.description: For an infinite Galois extension L/K, there is an inclusion-reversing bijection between intermediate fields and closed subgroups of Gal(L/K) in the Krull topology.
aliases: fundamental theorem of infinite Galois theory
nodes.source: Cassels & Fröhlich, Algebraic Number Theory (1967), Ch. V

nodes.name: Herbrand's theorem (upper numbering of ramification groups)
nodes.description: The ramification groups in upper numbering G^t = G_{ψ(t)} (defined via the Hasse–Arf function φ) are compatible with passage to quotients: for H normal in G, (G/H)^t = G^t·H/H.
nodes.source: Cassels & Fröhlich, Algebraic Number Theory (1967), Ch. I

nodes.name: Standard complex (bar resolution)
nodes.function_signature: (G-Module M) → (Group cohomology H^n(G,M), Group homology H_n(G,M))
nodes.description: The explicit free resolution of ℤ over ℤ[G] with B_n = ℤ[G^{n+1}] and boundary maps; produces group (co)homology via cochains/chains and enables concrete computations.
nodes.source: Cassels & Fröhlich, Algebraic Number Theory (1967), Ch. IV

nodes.name: Cohomology of idèles (local-to-global reduction)
nodes.function_signature: (Galois extension L/K, Idèle group I_L) → (H^n(Gal(L/K), I_L) via local cohomology)
nodes.description: Reduces the computation of H^n(Gal(L/K), I_L) to local cohomology computations via the decomposition I_L = ∏'_w L_w* and Shapiro's lemma.
nodes.source: Cassels & Fröhlich, Algebraic Number Theory (1967), Ch. VII

nodes.name: Lyndon–Hochschild–Serre spectral sequence
nodes.function_signature: (Group extension 1 → N → G → G/N → 1, G-Module M) → (Spectral sequence E₂^{p,q} = H^p(G/N, H^q(N,M)) ⟹ H^{p+q}(G,M))
nodes.description: For N normal in G, a spectral sequence converging to H^*(G,M) with E₂ page given by the cohomology of G/N with coefficients in H^*(N,M); the five-term exact sequence is its low-degree truncation.
nodes.source: Cassels & Fröhlich, Algebraic Number Theory (1967), Ch. IV

nodes.name: Projective modules over Dedekind domains
nodes.description: Every finitely generated projective module over a Dedekind domain R is isomorphic to a direct sum of ideals; equivalently, it has the form R^{n-1} ⊕ I for some ideal I.

nodes.name: Non-archimedean absolute value
nodes.description: An absolute value |·| on a field satisfying the ultrametric inequality |x+y| ≤ max(|x|,|y|), equivalently one for which |n| ≤ 1 for all integers n.

nodes.name: Trace form
nodes.description: The symmetric bilinear form (x,y) ↦ Tr_{L/K}(xy) on a finite separable extension L/K, whose discriminant equals the field discriminant d_{L/K}.

nodes.name: Different–ramification theorem
nodes.description: A prime P of O_L divides the different D_{L/K} if and only if P is ramified over K; the exponent of P in D_{L/K} satisfies d_P ≥ e_P − 1 with equality iff the ramification is tame.

nodes.name: Discriminant–ramification theorem
nodes.description: A prime p of O_K ramifies in L/K if and only if p divides the discriminant d_{L/K}; follows from the different–discriminant relation N_{L/K}(D_{L/K}) = d_{L/K}.

nodes.name: Ring of integers of cyclotomic fields
nodes.description: The ring of integers of Q(ζ_n) is Z[ζ_n], generated as a Z-module by powers of a primitive n-th root of unity.

nodes.name: Ramification in cyclotomic fields
nodes.description: In Q(ζ_n)/Q, a prime p ramifies if and only if p divides n; specifically pO_{Q(ζ_{p^r})} = (1 − ζ_{p^r})^{φ(p^r)} and the ramification is totally ramified with index φ(p^r).

nodes.name: Gauss sum norm formula
nodes.description: For a primitive Dirichlet character χ mod m, the Gauss sum satisfies |g(χ)|² = m, and more generally g(χ)g(χ̄) = χ(−1)m.

nodes.name: Stickelberger element
nodes.description: The element θ = ∑_{a ∈ (Z/mZ)×} (a/m) σ_a⁻¹ in the group ring Q[Gal(Q(ζ_m)/Q)], whose annihilation properties on the class group are given by Stickelberger’s theorem.

nodes.name: Volume computation of fundamental domain
nodes.function_signature: (Lattice Λ ⊂ R^n, number field K) → (vol(R^n/Λ) = 2^{−r_2}|d_K|^{1/2})
nodes.description: Computing the volume of the fundamental parallelotope of the image of O_K under the Minkowski embedding, yielding the key factor in Minkowski’s bound.

nodes.name: Counting ideals of bounded norm
nodes.description: The number of integral ideals of norm ≤ x in a number field K satisfies #{a ⊂ O_K : N(a) ≤ x} = κ·x + O(x^{1−1/[K:Q]}) where κ = (2^{r_1}(2π)^{r_2}R_K h_K)/(w_K |d_K|^{1/2}).

nodes.name: Lattice points in homogeneously expanding domains
nodes.function_signature: (Bounded region S ⊂ R^n, lattice Λ, parameter t) → (|tS ∩ Λ| ∼ t^n vol(S)/vol(R^n/Λ))
nodes.description: Estimating the number of lattice points in a region scaled by parameter t, the fundamental counting technique behind ideal-counting and class number formulas.

nodes.name: Content (idèle norm) map
nodes.description: The continuous homomorphism ||·||: J_K → R>0 defined by ||x|| = ∏_v |x_v|_v, whose kernel J_K^1 contains K× by the product formula, yielding the exact sequence 1 → C_K^1 → C_K → R>0 → 1.

nodes.name: Compactness of C_K^1
nodes.description: The norm-one idèle class group C_K^1 = J_K^1/K× is compact, encoding both finiteness of the class number and Dirichlet’s unit theorem in a single topological statement.

nodes.name: Relationship between idèle class group and ray class groups
nodes.description: For a modulus m, the ray class group Cl_m(K) is canonically isomorphic to C_K / U_m K× where U_m is the open subgroup of idèles congruent to 1 mod m, connecting the idelic and classical formulations.

nodes.name: Galois action on idèles
nodes.description: For a Galois extension L/K, the Galois group Gal(L/K) acts on J_L by permuting components according to its action on places; the fixed subgroup satisfies J_L^{Gal(L/K)} = J_K (embedded diagonally at places above each v).

nodes.name: Convergence and Euler product for ζ_K
nodes.description: The Dedekind zeta function ζ_K(s) = ∑_{a ⊂ O_K} N(a)^{−s} converges absolutely for Re(s) > 1 and admits an Euler product ζ_K(s) = ∏_p (1 − N(p)^{−s})^{−1} over prime ideals p of O_K.

nodes.name: Faltings’ finiteness theorem (Shafarevich conjecture)
nodes.description: Up to isomorphism, there are only finitely many abelian varieties of given dimension over a number field K with good reduction outside a fixed finite set of primes; implies the Mordell conjecture.

nodes.name: Local norm group
nodes.description: For a finite extension L_w/K_v of local fields, the norm group N_{L_w/K_v}(L_w×) is an open subgroup of finite index in K_v×, and the map L ↦ N_{L/K}(L×) gives a bijection between finite abelian extensions and open subgroups of finite index.

nodes.name: Local norm index theorem
nodes.description: [K_v× : N_{L_w/K_v}(L_w×)] = [L_w : K_v] for any finite Galois extension L_w/K_v of local fields; equivalently |Ĥ⁰(G, L_w×)| = n.

nodes.name: p-adic exponential and logarithm
nodes.function_signature: (p-adic number x with v_p(x) > 1/(p−1)) → (exp_p(x), log_p(1+x))
nodes.description: The p-adic exponential exp_p(x) = ∑ x^n/n! converges for v_p(x) > 1/(p−1) and the p-adic logarithm log_p(1+x) = ∑ (−1)^{n+1} x^n/n converges for |x|_p < 1, providing isomorphisms between additive and multiplicative subgroups of Z_p.

nodes.name: Structure of local units
nodes.description: For a local field K_v with residue field of order q = p^f, the unit group O_v× ≅ μ_{q−1} × Z_p^f as a topological group, where μ_{q−1} is the group of (q−1)-th roots of unity (Teichmüller representatives).

nodes.name: Global cyclic norm index inequality
nodes.description: For a cyclic extension L/K of number fields of degree n, the norm index [J_K : K× · N_{L/K}(J_L)] divides n, a key step toward proving the first and second inequalities of class field theory.

nodes.name: Takagi’s existence theorem
nodes.description: Every open subgroup of finite index in the idèle class group C_K (equivalently, every congruence subgroup defined by a modulus m) is the norm group N_{L/K}(C_L) of a unique finite abelian extension L/K.

nodes.name: Conductor–class field relationship
nodes.description: The conductor f(L/K) of an abelian extension L/K is the smallest modulus m such that L is contained in the ray class field K_m; a prime ramifies in L/K if and only if it divides f(L/K).

nodes.name: Existence theorem of class field theory
nodes.description: The correspondence L ↦ N_{L/K}(C_L) is an inclusion-reversing bijection between finite abelian extensions of K and open subgroups of finite index in C_K, with [C_K : N_{L/K}(C_L)] = [L:K].

nodes.name: Reduction to Kummer extensions
nodes.function_signature: (Abelian extension L/K) → (Reduced to cyclic extensions of prime degree via Kummer theory)
nodes.description: Proving the main theorems of CFT by first adjoining enough roots of unity to reduce to the case where the extension is Kummer, then using explicit norm computations in Kummer extensions.

nodes.name: Complete splitting theorem
nodes.description: A prime p of K splits completely in an abelian extension L/K if and only if p lies in the norm group N_{L/K}(C_L); equivalently, the Frobenius at p is trivial iff the local norm group at p equals K_p×.

nodes.name: Ramification theorem (class field theory)
nodes.description: A prime p of K is unramified in the abelian extension L/K if and only if the local norm group N_{L_P/K_p}(L_P×) contains the local units O_{K_p}×; the conductor f(L/K) encodes exactly the ramified primes.

nodes.name: Infinite divisibility of universal norms
nodes.description: The intersection ∩_L N_{L/K}(L×) over all finite extensions L/K equals {1} in K× (or the connected component in the local case), meaning elements that are norms from every extension are infinitely divisible.

nodes.name: Induced character and L-series factorization
nodes.description: Writing ρ = ∑ n_i Ind_{H_i}^G χ_i by Brauer’s theorem gives L(s,ρ,L/K) = ∏ L(s,χ_i,L/L^{H_i})^{n_i}, reducing non-abelian Artin L-functions to products of abelian ones (Hecke L-functions).

nodes.name: Local additive duality (self-duality of K_v)
nodes.description: For a local field K_v, the map x ↦ ψ_v(x·) gives an isomorphism K_v ≅ K̂_v between K_v and its Pontryagin dual, making K_v additively self-dual; the self-dual Haar measure is normalized by |d_v|^{1/2}.

nodes.name: Dirichlet integral
nodes.function_signature: (Dirichlet series ∑ a_n n^{−s}, contour) → (Partial sums A(x) via Perron’s formula)
nodes.description: Recovering partial sums of arithmetic functions from their Dirichlet series via the integral (1/2πi) ∫ f(s) x^s/s ds, the analytic bridge between multiplicative and additive number theory.

nodes.name: Tauberian theorem for Dirichlet series
nodes.description: If f(s) = ∑ a_n n^{−s} with a_n ≥ 0 has a simple pole at s = 1 with residue c, and is otherwise analytic on Re(s) ≥ 1, then ∑_{n≤x} a_n ∼ cx, converting analytic information into asymptotic counts.

nodes.name: Non-vanishing of L(1, χ) for Hecke characters
nodes.description: For a nontrivial Hecke character χ (Grössencharakter) of a number field K, L(1, χ) ≠ 0; generalizes the classical Dirichlet non-vanishing and is essential for the Chebotarev density theorem.

nodes.name: Dirichlet’s theorem as special case of Chebotarev
nodes.description: Dirichlet’s theorem on primes in arithmetic progressions follows from the Chebotarev density theorem applied to the cyclotomic extension Q(ζ_m)/Q, where Frobenius classes correspond to residue classes mod m.

nodes.name: Upper estimate for residue of ζ_K at s = 1
nodes.description: The residue κ_K of ζ_K(s) at s = 1 satisfies κ_K ≤ c(ε) |d_K|^ε for every ε > 0, where c(ε) depends only on the degree [K:Q] and ε; controls the class number times regulator from above.

nodes.name: Siegel’s lower bound for the residue
nodes.description: For totally real fields K (and more generally), κ_K ≥ c(ε) |d_K|^{−ε} for every ε > 0; the constant c(ε) is ineffective due to the possible existence of Siegel zeros.

nodes.name: Comparison of residues in normal extensions
nodes.function_signature: (Normal extension L/K, ζ_K, ζ_L) → (Ratio κ_L/κ_K^{[L:K]} bounded in terms of discriminants)
nodes.description: Comparing the residues of Dedekind zeta functions of a normal extension L/K by factoring ζ_L/ζ_K into Artin L-functions and bounding each factor, a key step in the proof of the Brauer–Siegel theorem.

nodes.name: Weierstrass product for completed L-function
nodes.description: The completed L-function Λ(s, χ) admits a Hadamard product Λ(s, χ) = e^{A+Bs} ∏_ρ (1 − s/ρ) e^{s/ρ} over its nontrivial zeros ρ, encoding the distribution of zeros in the critical strip.

nodes.name: Logarithmic derivative ξ’/ξ
nodes.function_signature: (Completed L-function ξ(s)) → (Sum over zeros ∑_ρ 1/(s−ρ))
nodes.description: Taking the logarithmic derivative of the Hadamard product to express ξ’/ξ(s) = B + ∑_ρ (1/(s−ρ) + 1/ρ), the basic tool for relating zeros to prime-counting functions.

nodes.name: Estimate for ξ’/ξ
nodes.description: The bound ∑_ρ 1/|s−ρ|² = O(log |t|) for |Im(s)| = t → ∞ away from zeros, and the consequence that ξ’/ξ(s) = ∑_{|γ−t|≤1} 1/(s−ρ) + O(log t), localizing the contribution to nearby zeros.

nodes.name: Weil’s positivity criterion
nodes.description: The Riemann hypothesis for ζ_K is equivalent to the positivity ∑_{ρ} ĥ(ρ) ≥ 0 for all test functions h in a suitable class, reformulating RH as a positive-definiteness condition.

nodes.name: Evaluation of basic sum (Part 1)
nodes.function_signature: (Test function h, explicit formula) → (∑_p log p · h(log p) expressed via ĥ and zeros)
nodes.description: First stage of evaluating the prime-side sum in Weil’s explicit formula by Fourier analysis, converting the sum over primes into integrals involving the Fourier transform of the test function.

nodes.name: Evaluation of basic sum (Part 2)
nodes.function_signature: (Fourier-side expression from Part 1) → (Final explicit relation between primes and zeros)
nodes.description: Second stage completing the evaluation by handling archimedean contributions and the integral terms, yielding the full Weil explicit formula relating prime sums to zero sums.

nodes.name: Characteristic of a field
nodes.description: The smallest positive integer p such that p·1 = 0 in the field, or 0 if no such integer exists; a field has characteristic 0 or a prime.

nodes.name: Cyclicity of F_q*
nodes.description: The multiplicative group F_q* of a finite field with q elements is cyclic of order q − 1.

nodes.name: Character sum method for counting solutions
nodes.function_signature: (System of polynomial equations over F_q, characters of F_q) → (Exact count of solutions)
nodes.description: Expresses the number of solutions of equations over a finite field as sums involving multiplicative and additive characters, reducing counting to evaluation of character sums.

nodes.name: Units of Z_p
nodes.description: Z_p* = {x ∈ Z_p : |x|_p = 1} is the group of p-adic integers with p-adic absolute value 1, equivalently those x with x mod p ≠ 0.

nodes.name: Compactness of Z_p
nodes.description: The ring Z_p of p-adic integers is compact and totally disconnected in the p-adic topology, being the inverse limit of the finite rings Z/p^nZ.

nodes.name: Structure of Q_p*
nodes.description: Q_p* ≅ p^Z × μ_{p−1} × (1 + pZ_p) for p odd, where μ_{p−1} is the group of Teichmüller representatives and 1 + pZ_p ≅ Z_p as topological groups.

nodes.name: Squares in Q_p*
nodes.description: For p odd, Q_p*/Q_p*² ≅ (Z/2Z)² has order 4, generated by the classes of p and a non-square unit; for p = 2, Q_2*/Q_2*² ≅ (Z/2Z)³ has order 8.

nodes.name: Density of Q in Q_p
nodes.description: The rational numbers Q are dense in Q_p with respect to the p-adic topology, since every p-adic number is a limit of rationals.

nodes.name: Hilbert symbol at the archimedean place
nodes.description: The Hilbert symbol (a,b)_∞ for a, b ∈ R* equals −1 if and only if a < 0 and b < 0, reflecting the sign obstruction for the real norm form.

nodes.name: Bilinearity and non-degeneracy of the Hilbert symbol
nodes.description: The Hilbert symbol (·,·)_v : K_v*/K_v*² × K_v*/K_v*² → {±1} is bimultiplicative, symmetric, satisfies (a,1−a)_v = 1, and is non-degenerate in each variable.

nodes.name: Hilbert symbol computation for odd p
nodes.description: For odd p and units u, v ∈ Z_p*, (u,v)_p = 1, (u,p)_p = (u/p), and (p^a u, p^b v)_p = (−1)^{ab(p−1)/2}(u/p)^b(v/p)^a.

nodes.name: Existence theorem for prescribed Hilbert symbols
nodes.description: Given local invariants (ε_v) ∈ {±1} at finitely many places with ∏_v ε_v = 1, there exist a, b ∈ Q* with (a,b)_v = ε_v for all v.

nodes.name: Discriminant of a quadratic form
nodes.description: The determinant of the Gram matrix of a non-degenerate quadratic form, viewed as an element of K*/K*², an invariant under equivalence.

nodes.name: Hasse–Witt invariant
nodes.description: For a diagonal form ⟨a_1,…,a_n⟩ over a local field K_v, the product ε_v = ∏_{i<j}(a_i,a_j)_v ∈ {±1}, a complete local invariant complementing rank and discriminant.

nodes.name: Isotropic quadratic form
nodes.description: A quadratic form Q over a field K is isotropic if there exists a nonzero vector v ∈ K^n with Q(v) = 0; otherwise it is anisotropic.

nodes.name: Witt decomposition
nodes.description: Every non-degenerate quadratic form over a field decomposes uniquely as an orthogonal sum of hyperbolic planes and an anisotropic form.

nodes.name: Classification of quadratic forms over Q_p
nodes.description: A non-degenerate quadratic form over Q_p is determined up to equivalence by its rank, discriminant in Q_p*/Q_p*², and Hasse–Witt invariant ε_p ∈ {±1}.

nodes.name: Representation theorem for quadratic forms over Q_p
nodes.description: A non-degenerate quadratic form of rank ≥ 2 over Q_p represents a ∈ Q_p* if and only if the form ⟨Q, −a⟩ has the correct Hasse–Witt invariant.

nodes.name: Classification of quadratic forms over Q
nodes.description: By Hasse–Minkowski, a non-degenerate quadratic form over Q is determined up to equivalence by its rank, signature, discriminant, and Hasse–Witt invariants at all primes.

nodes.name: Hasse invariant computation
nodes.function_signature: (Diagonal quadratic form ⟨a_1,…,a_n⟩, local field K_v) → (ε_v ∈ {±1})
nodes.description: Computes the Hasse–Witt invariant ε_v = ∏_{i<j}(a_i,a_j)_v by reducing Hilbert symbols to Legendre symbols and explicit formulas.

nodes.name: Unimodular lattice
nodes.description: An integral lattice L whose Gram matrix has determinant ±1, equivalently L = L* (self-dual with respect to the bilinear form).

nodes.name: Even (type II) lattice
nodes.description: An integral lattice in which every vector has even norm Q(v) ∈ 2Z for all v ∈ L; if unimodular, its rank must be divisible by 8.

nodes.name: Odd (type I) lattice
nodes.description: An integral unimodular lattice that is not even, i.e., some vector v ∈ L satisfies Q(v) ≡ 1 mod 2.

nodes.name: Signature of a real quadratic form
nodes.description: The pair (p, q) where p is the number of positive and q the number of negative eigenvalues, with p + q = n by Sylvester's law of inertia.

nodes.name: E_8 lattice
nodes.description: The unique positive definite even unimodular lattice of rank 8, with root system E_8, minimal norm 2, and 240 roots.

nodes.name: Classification of even unimodular lattices
nodes.description: Positive definite even unimodular lattices exist only in ranks divisible by 8; unique in rank 8 (E_8) and rank 16, with 24 in rank 24 (Niemeier lattices).

nodes.name: Classification of indefinite unimodular lattices
nodes.description: An indefinite unimodular lattice is determined up to isometry by its rank, signature, and type (even or odd); the even case requires signature ≡ 0 mod 8.

nodes.name: Genus of an integral quadratic form
nodes.description: The equivalence class of an integral quadratic form under Z_p-equivalence at all primes p and R-equivalence; forms in the same genus are locally equivalent everywhere.

nodes.name: Genus determines rational equivalence
nodes.description: Two integral quadratic forms in the same genus are equivalent over Q, though they need not be equivalent over Z.

nodes.name: Local-to-global passage for lattices
nodes.function_signature: (Local data at all primes p and at ∞) → (Global integral form up to genus)
nodes.description: Constructs or classifies integral quadratic forms by assembling local conditions at each prime and the archimedean place, using strong approximation or mass formulas.

nodes.name: Character of a finite abelian group
nodes.description: A group homomorphism χ: G → C* from a finite abelian group G to the multiplicative group of nonzero complex numbers; the characters form the dual group Ĝ ≅ G.

nodes.name: Modular function
nodes.description: A meromorphic function on the upper half-plane invariant under SL₂(Z) (weight 0) and meromorphic at the cusp; the field of modular functions is C(j).

nodes.name: Fourier expansion (q-expansion) of a modular form
nodes.description: The expansion f(τ) = Σ_{n≥0} a_n q^n with q = e^{2πiτ}, expressing a modular form as a power series in q; a cusp form has a_0 = 0.

nodes.name: Valence formula for modular forms
nodes.description: For a nonzero modular form f of weight k on SL₂(Z), v_∞(f) + v_i(f)/2 + v_ρ(f)/3 + Σ'_P v_P(f) = k/12.

nodes.name: Decomposition M_k = C·E_k ⊕ S_k
nodes.description: For even k ≥ 4, M_k(SL₂(Z)) decomposes as the direct sum of the one-dimensional span of the Eisenstein series E_k and the space S_k of cusp forms.

nodes.name: Structure of the algebra of modular forms
nodes.description: The graded algebra M_*(SL₂(Z)) = ⊕_{k≥0} M_k(SL₂(Z)) is the polynomial ring C[E_4, E_6], freely generated by Eisenstein series of weights 4 and 6.

nodes.name: Relation Δ = (E_4³ − E_6²)/1728
nodes.description: The modular discriminant Δ equals (E_4³ − E_6²)/1728 as a weight-12 cusp form, following from the structure of M_12(SL₂(Z)).

nodes.name: Hecke operators are self-adjoint
nodes.description: The Hecke operators T_n on S_k(SL₂(Z)) are self-adjoint with respect to the Petersson inner product: ⟨T_n f, g⟩ = ⟨f, T_n g⟩.

nodes.name: Multiplicativity of the Ramanujan tau function
nodes.description: τ(mn) = τ(m)τ(n) for gcd(m,n) = 1 and τ(p^{a+1}) = τ(p)τ(p^a) − p^{11}τ(p^{a−1}), since Δ is a Hecke eigenform.

nodes.name: Theta function of a quadratic form is a modular form
nodes.description: For a positive definite integral quadratic form Q in m variables, θ_Q(τ) is a modular form of weight m/2 for a congruence subgroup determined by Q.

nodes.name: Representation numbers via modular forms
nodes.description: The number r_Q(n) of representations of n by Q equals the n-th Fourier coefficient of θ_Q, enabling exact formulas by decomposing θ_Q into Eisenstein and cusp parts.

nodes.name: Eight squares formula
nodes.description: The number of representations of n as a sum of eight squares is r_8(n) = 16Σ_{d|n}(−1)^{n+d}d³, derived from the identity θ⁸ = E_4.

nodes.name: Growth bound for Fourier coefficients of modular forms
nodes.description: For a modular form of weight k, a_n = O(n^{k−1}); for a cusp form, a_n = O(n^{k/2}) from the boundedness of y^{k/2}|f(z)| on H.

nodes.name: Contour integration on the fundamental domain
nodes.function_signature: (Modular form f of weight k, boundary ∂F) → (Weighted zero count = k/12)
nodes.description: Integrates f'/f around the boundary of the fundamental domain, using modular transformation laws to match boundary segments, yielding the valence formula.

nodes.name: Poisson summation for theta functions
nodes.function_signature: (Theta series θ_Q(τ), Poisson summation formula) → (Transformation law under τ → −1/τ)
nodes.description: Applies Poisson summation to the lattice sum defining a theta function to derive its modular transformation property under τ → −1/τ.

nodes.name: Hecke eigenform method
nodes.function_signature: (Space S_k, Hecke operators {T_n}, Petersson inner product) → (Basis of eigenforms with Euler products)
nodes.description: Simultaneously diagonalizes the commuting self-adjoint Hecke operators on the space of cusp forms to produce eigenforms whose L-functions have Euler products.

nodes.name: Farey sequence F_n
nodes.description: The ascending sequence of all irreducible fractions h/k with 0 ≤ h/k ≤ 1 and 1 ≤ k ≤ n.

nodes.name: Mediant of two fractions
nodes.description: The mediant of a/b and c/d is the fraction (a+c)/(b+d).

nodes.name: Normal number
nodes.description: A real number x is normal in base r if every block of k consecutive digits appears in its base-r expansion with asymptotic frequency r⁻ᵏ.

nodes.name: Simply normal number
nodes.description: A real number x is simply normal in base r if each digit 0, 1, …, r−1 occurs with frequency 1/r in its base-r expansion.

nodes.name: Absolutely normal number
nodes.description: A real number that is normal in every integer base r ≥ 2.

nodes.name: Badly approximable number
nodes.description: An irrational α with inf_{p,q} q²|α − p/q| > 0, equivalently one whose continued fraction partial quotients are bounded.

nodes.name: Durfee square
nodes.description: The side length of the largest square fitting in the upper-left corner of the Ferrers diagram of a partition.

nodes.name: Stern–Brocot tree
nodes.description: The complete infinite binary tree of all positive rationals constructed by iterated mediant insertion between 0/1 and 1/0.

nodes.name: Density of visible lattice points
nodes.description: The number of lattice points (x,y) visible from the origin with |x|,|y| ≤ n is asymptotically 6n²/π², equivalently the probability two random integers are coprime is 6/π².

nodes.name: Fibonacci numbers as convergents of the golden ratio
nodes.description: The convergents of the continued fraction [1; 1, 1, 1, …] for the golden ratio φ = (1+√5)/2 are F_{n+1}/F_n, yielding the slowest-converging simple continued fraction.

nodes.name: Failure of unique factorization in ℤ[√(−5)]
nodes.description: The ring ℤ[√(−5)] is not a UFD: 6 = 2·3 = (1+√(−5))(1−√(−5)) gives two essentially distinct factorizations into irreducibles.

nodes.name: Sharpness of √5 in Hurwitz's theorem
nodes.description: The constant √5 in Hurwitz's approximation theorem is best possible: for α = (1+√5)/2 the inequality |α − p/q| < 1/(cq²) has infinitely many solutions iff c ≤ √5.

nodes.name: Lower bound for g(k) in Waring's problem
nodes.description: g(k) ≥ 2ᵏ + ⌊(3/2)ᵏ⌋ − 2 for all k ≥ 2, attained by integers just below 3ᵏ that require many k-th powers.

nodes.name: Lower bounds for G(k) in Waring's problem
nodes.description: G(k) ≥ k+1 for all k ≥ 2 by counting arguments; G(2ᶿ) ≥ 2ᶿ⁺² for θ ≥ 2 and G(4) ≥ 16 by congruence obstructions.

nodes.name: Farey neighbor property
nodes.description: If h/k and h'/k' are consecutive fractions in the Farey sequence F_n, then k·h' − h·k' = 1.

nodes.name: Farey mediant property
nodes.description: If h/k, h″/k″, h'/k' are three consecutive terms of F_n, then h″ = h + h' and k″ = k + k', i.e., the middle term is the mediant of its neighbors.

nodes.name: Borel's normal number theorem
nodes.description: Almost all real numbers in the sense of Lebesgue measure are absolutely normal.

nodes.name: Kempner series convergence
nodes.description: The sum of 1/n over all positive integers n whose base-10 representation omits a given digit converges.

nodes.name: Lagrange's periodic continued fraction theorem
nodes.description: A real number has an eventually periodic continued fraction expansion if and only if it is a quadratic irrational.

nodes.name: Galois's theorem on purely periodic continued fractions
nodes.description: A continued fraction [a₀; a₁, a₂, …] is purely periodic if and only if it represents a reduced quadratic surd α > 1 whose conjugate α' satisfies −1 < α' < 0.

nodes.name: Leudesdorf's theorem
nodes.description: A generalization of Wolstenholme's theorem giving divisibility conditions on sums of reciprocals of integers coprime to a composite modulus.

nodes.name: Bauer's identical congruence
nodes.description: For prime p, the product ∏_{a=1}^{p−1}(x − a) ≡ x^{p−1} − 1 (mod p) holds as an identity in x.

nodes.name: Kronecker's approximation theorem
nodes.description: If θ is irrational, then the set {nθ mod 1 : n ∈ ℕ} is dense in [0, 1); for any α and ε > 0 there exist integers n, p with |nθ − p − α| < ε.

nodes.name: Kronecker's simultaneous approximation theorem
nodes.description: If θ₁, …, θₖ, 1 are linearly independent over ℚ, then the vectors (nθ₁, …, nθₖ) mod 1 are dense in [0,1)ᵏ.

nodes.name: Classification of Euclidean quadratic fields
nodes.description: The ring of integers of ℚ(√d) is Euclidean under the norm for d ∈ {−11, −7, −3, −2, −1, 2, 3, 5, 6, 7, 11, 13, …}; a finite list for imaginary quadratic fields.

nodes.name: Minkowski's theorem on linear forms
nodes.description: If ξ₁, …, ξₙ are homogeneous linear forms with determinant Δ and λ₁⋯λₙ ≥ |Δ|, then there exist integers x₁, …, xₙ not all zero with |ξᵢ| ≤ λᵢ.

nodes.name: Tchebotaref's theorem on inhomogeneous forms
nodes.description: For homogeneous linear forms ξᵢ with determinant Δ and arbitrary real shifts ρᵢ: inf |(ξ₁−ρ₁)⋯(ξₙ−ρₙ)| ≤ 2⁻ⁿ|Δ| over all integer points.

nodes.name: Quaternion norm descent
nodes.function_signature: (ℍ, prime p) → (a,b,c,d with a²+b²+c²+d² = p)
nodes.description: Use Hurwitz quaternion arithmetic with multiplicative norm to express primes as sums of four squares via descent.

nodes.name: Durfee square decomposition
nodes.function_signature: (Partition λ) → (Durfee square + two sub-partitions)
nodes.description: Decompose a partition at its Durfee square to derive generating function identities relating partitions to q-series.

nodes.name: Franklin's involution
nodes.function_signature: (Partition into distinct parts) → (Partition into distinct parts)
nodes.description: A sign-reversing involution on partitions into distinct parts that bijects even-part and odd-part partitions except at pentagonal numbers, proving Euler's pentagonal theorem.

nodes.name: Lettenmeyer's proof of Kronecker's theorem
nodes.function_signature: (Irrational θ, ε > 0) → (n with {nθ} in target interval)
nodes.description: An elementary geometric proof of Kronecker's approximation theorem by pigeonhole on ε-neighborhoods in the unit torus, extended to k dimensions by induction.

nodes.name: Chord-and-tangent addition on elliptic curves
nodes.function_signature: (E(K), P, Q) → P + Q ∈ E(K)
nodes.description: Given points P, Q on an elliptic curve, draw line PQ (or tangent if P=Q), find the third intersection R with the curve, and reflect to obtain P+Q = −R, defining an abelian group law.

nodes.name: Polygonal number p_m(k)
nodes.description: The k-th m-gonal number p_m(k) = (m−2)·k(k−1)/2 + k, generalizing triangular, square, and pentagonal numbers to arbitrary polygon order m ≥ 3.

nodes.name: Cauchy’s polygonal number theorem
nodes.description: Every positive integer is the sum of at most m m-gonal numbers, of which all but four equal 0 or 1, completing the proof of Fermat’s polygonal number conjecture.

nodes.name: Cauchy’s lemma (polygonal numbers)
nodes.description: If b ≥ 2a and b ≡ a (mod 2), then every integer in the interval [2a + b, 4a + 2b − 2] is a sum a·x₁² + b·x₂² with x₁, x₂ ∈ {0,1}, used in proving the polygonal number theorem.

nodes.name: Pépin’s theorem on five pentagonal numbers
nodes.description: Every sufficiently large positive integer is the sum of at most five pentagonal numbers, sharpening the general polygonal number theorem for m = 5.

nodes.name: Waring’s function g(k)
nodes.description: g(k) is the smallest s such that every positive integer is representable as a sum of at most s perfect k-th powers.

nodes.name: Asymptotic Waring function G(k)
nodes.description: G(k) is the smallest s such that every sufficiently large integer is representable as a sum of s perfect k-th powers.

nodes.name: Wieferich–Kempner theorem (g(3) = 9)
nodes.description: Every positive integer is the sum of at most nine positive cubes, and nine are necessary (for 23 and 239), establishing g(3) = 9.

nodes.name: Linnik’s theorem on sums of seven cubes (G(3) ≤ 7)
nodes.description: Every sufficiently large integer is the sum of at most seven positive cubes, i.e., G(3) ≤ 7, proved by Linnik using an elementary additive method.

nodes.name: Impossibility of representing all integers as sums of few cubes
nodes.description: Integers ≡ ±4 (mod 9) cannot be sums of three cubes, since cubes are congruent to 0 or ±1 modulo 9, giving G(3) ≥ 4.

nodes.name: Ideal Waring conjecture
nodes.description: g(k) = 2^k + ⌊(3/2)^k⌋ − 2 for all k ≥ 1, asserting that the lower bound from numbers just below 2^k is always tight.

nodes.name: Hilbert’s proof via multilinear identities
nodes.function_signature: (k-th power representation goal) → (existence of g(k) via algebraic identities)
nodes.description: Hilbert’s original proof of the Waring–Hilbert theorem using multilinear algebraic identities to reduce higher powers to sums of 2k-th powers, combined with induction on k.

nodes.name: Schur’s trick
nodes.function_signature: (Identity with possibly negative coefficients) → (Identity with non-negative integer coefficients)
nodes.description: Replaces a polynomial identity with possibly negative coefficients by a sum-of-squares identity with non-negative integer coefficients, used to simplify Hilbert’s proof of Waring’s theorem.

nodes.name: Stridsberg’s improvement of Hilbert’s bound
nodes.description: Improved the explicit upper bound on g(k) obtained from Hilbert’s algebraic identity method by optimizing the number of variables in the multilinear identity approach.

nodes.name: Dress’s simplification of Hilbert’s proof
nodes.function_signature: (Hilbert’s multilinear identity proof) → (Simplified elementary proof of Waring–Hilbert theorem)
nodes.description: Streamlined Hilbert’s proof of the Waring theorem by replacing complicated algebraic identity constructions with a cleaner inductive argument.

nodes.name: Hurwitz identity for sums of squares
nodes.description: A composition identity (x₁² + ··· + xₙ²)(y₁² + ··· + yₙ²) = z₁² + ··· + zₙ² with each zᵢ bilinear in x and y, existing only for n = 1, 2, 4, 8.

nodes.name: Weyl’s inequality
nodes.description: If α has a rational approximation a/q with |α − a/q| ≤ q⁻², then |∑_{n≤N} e(αnᵏ)| ≪ N^{1+ε}(q⁻¹ + N⁻¹ + qN⁻ᵏ)^{2^{1−k}}, bounding exponential sums via Diophantine approximation quality.

nodes.name: Hua’s lemma proof by iterative squaring
nodes.function_signature: (Exponential sum S = ∑ e(αnᵏ)) → (Bound on ∫|S|^{2^k} dα via repeated squaring and differencing)
nodes.description: Proves Hua’s inequality by iteratively squaring the exponential sum and applying Weyl differencing at each step, reducing the mean value estimate to counting solutions of a Diophantine system.

nodes.name: Singular series S(n) for Waring’s problem
nodes.description: S(n) = ∑_{q≥1} ∑_{(a,q)=1} q⁻ˢ S(q,a)ˢ e(−an/q), the arithmetic factor in the Hardy–Littlewood asymptotic formula for representations of n as a sum of s k-th powers.

nodes.name: Singular integral J(n) for Waring’s problem
nodes.description: J(n) = ∫(∫₀¹ e(βxᵏ)dx)ˢ e(−βn)dβ, the real-analytic density factor in the Hardy–Littlewood asymptotic formula measuring the volume of the real solution set.

nodes.name: Positivity of the singular series for Waring’s problem
nodes.description: For s sufficiently large relative to k, the singular series S(n) satisfies S(n) ≥ c > 0 for all n, proved by showing local solubility at every prime via Hensel’s lemma.

nodes.name: Complete exponential sum mod q
nodes.description: S(q,a) = ∑_{x=1}^{q} e(axᵏ/q), the complete exponential sum of a k-th power phase over a full residue system modulo q, the local factor in the singular series.

nodes.name: Pruning (circle method)
nodes.function_signature: (Major arcs with wide Diophantine conditions) → (Narrower major arcs with tighter conditions and negligible complement)
nodes.description: Restricts the major arcs to a narrower set where singular series and singular integral approximations are more precise, showing the contribution from the pruned region is negligible.

nodes.name: Local solubility condition for Waring’s problem
nodes.description: For every prime p and every n, the congruence x₁ᵏ + ··· + xₛᵏ ≡ n (mod pʲ) has a solution for all j ≥ 1, ensuring the p-adic singular series factor is positive.

nodes.name: Asymptotic formula for three-prime representations
nodes.description: The number of representations of a large odd N as p₁ + p₂ + p₃ is asymptotic to ½·𝔖(N)·N²/(log N)³, where 𝔖(N) is the singular series for the ternary Goldbach problem.

nodes.name: Major arc approximation for prime exponential sums
nodes.function_signature: (S(α) = ∑ Λ(n)e(nα) on major arc) → (Approximation via Dirichlet characters and L-functions)
nodes.description: On major arcs, approximates the exponential sum over primes by a product of a Ramanujan-type sum and a smooth integral, using the Siegel–Walfisz theorem for primes in arithmetic progressions.

nodes.name: Goldbach exceptional set
nodes.description: E(X) = |{n ≤ X : n even, n ≠ p₁ + p₂}| is the count of even numbers up to X failing binary Goldbach; the best known bound is E(X) ≪ X^{0.879}.

nodes.name: Vinogradov’s bound on G(k)
nodes.description: G(k) ≤ 2k(log k + log log k + O(1)), proved using the circle method with Vinogradov’s mean value theorem, giving the best known general upper bound on the asymptotic Waring function.

nodes.name: Easy Waring problem
nodes.description: The variant of Waring’s problem asking for the minimal s such that almost all positive integers are sums of s k-th powers, where the threshold is lower than G(k).

nodes.name: Segre–Mahler–Wright theorem
nodes.description: Almost all positive integers are sums of O(k log k) perfect k-th powers, giving a density-one result with fewer summands than G(k) requires for all sufficiently large integers.

nodes.name: Efficient differencing (Vinogradov–Wooley)
nodes.function_signature: (Vinogradov mean value integral Jₛ,ₖ(X)) → (Improved bound via iterative differencing with efficient variable usage)
nodes.description: Refines Vinogradov’s mean value method by reusing variables across differencing steps, achieving near-optimal bounds on the mean value integral for exponential sums.

nodes.name: Davenport’s theorem G(4) = 15
nodes.description: Every sufficiently large integer is the sum of at most 15 fourth powers, and 15 is best possible since numbers of the form 16ᵐ·31 require 15 fourth powers.

nodes.name: G(2) = 4
nodes.description: Every sufficiently large integer is the sum of at most four squares, and four is necessary since integers of the form 4ᵃ(8b+7) require four squares.

nodes.name: Wooley’s refinement of Vinogradov’s mean value theorem
nodes.description: Establishes the main conjecture for Vinogradov’s mean value theorem: Jₛ,ₖ(X) ≪ X^{s+ε} + X^{2s−k(k+1)/2+ε} for all s, k, via efficient congruencing or decoupling.

nodes.name: Asymptotic basis of order h
nodes.description: A set A ⊆ ℕ₀ is an asymptotic basis of order h if every sufficiently large positive integer is representable as a sum of at most h elements of A.

nodes.name: Schnirelmann’s theorem (primes form an additive basis)
nodes.description: The set of primes together with {0, 1} is an additive basis of finite order: there exists h such that every integer ≥ 2 is a sum of at most h primes.

nodes.name: Schnirelmann’s inequality
nodes.description: σ(A + B) ≥ σ(A) + σ(B) − σ(A)σ(B) for sets A, B ⊆ ℕ₀ with 0 ∈ A ∩ B, where σ denotes Schnirelmann density.

nodes.name: Mann’s theorem
nodes.description: σ(A + B) ≥ min(1, σ(A) + σ(B)) for sets A, B ⊆ ℕ₀ with 0 ∈ A ∩ B, strengthening Schnirelmann’s inequality to a sharp lower bound on sumset density.

nodes.name: Khinchin’s addition theorem
nodes.description: If A is an asymptotic basis of order h and B has positive Schnirelmann density, then A + B is an asymptotic basis of order at most h.

nodes.name: Essential component
nodes.description: A set B ⊆ ℕ₀ is an essential component if σ(A + B) > σ(A) for every set A with 0 < σ(A) < 1, meaning B always increases Schnirelmann density.

nodes.name: Primes are an essential component
nodes.description: The set of primes (with 0 and 1 adjoined) is an essential component: for any A ⊆ ℕ₀ with 0 < σ(A) < 1, we have σ(A + P) > σ(A).

nodes.name: Khinchin’s theorem on essential components
nodes.description: Every asymptotic basis of finite order is an essential component, providing a sufficient condition for a set to increase the Schnirelmann density of any incomplete set.

nodes.name: Erdős’s theorem on essential components
nodes.description: If ∑_{n=1}^∞ B(n)/n² = ∞ where B(n) = |B ∩ [1,n]|, then B is an essential component, giving a counting-function criterion weaker than being an asymptotic basis.

nodes.name: Mann’s proof via sequential addition
nodes.function_signature: (Sets A, B with Schnirelmann densities) → (Proof that σ(A+B) ≥ min(1, σ(A)+σ(B)))
nodes.description: Proves Mann’s theorem by constructing the sumset incrementally, adding one element of B at a time and tracking how each addition increases the counting function.

nodes.name: Selberg sieve applied to Goldbach
nodes.description: Applying the Selberg upper-bound sieve to binary Goldbach yields that representations of even n as p + p’ number ≪ n·∏_{p|n}(1+1/p)/(log n)².

nodes.name: Romanov’s theorem
nodes.description: A positive proportion of positive integers can be represented as p + 2ᵏ for some prime p and non-negative integer k.

nodes.name: Dickson–Pillai theorem on g(k)
nodes.description: g(k) = 2ᵏ + ⌊(3/2)ᵏ⌋ − 2 provided 2ᵏ{(3/2)ᵏ} + ⌊(3/2)ᵏ⌋ ≤ 2ᵏ, reducing the ideal Waring conjecture to a condition on fractional parts of powers of 3/2.

nodes.name: Balasubramanian–Deshouillers–Dress theorem (g(4) = 19)
nodes.description: Every positive integer is the sum of at most 19 fourth powers, establishing g(4) = 19 via a combination of computational verification and analytic methods.

nodes.name: Euler product for the singular series
nodes.description: The singular series factors as S(n) = ∏_p σ_p(n), expressing the global arithmetic factor as a product of local p-adic densities for Waring representations.

nodes.name: Hua’s theorem on sums of cubes of primes
nodes.description: Every sufficiently large odd integer is the sum of nine cubes of primes, establishing a Waring–Goldbach result for cubes using the circle method.

nodes.name: Waring’s problem for primes (Waring–Goldbach problem)
nodes.description: The problem of determining the smallest s such that every sufficiently large integer satisfying necessary congruence conditions is the sum of s k-th powers of primes.

nodes.name: Davenport–Heilbronn method
nodes.function_signature: (Diophantine inequality with irrational coefficients) → (Asymptotic count via modified circle method)
nodes.description: Adapts the circle method to Diophantine inequalities rather than equations by exploiting irrationality of coefficients to avoid a singular series.

nodes.name: Representation function for polygonal numbers
nodes.description: r_{m,s}(n) counts the number of ways to write n as a sum of s m-gonal numbers, the fundamental counting function in the additive theory of figurate numbers.

nodes.name: Representation function r_{s,k}(n)
nodes.description: r_{s,k}(n) = |{(x₁,…,xₛ) ∈ ℕ₀ˢ : x₁ᵏ + ··· + xₛᵏ = n}| counts representations of n as a sum of s non-negative k-th powers.

nodes.name: Liouville’s identity (sums of squares)
nodes.description: Liouville’s identity expressing r₄(n) = 8∑_{d|n, 4∤d} d, giving an exact divisor-sum formula for the number of representations as a sum of four squares.

nodes.name: Connection between quadratic forms and sums of squares
nodes.description: The representability of integers as sums of k squares is equivalent to representation by the standard positive-definite quadratic form of rank k, linking Waring-type questions to genera and class numbers.

nodes.name: h-fold sumset hA
nodes.description: For A ⊆ ℕ₀ and h ≥ 1, the h-fold sumset hA = {a₁ + ··· + aₕ : aᵢ ∈ A} is the set of all sums of exactly h elements of A with repetition.

nodes.name: h-fold representation function r_{A,h}(n)
nodes.description: r_{A,h}(n) = |{(a₁,…,aₕ) ∈ Aʰ : a₁ + ··· + aₕ = n}| counts ordered representations of n as a sum of h elements from A.

nodes.name: Counting function A(n)
nodes.description: A(n) = |A ∩ [0,n]| for A ⊆ ℕ₀, the counting function measuring elements of A up to n, fundamental to Schnirelmann and asymptotic density.

nodes.name: Schnirelmann’s original density argument
nodes.function_signature: (Set A with σ(A) > 0) → (A is additive basis of finite order)
nodes.description: Schnirelmann’s proof that positive Schnirelmann density implies basis property, using iterated sumset density inequalities to show σ(hA) → 1 as h increases.

nodes.name: Generating function for Waring’s problem
nodes.description: f(α) = ∑_{m=0}^{N^{1/k}} e(αmᵏ), the exponential generating function whose s-th power’s Fourier coefficients equal the Waring representation function r_{s,k}(n).

nodes.name: p-adic solubility for Waring’s problem
nodes.description: The equation x₁ᵏ + ··· + xₛᵏ = n has a non-trivial solution in ℤ_p for every prime p, equivalent to positivity of the local factor σ_p(n) in the singular series.

nodes.name: Minor arc estimate for Waring’s problem
nodes.description: ∫_{𝔪} |f(α)|ˢ e(−nα)dα = o(n^{s/k−1}) for s sufficiently large, showing the minor arc contribution is negligible compared to the main term.

nodes.name: Minor arc estimate for the three-primes problem
nodes.description: sup_{α ∈ 𝔪} |S(α)| ≪ N/(log N)^A for any A > 0 on the minor arcs, where S(α) = ∑_{n≤N} Λ(n)e(nα), by Vinogradov’s method.

nodes.name: Major arc contribution for Waring’s problem
nodes.description: ∫_{𝔐} f(α)ˢ e(−nα)dα = S(n)·J(n)·n^{s/k−1} + o(n^{s/k−1}), expressing the major arc integral as the product of singular series and singular integral.

nodes.name: Four cubes impossibility modulo 9
nodes.description: Integers ≡ ±4 (mod 9) cannot be represented as sums of three cubes, since cubes are ≡ 0, ±1 (mod 9), constraining local solubility of sums of few cubes.

nodes.name: 23 and 239 require nine cubes
nodes.description: The integers 23 and 239 are the only positive integers requiring exactly nine positive cubes for their representation, establishing that g(3) = 9 is tight.

nodes.name: Descent method for four squares
nodes.function_signature: (mp = x₁² + x₂² + x₃² + x₄² with m > 1) → (p = y₁² + y₂² + y₃² + y₄² by iterative reduction)
nodes.description: Proves Lagrange’s four-square theorem by showing that if mp is a sum of four squares with m > 1, then m can be reduced, iterating until m = 1.

nodes.name: Linnik’s elementary method for sums of cubes
nodes.function_signature: (Large integer n) → (Representation as sum of 7 cubes via combinatorial and p-adic estimates)
nodes.description: An elementary approach avoiding the full circle method, using combinatorial arguments and local density estimates to prove G(3) ≤ 7.

nodes.name: Subgroup
nodes.description: A subset of a group that is itself a group under the inherited operation.

nodes.name: Normal subgroup
nodes.description: A subgroup N of G such that gNg⁻¹ = N for all g in G.

nodes.name: Quotient group
nodes.description: The group G/N of cosets of a normal subgroup N in G, with multiplication induced from G.

nodes.name: Index of a subgroup
nodes.description: The number of left (or right) cosets of a subgroup H in G, denoted [G:H].

nodes.name: Center of a group
nodes.description: The set Z(G) = {z ∈ G : zg = gz for all g ∈ G} of elements that commute with every element of G.

nodes.name: Centralizer
nodes.description: The subgroup C_G(S) of elements of G that commute with every element of a subset S.

nodes.name: Normalizer
nodes.description: The subgroup N_G(H) = {g ∈ G : gHg⁻¹ = H} of elements that normalize a subgroup H.

nodes.name: Commutator subgroup
nodes.description: The subgroup [G,G] generated by all commutators [x,y] = xyx⁻¹y⁻¹, also called the derived subgroup.

nodes.name: p-group
nodes.description: A group in which every element has order a power of the prime p.

nodes.name: Sylow p-subgroup
nodes.description: A maximal p-subgroup of a finite group G, having order p^a where p^a divides |G| but p^(a+1) does not.

nodes.name: Group presentation
nodes.description: A description of a group as a quotient of a free group by a normal subgroup generated by specified relations.

nodes.name: Orbit of a group action
nodes.description: The set Orb(x) = {g·x : g ∈ G} of all images of an element x under a group action.

nodes.name: Stabilizer of a group action
nodes.description: The subgroup Stab(x) = {g ∈ G : g·x = x} of elements fixing a point x under a group action.

nodes.name: Conjugacy class
nodes.description: The orbit of an element under the conjugation action, i.e., the set {gxg⁻¹ : g ∈ G}.

nodes.name: Exponent of a group
nodes.description: The least common multiple of the orders of all elements of a group, or infinity if no such finite number exists.

nodes.name: Lower central series
nodes.description: The descending series G = γ₁(G) ⊇ γ₂(G) ⊇ ··· where γᵢ₊₁(G) = [γᵢ(G), G].

nodes.name: Upper central series
nodes.description: The ascending series 1 = Z₀(G) ≤ Z₁(G) ≤ ··· where Zᵢ₊₁(G)/Zᵢ(G) = Z(G/Zᵢ(G)).

nodes.name: Fitting subgroup
nodes.description: The unique largest nilpotent normal subgroup F(G) of a finite group G, generated by all nilpotent normal subgroups.

nodes.name: Socle of a group
nodes.description: The subgroup generated by all minimal normal subgroups of a group G.

nodes.name: Automorphism group of a group
nodes.description: The group Aut(G) of all group automorphisms of G under composition.

nodes.name: Inner automorphism group
nodes.description: The normal subgroup Inn(G) of Aut(G) consisting of conjugation maps x ↦ gxg⁻¹ for g ∈ G.

nodes.name: Outer automorphism group
nodes.description: The quotient group Out(G) = Aut(G)/Inn(G) measuring automorphisms not arising from conjugation.

nodes.name: Lagrange's theorem (group theory)
nodes.description: The order of a subgroup H of a finite group G divides the order of G, with |G| = [G:H]·|H|.

nodes.name: Second isomorphism theorem for groups
nodes.description: If H ≤ G and N ⊴ G then HN/N ≅ H/(H ∩ N).

nodes.name: Third isomorphism theorem for groups
nodes.description: If N ⊆ M are normal subgroups of G then (G/N)/(M/N) ≅ G/M.

nodes.name: Lattice isomorphism theorem for groups
nodes.description: Subgroups of G/N correspond bijectively with subgroups of G containing N, preserving normality and index.

nodes.name: Sylow's first theorem
nodes.description: If p^a divides the order of a finite group G, then G has a subgroup of order p^a; in particular, Sylow p-subgroups exist.

nodes.name: Sylow's second theorem
nodes.description: All Sylow p-subgroups of a finite group G are conjugate to each other.

nodes.name: Sylow's third theorem
nodes.description: The number n_p of Sylow p-subgroups of a finite group G satisfies n_p ≡ 1 (mod p) and n_p divides |G|.

nodes.name: Fitting's theorem on Fitting subgroup
nodes.description: The Fitting subgroup of a finite group G is nilpotent and contains every nilpotent normal subgroup of G.

nodes.name: Sylow theory argument
nodes.description: Using the Sylow theorems to constrain the structure of finite groups by analyzing numbers and conjugacy of p-subgroups.
nodes.function_signature: (Finite group G, prime p) → (Structural constraints on G)

nodes.name: Counting via group actions
nodes.description: Applying the orbit-stabilizer theorem or Burnside's lemma to enumeration problems by identifying the relevant group action.
nodes.function_signature: (Group action G × S → S) → (Orbit count or size)

nodes.name: Composition series analysis
nodes.description: Analyzing a group by examining its composition series and composition factors, using the Jordan-Hölder theorem to extract structural invariants.
nodes.function_signature: (Group with composition series) → (Multiset of simple composition factors)

nodes.name: Ideal (of a ring)
nodes.description: A two-sided ideal I of a ring R is an additive subgroup such that ra ∈ I and ar ∈ I for all r ∈ R, a ∈ I.

nodes.name: Quotient ring
nodes.description: The ring R/I of cosets of a two-sided ideal I, with operations induced from R.

nodes.name: Nilpotent element
nodes.description: An element a of a ring R such that a^n = 0 for some positive integer n.

nodes.name: Nilradical of a ring
nodes.description: The ideal nil(R) of all nilpotent elements in a commutative ring R, equal to the intersection of all prime ideals.

nodes.name: Jacobson radical of a ring
nodes.description: The ideal J(R) equal to the intersection of all maximal ideals (or all maximal left ideals) of a ring R.

nodes.name: Fraction field
nodes.description: The field of fractions Frac(R) of an integral domain R, obtained by localizing at the multiplicative set R \ {0}.

nodes.name: Group of units
nodes.description: The group R× = R* of invertible elements of a ring R under multiplication.

nodes.name: First isomorphism theorem for rings
nodes.description: If f: R → S is a ring homomorphism then R/ker(f) ≅ im(f) as rings.

nodes.name: Every maximal ideal is prime
nodes.description: In a commutative ring with unity, every maximal ideal is a prime ideal.

nodes.name: Every PID is a UFD
nodes.description: Every principal ideal domain is a unique factorization domain.

nodes.name: Euclidean domain is a PID
nodes.description: Every Euclidean domain is a principal ideal domain.

nodes.name: Zorn's lemma implies maximal ideals exist
nodes.description: Every nonzero ring with unity contains at least one maximal ideal, proved using Zorn's lemma.

nodes.name: Nilradical equals intersection of primes
nodes.description: The nilradical of a commutative ring equals the intersection of all its prime ideals.

nodes.name: Gauss's lemma (content of polynomials)
nodes.description: The product of two primitive polynomials over a UFD is primitive; equivalently, the content is multiplicative.

nodes.name: Eisenstein's irreducibility criterion
nodes.description: A polynomial f(x) = aₙxⁿ + ··· + a₀ over a UFD is irreducible if a prime p divides a₀,...,aₙ₋₁ but not aₙ, and p² does not divide a₀.

nodes.name: Polynomial ring over UFD is UFD
nodes.description: If R is a unique factorization domain, then the polynomial ring R[x] is also a unique factorization domain.

nodes.name: Module over a ring
nodes.description: An abelian group M with a scalar multiplication R × M → M satisfying associativity, distributivity, and unital conditions with respect to a ring R.

nodes.name: Submodule
nodes.description: A subset N of an R-module M that is itself an R-module under the inherited operations.

nodes.name: Quotient module
nodes.description: The R-module M/N of cosets of a submodule N, with operations induced from M.

nodes.name: Projective module
nodes.description: An R-module P such that every surjection onto P splits, equivalently a direct summand of a free module.

nodes.name: Exact sequence
nodes.description: A sequence of module homomorphisms ··· → Mᵢ₋₁ → Mᵢ → Mᵢ₊₁ → ··· where the image of each map equals the kernel of the next.

nodes.name: Short exact sequence
