nodes.description: An exact sequence 0 → A → B → C → 0, equivalently A embeds in B with quotient C.

nodes.name: Length of a module
nodes.description: The length ℓ(M) of a composition series of a module M, well-defined by the Jordan-Hölder theorem; finite iff M is both Noetherian and Artinian.

nodes.name: Bimodule
nodes.description: An abelian group M that is simultaneously a left R-module and a right S-module with compatible actions: (rm)s = r(ms).

nodes.name: Cokernel of a module homomorphism
nodes.description: The quotient module coker(f) = N/im(f) for a homomorphism f: M → N.

nodes.name: Structure theorem for modules over a PID
nodes.description: Every finitely generated module over a PID is isomorphic to a direct sum of cyclic modules R/(d₁) ⊕ ··· ⊕ R/(dₖ) ⊕ Rʳ with d₁|d₂|···|dₖ.

nodes.name: Characterization of projective modules
nodes.description: An R-module P is projective if and only if P is a direct summand of a free module, if and only if every short exact sequence ending in P splits.

nodes.name: Baer's criterion for injectivity
nodes.description: An R-module Q is injective if and only if every homomorphism from an ideal of R to Q extends to a homomorphism from R to Q.

nodes.name: Every module embeds in an injective module
nodes.description: For any ring R and any R-module M, there exists an injective R-module containing M as a submodule.

nodes.name: Schanuel's lemma
nodes.description: If 0 → K₁ → P₁ → M → 0 and 0 → K₂ → P₂ → M → 0 with P₁, P₂ projective, then K₁ ⊕ P₂ ≅ K₂ ⊕ P₁.

nodes.name: Eilenberg swindle
nodes.description: Over a ring with infinite direct sums, every projective module is a direct summand of a free module by the trick P ⊕ P^∞ ≅ P^∞.

nodes.name: Jordan-Hölder theorem for modules
nodes.description: Any two composition series of a module have the same length and isomorphic composition factors up to permutation.

nodes.name: Localization of modules
nodes.description: Extending scalars of a module M to S⁻¹R to study local properties, using the exact functor S⁻¹(−).
nodes.function_signature: (R-module M, multiplicative set S) → (S⁻¹R-module S⁻¹M)

nodes.name: Diagram chasing
nodes.description: Proving exactness or isomorphism properties in commutative diagrams by systematically tracking elements through the maps.
nodes.function_signature: (Commutative diagram of exact sequences) → (Exactness or isomorphism conclusion)

nodes.name: Nakayama's lemma argument
nodes.description: Applying Nakayama's lemma to conclude that a module or ideal vanishes, or that generators lift from a quotient.
nodes.function_signature: (Finitely generated module over local ring, 𝔪M = M) → (M = 0)

nodes.name: Content of a polynomial
nodes.description: The greatest common divisor c(f) of the coefficients of a polynomial f over a UFD.

nodes.name: Primitive polynomial
nodes.description: A polynomial over a UFD whose content is a unit.

nodes.name: Symmetric polynomial
nodes.description: A polynomial f(x₁,...,xₙ) invariant under all permutations of the variables.

nodes.name: Power sum symmetric polynomials
nodes.description: The symmetric polynomials pₖ(x₁,...,xₙ) = x₁ᵏ + ··· + xₙᵏ for positive integers k.

nodes.name: Resultant of two polynomials
nodes.description: The determinant Res(f,g) of the Sylvester matrix of polynomials f and g, vanishing iff f and g share a common root.

nodes.name: Discriminant of a polynomial
nodes.description: The quantity Δ(f) = (−1)^{n(n−1)/2} Res(f,f')/aₙ for a polynomial f of degree n, measuring separation of roots.

nodes.name: Newton's identities
nodes.description: Recursive relations connecting power sum symmetric polynomials pₖ to elementary symmetric polynomials eₖ: kEₖ = Σᵢ₌₁ᵏ (−1)ⁱ⁻¹pᵢeₖ₋ᵢ.

nodes.name: Minimal polynomial
nodes.description: The unique monic polynomial of smallest degree in K[x] having α as a root, generating the kernel of the evaluation map K[x] → K(α).

nodes.name: Algebraic extension
nodes.description: A field extension L/K in which every element of L is algebraic over K.

nodes.name: Separable extension
nodes.description: An algebraic extension L/K in which the minimal polynomial of every element of L over K is separable.

nodes.name: Purely inseparable extension
nodes.description: An algebraic extension L/K in characteristic p where every element α satisfies α^{p^n} ∈ K for some n.

nodes.name: Separable degree
nodes.description: The number [L:K]_s of K-embeddings of L into an algebraic closure, equals [L:K] when the extension is separable.

nodes.name: Inseparable degree
nodes.description: The quotient [L:K]_i = [L:K]/[L:K]_s, always a power of the characteristic.

nodes.name: Finite field
nodes.description: A field with finitely many elements; for each prime power q = pⁿ there exists a unique finite field 𝔽_q up to isomorphism.

nodes.name: Existence and uniqueness of finite fields
nodes.description: For each prime power q = pⁿ there exists a unique (up to isomorphism) field with q elements, namely the splitting field of x^q − x over 𝔽_p.

nodes.name: Frobenius generates Galois group of finite field
nodes.description: The Galois group Gal(𝔽_{pⁿ}/𝔽_p) is cyclic of order n, generated by the Frobenius automorphism x ↦ xᵖ.

nodes.name: Galois extension
nodes.description: A finite field extension L/K that is both normal and separable, equivalently |Aut(L/K)| = [L:K].

nodes.name: Fixed field
nodes.description: The subfield L^H = {x ∈ L : σ(x) = x for all σ ∈ H} of elements fixed by a subgroup H of Aut(L/K).

nodes.name: Radical extension
nodes.description: A field extension obtained by successive adjunction of n-th roots: K = K₀ ⊂ K₁ ⊂ ··· ⊂ Kₘ with Kᵢ₊₁ = Kᵢ(αᵢ^{1/nᵢ}).

nodes.name: Krull topology
nodes.description: The profinite topology on the Galois group of an infinite Galois extension, making it a compact totally disconnected topological group.

nodes.name: Artin's lemma on fixed fields
nodes.description: If G is a finite group of automorphisms of a field L, then [L:L^G] = |G| and L/L^G is a Galois extension with Galois group G.

nodes.name: Dedekind's independence of characters
nodes.description: Distinct characters (group homomorphisms to a field's multiplicative group) are linearly independent over that field.

nodes.name: Hilbert's Theorem 90 (additive form)
nodes.description: For a cyclic Galois extension L/K with generator σ, an element a ∈ L has trace 0 if and only if a = b − σ(b) for some b ∈ L.

nodes.name: Kummer theory classification
nodes.description: If K contains a primitive n-th root of unity, abelian extensions of K with exponent dividing n correspond bijectively to subgroups of K×/(K×)ⁿ via L ↦ L× ∩ K×/(K×)ⁿ.

nodes.name: Solvability by radicals criterion
nodes.description: A polynomial f ∈ K[x] is solvable by radicals if and only if its Galois group over K is a solvable group (assuming char(K) = 0).

nodes.name: Infinite Galois correspondence
nodes.description: For an infinite Galois extension L/K, closed subgroups of Gal(L/K) in the Krull topology correspond bijectively with intermediate fields.

nodes.name: Galois correspondence method
nodes.description: Using the bijection between subgroups of the Galois group and intermediate fields to translate group-theoretic properties into field-theoretic ones and vice versa.
nodes.function_signature: (Galois extension L/K) → (Lattice of intermediate fields via subgroup lattice)

nodes.name: Kummer theory technique
nodes.description: Classifying abelian extensions by adjoining n-th roots when n-th roots of unity are available, reducing field extension problems to multiplicative group computations.
nodes.function_signature: (Field K with μₙ, subgroup of K×/(K×)ⁿ) → (Abelian extension of exponent n)

nodes.name: Radical extension analysis
nodes.description: Determining solvability of polynomial equations by analyzing whether the Galois group admits a composition series with cyclic factors.
nodes.function_signature: (Polynomial f over K) → (Solvability by radicals or obstruction)

nodes.name: Integral element over a ring
nodes.description: An element α in a ring extension S/R that satisfies a monic polynomial equation αⁿ + rₙ₋₁αⁿ⁻¹ + ··· + r₀ = 0 with coefficients in R.

nodes.name: Integrally closed domain
nodes.description: An integral domain R that equals its own integral closure in its fraction field.

nodes.name: Noetherian ring
nodes.description: A ring satisfying the ascending chain condition on ideals, equivalently every ideal is finitely generated.

nodes.name: Jacobson ring
nodes.description: A ring in which every prime ideal is an intersection of maximal ideals.

nodes.name: Integrality is transitive
nodes.description: If S is integral over R and T is integral over S, then T is integral over R.

nodes.name: Incomparability theorem
nodes.description: If R ⊆ S is integral and 𝔮₁ ⊊ 𝔮₂ are primes of S lying over the same prime of R, this is impossible: distinct primes over the same prime are incomparable.

nodes.name: Hilbert's Nullstellensatz (weak form)
nodes.description: Every maximal ideal of k[x₁,...,xₙ] over an algebraically closed field k has the form (x₁ − a₁,...,xₙ − aₙ) for some aᵢ ∈ k.

nodes.name: Hilbert's Nullstellensatz (strong form)
nodes.description: For an ideal I in k[x₁,...,xₙ] over an algebraically closed field k, the ideal of functions vanishing on V(I) equals the radical: I(V(I)) = √I.

nodes.name: Fractional ideals of Dedekind domains are invertible
nodes.description: Every nonzero fractional ideal of a Dedekind domain is invertible: I · I⁻¹ = R.

nodes.name: Krull's intersection theorem
nodes.description: In a Noetherian local ring (R, 𝔪), the intersection ∩ₙ 𝔪ⁿ = 0.

nodes.name: Going-up/going-down method
nodes.description: Using the going-up and going-down theorems to lift or descend chains of prime ideals through integral extensions.
nodes.function_signature: (Integral extension R ⊆ S, prime chain in R) → (Compatible prime chain in S)

nodes.name: Noether normalization technique
nodes.description: Applying Noether normalization to reduce questions about finitely generated algebras to questions about polynomial rings.
nodes.function_signature: (Finitely generated k-algebra A) → (Polynomial subring k[y₁,...,y_d] with A integral over it)

nodes.name: Algebraic independence
nodes.description: Elements α₁,...,αₙ in an extension L/K are algebraically independent if no nonzero polynomial in K[x₁,...,xₙ] vanishes at (α₁,...,αₙ).

nodes.name: Purely transcendental extension
nodes.description: A field extension L/K isomorphic to K(x₁,...,xₙ) or K({xᵢ}_{i∈I}) for a set of algebraically independent indeterminates.

nodes.name: Linearly disjoint extensions
nodes.description: Field extensions L₁/K and L₂/K inside a common overfield are linearly disjoint if the natural map L₁ ⊗_K L₂ → L₁L₂ is injective.

nodes.name: Separably generated extension
nodes.description: A finitely generated field extension L/K admitting a separating transcendence basis {t₁,...,tᵣ} such that L is separable algebraic over K(t₁,...,tᵣ).

nodes.name: Module of Kähler differentials
nodes.description: The A-module Ω_{A/R} representing derivations from A to A-modules, universal among R-derivations of A.

nodes.name: Derivation on an algebra
nodes.description: An R-linear map D: A → M satisfying the Leibniz rule D(ab) = aD(b) + bD(a).

nodes.name: Transcendence degree is well-defined
nodes.description: Any two transcendence bases of a field extension L/K have the same cardinality.

nodes.name: Lüroth's theorem
nodes.description: Every intermediate field K ⊊ E ⊆ K(t) of a purely transcendental extension of transcendence degree 1 is itself purely transcendental: E = K(u) for some u.

nodes.name: Mac Lane's separability criterion
nodes.description: A finitely generated extension L/K in characteristic p is separably generated if and only if L and K^{1/p} are linearly disjoint over K.

nodes.name: First exact sequence of Kähler differentials
nodes.description: For ring maps R → A → B, there is an exact sequence B ⊗_A Ω_{A/R} → Ω_{B/R} → Ω_{B/A} → 0.

nodes.name: Second exact sequence of Kähler differentials
nodes.description: For an ideal I with A = R/I, there is an exact sequence I/I² → A ⊗_R Ω_{R/K} → Ω_{A/K} → 0 (conormal sequence).

nodes.name: Affine algebraic set
nodes.description: The set V(I) = {a ∈ kⁿ : f(a) = 0 for all f ∈ I} of common zeros of an ideal I ⊆ k[x₁,...,xₙ].

nodes.name: Coordinate ring of an algebraic set
nodes.description: The quotient ring k[V] = k[x₁,...,xₙ]/I(V) of polynomial functions on an algebraic set V.

nodes.name: Irreducible algebraic set
nodes.description: An algebraic set that cannot be expressed as a union of two proper algebraic subsets.

nodes.name: Function field of a variety
nodes.description: The field of fractions of the coordinate ring of an irreducible variety, representing rational functions on the variety.

nodes.name: Nullstellensatz correspondence
nodes.description: Over an algebraically closed field k, there is an inclusion-reversing bijection between radical ideals of k[x₁,...,xₙ] and algebraic subsets of kⁿ.

nodes.name: Dimension equals transcendence degree
nodes.description: The Krull dimension of the coordinate ring of an irreducible variety equals the transcendence degree of its function field over the base field.

nodes.name: Reduced trace
nodes.description: For a central simple algebra A over K, the trace Trd: A → K induced from the matrix trace after splitting.

nodes.name: Reduced norm
nodes.description: For a central simple algebra A over K, the norm Nrd: A → K induced from the matrix determinant after splitting.

nodes.name: Index of a central simple algebra
nodes.description: The degree of the unique division algebra D Brauer-equivalent to a central simple algebra A, denoted ind(A) = √(dim_K D).

nodes.name: Tensor product of central simple algebras
nodes.description: If A and B are central simple algebras over K, then A ⊗_K B is central simple over K.

nodes.name: Brauer group is torsion
nodes.description: Every element of the Brauer group Br(K) has finite order, and the order equals the index.

nodes.name: Representation of a group
nodes.description: A group homomorphism ρ: G → GL(V) from a group G to the general linear group of a vector space V over a field k.

nodes.name: Mackey decomposition formula
nodes.description: For subgroups H, K ≤ G and an H-module V: Res_K Ind_H^G V ≅ ⊕_{g∈K\G/H} Ind_{K∩gHg⁻¹}^K (gV), where the sum is over double coset representatives.

nodes.name: Mackey irreducibility criterion
nodes.description: An induced representation Ind_H^G V is irreducible if and only if V is irreducible and for every g ∉ H, the representations V and gV have no common irreducible constituent when restricted to H ∩ gHg⁻¹.

nodes.name: Character table computation
nodes.description: Systematically computing the character table of a finite group using orthogonality relations, induction, and restriction.
nodes.function_signature: (Finite group G) → (Character table of G)

nodes.name: Frobenius reciprocity method
nodes.description: Using Frobenius reciprocity to decompose induced representations or compute intertwining numbers between representations.
nodes.function_signature: (H-module V, G-module W) → (Multiplicity of W in Ind V, or V in Res W)

nodes.name: General linear group
nodes.description: The group GL_n(K) of n×n invertible matrices over a field K, or equivalently the automorphism group of K^n.

nodes.name: Special linear group
nodes.description: The normal subgroup SL_n(K) = ker(det: GL_n(K) → K×) of matrices with determinant 1.

nodes.name: Orthogonal group
nodes.description: The group O(V,q) = {g ∈ GL(V) : q(gv) = q(v) for all v} of isometries of a quadratic form.

nodes.name: Unitary group
nodes.description: The group U(V,h) of linear transformations preserving a non-degenerate hermitian form h.

nodes.name: Parabolic subgroup
nodes.description: A subgroup of a linear algebraic group containing a Borel subgroup.

nodes.name: Elementary matrix
nodes.description: A matrix differing from the identity by a single off-diagonal entry: Eᵢⱼ(a) = I + aeᵢⱼ for i ≠ j.

nodes.name: SL_n generated by elementary matrices
nodes.description: For any field K and n ≥ 2, the special linear group SL_n(K) is generated by elementary matrices.

nodes.name: PSL_2(F_q) is simple
nodes.description: The projective special linear group PSL_2(𝔽_q) is simple for all prime powers q ≥ 4.

nodes.name: Bilinear form
nodes.description: A map B: V × V → K that is linear in each variable, which may be symmetric, alternating, or hermitian.

nodes.name: Quadratic form
nodes.description: A map Q: V → K with Q(av) = a²Q(v) such that the associated bilinear form B(x,y) = Q(x+y) − Q(x) − Q(y) is bilinear.

nodes.name: Non-degenerate bilinear form
nodes.description: A bilinear form B on V such that the map V → V* given by v ↦ B(v,−) is an isomorphism.

nodes.name: Hyperbolic plane
nodes.description: A two-dimensional vector space with a non-degenerate symmetric bilinear form represented by the matrix (0 1; 1 0).

nodes.name: Anisotropic form
nodes.description: A quadratic form Q such that Q(v) = 0 implies v = 0.

nodes.name: Witt index
nodes.description: The maximum dimension of a totally isotropic subspace of a quadratic space (V, Q).

nodes.name: Witt ring
nodes.description: The ring structure on W(K) with tensor product of quadratic forms as multiplication.

nodes.name: Even Clifford algebra
nodes.description: The subalgebra Cl⁰(V,Q) of elements of even degree in the Clifford algebra, a central simple or product of central simple algebras.

nodes.name: Pfaffian
nodes.description: For an alternating matrix A of even size 2n, the polynomial Pf(A) satisfying Pf(A)² = det(A).

nodes.name: Witt's cancellation theorem
nodes.description: If (V₁, Q₁) ⊥ (W, Q) ≅ (V₂, Q₂) ⊥ (W, Q) as quadratic spaces, then (V₁, Q₁) ≅ (V₂, Q₂).

nodes.name: Witt decomposition theorem
nodes.description: Every quadratic space decomposes as an orthogonal sum of an anisotropic space and a number of hyperbolic planes: (V,Q) ≅ V_an ⊥ ℍʳ.

nodes.name: Sylvester's law of inertia
nodes.description: A real symmetric bilinear form is classified up to congruence by its signature (p, q), the numbers of positive and negative diagonal entries after diagonalization.

nodes.name: Structure of Clifford algebras
nodes.description: The Clifford algebra Cl(V,Q) is central simple when dim V is odd, and a product of two central simple algebras when dim V is even.

nodes.name: Every alternating form has even rank
nodes.description: A non-degenerate alternating bilinear form exists only on even-dimensional spaces; every alternating form has even rank.

nodes.name: Minimal polynomial of a linear map
nodes.description: The unique monic polynomial m_A(t) of lowest degree satisfying m_A(A) = 0.

nodes.name: Adjoint functor pair
nodes.description: Functors F: C → D and G: D → C with a natural bijection Hom_D(FX, Y) ≅ Hom_C(X, GY).

nodes.name: Representable functor
nodes.description: A functor naturally isomorphic to Hom(A, −) (covariant) or Hom(−, A) (contravariant) for some object A.

nodes.name: Additive category
nodes.description: A category enriched over abelian groups: Hom sets are abelian groups, composition is bilinear, and finite products and coproducts exist and coincide.

nodes.name: Product of objects in a category
nodes.description: An object ∏Xᵢ with projection morphisms satisfying the universal property: morphisms to ∏Xᵢ correspond to families of morphisms to each Xᵢ.

nodes.name: Coproduct of objects in a category
nodes.description: An object ∐Xᵢ with injection morphisms satisfying the universal property: morphisms from ∐Xᵢ correspond to families from each Xᵢ.

nodes.name: Direct limit (filtered colimit)
nodes.description: The colimit of a directed system of objects and morphisms in a category.

nodes.name: Inverse limit
nodes.description: The limit of an inverse system of objects and morphisms in a category.

nodes.name: Left exact functor
nodes.description: An additive functor preserving left-exact sequences: if 0 → A → B → C is exact then 0 → F(A) → F(B) → F(C) is exact.

nodes.name: Right exact functor
nodes.description: An additive functor preserving right-exact sequences: if A → B → C → 0 is exact then F(A) → F(B) → F(C) → 0 is exact.

nodes.name: Exact functor
nodes.description: A functor that is both left exact and right exact, preserving all short exact sequences.

nodes.name: Projective resolution
nodes.description: An exact sequence ··· → P₁ → P₀ → M → 0 with each Pᵢ a projective module.

nodes.name: Injective resolution
nodes.description: An exact sequence 0 → M → I⁰ → I¹ → ··· with each Iⁿ an injective module.

nodes.name: Enough projectives
nodes.description: A category has enough projectives if for every object M there exists an epimorphism P → M with P projective.

nodes.name: Enough injectives
nodes.description: A category has enough injectives if for every object M there exists a monomorphism M → I with I injective.

nodes.name: Hom is left exact
nodes.description: The functor Hom_R(M, −) is left exact for any module M, and Hom_R(−, N) is left exact contravariant.

nodes.name: Tensor is right exact
nodes.description: The functor − ⊗_R M is right exact for any R-module M.

nodes.name: Comparison theorem for resolutions
nodes.description: Any morphism M → N lifts to a chain map between projective (or injective) resolutions, unique up to chain homotopy.

nodes.name: Horseshoe lemma
nodes.description: Given a short exact sequence 0 → A → B → C → 0 and projective resolutions of A and C, one can construct a projective resolution of B fitting into a short exact sequence of complexes.

nodes.name: Long exact sequence from short exact sequence of complexes
nodes.description: A short exact sequence of chain complexes 0 → A• → B• → C• → 0 induces a long exact sequence ··· → Hₙ(A) → Hₙ(B) → Hₙ(C) → Hₙ₋₁(A) → ···.

nodes.name: Nine lemma (3×3 lemma)
nodes.description: In a 3×3 commutative diagram where all columns and two of the three rows are exact, the third row is also exact.

nodes.name: Group extension
nodes.description: A short exact sequence 1 → N → G → Q → 1 of groups, expressing G as an extension of Q by N.

nodes.name: Factor set (2-cocycle)
nodes.description: A function f: Q × Q → N satisfying the cocycle condition, determining a group extension of Q by N up to equivalence.

nodes.name: Corestriction (transfer) map
nodes.description: The map Cor: Hⁿ(H, M) → Hⁿ(G, M) for a subgroup H of finite index in G, a transfer homomorphism on cohomology.

nodes.name: Cup product in group cohomology
nodes.description: A bilinear pairing Hᵖ(G, M) × Hᵍ(G, N) → Hᵖ⁺ᵍ(G, M ⊗ N) making H*(G, −) a graded ring.

nodes.name: Crossed homomorphism
nodes.description: A map f: G → M satisfying f(στ) = σ·f(τ) + f(σ), a 1-cocycle in group cohomology with H¹(G,M) classifying these modulo principal ones.

nodes.name: H² classifies group extensions
nodes.description: The second cohomology group H²(G, A) is in bijection with equivalence classes of extensions of G by the abelian group A with the given G-action.

nodes.name: Herbrand quotient is multiplicative
nodes.description: For a short exact sequence 0 → A → B → C → 0 of modules for a cyclic group, h(B) = h(A)·h(C) when all quotients are defined.

nodes.name: Cohomology of cyclic groups is periodic
nodes.description: For a cyclic group G, Tate cohomology is 2-periodic: Ĥⁿ(G, M) ≅ Ĥⁿ⁺²(G, M) for all n.

nodes.name: Left derived functor
nodes.description: The functors LₙF obtained by applying a right exact functor F to a projective resolution and taking homology.

nodes.name: Right derived functor
nodes.description: The functors RⁿF obtained by applying a left exact functor F to an injective resolution and taking cohomology.

nodes.name: Universal δ-functor
nodes.description: A connected sequence of functors {Tⁿ} with connecting homomorphisms such that any natural transformation from T⁰ extends uniquely to the whole sequence.

nodes.name: Effaceable functor
nodes.description: An additive functor T such that for every object M there exists a monomorphism M → I with T(I) = 0.

nodes.name: Projective dimension
nodes.description: The minimum length pd(M) of a projective resolution of a module M, or ∞ if no finite resolution exists.

nodes.name: Injective dimension
nodes.description: The minimum length id(M) of an injective resolution of a module M.

nodes.name: Global dimension of a ring
nodes.description: The supremum gl.dim(R) = sup{pd(M)} over all R-modules M.

nodes.name: Weak (flat) dimension
nodes.description: The supremum w.dim(R) of flat dimensions of all R-modules, always ≤ gl.dim(R).

nodes.name: Ext is independent of resolution
nodes.description: The groups Extⁿ_R(M, N) computed via a projective resolution of M or an injective resolution of N are naturally isomorphic.

nodes.name: Tor is independent of resolution
nodes.description: The groups Torₙ^R(M, N) computed via projective resolutions of either variable are naturally isomorphic.

nodes.name: Long exact sequence for Ext
nodes.description: A short exact sequence 0 → A → B → C → 0 induces long exact sequences ··· → Extⁿ(M,A) → Extⁿ(M,B) → Extⁿ(M,C) → Extⁿ⁺¹(M,A) → ···.

nodes.name: Long exact sequence for Tor
nodes.description: A short exact sequence 0 → A → B → C → 0 induces ··· → Torₙ(M,A) → Torₙ(M,B) → Torₙ(M,C) → Torₙ₋₁(M,A) → ···.

nodes.name: Ext¹ classifies extensions
nodes.description: The group Ext¹_R(C, A) is in bijection with equivalence classes of short exact sequences 0 → A → B → C → 0.

nodes.name: Tor₁ characterizes flatness
nodes.description: An R-module M is flat if and only if Tor₁^R(M, N) = 0 for all R-modules N.

nodes.name: Grothendieck's universality theorem
nodes.description: An effaceable δ-functor is universal, so derived functors are characterized by their universal property.

nodes.name: Dimension shifting
nodes.description: If 0 → K → P → M → 0 with P projective, then Extⁿ⁺¹(M, N) ≅ Extⁿ(K, N) for n ≥ 1, reducing higher Ext to lower Ext.

nodes.name: Auslander-Buchsbaum-Serre theorem
nodes.description: A Noetherian local ring is regular if and only if it has finite global dimension, in which case gl.dim equals the Krull dimension.

nodes.name: Dimension shifting technique
nodes.description: Reducing computation of higher Ext or Tor groups to lower ones by splicing short exact sequences from projective or injective resolutions.
nodes.function_signature: (Module M, short exact sequence with projective/injective term) → (Extⁿ⁺¹ ≅ Extⁿ of a related module)

nodes.name: Resolution comparison technique
nodes.description: Using the comparison theorem to relate different resolutions of the same module, showing derived functor independence of resolution choice.
nodes.function_signature: (Two resolutions of M, morphism M → M) → (Chain map unique up to homotopy)

nodes.name: Derived functor computation via acyclic resolutions
nodes.description: Computing derived functors using acyclic resolutions (F-acyclic objects) instead of projective or injective resolutions.
nodes.function_signature: (Left exact functor F, F-acyclic resolution) → (Derived functors RⁿF)

nodes.name: Filtered complex
nodes.description: A chain or cochain complex C with a decreasing filtration F^p C ⊇ F^{p+1} C compatible with the differential.

nodes.name: Double complex
nodes.description: A bigraded module C^{p,q} with horizontal and vertical differentials d_h and d_v satisfying d_h² = d_v² = 0 and d_h d_v + d_v d_h = 0.

nodes.name: Total complex of a double complex
nodes.description: The single complex Tot(C)^n = ⊕_{p+q=n} C^{p,q} with differential d = d_h + d_v.

nodes.name: Edge homomorphism
nodes.description: Natural maps from the abutment to E₂^{0,n} or from E₂^{n,0} to the abutment, coming from the filtration on convergence of a spectral sequence.

nodes.name: Balancing Tor via double complexes
nodes.description: Torₙ^R(M, N) can be computed from either variable's resolution using a double complex, establishing the symmetry of Tor.

nodes.name: Spectral sequence argument
nodes.description: Using spectral sequence convergence to compute or constrain (co)homology groups, especially via degeneration at E₂.
nodes.function_signature: (Filtered complex or composed functors) → (Cohomology via successive approximation)

nodes.name: Double complex filtration technique
nodes.description: Choosing row or column filtration of a double complex to obtain spectral sequences computing the total complex's cohomology.
nodes.function_signature: (Double complex C^{•,•}) → (Two spectral sequences converging to H*(Tot(C)))

nodes.name: Depth of a module
nodes.description: The length of a maximal regular sequence in an ideal I on a module M, denoted depth_I(M).

nodes.name: Cohen-Macaulay module
nodes.description: A finitely generated module M over a Noetherian local ring such that depth(M) = dim(M).

nodes.name: Koszul complex acyclicity
nodes.description: If x₁,...,xₙ is a regular sequence on a module M, then the Koszul complex K(x₁,...,xₙ; M) is acyclic (exact except in degree 0).

nodes.name: Regular local ring is UFD
nodes.description: Every regular local ring is a unique factorization domain.

nodes.name: Regular local ring has finite global dimension
nodes.description: A regular local ring of dimension d has global dimension d, proved by using the Koszul complex on a regular system of parameters.

nodes.name: Koszul complex technique
nodes.description: Using the Koszul complex K(x₁,...,xₙ) to compute Tor, detect regular sequences, and study depth and projective dimension.
nodes.function_signature: (Regular sequence x₁,...,xₙ in R, module M) → (Homology H_*(K(x; M)) detecting depth/regularity)

nodes.name: Long exact sequence construction
nodes.description: Constructing long exact sequences in (co)homology from short exact sequences of complexes via the connecting homomorphism.
nodes.function_signature: (Short exact sequence of complexes) → (Long exact sequence of (co)homology groups)

nodes.name: Ordered field
nodes.description: A field K with a total order compatible with addition and multiplication: a > 0 and b > 0 imply a + b > 0 and ab > 0.

nodes.name: Valuation ring of an absolute value
nodes.description: The subring O_v = {a ∈ K : |a| ≤ 1} of a field with a non-archimedean absolute value.

nodes.name: Sturm's theorem
nodes.description: The number of distinct real roots of a polynomial in an interval (a,b) equals the difference in the number of sign changes of the Sturm sequence at a and b.

nodes.name: Ostrowski's theorem
nodes.description: Every nontrivial absolute value on ℚ is equivalent to either the usual real absolute value or a p-adic absolute value for some prime p.

nodes.name: Extension of absolute values
nodes.description: Every absolute value on a field K extends to any algebraic extension L/K, and the extension is unique if K is complete.

nodes.name: Dihedral Group D_{2n}
nodes.description: The group of symmetries of a regular n-gon, of order 2n, generated by a rotation r of order n and a reflection s with srs = r^{-1}.

nodes.name: Quaternion Group Q_8
nodes.description: The non-abelian group of order 8 consisting of {+/-1, +/-i, +/-j, +/-k} with i^2 = j^2 = k^2 = ijk = -1, the smallest non-abelian group in which every subgroup is normal.

nodes.name: Klein Four-Group V_4
nodes.description: The abelian group Z/2Z x Z/2Z of order 4, the smallest non-cyclic group, isomorphic to the normal subgroup {e, (12)(34), (13)(24), (14)(23)} in S_4.

nodes.name: Lattice of Subgroups
nodes.description: The partially ordered set of all subgroups of a group G ordered by inclusion, forming a complete lattice with meet given by intersection and join by the subgroup generated by the union.

nodes.name: Abelianization
nodes.description: The quotient G/[G,G] of a group G by its commutator subgroup, the largest abelian quotient of G satisfying the universal property that every homomorphism from G to an abelian group factors through it.

nodes.name: Classification of Groups of Small Order
nodes.function_signature: (Integer n, Sylow theorems, semidirect products) -> (List of isomorphism classes of groups of order n)
nodes.description: Systematic enumeration of all groups of a given small order using Sylow theory, semidirect product constructions, and extensions to determine all isomorphism types.

nodes.name: Holder Program
nodes.function_signature: (Finite group G) -> (Composition factors, extension data)
nodes.description: The program to classify all finite groups by first classifying all finite simple groups (composition factors via Jordan-Holder) and then solving the extension problem to reconstruct all groups with given composition factors.

nodes.name: Chinese Remainder Theorem for Commutative Rings
nodes.description: If I_1, ..., I_n are pairwise coprime ideals (I_j + I_k = R for j != k) in a commutative ring R, then R/(I_1 cap ... cap I_n) is isomorphic to R/I_1 x ... x R/I_n.

nodes.name: Quotient by Prime Ideal is Integral Domain
nodes.description: An ideal P of a commutative ring R is prime if and only if the quotient ring R/P is an integral domain.

nodes.name: Quotient by Maximal Ideal is Field
nodes.description: An ideal M of a commutative ring R with identity is maximal if and only if the quotient ring R/M is a field.

nodes.name: Associate Elements in a Ring
nodes.description: Two elements a and b of an integral domain are associates if a = ub for some unit u, forming an equivalence relation that identifies elements differing only by a unit factor.

nodes.name: Irreducible Element
nodes.description: A nonzero non-unit element a of an integral domain such that if a = bc then b or c is a unit; in a UFD, irreducibility is equivalent to generating a maximal principal ideal among proper principal ideals.

nodes.name: Prime Element in a Ring
nodes.description: A nonzero non-unit element p of an integral domain such that if p divides ab then p divides a or p divides b; equivalently (p) is a prime ideal, and every prime is irreducible but the converse holds only in UFDs.

nodes.name: Polynomial Ring over a Field is a Euclidean Domain
nodes.description: If F is a field, then F[x] is a Euclidean domain with the degree function as Euclidean norm, and hence is also a principal ideal domain and a unique factorization domain.

nodes.name: Rational Root Theorem
nodes.description: If p/q in lowest terms is a rational root of a polynomial a_n x^n + ... + a_0 with integer coefficients, then p divides a_0 and q divides a_n.

nodes.name: Mod p Irreducibility Test
nodes.function_signature: (Polynomial f in Z[x], prime p) -> (Irreducibility of f over Q)
nodes.description: If a monic polynomial f in Z[x] reduces modulo a prime p to an irreducible polynomial in F_p[x] of the same degree, then f is irreducible over Q.

nodes.name: Evaluation Homomorphism
nodes.description: The ring homomorphism phi_a: R[x] -> R defined by phi_a(f) = f(a) for a fixed element a, whose kernel when R is a field is the principal ideal (x - a) if a is a root.

nodes.name: Root-Factor Theorem
nodes.description: An element a is a root of a polynomial f(x) over a field F if and only if (x - a) divides f(x) in F[x], so a polynomial of degree n has at most n roots in F.

nodes.name: Splitting Lemma for Modules
nodes.description: A short exact sequence 0 -> A -> B -> C -> 0 of R-modules splits (B is isomorphic to A direct sum C) if and only if there exists a section C -> B, equivalently a retraction B -> A.

nodes.name: Companion Matrix
nodes.description: The n x n matrix C(p) associated to a monic polynomial p(x) = x^n + a_{n-1}x^{n-1} + ... + a_0 with last column (-a_0, -a_1, ..., -a_{n-1})^T and 1's on the subdiagonal, whose characteristic and minimal polynomial both equal p(x).

nodes.name: Jordan Block
nodes.description: The n x n matrix J_n(lambda) with eigenvalue lambda on the diagonal, 1's on the superdiagonal, and 0's elsewhere; the building block of Jordan canonical form corresponding to an indecomposable F[x]-module F[x]/(x - lambda)^n.

nodes.name: F[x]-Module Structure on a Vector Space
nodes.description: A finite-dimensional vector space V over F equipped with an endomorphism T becomes an F[x]-module via f(x).v = f(T)(v), establishing an equivalence between studying T and studying finitely generated torsion F[x]-modules that underpins rational and Jordan canonical forms.

nodes.name: Computing Galois Groups of Small Degree Polynomials
nodes.function_signature: (Irreducible polynomial f of degree 2,3,4,5 over Q) -> (Galois group as transitive subgroup of S_n)
nodes.description: Determination of the Galois group of a low-degree polynomial using the discriminant, resolvent cubic/sextic, and transitive subgroup classification to identify the group among finitely many possibilities.

nodes.name: Galois Closure
nodes.description: The smallest Galois extension of the base field containing a given finite extension L/K, obtained as the splitting field of the minimal polynomial of a primitive element of L over K, also called the normal closure.

nodes.name: Composite Field Extension (Compositum)
nodes.description: For field extensions E/K and F/K inside a common overfield, their compositum EF is the smallest subfield containing both E and F; if E/K and F/K are Galois with trivial intersection of Galois groups, then [EF:K] = [E:K][F:K].

nodes.name: Inner Product of Class Functions
nodes.description: The Hermitian inner product <phi, psi> = (1/|G|) sum_{g in G} phi(g) psi(g)* on the space of class functions of a finite group G, under which the irreducible characters form an orthonormal basis.

nodes.name: Permutation Representation
nodes.description: A representation rho: G -> GL(V) arising from a group action of G on a finite set X by permuting basis vectors {e_x}_{x in X} of the free vector space V = k^X, with character chi(g) equal to the number of fixed points of g.

nodes.name: Symmetric and Exterior Powers of Representations
nodes.description: For a representation V of G, the symmetric power Sym^n(V) and exterior power Lambda^n(V) are representations whose characters are expressible via Newton's identities in terms of the character of V.

nodes.name: Frobenius-Schur Indicator
nodes.description: The quantity nu(chi) = (1/|G|) sum_{g in G} chi(g^2) for an irreducible character chi, taking values +1, -1, or 0 according to whether the representation is real (orthogonal), quaternionic (symplectic), or genuinely complex.

nodes.name: Representations as k[G]-Modules
nodes.function_signature: (Group G, field k) -> (Equivalence: k-representations of G = left k[G]-modules)
nodes.description: The category of finite-dimensional k-representations of a group G is equivalent to the category of finitely generated left k[G]-modules, translating representation-theoretic questions into module theory over the group algebra.

nodes.name: Character Theory for Simplicity Proofs
nodes.function_signature: (Finite group G, character table) -> (Proof of simplicity or identification of normal subgroups)
nodes.description: Using the fact that normal subgroups are exactly unions of conjugacy classes and kernels of characters to prove simplicity by showing no proper nontrivial subset of conjugacy classes satisfies the closure conditions, applied classically to A_n and PSL_2(F_q).

nodes.name: Von Dyck's theorem
nodes.description: If G = ⟨S | R⟩ is a group presentation and H is any group whose generators satisfy the relations R, then there exists a surjective homomorphism G → H.

nodes.name: Chief series
nodes.description: A normal series G = G₀ ▷ G₁ ▷ ··· ▷ Gₙ = {e} where each Gᵢ is normal in G and each factor Gᵢ/Gᵢ₊₁ is a minimal normal subgroup of G/Gᵢ₊₁.

nodes.name: Chief factors
nodes.description: The factor groups Gᵢ/Gᵢ₊₁ of a chief series, each of which is characteristically simple.

nodes.name: Indecomposable group
nodes.description: A nontrivial group that cannot be expressed as a direct product of two nontrivial subgroups.

nodes.name: Krull-Schmidt theorem for groups
nodes.description: If a group G satisfies both ACC and DCC on normal subgroups, then any two decompositions of G into direct products of indecomposable factors have the same number of factors, and the factors are pairwise isomorphic up to reordering.

nodes.name: Free product with amalgamation
nodes.description: For groups G₁, G₂ and monomorphisms φᵢ: H → Gᵢ, the quotient of the free product G₁ * G₂ by the normal closure of {φ₁(h)φ₂(h)⁻¹ : h ∈ H}.

nodes.name: Subnormal subgroup
nodes.description: A subgroup H of G for which there exists a finite chain H = Hₖ ◁ Hₖ₋₁ ◁ ··· ◁ H₀ = G where each term is normal in its predecessor.

nodes.name: Zero divisor
nodes.description: A nonzero element a of a ring R such that ab = 0 or ba = 0 for some nonzero b ∈ R.

nodes.name: Nil ideal
nodes.description: An ideal of a ring in which every element is nilpotent.

nodes.name: Nilpotent ideal
nodes.description: An ideal I of a ring R such that Iⁿ = 0 for some positive integer n.

nodes.name: Primitive ring
nodes.description: A ring possessing a faithful simple left module.

nodes.name: Semiprimitive ring
nodes.description: A ring R whose Jacobson radical is zero: J(R) = 0.

nodes.name: Dense ring of linear transformations
nodes.description: A subring D of End_k(V) such that for any finite linearly independent set v₁,...,vₙ and arbitrary w₁,...,wₙ, there exists d ∈ D with d(vᵢ) = wᵢ.

nodes.name: Group ring
nodes.description: For a ring R and group G, the ring R[G] of formal finite sums Σ aᵍg with convolution multiplication.

nodes.name: Semiprime ring
nodes.description: A ring with no nonzero nilpotent two-sided ideals.

nodes.name: Essential submodule
nodes.description: A submodule N of M such that N ∩ K ≠ 0 for every nonzero submodule K of M.

nodes.name: Divisible abelian group
nodes.description: An abelian group D such that for every d ∈ D and nonzero integer n, there exists x ∈ D with nx = d.

nodes.name: Invariant basis number
nodes.description: A ring R has IBN if any two bases of a free R-module have the same cardinality; all commutative rings and all left-Noetherian rings have IBN.

nodes.name: Comparison theorem for resolutions
nodes.description: Given a module map f: M → N and projective resolutions P• → M and Q• → N, there exists a chain map lifting f, unique up to chain homotopy.

nodes.name: Torsion module
nodes.description: An R-module M over a domain such that every element is torsion: for each m ∈ M there exists nonzero r ∈ R with rm = 0.

nodes.name: Cyclic module
nodes.description: An R-module generated by a single element, isomorphic to R/I for some left ideal I.

nodes.name: Progenerator
nodes.description: A finitely generated projective generator module; rings R and S are Morita equivalent iff S ≅ End_R(P) for a progenerator P.

nodes.name: Endomorphism ring of a module
nodes.description: The ring End_R(M) = Hom_R(M, M) with composition as multiplication, for an R-module M.

nodes.name: MacLane separability criterion
nodes.description: A field extension F/K in characteristic p is separable if and only if F and K^{1/p} are linearly disjoint over K.

nodes.name: Separating transcendence basis
nodes.description: A transcendence basis B of F/K such that F is separable algebraic over K(B).

nodes.name: Separable closure in an extension
nodes.description: For F/K, the subfield Kₛ of elements separable over K; F/Kₛ is purely inseparable and Kₛ/K is separable.

nodes.name: Compositum of fields
nodes.description: For subfields E, F of a common overfield containing K, the smallest subfield containing both E and F.

nodes.name: Artin-Schreier map
nodes.description: The additive map ℘: K → K defined by ℘(x) = xᵖ − x in characteristic p, whose cokernel K/℘(K) classifies cyclic extensions of degree p.

nodes.name: Natural transformation
nodes.description: Given functors F, G: C → D, a family of morphisms ηₐ: F(A) → G(A) indexed by objects of C such that G(f)∘ηₐ = ηᵦ∘F(f) for every morphism f: A → B.

nodes.name: Functor category
nodes.description: The category [C, D] whose objects are functors C → D and whose morphisms are natural transformations.

nodes.name: Equalizer
nodes.description: For parallel morphisms f, g: A → B in a category, an object E with e: E → A satisfying fe = ge, universal among such.

nodes.name: Coequalizer
nodes.description: For parallel morphisms f, g: A → B, an object Q with q: B → Q satisfying qf = qg, universal among such; the categorical dual of equalizer.

nodes.name: Pullback (categorical)
nodes.description: For morphisms f: A → C and g: B → C, a limit over the diagram A → C ← B; the categorical fiber product.

nodes.name: Pushout (categorical)
nodes.description: For morphisms f: C → A and g: C → B, a colimit over the diagram A ← C → B; the categorical dual of pullback.

nodes.name: Complete category
nodes.description: A category in which all small limits exist.

nodes.name: Cocomplete category
nodes.description: A category in which all small colimits exist.

nodes.name: Initial object
nodes.description: An object I in a category such that for every object A there exists exactly one morphism I → A.

nodes.name: Terminal object
nodes.description: An object T in a category such that for every object A there exists exactly one morphism A → T.

nodes.name: Zero object (category)
nodes.description: An object that is both initial and terminal in a category.

nodes.name: Cone over a diagram
nodes.description: A family of morphisms from a fixed object to each object in a diagram, compatible with the diagram morphisms.

nodes.name: Cocone under a diagram
nodes.description: A family of morphisms from each diagram object to a fixed object, compatible with the diagram morphisms.

nodes.name: Unit of adjunction
nodes.description: The natural transformation η: Id_C → GF defined by η_A corresponding to id_{F(A)} under the adjunction bijection Hom(FA,FA) ≅ Hom(A,GFA).

nodes.name: Counit of adjunction
nodes.description: The natural transformation ε: FG → Id_D defined by ε_B corresponding to id_{G(B)} under the adjunction bijection.

nodes.name: Additive functor
nodes.description: A functor F between additive categories such that F: Hom(A,B) → Hom(FA,FB) is a group homomorphism for all A, B.

nodes.name: Image in abelian category
nodes.description: For a morphism f in an abelian category, im(f) = ker(coker(f)), the smallest subobject through which f factors.

nodes.name: Triangle identities for adjunction
nodes.description: For an adjunction (F ⊣ G, η, ε), the composites εF∘Fη = id_F and Gε∘ηG = id_G hold.

nodes.name: Limits from products and equalizers
nodes.description: A category has all small limits if and only if it has all small products and all equalizers.

nodes.name: Colimits from coproducts and coequalizers
nodes.description: A category has all small colimits if and only if it has all small coproducts and all coequalizers.

nodes.name: Right adjoints preserve limits
nodes.description: If a functor G has a left adjoint, then G preserves all small limits.

nodes.name: Left adjoints preserve colimits
nodes.description: If a functor F has a right adjoint, then F preserves all small colimits.

nodes.name: Characterization of equivalence of categories
nodes.description: A functor F: C → D is an equivalence of categories iff F is full, faithful, and essentially surjective.

nodes.name: p-primary component
nodes.description: For a prime p in a PID R and torsion module M, the submodule M_p = {m ∈ M : p^k m = 0 for some k ≥ 1}.

nodes.name: Matrix equivalence
nodes.description: Matrices A and B over a ring R are equivalent if B = PAQ for invertible matrices P, Q.

nodes.name: Matrix similarity
nodes.description: Matrices A and B over a field F are similar if B = P⁻¹AP for some invertible P.

nodes.name: Embedded associated prime
nodes.description: An associated prime of an ideal that properly contains another associated prime.

nodes.name: Isolated associated prime
nodes.description: An associated prime of an ideal that is minimal among all associated primes.

nodes.name: Minimal primary decomposition
nodes.description: A primary decomposition I = Q₁ ∩ ··· ∩ Qₙ where no Qᵢ is redundant and all associated primes rad(Qᵢ) are distinct.

nodes.name: Von Dyck presentation argument
nodes.description: Construct an epimorphism from a presented group to any group whose generators satisfy the given relations.
nodes.type_signature: (Group presentation ⟨S|R⟩, group H satisfying R) → Surjective homomorphism ⟨S|R⟩ → H

nodes.name: Horseshoe lemma construction
nodes.description: Construct a projective resolution of the middle term from resolutions of the outer terms using direct sums.
nodes.type_signature: (SES 0→A→B→C→0, proj. resolutions of A and C) → Projective resolution of B

nodes.name: Comparison theorem lifting
nodes.description: Lift a module homomorphism to a chain map between projective resolutions, unique up to chain homotopy.
nodes.type_signature: (Module map f: M→N, proj. resolutions P•→M, Q•→N) → Chain map F: P•→Q• lifting f

nodes.name: Universal property argument
nodes.description: Verify existence and uniqueness of morphisms by checking the universal property diagram commutes.
nodes.type_signature: (Universal property of a construction, candidate morphism) → Unique morphism with prescribed behavior

nodes.name: Yoneda argument
nodes.description: Use the bijection Nat(Hom(A,−), F) ≅ F(A) to reduce categorical statements to set-theoretic ones.
nodes.type_signature: (Objects or functors to compare) → Isomorphisms or natural transformations via Yoneda bijection

nodes.name: Adjunction construction via universal arrows
nodes.description: Assemble universal arrows into an adjoint functor pair.
nodes.type_signature: (Universal arrows from objects to functor G) → Left adjoint F to G with unit η

nodes.name: Diagram chasing in abelian categories
nodes.description: Chase elements through diagrams using the embedding theorem to prove exactness or isomorphism results.
nodes.type_signature: (Commutative diagram with exact rows/columns in abelian category) → Exactness statements and connecting morphisms

nodes.name: Cycle decomposition of permutations
nodes.function_signature: (Permutation σ ∈ S_n) → (Product of disjoint cycles)
nodes.description: Writing a permutation as a product of disjoint cycles to determine its order, cycle type, and conjugacy class.

nodes.name: Simplicity of A_n for n ≥ 5
nodes.description: The alternating group A_n is simple (has no proper nontrivial normal subgroups) for all n ≥ 5.

nodes.name: R UFD implies R[x] UFD
nodes.description: If R is a unique factorization domain, then the polynomial ring R[x] is also a unique factorization domain.

nodes.name: Fundamental theorem of algebra via real closed fields
nodes.description: If R is a real closed field, then R[i] = R[x]/(x² + 1) is algebraically closed; in particular ℂ = ℝ[i] is algebraically closed.

nodes.name: Budan–Fourier theorem
nodes.description: The number of real roots of a polynomial f in an interval (a, b] is at most the difference in the number of sign changes of f, f', f'', ... evaluated at a and b, with equality modulo 2.

nodes.name: Distributive lattice
nodes.description: A lattice satisfying the distributive law: a ∧ (b ∨ c) = (a ∧ b) ∨ (a ∧ c) for all elements a, b, c.

nodes.name: Complemented lattice
nodes.description: A bounded lattice in which every element a has a complement b satisfying a ∧ b = 0 and a ∨ b = 1.

nodes.name: Jordan–Dedekind chain condition
nodes.description: In a modular lattice of finite length, all maximal chains between any two comparable elements have the same length.

nodes.name: Universal algebra (Ω-algebra)
nodes.description: A set A equipped with a family Ω of finitary operations ω: A^{n_ω} → A, providing a general framework encompassing groups, rings, lattices, and other algebraic structures.

nodes.name: Congruence relation
nodes.description: An equivalence relation on an algebra compatible with all operations: if a_i ≡ b_i then ω(a_1,...,a_n) ≡ ω(b_1,...,b_n) for every operation ω.

nodes.name: Free algebra (universal algebra)
nodes.description: The Ω-algebra F(X) on a generating set X satisfying the universal property: every map X → A to an Ω-algebra A extends uniquely to a homomorphism F(X) → A.

nodes.name: Variety (equational class)
nodes.description: A class of Ω-algebras defined by a set of universally quantified identities; equivalently, a class closed under homomorphic images, subalgebras, and direct products.

nodes.name: Birkhoff's HSP theorem
nodes.description: A class of algebras is a variety (definable by identities) if and only if it is closed under homomorphic images (H), subalgebras (S), and direct products (P).

nodes.name: Subdirect product
nodes.description: A subalgebra of a direct product ∏ A_i whose projection onto each factor A_i is surjective.

nodes.name: Birkhoff's subdirect representation theorem
nodes.description: Every algebra is isomorphic to a subdirect product of subdirectly irreducible algebras.

nodes.name: Completely reducible module
nodes.description: A module in which every submodule is a direct summand; equivalent to being a direct sum of simple submodules (semisimple).

nodes.name: Composition length
nodes.description: The length of a composition series of a module, when one exists; well-defined by the Jordan–Hölder theorem.

nodes.name: Krull dimension
nodes.description: The supremum of lengths of all chains of prime ideals p_0 ⊊ p_1 ⊊ ⋯ ⊊ p_d in a commutative ring R.

nodes.name: Prüfer domain
nodes.description: An integral domain in which every finitely generated nonzero ideal is invertible; equivalently, every localization at a maximal ideal is a valuation ring.

nodes.name: Characterizations of Prüfer domains
nodes.description: An integral domain R is a Prüfer domain if and only if R_M is a valuation ring for every maximal ideal M, if and only if every finitely generated torsion-free R-module is flat.

nodes.name: Homology of a chain complex
nodes.description: The graded module H_n(C) = ker(d_n)/im(d_{n+1}) measuring the failure of exactness of a chain complex C at position n.

nodes.name: Abelian p-extensions via Witt vectors
nodes.description: Over a field of characteristic p, abelian extensions of exponent p^n correspond bijectively to quotients of the additive group of Witt vectors W_n(K) modulo the image of the operator ℘ = F − id.

nodes.name: Integrality of characters
nodes.description: The character values χ(g) of a finite group representation over ℂ are algebraic integers, and |G|/dim(V) times the character value at any element is an algebraic integer.

nodes.name: Modular representation theory
nodes.function_signature: (Finite group G, Field k with char(k) | |G|) → (Block decomposition, Brauer characters, decomposition numbers)
nodes.description: Study of representations of finite groups over fields whose characteristic divides the group order, where Maschke's theorem fails and indecomposable modules need not be simple.

nodes.name: Division algorithm for integers
nodes.description: For integers a, b with b > 0, there exist unique integers q, r with a = bq + r and 0 <= r < b.

nodes.name: Euclidean algorithm for integers
nodes.function_signature: (a: Z, b: Z) -> gcd(a, b): Z
nodes.description: Iterative procedure computing gcd(a, b) by repeated division: gcd(a, b) = gcd(b, a mod b), terminating when the remainder is 0.

nodes.name: Division algorithm for polynomials
nodes.description: For polynomials f, g in F[X] with g nonzero, there exist unique q, r in F[X] with f = gq + r and either r = 0 or deg(r) < deg(g).

nodes.name: Euclidean algorithm for polynomials
nodes.function_signature: (f: F[X], g: F[X]) -> gcd(f, g): F[X]
nodes.description: Iterative procedure computing gcd(f, g) in F[X] by repeated polynomial division, analogous to the integer Euclidean algorithm.

nodes.name: Irreducible polynomials over R
nodes.description: The irreducible polynomials over the reals are precisely the linear polynomials and the quadratic polynomials with negative discriminant.

nodes.name: Sign of a permutation
nodes.description: The sign sgn(sigma) = (-1)^(number of transpositions) defines a group homomorphism from S_n to {+/-1}, with even permutations forming the kernel.

nodes.name: Row reduction (Gaussian elimination)
nodes.function_signature: (A: M_{m x n}(F)) -> (R: row echelon form)
nodes.description: Systematic algorithm transforming a matrix to row echelon form via elementary row operations; the reduced row echelon form is unique.

nodes.name: Matrix algebra
nodes.description: The set of n x n matrices over a field F with addition, scalar multiplication, and matrix multiplication, forming a generally non-commutative ring with identity I_n.

nodes.name: Matrix inverse
nodes.description: A square matrix A is invertible if there exists A^{-1} with AA^{-1} = A^{-1}A = I, computable via row reduction of the augmented matrix [A|I].

nodes.name: One-sided inverse implies two-sided inverse
nodes.description: For a square matrix A, if AB = I for some matrix B then BA = I, so B = A^{-1}.

nodes.name: Vector space
nodes.description: A set V over a field F with vector addition and scalar multiplication satisfying eight axioms: associativity, commutativity, additive identity/inverses, scalar identity, and distributive laws.

nodes.name: Subspace of a vector space
nodes.description: A nonempty subset W of a vector space V that is closed under addition and scalar multiplication, forming a vector space in its own right.

nodes.name: Linear independence
nodes.description: Vectors v_1, ..., v_n are linearly independent if the equation c_1 v_1 + ... + c_n v_n = 0 implies c_1 = ... = c_n = 0.

nodes.name: Basis extension theorem
nodes.description: Any linearly independent set in a finite-dimensional vector space can be extended to a basis, and any spanning set contains a basis.

nodes.name: Linear map
nodes.description: A function T: V -> W between vector spaces preserving addition T(u+v) = T(u)+T(v) and scalar multiplication T(cv) = cT(v).

nodes.name: Kernel and image of a linear map
nodes.description: For T: V -> W, ker(T) = {v in V : T(v) = 0} and im(T) = {T(v) : v in V} are subspaces; T is injective iff ker(T) = {0}.

nodes.name: Matrix of a linear map
nodes.description: Given ordered bases for V and W, each linear map T: V -> W is uniquely represented by the matrix whose columns are the coordinate vectors of T applied to the basis vectors.

nodes.name: Quotient vector space V/W
nodes.description: For a subspace W of V, the space of cosets v + W with induced vector space operations, satisfying dim(V/W) = dim(V) - dim(W).

nodes.name: Internal direct sum of subspaces
nodes.description: V = W_1 + ... + W_k is an internal direct sum if every v in V has a unique expression w_1 + ... + w_k with w_i in W_i.

nodes.name: External direct sum of vector spaces
nodes.description: The space of tuples with componentwise operations, satisfying dim(V_1 + ... + V_k) = sum of dim(V_i), with a universal mapping property.

nodes.name: Dimension formula for subspaces
nodes.description: For subspaces U, W of V: dim(U + W) = dim(U) + dim(W) - dim(U intersection W).

nodes.name: Multiplicativity of determinants
nodes.description: For square matrices A, B: det(AB) = det(A) det(B); also det(A^T) = det(A).

nodes.name: Determinant and invertibility
nodes.description: A square matrix A is invertible if and only if det(A) is nonzero; when invertible, A^{-1} = adj(A)/det(A).

nodes.name: Inner product
nodes.description: A positive-definite bilinear (real) or sesquilinear Hermitian (complex) form on V, inducing the norm ||v|| = sqrt(<v,v>).

nodes.name: Self-adjoint (Hermitian) linear map
nodes.description: A linear map T on an inner-product space with T* = T, satisfying <Tv, w> = <v, Tw>; represented by symmetric (real) or Hermitian (complex) matrices.

nodes.name: Unitary (orthogonal) linear map
nodes.description: A linear map U preserving inner products: <Uv, Uw> = <v, w>; real version is orthogonal (Q^T Q = I), complex version is unitary (U*U = I).

nodes.name: Positive semidefinite operator
nodes.description: A self-adjoint operator T with <Tv, v> >= 0 for all v, equivalently all eigenvalues >= 0; has a unique positive semidefinite square root.

nodes.name: Polar decomposition
nodes.description: Every linear map T on a finite-dimensional inner-product space factors as T = UP with U unitary/isometric and P = sqrt(T*T) positive semidefinite.

nodes.name: Free abelian group
nodes.description: An abelian group isomorphic to Z^n with a basis of well-defined rank; every subgroup of a free abelian group of finite rank is itself free abelian.

nodes.name: Classification of groups of order pq
nodes.description: For primes p < q: if p does not divide q-1 then every group of order pq is cyclic; if p divides q-1, there also exists a nonabelian semidirect product.

nodes.name: Minimal polynomial divides characteristic polynomial
nodes.description: The minimal polynomial m_A(t) divides the characteristic polynomial chi_A(t), and they share the same irreducible factors over the base field.

nodes.name: Diagonalizability criterion
nodes.description: A matrix is diagonalizable iff its minimal polynomial is a product of distinct linear factors, equivalently iff algebraic and geometric multiplicities coincide for each eigenvalue.

nodes.name: Projection operator (idempotent)
nodes.description: A linear map E with E^2 = E, yielding the decomposition V = im(E) + ker(E); complementary projections E_1 + ... + E_k = I with E_i E_j = 0 correspond to direct sum decompositions.

nodes.name: T-invariant subspace
nodes.description: A subspace W of V with T(W) contained in W, so T restricts to a well-defined linear map T|_W: W -> W.

nodes.name: Primary decomposition theorem (linear algebra)
nodes.description: If the minimal polynomial factors as m(t) = p_1(t)^{e_1} ... p_k(t)^{e_k} with distinct irreducible factors, then V decomposes as a direct sum of the kernels ker(p_i(T)^{e_i}).

nodes.name: Generalized eigenspace
nodes.description: The subspace V_lambda = ker((T - lambda I)^k) for sufficiently large k, forming the primary component when the irreducible factor is (t - lambda).

nodes.name: Determinant over a commutative ring
nodes.description: Extension of the determinant to matrices over any commutative ring with 1 via the Leibniz formula, used for characteristic polynomials over polynomial rings.

nodes.name: Gram matrix
nodes.description: For vectors v_1, ..., v_n in an inner-product space, the matrix G with G_{ij} = <v_i, v_j>; the vectors are linearly independent iff det(G) is nonzero.

nodes.name: Equivalence class partition theorem
nodes.description: An equivalence relation on a set S induces a partition of S into disjoint equivalence classes, and conversely every partition defines an equivalence relation.

nodes.name: Well-ordering principle
nodes.description: Every nonempty set can be well-ordered, meaning equipped with a total order in which every nonempty subset has a least element; equivalent to the Axiom of Choice and Zorn's lemma.

nodes.name: Semisimple module decomposition theorem
nodes.description: Every semisimple module is isomorphic to a direct sum of simple modules, and every submodule of a semisimple module is a direct summand.

nodes.name: Ascending chain condition (Noetherian condition for modules)
nodes.description: A module M satisfies the ACC if every ascending chain of submodules eventually stabilizes; equivalently, every nonempty set of submodules has a maximal element.

nodes.name: Descending chain condition (Artinian condition for modules)
nodes.description: A module M satisfies the DCC if every descending chain of submodules eventually stabilizes; equivalently, every nonempty set of submodules has a minimal element.

nodes.name: Composition series existence criterion
nodes.description: A module M has a composition series if and only if it satisfies both the ascending chain condition and the descending chain condition on submodules.

nodes.name: Tensor product distributes over direct sum
nodes.description: The tensor product commutes with direct sums: M tensor (direct sum N_i) is naturally isomorphic to the direct sum of (M tensor N_i), and dually for Hom.

nodes.name: Cochain complex
nodes.description: A sequence of module homomorphisms with d^{n+1} composed with d^n = 0 for all n, obtained by reversing the grading of a chain complex.

nodes.name: Cohomology of a cochain complex
nodes.description: The n-th cohomology module H^n(C) = ker(d^n)/im(d^{n-1}), measuring the failure of the cochain complex to be exact at position n.

nodes.name: Chain map
nodes.description: A morphism between chain complexes consisting of module maps f_n: C_n -> D_n commuting with the differentials, inducing well-defined maps on homology.

nodes.name: Derived functor construction (left derived functors)
nodes.function_signature: (F: right exact functor, M: module) -> L_n F(M)
nodes.description: Given a right exact additive functor F, the left derived functors L_n F(M) are obtained by choosing a projective resolution, deleting M, applying F, and taking homology.

nodes.name: Derived functor construction (right derived functors)
nodes.function_signature: (F: left exact functor, M: module) -> R^n F(M)
nodes.description: Given a left exact additive functor F, the right derived functors R^n F(M) are obtained by choosing an injective resolution, deleting M, applying F, and taking cohomology.

nodes.name: Long exact sequence of derived functors
nodes.description: A short exact sequence 0 -> A -> B -> C -> 0 induces a long exact sequence connecting the derived functors L_n F or R^n F with connecting homomorphisms.

nodes.name: Hom-tensor change of rings
nodes.function_signature: (phi: R -> S, M: R-Mod) -> (S tensor_R M: S-Mod)
nodes.description: Given a ring homomorphism R -> S, extension of scalars M -> S tensor_R M is left adjoint to restriction of scalars, mediating change of base ring via bimodule structures.

nodes.name: Hom functor exactness failure
nodes.description: The functor Hom_R(M, -) is left exact but not exact in general; the failure of full exactness is measured by the Ext functors.

nodes.name: Tensor product exactness failure
nodes.description: The functor M tensor_R - is right exact but not exact in general; the failure of full exactness is measured by the Tor functors, and M is flat precisely when the functor is exact.

nodes.name: Diagonalization of symmetric bilinear forms
nodes.description: Every symmetric bilinear form on a finite-dimensional vector space over a field of characteristic not 2 admits a basis in which the form is diagonal.

nodes.name: Normal form of alternating bilinear forms
nodes.description: Every alternating bilinear form on a finite-dimensional vector space has a symplectic basis yielding a block-diagonal matrix of 2x2 blocks [[0,1],[-1,0]], with rank always even.

nodes.name: Tensor product of two vector spaces
nodes.description: For vector spaces V, W over F, the tensor product V tensor W is a vector space with a bilinear map V x W -> V tensor W through which every bilinear map from V x W factors uniquely.

nodes.name: Existence and uniqueness of tensor product
nodes.description: The tensor product V tensor W exists for any vector spaces V, W and is unique up to canonical isomorphism, with dim(V tensor W) = dim V * dim W.

nodes.name: Tensor product of linear maps
nodes.description: Given linear maps f: V -> V' and g: W -> W', there is a unique linear map f tensor g: V tensor W -> V' tensor W' satisfying (f tensor g)(v tensor w) = f(v) tensor g(w).

nodes.name: Tensor product of multiple vector spaces
nodes.description: For vector spaces V_1, ..., V_k, the tensor product V_1 tensor ... tensor V_k is defined by the universal property for k-multilinear maps and is associative up to canonical isomorphism.

nodes.name: Associativity of tensor product
nodes.description: (V tensor W) tensor U is canonically isomorphic to V tensor (W tensor U), so the tensor product of multiple spaces is well-defined without parentheses.

nodes.name: Universal property of the tensor algebra
nodes.description: Any linear map from V into an associative algebra A with identity extends uniquely to a unital algebra homomorphism T(V) -> A.

nodes.name: Universal property of the symmetric algebra
nodes.description: Any linear map from V into a commutative associative algebra A with identity extends uniquely to an algebra homomorphism S(V) -> A, and S(V) is isomorphic to the polynomial ring when V is finite-dimensional.

nodes.name: Universal property of the exterior algebra
nodes.description: Any linear map f: V -> A into an associative algebra with identity satisfying f(v)^2 = 0 for all v extends uniquely to an algebra homomorphism Lambda(V) -> A.

nodes.name: Determinant via exterior algebra
nodes.description: For a linear endomorphism T of an n-dimensional space V, the induced map on Lambda^n(V) is multiplication by det(T), giving a coordinate-free definition of the determinant.

nodes.name: Basis for exterior powers
nodes.description: If {e_1,...,e_n} is a basis for V, then the set of all e_{i_1} wedge ... wedge e_{i_k} with i_1 < ... < i_k is a basis for Lambda^k(V), so dim Lambda^k(V) = C(n,k).

nodes.name: Dual space and tensor products
nodes.description: For finite-dimensional vector spaces V and W, the space Hom(V, W) is naturally isomorphic to V* tensor W, and multilinear forms on V correspond to elements of tensor powers of V*.

nodes.name: Universal property of free groups
nodes.description: Any set map from the generating set S to a group G extends uniquely to a group homomorphism F(S) -> G, making F(S) the coproduct of |S| copies of Z in the category of groups.

nodes.name: Schreier index formula
nodes.description: If H is a subgroup of index j in a free group of rank n, then H is free of rank j(n-1) + 1.

nodes.name: Simple extension
nodes.description: A field extension K/F of the form K = F(alpha) for a single element alpha; if alpha is algebraic with minimal polynomial p(x) of degree n, then F(alpha) is isomorphic to F[x]/(p(x)) with [F(alpha):F] = n.

nodes.name: Lagrange resolvent
nodes.function_signature: (Element a in cyclic Galois extension K/F of degree n, primitive nth root of unity zeta) -> (Resolvent (a, zeta) = sum sigma^i(a) * zeta^{-i} expressing roots via radicals)
nodes.description: For a cyclic Galois extension with generator sigma, the Lagrange resolvent (a, zeta) = sum_{i=0}^{n-1} sigma^i(a) * zeta^{-i} is used to express roots in terms of radicals.

nodes.name: Field polynomial
nodes.description: For alpha in a finite extension K/F, the field polynomial is the characteristic polynomial of the F-linear map x -> alpha*x on K; it is a power of the minimal polynomial with coefficients giving the norm and trace.

nodes.name: Discriminant determines alternating Galois group
nodes.description: The Galois group of a separable polynomial f over F is contained in the alternating group A_n if and only if the discriminant disc(f) is a square in F.

nodes.name: Reduction modulo p for Galois groups
nodes.function_signature: (Monic polynomial f in Z[x], prime p with f mod p separable) -> (Cycle type constraint on Gal(f/Q))
nodes.description: If f mod p is separable over F_p with factorization type (d_1,...,d_k), then the Galois group of f over Q contains a permutation of that cycle type.

nodes.name: Characterization of semisimple modules
nodes.description: For a module M, the following are equivalent: M is a sum of simple submodules, M is a direct sum of simple submodules, and every submodule of M is a direct summand.

nodes.name: ACC and DCC imply composition series
nodes.description: A module has a composition series if and only if it satisfies both the ascending and descending chain conditions on submodules.

nodes.name: Indecomposable module
nodes.description: A nonzero module M that cannot be written as a direct sum M = A + B with both A and B nonzero; every simple module is indecomposable but not conversely.

nodes.name: Direct sum and direct product of modules
nodes.description: The direct sum of a family of modules consists of tuples with finitely many nonzero components, serving as the coproduct in the category of R-modules, while the direct product is the categorical product.

nodes.name: Symmetric group S_n as Galois group
nodes.description: For each n, there exists a polynomial of degree n over Q whose Galois group is the full symmetric group S_n; for n >= 5 this yields explicit polynomials not solvable by radicals.

nodes.name: Multiplicativity of norm and trace in towers
nodes.description: For field extensions F subset K subset L, the norm and trace satisfy N_{L/F} = N_{K/F} o N_{L/K} and Tr_{L/F} = Tr_{K/F} o Tr_{L/K}.

nodes.name: Primary decomposition for modules over PIDs
nodes.description: A finitely generated torsion module over a PID decomposes uniquely as a direct sum of primary cyclic modules R/(p^k), giving the elementary divisor form of the structure theorem.

nodes.name: Localization is exact
nodes.description: The localization functor S^{-1}(-) is exact, preserving short exact sequences of modules; equivalently, S^{-1}R is a flat R-module.

nodes.name: Archimedean and non-archimedean places
nodes.description: A place of a number field K is an equivalence class of absolute values; archimedean places correspond to embeddings K → ℝ or ℂ, non-archimedean places to prime ideals of O_K; there are r_1+r_2 archimedean and infinitely many non-archimedean places.

nodes.name: Artin's theorem on simple rings
nodes.description: A left Artinian simple ring is isomorphic to M_n(D) for some division ring D and positive integer n; equivalently, a simple ring is left semisimple if and only if it is left Artinian.

nodes.name: Buchberger's algorithm
nodes.function_signature: (Finite generating set of polynomial ideal, Monomial order) → (Gröbner basis)
nodes.description: An algorithm that computes a Gröbner basis from any finite generating set of a polynomial ideal by iteratively computing S-polynomials, reducing, and adjoining nonzero remainders.

nodes.name: Buchberger's criterion
nodes.description: A finite set G is a Gröbner basis for the ideal it generates iff for every pair g_i, g_j in G, the remainder of S(g_i,g_j) on division by G is zero.

nodes.name: Burnside's theorem on matrix algebras
nodes.description: If V is a finite-dimensional vector space over an algebraically closed field F, then any subalgebra of End_F(V) acting irreducibly on V equals all of End_F(V) ≅ M_n(F).

nodes.name: Change of rings for Ext
nodes.description: For a ring homomorphism φ: R → S, there are natural maps and spectral sequences relating Ext over R and Ext over S; in particular, if S is flat over R, then Ext^n_S(M⊗_R S, N) relates to Ext^n_R(M, N).

nodes.name: Change of rings for Tor
nodes.description: For a ring homomorphism R → S and modules M_R, _SN, there is a natural isomorphism Tor_n^R(M, N) ≅ Tor_n^S(M⊗_R S, N) when S is flat as a right R-module.

nodes.name: Cocycle and coboundary (group cohomology)
nodes.description: An n-cocycle is an n-cochain f: G^n → M satisfying δf = 0; an n-coboundary is f = δg for an (n-1)-cochain g; H^n(G,M) = Z^n/B^n where Z^n = ker δ, B^n = im δ.

nodes.name: Comparison theorem (projective resolutions)
nodes.description: Any module homomorphism M → N lifts to a chain map between projective resolutions of M and N, and this lift is unique up to chain homotopy.

nodes.name: Composition of binary quadratic forms (Gauss composition)
nodes.function_signature: (Two primitive binary quadratic forms of discriminant D) → (Composed form class)
nodes.description: Gauss's law of composition defines a group operation on proper equivalence classes of primitive binary quadratic forms of fixed discriminant D, making them into a finite abelian group called the form class group.

nodes.name: Correspondence between forms and ideals
nodes.description: There is a canonical bijection between proper equivalence classes of primitive binary quadratic forms of discriminant D and strict equivalence classes of ideals in the ring of integers of ℚ(√D), compatible with composition and multiplication.

nodes.name: Crossed product algebra
nodes.description: For a Galois extension K/F with group G and factor set f, the crossed product (K/F, G, f) = ⊕_{σ∈G} Ku_σ with multiplication u_σ u_τ = f(σ,τ)u_{στ} and u_σ a = σ(a)u_σ for a ∈ K; it is a central simple algebra over F.

nodes.name: Cyclic algebra
nodes.description: For a cyclic extension K/F of degree n with generator σ and a ∈ F×, the cyclic algebra (K/F, σ, a) = ⊕_{i=0}^{n-1} Ku^i with u^n = a and ua = σ(a)u; a central simple algebra over F.

nodes.name: Delta-functor (universal)
nodes.description: A sequence of functors {T^n}_{n≥0} with connecting homomorphisms δ^n: T^n(C) → T^{n+1}(A) for each short exact sequence, forming long exact sequences; a universal δ-functor is characterized by T^n being coeffaceable for n ≥ 1.

nodes.name: Discriminant of a number field
nodes.description: For a number field K with [K:ℚ] = n and integral basis {ω_1,...,ω_n}, the discriminant d_K = det(σ_i(ω_j))^2 where σ_i are the n embeddings K → ℂ; an invariant of K detecting ramification.

nodes.name: Embedding of K into ℝ^n (real and complex places)
nodes.description: A number field K of degree n has r_1 real embeddings σ_i: K → ℝ and r_2 pairs of complex conjugate embeddings τ_j, τ̄_j: K → ℂ, with r_1 + 2r_2 = n; these define the archimedean places of K.

nodes.name: Euler product
nodes.description: A product representation ∏_p f(p,s) over primes p for a Dirichlet series, expressing multiplicativity of the coefficients; the Riemann zeta function has ζ(s) = ∏_p (1-p^{-s})^{-1}.

nodes.name: Exponent of a central simple algebra
nodes.description: The order of [A] in the Brauer group Br(F); always divides the index and shares the same prime factors: if ind(A) = p_1^{a_1}...p_k^{a_k}, then exp(A) = p_1^{b_1}...p_k^{b_k} with 1 ≤ b_i ≤ a_i.

nodes.name: Ext^1 and extensions
nodes.description: There is a natural bijection between Ext^1_R(C,A) and equivalence classes of short exact sequences 0 → A → B → C → 0, with the Baer sum making this correspondence a group isomorphism.

nodes.name: Finiteness of form classes
nodes.description: For any discriminant D < 0, the number of proper equivalence classes of primitive positive definite binary quadratic forms of discriminant D is finite.

nodes.name: Form class group
nodes.description: The finite abelian group of proper equivalence classes of primitive binary quadratic forms of discriminant D under Gauss composition; its order h(D) is the class number.

nodes.name: Frobenius theorem (real division algebras)
nodes.description: The only finite-dimensional associative division algebras over ℝ are ℝ, ℂ, and the quaternions ℍ.

nodes.name: Fundamental identity e·f·g = n
nodes.description: For a prime p in ℤ and K/ℚ of degree n, if pO_K = P_1^{e_1}...P_g^{e_g} with f_i = f(P_i|p), then ∑_{i=1}^g e_i f_i = n; in the Galois case all e_i and f_i are equal so efg = n.

nodes.name: Gauss's lemma (quadratic residues)
nodes.description: If p is an odd prime and gcd(a,p)=1, then (a/p) = (-1)^n where n is the number of least positive residues of a, 2a, ..., ((p-1)/2)a modulo p that exceed p/2.

nodes.name: Genus of a binary quadratic form
nodes.description: A genus is a set of proper equivalence classes of binary quadratic forms of discriminant D that represent the same values modulo D (or 4D); genera partition the form class group and form a quotient group.

nodes.name: Hilbert's theorem on Hilbert polynomial
nodes.description: For a finitely generated graded module over k[X_0,...,X_n], the Hilbert function agrees with a polynomial (the Hilbert polynomial) for all sufficiently large arguments.

nodes.name: Hom functor
