nodes.description: Two finite-dimensional complex representations of a finite group are isomorphic if and only if they have the same character.

nodes.name: Projection formula for representations
nodes.description: The projection onto the isotypic component of type V_i in a representation V is p_i = (dim V_i / |G|) sum_{g in G} conj(chi_i(g)) rho(g).

nodes.name: Representations of abelian groups
nodes.description: Every irreducible complex representation of a finite abelian group is one-dimensional; the number of such equals |G|, and they form the character group G-hat.

nodes.name: Standard representation of S_n
nodes.description: The (n-1)-dimensional irreducible representation of S_n obtained as the complement of the trivial subrepresentation in the permutation representation on C^n.

nodes.name: Sign (alternating) representation
nodes.description: The one-dimensional representation sgn: S_n -> {+1,-1} sending each permutation to its sign; the unique nontrivial one-dimensional representation of S_n for n >= 2.

nodes.name: Character of induced representation
nodes.description: The character of Ind_H^G(sigma) at g in G is chi^G(g) = (1/|H|) sum_{t in G, t^{-1}gt in H} chi_sigma(t^{-1}gt).

nodes.name: Conjugate (transpose) partition
nodes.description: The partition lambda' obtained by transposing the Young diagram of lambda, interchanging rows and columns.

nodes.name: Row group and column group of a Young tableau
nodes.description: For a Young tableau T, the row group R_T is the subgroup of permutations preserving rows, and the column group C_T preserves columns; they generate the Young symmetrizer.

nodes.name: Young symmetrizer
nodes.description: The element c_T = a_T b_T in C[S_d] where a_T = sum_{sigma in R_T} sigma and b_T = sum_{tau in C_T} sgn(tau) tau; the image c_T C[S_d] is an irreducible S_d-module.

nodes.name: Specht module V_lambda
nodes.description: The irreducible representation of S_d corresponding to a partition lambda, constructed as the image of the Young symmetrizer c_T in C[S_d].

nodes.name: Branching rule for S_d
nodes.description: The restriction of the Specht module V_lambda from S_d to S_{d-1} decomposes as Res V_lambda = direct_sum V_mu where mu ranges over all partitions obtained by removing a corner box from lambda.

nodes.name: Sign twist of Specht modules
nodes.description: Tensoring the Specht module V_lambda with the sign representation gives V_{lambda'}, where lambda' is the conjugate partition.

nodes.name: Frobenius character formula
nodes.description: The character value chi^lambda(mu) of the Specht module V_lambda on the conjugacy class of cycle type mu equals the coefficient connecting representation theory of S_d to symmetric functions via the Frobenius characteristic map.

nodes.name: Murnaghan--Nakayama rule
nodes.description: A combinatorial formula for the character chi^lambda(mu) of S_d as an alternating sum over rim-hook (border-strip) tableaux of shape lambda and type mu.

nodes.name: Young's rule
nodes.description: The permutation module M^mu = Ind_{S_mu}^{S_d}(trivial) decomposes as M^mu = direct_sum K_{lambda,mu} V_lambda where K_{lambda,mu} are the Kostka numbers.

nodes.name: Semistandard Young tableau
nodes.description: A filling of a Young diagram with positive integers that is weakly increasing along rows and strictly increasing down columns.

nodes.name: Young subgroup
nodes.description: For a composition mu of d, the subgroup S_mu = S_{mu_1} x ... x S_{mu_k} embedded in S_d as permutations preserving the blocks of sizes mu_i.

nodes.name: Representation ring of symmetric groups
nodes.description: The graded ring R = direct_sum_d R(S_d) with multiplication given by induction of external tensor products, isomorphic to the ring of symmetric functions Lambda via the Frobenius characteristic map.

nodes.name: Center of the group algebra
nodes.description: The center Z(C[G]) consists of class sums for each conjugacy class C; it has dimension equal to the number of conjugacy classes and acts on irreducible representations by scalars.

nodes.name: Primitive idempotents in the group algebra
nodes.description: The central primitive idempotents e_i = (dim V_i / |G|) sum_{g} chi_i(g^{-1}) g in C[G] satisfy e_i e_j = delta_{ij} e_i and sum e_i = 1, giving the Artin-Wedderburn decomposition.

nodes.name: Schur--Weyl duality
nodes.description: The actions of GL(V) and S_d on V^{tensor d} generate each other's commutant, yielding V^{tensor d} = direct_sum S^lambda(V) tensor V_lambda as a (GL(V) x S_d)-module.

nodes.name: Plethysm
nodes.description: The operation on symmetric functions corresponding to composition of polynomial functors: S^lambda(S^mu(V)), whose expansion in the Schur basis is combinatorially difficult.

nodes.name: Matrix Lie group
nodes.description: A closed subgroup of GL(n,C) or GL(n,R); equivalently a Lie group realized as a group of invertible matrices.

nodes.name: One-parameter subgroup of a Lie group
nodes.description: A smooth homomorphism gamma: R -> G from the additive reals to a Lie group, necessarily of the form gamma(t) = exp(tX) for a unique X in the Lie algebra.

nodes.name: Representation of a Lie group
nodes.description: A smooth homomorphism rho: G -> GL(V) from a Lie group to the general linear group of a finite-dimensional vector space.

nodes.name: Lie bracket of matrices
nodes.description: The commutator bracket [A,B] = AB - BA on gl(n), defining the Lie algebra structure on the tangent space at the identity of a matrix Lie group.

nodes.name: Semisimple Lie algebra is a direct sum of simple ideals
nodes.description: A semisimple Lie algebra decomposes uniquely as a direct sum of simple ideals; conversely any direct sum of simple Lie algebras is semisimple.

nodes.name: Preservation of Jordan decomposition under representations
nodes.description: Every representation of a semisimple Lie algebra preserves the abstract Jordan decomposition: phi(x_s) = phi(x)_s and phi(x_n) = phi(x)_n.

nodes.name: Correspondence between Lie group and Lie algebra representations
nodes.description: For a simply connected Lie group G with Lie algebra g, differentiation gives an equivalence between finite-dimensional representations of G and of g.

nodes.name: The Lie algebra sl_2(C)
nodes.description: The 3-dimensional simple complex Lie algebra of 2x2 traceless matrices, with standard basis H, E, F satisfying [H,E]=2E, [H,F]=-2F, [E,F]=H.

nodes.name: Standard basis {H,E,F} of sl_2
nodes.description: The basis H = diag(1,-1), E = e_{12}, F = e_{21} of sl_2(C) with relations [H,E]=2E, [H,F]=-2F, [E,F]=H.

nodes.name: Heisenberg algebra
nodes.description: The nilpotent Lie algebra with basis {p,q,z} and sole nontrivial bracket [p,q]=z; the Lie algebra of the Heisenberg group.

nodes.name: Classification of irreducible representations of sl_2
nodes.description: For each non-negative integer n, there is a unique (n+1)-dimensional irreducible representation V_n of sl_2(C) with weights n, n-2, ..., -n; these exhaust all finite-dimensional irreducibles.

nodes.name: Highest weight vector
nodes.description: A nonzero vector v in a representation annihilated by all positive root vectors (e_alpha.v = 0 for all alpha > 0), generating a highest weight submodule.

nodes.name: The Lie algebra sl_3(C)
nodes.description: The 8-dimensional simple complex Lie algebra of 3x3 traceless matrices, of type A_2 with rank 2; the prototypical example for developing semisimple Lie algebra theory.

nodes.name: Root and root space
nodes.description: A root alpha is a nonzero weight of the adjoint representation; its root space g_alpha = {x in g : [h,x] = alpha(h)x for all h in h} is one-dimensional for semisimple g.

nodes.name: Weight diagram
nodes.description: The graphical depiction of the weights of a representation as lattice points in h*_R with multiplicities, displaying representation structure.

nodes.name: Partial order on weights
nodes.description: The partial order mu <= lambda defined by lambda - mu being a non-negative integer combination of simple roots; every irreducible highest weight module has a unique maximal weight.

nodes.name: Weight lattice
nodes.description: The lattice P = {lambda in h* : <lambda, alpha^v> in Z for all coroots} of integral weights, containing the root lattice Q as a sublattice.

nodes.name: Weyl group action on weights
nodes.description: The Weyl group W preserves the set of weights of any representation, with equal multiplicities on each W-orbit.

nodes.name: Weyl vector rho
nodes.description: The half-sum of positive roots rho = (1/2) sum_{alpha > 0} alpha = omega_1 + ... + omega_n; satisfies <rho, alpha_i^v> = 1 and appears in Weyl character and dimension formulas.

nodes.name: Rank of a Lie algebra
nodes.description: The dimension of a Cartan subalgebra of a semisimple Lie algebra, equivalently the number of simple roots or Dynkin diagram nodes.

nodes.name: Fundamental representations of sl_n
nodes.description: The n-1 fundamental representations of sl_n(C) are the exterior powers Lambda^k(C^n) for k = 1,...,n-1, with highest weights omega_k.

nodes.name: Irreducible representations of sl_n via Young diagrams
nodes.description: The irreducible representations of sl_n are indexed by partitions with at most n-1 parts, realized by the Schur functor S^lambda(C^n).

nodes.name: Weyl dimension formula for sl_n
nodes.description: For sl_n(C) with highest weight lambda, dim V_lambda = prod_{1<=i<j<=n} (l_i - l_j)/(j - i) where l_i = lambda_i + n - i.

nodes.name: Fundamental representations of so_n
nodes.description: The fundamental representations of so_n(C): exterior powers and spin/half-spin representations, varying by type B_m or D_m.

nodes.name: Fundamental representations of sp_{2n}
nodes.description: The n fundamental representations of sp_{2n}(C) obtained as kernels of contraction maps on exterior powers of the standard representation.

nodes.name: Exceptional isomorphisms of low-rank Lie algebras
nodes.description: The coincidences A_1=B_1=C_1, B_2=C_2, D_2=A_1xA_1, A_3=D_3 arising from Dynkin diagram coincidences in small rank.

nodes.name: Spin representation of so_{2m+1}
nodes.description: The unique 2^m-dimensional irreducible representation of so_{2m+1}(C) with highest weight omega_m, constructed via the Clifford algebra.

nodes.name: Half-spin representations of so_{2m}
nodes.description: The two 2^{m-1}-dimensional irreducible representations S+ and S- of so_{2m}(C) corresponding to the two chiralities of the even Clifford algebra.

nodes.name: Triality for so_8
nodes.description: The Dynkin diagram D_4 has an order-3 automorphism that cyclically permutes the vector and two half-spin representations of so_8, giving an outer automorphism of Spin(8).

nodes.name: Weyl denominator formula
nodes.description: The identity sum_{w in W} (-1)^{l(w)} e^{w(rho)} = e^rho prod_{alpha > 0} (1 - e^{-alpha}), the lambda=0 case of the Weyl character formula.

nodes.name: Steinberg's formula for tensor product decomposition
nodes.description: The multiplicity of L(nu) in L(lambda) tensor L(mu) expressed via an alternating sum over pairs of Weyl group elements using the Kostant partition function.

nodes.name: Klimyk's formula
nodes.description: The tensor product L(lambda) tensor L(mu) decomposed by summing over weights of L(mu) with multiplicities, giving a quick but redundant formula.

nodes.name: Cartan involution
nodes.description: An involutive automorphism theta of a real semisimple Lie algebra such that B_theta(X,Y) = -B(X,theta(Y)) is positive definite; gives the Cartan decomposition g = k + p.

nodes.name: Maximal compact subgroup
nodes.description: A compact subgroup K of a connected semisimple Lie group G not contained in any larger compact subgroup; K = G^theta is unique up to conjugacy and G/K is contractible.

nodes.name: Classification of real forms of a complex semisimple Lie algebra
nodes.description: Real forms are classified by conjugacy classes of involutions; they include the compact real form and one or more non-compact forms including the split form.
aliases: real forms of semisimple Lie algebras

nodes.name: Split real form
nodes.description: The real form of a complex semisimple Lie algebra in which a Cartan subalgebra is entirely real (maximally split); e.g., sl_n(R) for sl_n(C).

nodes.name: Satake diagram
nodes.description: A decorated Dynkin diagram encoding a real form: painted/unpainted nodes and arrows classifying real forms of complex semisimple Lie algebras up to isomorphism.

nodes.name: Longest element w_0 of the Weyl group
nodes.description: The unique element w_0 in W of maximal length with w_0(Phi^+) = Phi^-; its length equals |Phi^+| and it sends highest weights to negatives of dual highest weights.

nodes.name: Dual representation via the longest element
nodes.description: The dual of L(lambda) is L(-w_0(lambda)); L(lambda) is self-dual iff -w_0(lambda) = lambda.

nodes.name: Parthasarathy--Ranga Rao--Varadarajan (PRV) theorem
nodes.description: For dominant weights lambda, mu, the irreducible L(lambda + w(mu)) occurs in L(lambda) tensor L(mu) for each w in W, with L(lambda + w_0(mu)) appearing with multiplicity one.

nodes.name: Exceptional Lie algebra G_2
nodes.description: The 14-dimensional exceptional simple complex Lie algebra of rank 2, the automorphism algebra of the octonions.

nodes.name: Exceptional Lie algebra F_4
nodes.description: The 52-dimensional exceptional simple complex Lie algebra of rank 4, the automorphism algebra of the exceptional Jordan algebra.

nodes.name: Exceptional Lie algebra E_6
nodes.description: The 78-dimensional exceptional simple complex Lie algebra of rank 6, with a 27-dimensional fundamental representation.

nodes.name: Exceptional Lie algebra E_7
nodes.description: The 133-dimensional exceptional simple complex Lie algebra of rank 7, with a 56-dimensional fundamental representation.

nodes.name: Exceptional Lie algebra E_8
nodes.description: The 248-dimensional exceptional simple complex Lie algebra of rank 8; its smallest representation is the adjoint (248-dimensional).

nodes.name: Decomposition via character inner products
nodes.function_signature: (chi_V, {chi_i}) -> {m_i}
nodes.description: Compute multiplicities m_i = <chi_V, chi_i> to decompose a representation V into irreducible summands.

nodes.name: Weight string analysis
nodes.function_signature: (g, V, alpha, mu) -> weight_string
nodes.description: Analyze the string of weights through mu in the direction of root alpha using the sl_2-subalgebra, constraining multiplicities and proving integrality.

nodes.name: Clifford algebra construction of spin representations
nodes.function_signature: (V, Q) -> Cl(V,Q) -> spin module S
nodes.description: Construct spin representations via the Clifford algebra Cl(V,Q), identifying so(V) with Cl^2(V) and letting it act on a minimal left ideal.

nodes.name: Character of tensor product
nodes.description: The character of a tensor product of representations satisfies chi_{V \otimes W}(g) = chi_V(g) \cdot chi_W(g) for all g in G.

nodes.name: Character of dual representation
nodes.description: The character of the contragredient representation satisfies chi_{V^*}(g) = \overline{chi_V(g)} = chi_V(g^{-1}) for all g in G.

nodes.name: Decomposition multiplicity formula
nodes.description: The multiplicity of an irreducible representation V_i in a representation V equals the inner product n_i = (chi_V, chi_{V_i}) of their characters.

nodes.name: Regular representation decomposition
nodes.description: The regular representation of a finite group G decomposes as the direct sum of all irreducible representations, each appearing with multiplicity equal to its dimension, so that sum_{i} (dim V_i)^2 = |G|.

nodes.name: Dimension divides group order
nodes.description: The dimension of every irreducible complex representation of a finite group G divides the order |G|.

nodes.name: Character criterion for irreducibility
nodes.description: A representation V of a finite group is irreducible if and only if (chi_V, chi_V) = 1.

nodes.name: Orthonormality of Brauer characters
nodes.description: The Brauer characters of the simple k[G]-modules form an orthonormal set with respect to the inner product restricted to p-regular elements.

nodes.name: Brauer-Nesbitt theorem
nodes.description: Two finite-dimensional k[G]-modules have the same composition factors (with multiplicities) if and only if they have the same Brauer character.

nodes.name: Number of simple modules equals p-regular classes
nodes.description: The number of isomorphism classes of simple k[G]-modules equals the number of p-regular conjugacy classes of G.

nodes.name: Cartan matrix is symmetric positive definite
nodes.description: The Cartan matrix C = D^T D of a p-modular system for a finite group is symmetric and positive definite, with determinant equal to a power of p.

nodes.name: p-regular element
nodes.description: An element g of a finite group G whose order is coprime to the prime p.

nodes.name: p-singular element
nodes.description: An element g of a finite group G whose order is divisible by the prime p.

nodes.name: Brauer character
nodes.description: For a representation of G over a field k of characteristic p, the class function on p-regular elements defined by lifting eigenvalues to characteristic zero and summing.

nodes.name: Block of group algebra
nodes.description: An indecomposable two-sided ideal B_i of k[G] as a direct summand algebra, so that k[G] = B_1 x ... x B_r and each indecomposable module belongs to exactly one block.

nodes.name: Defect group
nodes.description: A p-subgroup D of G associated to a block B of k[G], maximal with the property that e_B lies in the image of the relative trace map from C_G(D), unique up to G-conjugacy.

nodes.name: p-modular system
nodes.description: A triple (K, A, k) where A is a complete discrete valuation ring with field of fractions K of characteristic 0 and residue field k of characteristic p, used to pass between ordinary and modular representations.

nodes.name: Decomposition map
nodes.description: The group homomorphism d: R_K(G) -> R_k(G) sending a characteristic-zero representation to its reduction modulo p via an integral form.

nodes.name: Decomposition matrix
nodes.description: The matrix D = (d_{ij}) where d_{ij} is the multiplicity of the j-th simple k[G]-module as a composition factor in the reduction modulo p of the i-th ordinary irreducible representation.

nodes.name: Cartan matrix for modular representations
nodes.description: The matrix C = (c_{ij}) where c_{ij} is the multiplicity of the j-th simple k[G]-module as a composition factor of the projective cover of the i-th simple k[G]-module, satisfying C = D^T D.

nodes.name: Projective indecomposable module
nodes.description: An indecomposable projective k[G]-module, which is the projective cover of a simple module and whose isomorphism classes biject with simple k[G]-modules.

nodes.name: CDE triangle
nodes.description: The commutative triangle of group homomorphisms R_K(G) --d--> R_k(G) --c--> R_k(G) --e--> R_K(G) relating the decomposition map d, the Cartan map c, and the lifting map e, with c = d o e.

nodes.name: Cartan map
nodes.description: The group homomorphism c: P_k(G) -> R_k(G) from the Grothendieck group of projective k[G]-modules to R_k(G), sending a projective module to its class in the Grothendieck group.

nodes.name: Lifting map (Brauer)
nodes.description: The group homomorphism e: R_k(G) -> R_K(G) sending the class of a simple k[G]-module to the virtual character obtained by lifting its Brauer character.

nodes.name: Grothendieck group of modular representations
nodes.description: The Grothendieck group R_k(G) of finite-dimensional k[G]-modules modulo short exact sequences, where k is a field of characteristic p dividing |G|.

nodes.name: Generalized decomposition numbers
nodes.description: The algebraic integers d^u_{chi,phi} expressing the value of an ordinary character chi at a p-singular element us as chi(us) = sum_phi d^u_{chi,phi} phi(u), where phi ranges over irreducible Brauer characters of C_G(u).

nodes.name: Defect zero block
nodes.description: A block whose defect group is trivial, containing a single ordinary irreducible character whose degree is divisible by the full p-part of |G| and a single simple module that is also projective.

nodes.name: Block idempotent
nodes.description: A primitive central idempotent e_i in k[G] corresponding to a block B_i, satisfying k[G]e_i = B_i and sum e_i = 1.

nodes.name: Kernel of representation
nodes.description: The normal subgroup ker(rho) = {g in G : rho(g) = id_V} consisting of group elements acting trivially in a representation rho: G -> GL(V).

nodes.name: Inflation of representation
nodes.description: For a normal subgroup N of G and a representation rho of G/N, the representation inf(rho) of G obtained by composing rho with the quotient map G -> G/N.

nodes.name: Projective cover
nodes.description: For a finitely generated k[G]-module M, the projective module P(M) with an essential epimorphism P(M) -> M, unique up to isomorphism, whose existence is guaranteed by the Krull-Schmidt theorem for k[G].

nodes.name: Semi-direct product representation construction
nodes.function_signature: (Semi-direct product G = N rtimes H, irreducible representations of N and stabilizers in H) -> (Classification of irreducible representations of G)
nodes.description: Classifies irreducible representations of a semi-direct product by choosing an orbit of H on irreducible representations of N, picking a representative with its stabilizer, and inducing up from the stabilizer.

nodes.name: Averaging projection technique
nodes.function_signature: (Representation rho: G -> GL(V), subspace or linear map) -> (G-invariant projection or G-equivariant map)
nodes.description: Constructs a G-equivariant projection or intertwiner by averaging an arbitrary linear map over the group: pi = (1/|G|) sum_{g in G} rho(g).

nodes.name: Reduction modulo p for representations
nodes.function_signature: (Representation over K, A-lattice) -> (Representation over k = A/m)
nodes.description: Obtains a modular representation by choosing a G-stable A-lattice L in a K[G]-module V and reducing modulo the maximal ideal m to get the k[G]-module L/mL.

nodes.name: General linear Lie algebra gl(V)
nodes.description: The Lie algebra End(V) with bracket [x,y] = xy − yx, the associative algebra of all endomorphisms of a vector space V viewed as a Lie algebra.

nodes.name: Special linear Lie algebra sl(n,F)
nodes.description: The Lie subalgebra of gl(n,F) consisting of traceless matrices, simple for n ≥ 2 when char F does not divide n.

nodes.name: Classical Lie algebras (types B, C, D)
nodes.description: The orthogonal Lie algebras so(2l+1,F) (type B_l), symplectic sp(2l,F) (type C_l), and orthogonal so(2l,F) (type D_l), defined as matrices preserving a nondegenerate bilinear form.

nodes.name: Toral subalgebra
nodes.description: A subalgebra of a semisimple Lie algebra consisting entirely of ad-semisimple (ad-diagonalizable) elements; always abelian.

nodes.name: Maximal toral subalgebra
nodes.description: A toral subalgebra not properly contained in any other toral subalgebra; in a split semisimple Lie algebra over an algebraically closed field, equals the Cartan subalgebra.

nodes.name: Regular element of a Lie algebra
nodes.description: An element x of a Lie algebra L whose centralizer has the minimal possible dimension among all elements; equivalently, α(h) ≠ 0 for all roots α when x = h ∈ H.

nodes.name: Saturated set of weights
nodes.description: A subset S of the weight lattice such that if λ ∈ S and α ∈ Φ with ⟨λ,α⟩ > 0, then λ − α ∈ S; the set of weights of any finite-dimensional module is saturated.

nodes.name: Admissible lattice
nodes.description: A ℤ-lattice M in a finite-dimensional L-module V stable under all divided powers e_α^(n) = e_α^n/n! for all roots α and n ≥ 0, enabling reduction modulo a prime.

nodes.name: Derived series of a Lie algebra
nodes.description: The descending chain L^(0) = L, L^(i+1) = [L^(i), L^(i)] of iterated commutator ideals; its termination at zero defines solvability.

nodes.name: Lower central series of a Lie algebra
nodes.description: The descending chain L^0 = L, L^i = [L, L^(i−1)] used to define nilpotency; L is nilpotent iff L^n = 0 for some n.

nodes.name: Nilradical of a Lie algebra
nodes.description: The largest nilpotent ideal of a Lie algebra L, containing [L, Rad(L)] and contained in the radical.

nodes.name: Reflection s_α in a root system
nodes.description: The orthogonal reflection s_α(β) = β − ⟨β,α⟩α in the hyperplane perpendicular to the root α; generates the Weyl group and preserves the root system.

nodes.name: Root string
nodes.description: The α-string through β: the set {β + iα : −r ≤ i ≤ q} for maximal r,q ≥ 0 with β−rα, β+qα ∈ Φ, satisfying r − q = ⟨β,α⟩.

nodes.name: Height of a root
nodes.description: For a root β = Σ k_i α_i expressed in simple roots, ht(β) = Σ k_i; simple roots have height 1 and the highest root has maximal height.

nodes.name: Fundamental Weyl chamber
nodes.description: The open cone C(Δ) = {v ∈ E : (v,α_i) > 0 for all simple roots α_i ∈ Δ}, a fundamental domain for the Weyl group action on the Euclidean space.

nodes.name: Length function on the Weyl group
nodes.description: The function l(w) giving the minimum number of simple reflections needed to express w ∈ W; equivalently, l(w) equals the number of positive roots sent to negative roots by w.

nodes.name: Automorphism group of a root system
nodes.description: Aut(Φ) = W ⋊ Γ where W is the Weyl group and Γ is the group of Dynkin diagram automorphisms (graph automorphisms of the Dynkin diagram).

nodes.name: Triangular decomposition
nodes.description: The direct sum decomposition L = N⁻ ⊕ H ⊕ N⁺ of a semisimple Lie algebra, where N⁺ = ⊕_{α>0} L_α, N⁻ = ⊕_{α<0} L_α, and H is the Cartan subalgebra.

nodes.name: Filtration of the universal enveloping algebra
nodes.description: The canonical filtration U_0 ⊆ U_1 ⊆ ··· of U(L) by degree, whose associated graded algebra gr(U(L)) is isomorphic to the symmetric algebra S(L) by the PBW theorem.

nodes.name: Center of the universal enveloping algebra
nodes.description: Z(U(L)) for semisimple L is a polynomial algebra in l = rank(L) generators, isomorphic to S(H*)^W via the Harish-Chandra homomorphism.

nodes.name: Simple highest weight module L(λ)
nodes.description: The unique irreducible quotient L(λ) = M(λ)/N(λ) of the Verma module M(λ); finite-dimensional if and only if λ is a dominant integral weight.

nodes.name: Dot action (shifted Weyl group action)
nodes.description: The shifted action w · λ = w(λ + ρ) − ρ of the Weyl group W on H*, under which the Harish-Chandra central character is constant on W-orbits.

nodes.name: Character of a Verma module
nodes.description: ch(M(λ)) = e(λ) / ∏_{α∈Φ⁺}(1 − e(−α)) = e(λ) · P where P is the Kostant partition function generating series.

nodes.name: Ring of formal characters
nodes.description: The subring ℤ[Λ]^W of Weyl-group-invariant elements of the group ring ℤ[Λ], where ch(V⊗W) = ch(V)·ch(W) and ch(V⊕W) = ch(V)+ch(W).

nodes.name: Integral structure constants of a Chevalley basis
nodes.description: The structure constants N_{α,β} satisfying [e_α, e_β] = N_{α,β} e_{α+β} with N_{α,β} = ±(r+1) where r is the largest integer with β−rα ∈ Φ; always integers.

nodes.name: Kostant's ℤ-form
nodes.description: The ℤ-subalgebra U_ℤ of U(L) generated by the divided powers e_α^(n) = e_α^n/n!, providing an integral form of the universal enveloping algebra compatible with admissible lattices.

nodes.name: Root subgroup of a Chevalley group
nodes.description: The one-parameter subgroup X_α = {x_α(t) : t ∈ k} ⊂ G(Φ,k) corresponding to each root α, where x_α(t) = exp(t·e_α); the root subgroups generate the Chevalley group.

nodes.name: Steinberg relations in Chevalley groups
nodes.description: The commutator relations [x_α(t), x_β(u)] = ∏ x_{iα+jβ}(c_{ij} t^i u^j) for α+β ≠ 0 in a Chevalley group, with integer constants c_{ij} determined by the root system structure constants.

nodes.name: Dual Coxeter number
nodes.description: The integer h∨ = 1 + ⟨ρ, θ∨⟩ where θ is the highest root; equals (dim L)/rank − 1 and governs the normalization of the Killing form.

nodes.name: Highest root
nodes.description: The unique root θ of maximum height in a root system Φ, satisfying ⟨θ, α_i⟩ ≥ 0 for all simple roots α_i; its height equals h − 1 where h is the Coxeter number.

nodes.name: Invariant bilinear form on a module
nodes.description: A nondegenerate L-invariant symmetric bilinear form on the irreducible module L(λ) exists if and only if λ = −w_0(λ), where w_0 is the longest element of the Weyl group.

nodes.name: Minuscule weight
nodes.description: A dominant weight ω such that the Weyl group orbit W·ω equals the full set of weights of L(ω), i.e., all weights have multiplicity 1 and form a single orbit.

nodes.name: Simultaneous triangularization (corollary of Lie's theorem)
nodes.description: Every solvable Lie subalgebra of gl(V) over an algebraically closed field of characteristic 0 can be simultaneously upper-triangularized with respect to some basis of V.

nodes.name: Decomposition of semisimple Lie algebras into simple ideals
nodes.description: A finite-dimensional semisimple Lie algebra decomposes uniquely as a direct sum L = L_1 ⊕ ··· ⊕ L_k of simple ideals, and every ideal of L is a sum of some subset of these simple summands.

nodes.name: All derivations are inner (semisimple case)
nodes.description: For a semisimple Lie algebra L, every derivation is inner: Der(L) = ad(L), so Aut(L)₀ = Int(L).

nodes.name: Properties of the root space decomposition
nodes.description: For a semisimple Lie algebra: [L_α, L_β] ⊆ L_{α+β}; L_α and L_β are Killing-form-orthogonal unless α+β=0; each root space L_α is 1-dimensional; and α ∈ Φ implies −α ∈ Φ.

nodes.name: Existence and conjugacy of bases of root systems
nodes.description: Every root system possesses a base (simple system), and any two bases are conjugate under the action of the Weyl group; bases correspond bijectively to Weyl chambers.

nodes.name: Simple reflections generate the Weyl group
nodes.description: The Weyl group W is generated by the simple reflections s_{α_1}, ..., s_{α_l}; together with the relations (s_i s_j)^{m_{ij}} = 1 they form a finite Coxeter group.

nodes.name: Cartan matrix determines the root system
nodes.description: The Cartan matrix A = (⟨α_i,α_j⟩) of a base determines the root system up to isomorphism, and equivalently determines the Weyl group and the Lie algebra up to isomorphism.

nodes.name: Isomorphism theorem for semisimple Lie algebras
nodes.description: Two semisimple Lie algebras over an algebraically closed field of characteristic 0 are isomorphic if and only if their root systems are isomorphic.

nodes.name: Conjugacy of Borel subalgebras
nodes.description: Any two Borel subalgebras (maximal solvable subalgebras) of a semisimple Lie algebra are conjugate under the group Int(L) of inner automorphisms.

nodes.name: Chevalley's theorem on invariant polynomials
nodes.description: The algebra S(H*)^W of W-invariant polynomial functions on the Cartan subalgebra H is a polynomial algebra in l = rank(L) algebraically independent homogeneous generators.

nodes.name: Universal property of the enveloping algebra
nodes.description: For any associative algebra A and Lie algebra homomorphism φ: L → A^{Lie}, there exists a unique algebra homomorphism Φ: U(L) → A extending φ; L-modules correspond bijectively to U(L)-modules.

nodes.name: Chevalley's theorem on integral bases
nodes.description: Every complex semisimple Lie algebra admits a Chevalley basis with integer structure constants, obtained by careful normalization of root vectors using sl(2)-representation theory.

nodes.name: Structure of Aut(L) for semisimple L
nodes.description: For a semisimple Lie algebra L, Aut(L)/Int(L) is isomorphic to the automorphism group Aut(Δ) of the Dynkin diagram; the full automorphism group is a semidirect product Int(L) ⋊ Aut(Δ).

nodes.name: Simplicity of Chevalley groups
nodes.description: For most fields k and irreducible root systems Φ of rank ≥ 1, the quotient G(Φ,k)/Z(G(Φ,k)) is a simple group, with explicit small exceptions for |k| ≤ 3 and rank 1–2 cases.

nodes.name: Dynkin diagram classification by elimination
nodes.function_signature: (Cartan matrix, Dynkin diagram) → (classified irreducible root systems A_l–G_2)
nodes.description: Classifies connected Dynkin diagrams by exploiting the constraint a_{ij}a_{ji} ∈ {0,1,2,3} and cos²θ = a_{ij}a_{ji}/4 to systematically eliminate impossible subdiagrams.

nodes.name: Explicit construction of root systems
nodes.function_signature: (root system type A_l–G_2) → (root system in ℝ^n)
nodes.description: Constructs each irreducible root system A_l through G_2 explicitly as a set of vectors in ℝ^n using standard basis vectors e_i, verifying root system axioms.

nodes.name: PBW basis construction
nodes.function_signature: (Lie algebra L, ordered basis) → (monomial basis of U(L))
nodes.description: Constructs the Poincaré–Birkhoff–Witt monomial basis {x_1^{a_1}···x_n^{a_n}} of U(L) from an ordered basis of L, establishing that gr(U(L)) ≅ S(L).

nodes.name: Verma module construction by parabolic induction
nodes.function_signature: (U(L), Borel subalgebra B, weight λ) → (Verma module M(λ), simple module L(λ))
nodes.description: Induces from the 1-dimensional B-module F_λ to construct M(λ) = U(L) ⊗_{U(B)} F_λ ≅ U(N⁻) as a vector space; the unique simple quotient L(λ) is finite-dimensional iff λ ∈ Λ⁺.

nodes.name: Complete reducibility via Casimir element
nodes.function_signature: (semisimple L, Killing form κ, module V) → (V is completely reducible)
nodes.description: Proves Weyl's complete reducibility theorem using the Casimir element c_κ ∈ Z(U(L)): since c_κ acts by the scalar (λ,λ+2ρ) on L(λ), distinct irreducible summands are separated by eigenvalues.

nodes.name: Freudenthal's recursive multiplicity algorithm
nodes.function_signature: (highest weight λ, Killing form) → (weight multiplicities dim V_μ)
nodes.description: Computes weight multiplicities top-down: starting from dim V_λ = 1 and descending through the partial order, using Freudenthal's recursive formula involving inner products and already-computed higher multiplicities.

nodes.name: Killing form computation via roots
nodes.function_signature: (Lie algebra L, root space decomposition) → (explicit Killing form values)
nodes.description: Computes the Killing form explicitly using κ(h,h') = Σ_{α∈Φ} α(h)α(h') for h,h' ∈ H, reducing the trace computation to a sum over roots.

nodes.name: Cartan subalgebra construction from regular elements
nodes.function_signature: (Lie algebra L, regular element x) → (Cartan subalgebra H)
nodes.description: Constructs a Cartan subalgebra as the Fitting null-component (generalized 0-eigenspace) of ad x for a regular element x ∈ L.

nodes.name: Chevalley group construction
nodes.function_signature: (Chevalley basis, root system Φ, field k) → (Chevalley group G(Φ,k))
nodes.description: Exponentiates nilpotent basis elements x_α(t) = exp(t·e_α) in GL(V_k) for an admissible lattice V reduced to a field k, generating the Chevalley group G(Φ,k) of Lie type.

nodes.name: sl(2)-triple technique
nodes.function_signature: (semisimple L, root α) → (sl(2)-subalgebra ⟨e_α, f_α, h_α⟩)
nodes.description: For each root α, constructs e_α ∈ L_α, f_α ∈ L_{-α}, h_α = [e_α, f_α] spanning a subalgebra ≅ sl(2,F), reducing structural questions to sl(2) representation theory.

nodes.name: Ordered set (partially ordered set)
nodes.description: A set S with a relation < satisfying trichotomy and transitivity (total order) or reflexivity, antisymmetry, and transitivity (partial order).

nodes.name: Field axioms
nodes.description: A set F with two operations +, * satisfying commutativity, associativity, distributivity, existence of identity and inverse elements for both operations.

nodes.name: Upper bound and supremum
nodes.description: An element b in an ordered set S is an upper bound for E subset S if x <= b for all x in E; the supremum is the smallest such b.

nodes.name: Lower bound and infimum
nodes.description: An element b in an ordered set S is a lower bound for E subset S if b <= x for all x in E; the infimum is the largest such b.

nodes.name: Dedekind cuts construction of R
nodes.description: Construction of the real numbers as the set of Dedekind cuts in Q, where a cut is a pair (A,B) partitioning Q with every element of A less than every element of B and A having no greatest element.

nodes.name: Uniqueness of least upper bound
nodes.description: If a nonempty subset of an ordered set has a least upper bound, then that least upper bound is unique.

nodes.name: Existence of nth roots in R
nodes.description: For every real x > 0 and positive integer n, there exists a unique positive real y such that y^n = x.

nodes.name: Limit point of a set
nodes.description: A point p in a metric space X is a limit point of E subset X if every neighborhood of p contains a point q in E with q != p.

nodes.name: Isolated point
nodes.description: A point p in E that is not a limit point of E; equivalently, there exists a neighborhood of p containing no other point of E.

nodes.name: Perfect set
nodes.description: A closed set in which every point is a limit point; equivalently, a closed set with no isolated points.

nodes.name: Bounded set in a metric space
nodes.description: A subset E of a metric space (X,d) is bounded if there exists M > 0 and p in X such that d(x,p) < M for all x in E.

nodes.name: Dense set
nodes.description: A subset E of a metric space X is dense if every point of X is a limit point of E or a point of E; equivalently, the closure of E is X.

nodes.name: Open cover
nodes.description: A collection {G_alpha} of open sets whose union contains a given set K; K is compact if every open cover has a finite subcover.

nodes.name: Compact set
nodes.description: A subset K of a topological space such that every open cover of K has a finite subcover.

nodes.name: Separated sets
nodes.description: Two subsets A, B of a metric space are separated if both A intersect closure(B) and closure(A) intersect B are empty.

nodes.name: Countability of the rationals
nodes.description: The set Q of rational numbers is countable, as demonstrated by a bijection with N via diagonal enumeration.

nodes.name: Countable union of countable sets is countable
nodes.description: If {E_n} is a sequence of countable sets, then their union is countable.

nodes.name: Every neighborhood is an open set
nodes.description: In a metric space, every open ball B(p,r) = {x : d(x,p) < r} is an open set.

nodes.name: De Morgan laws for open and closed sets
nodes.description: The complement of a union of sets is the intersection of complements, and vice versa; a set is open iff its complement is closed.

nodes.name: Compact subsets of metric spaces are closed
nodes.description: Every compact subset of a metric space is closed and bounded.

nodes.name: Infinite subset of compact set has a limit point
nodes.description: If E is an infinite subset of a compact set K, then E has a limit point in K.

nodes.name: Every k-cell is compact
nodes.description: Every closed k-cell [a1,b1] x ... x [ak,bk] in R^k is compact.

nodes.name: Compact metric space is separable
nodes.description: Every compact metric space has a countable dense subset and hence a countable base.

nodes.name: Connected subsets of R are intervals
nodes.description: A subset E of R is connected if and only if for any x,y in E with x < z < y, z is in E.

nodes.name: Cantor set
nodes.description: The set obtained by iteratively removing open middle thirds from [0,1]; a perfect, compact, uncountable, nowhere dense set of measure zero.

nodes.name: Cantor diagonalization technique
nodes.function_signature: (Assumed enumeration of a set) -> (Contradiction via constructing element not in enumeration)
nodes.description: Constructs an element differing from each listed element in its corresponding position, proving uncountability or non-surjectivity.

nodes.name: Nested intervals technique
nodes.function_signature: (Sequence of nested closed intervals with lengths tending to 0) -> (Unique point in intersection)
nodes.description: Uses the completeness of R to extract a limit point from a sequence of nested closed intervals whose lengths shrink to zero.

nodes.name: Convergent sequence in a metric space
nodes.description: A sequence {p_n} in a metric space (X,d) converges to p if for every epsilon > 0 there exists N such that d(p_n,p) < epsilon for all n >= N.

nodes.name: Subsequence
nodes.description: A sequence {p_{n_k}} obtained from {p_n} by selecting terms along a strictly increasing sequence of indices n_1 < n_2 < ... .

nodes.name: Subsequential limit
nodes.description: A point p such that some subsequence of a given sequence converges to p; the set of all subsequential limits is denoted E*.

nodes.name: Series convergence
nodes.description: A series sum a_n converges if the sequence of partial sums s_N = sum_{n=1}^{N} a_n converges; otherwise it diverges.

nodes.name: Absolute convergence
nodes.description: A series sum a_n converges absolutely if sum |a_n| converges; absolute convergence implies convergence.

nodes.name: Conditional convergence
nodes.description: A series converges conditionally if it converges but does not converge absolutely.

nodes.name: Power series
nodes.description: A series of the form sum c_n (x - a)^n, converging in a disk of radius R (the radius of convergence) centered at a.

nodes.name: Radius of convergence
nodes.description: The nonneg extended real R such that a power series sum c_n z^n converges absolutely for |z| < R and diverges for |z| > R.

nodes.name: Rearrangement of a series
nodes.description: A series sum a_{sigma(n)} obtained from sum a_n by composing with a bijection sigma: N -> N.

nodes.name: Uniqueness of limits in metric spaces
nodes.description: A convergent sequence in a metric space has exactly one limit.

nodes.name: Convergent sequences are bounded
nodes.description: If {p_n} converges in a metric space, then {p_n} is bounded.

nodes.name: Algebraic limit theorem for sequences
nodes.description: If {s_n} -> s and {t_n} -> t, then s_n + t_n -> s+t, s_n * t_n -> s*t, and s_n/t_n -> s/t (when t != 0).

nodes.name: Subsequences converge to the same limit
nodes.description: If {p_n} converges to p, then every subsequence of {p_n} also converges to p.

nodes.name: Completeness of R^k
nodes.description: The Euclidean space R^k is a complete metric space: every Cauchy sequence in R^k converges.

nodes.name: Limsup and liminf always exist in the extended reals
nodes.description: For any sequence {s_n} of real numbers, lim sup s_n and lim inf s_n always exist in the extended real number system.

nodes.name: Cauchy criterion for series convergence
nodes.description: The series sum a_n converges iff for every epsilon > 0 there exists N such that |sum_{n=m}^{p} a_n| < epsilon for all p >= m >= N.

nodes.name: Comparison test for series
nodes.description: If |a_n| <= c_n for all n >= N_0 and sum c_n converges, then sum a_n converges absolutely.

nodes.name: Cauchy condensation test
nodes.description: If a_1 >= a_2 >= ... >= 0, then sum a_n converges if and only if sum 2^k a_{2^k} converges.

nodes.name: p-series convergence
nodes.description: The series sum 1/n^p converges if and only if p > 1.

nodes.name: Convergence of e = sum 1/n!
nodes.description: The series sum 1/n! converges, and its sum defines the number e; moreover, e is irrational.

nodes.name: Root test (Cauchy)
nodes.description: Let alpha = lim sup |a_n|^{1/n}. If alpha < 1, sum a_n converges absolutely; if alpha > 1, it diverges.

nodes.name: Ratio test (d'Alembert)
nodes.description: If lim sup |a_{n+1}/a_n| < 1, sum a_n converges; if |a_{n+1}/a_n| >= 1 for all n >= N, it diverges.

nodes.name: Root test is at least as strong as ratio test
nodes.description: lim inf |a_{n+1}/a_n| <= lim inf |a_n|^{1/n} <= lim sup |a_n|^{1/n} <= lim sup |a_{n+1}/a_n|.

nodes.name: Absolute convergence implies convergence
nodes.description: If a series sum a_n converges absolutely, then it converges.

nodes.name: Abel's theorem on power series
nodes.description: If sum c_n converges to s, then lim_{x->1^-} sum c_n x^n = s.

nodes.name: Cauchy-Hadamard formula for radius of convergence
nodes.description: The radius of convergence of sum c_n z^n is R = 1 / lim sup |c_n|^{1/n}.

nodes.name: Riemann rearrangement theorem
nodes.description: If sum a_n is conditionally convergent, then for any alpha in [-inf, +inf] there exists a rearrangement converging to alpha.

nodes.name: Dirichlet's test for series convergence
nodes.description: If the partial sums of sum b_n are bounded and {a_n} is monotonically decreasing to 0, then sum a_n b_n converges.

nodes.name: Comparison test technique
nodes.function_signature: (Series sum a_n, dominating convergent series sum c_n) -> (Convergence of sum a_n)
nodes.description: Bounds the terms of a given series by those of a known convergent series to establish convergence.

nodes.name: Root and ratio test technique
nodes.function_signature: (Series sum a_n) -> (Convergence/divergence via lim sup of |a_n|^{1/n} or |a_{n+1}/a_n|)
nodes.description: Applies the root or ratio test to determine convergence by comparing the growth rate of terms to a geometric series.

nodes.name: Abel summation technique
nodes.function_signature: (Partial sums B_n of {b_n}, monotone sequence {a_n}) -> (Sum sum a_n b_n via summation by parts)
nodes.description: Rewrites sum a_n b_n using partial summation (discrete integration by parts) to transfer convergence.

nodes.name: Limit of a function at a point
nodes.description: f(x) -> q as x -> p means: for every epsilon > 0 there exists delta > 0 such that 0 < d(x,p) < delta implies d(f(x),q) < epsilon.

nodes.name: Uniformly continuous function
nodes.description: A function f: X -> Y between metric spaces is uniformly continuous if for every epsilon > 0 there exists delta > 0 such that d(x,y) < delta implies d(f(x),f(y)) < epsilon for all x,y.

nodes.name: Classification of discontinuities
nodes.description: A function has a discontinuity of the first kind (jump) at x if one-sided limits exist but differ; of the second kind if at least one one-sided limit fails to exist.

nodes.name: Composition of continuous functions is continuous
nodes.description: If f: X -> Y and g: Y -> Z are continuous, then g compose f: X -> Z is continuous.

nodes.name: Continuous image of compact set is compact
nodes.description: If f: X -> Y is continuous and K subset X is compact, then f(K) is compact in Y.

nodes.name: Continuous image of connected set is connected
nodes.description: If f: X -> Y is continuous and E subset X is connected, then f(E) is connected.

nodes.name: Monotonic functions have countably many discontinuities
nodes.description: A monotonic function on an interval has at most countably many points of discontinuity, all of the first kind (jumps).

nodes.name: Uniform continuity theorem
nodes.description: A continuous function on a compact metric space is uniformly continuous.

nodes.name: Continuous bijection from compact to Hausdorff is homeomorphism
nodes.description: A continuous bijection from a compact space to a Hausdorff space is a homeomorphism.

nodes.name: Epsilon-delta technique
nodes.function_signature: (Target bound epsilon > 0) -> (Choice of delta > 0 ensuring the bound)
nodes.description: The standard technique for proving limits and continuity by choosing delta as a function of epsilon.

nodes.name: Continuously differentiable function (C^1)
nodes.description: A function f is continuously differentiable on an interval if f' exists and is continuous on that interval.

nodes.name: Differentiability implies continuity
nodes.description: If f is differentiable at a point x, then f is continuous at x.

nodes.name: Local extremum theorem
nodes.description: If f has a local maximum or minimum at an interior point x and f'(x) exists, then f'(x) = 0.

nodes.name: Differentiation of vector-valued functions
nodes.description: The derivative of f: [a,b] -> R^k exists iff each component has a derivative, and f' = (f_1', ..., f_k').

nodes.name: Mean value theorem technique
nodes.function_signature: (Differentiable f on [a,b]) -> (Existence of c in (a,b) with f(b)-f(a) = f'(c)(b-a))
nodes.description: Applies the mean value theorem to connect the global change of a function to its derivative at an intermediate point.

nodes.name: L'Hopital technique
nodes.function_signature: (Indeterminate form 0/0 or inf/inf) -> (Limit via ratio of derivatives)
nodes.description: Evaluates limits of indeterminate forms by replacing f(x)/g(x) with f'(x)/g'(x).

nodes.name: Taylor expansion technique
nodes.function_signature: (n-times differentiable f at a) -> (Polynomial approximation with remainder estimate)
nodes.description: Approximates a function near a point by its Taylor polynomial and estimates the remainder.

nodes.name: Partition of an interval
nodes.description: A finite set of points P = {x_0, x_1, ..., x_n} with a = x_0 < x_1 < ... < x_n = b, dividing [a,b] into subintervals.

nodes.name: Upper and lower Riemann-Stieltjes sums
nodes.description: For bounded f on [a,b] with increasing integrator alpha and partition P: U(P,f,alpha) = sum sup f * Delta alpha and L(P,f,alpha) = sum inf f * Delta alpha.

nodes.name: Riemann-Stieltjes integral
nodes.description: The integral of f with respect to alpha on [a,b], defined as the common value of inf U(P,f,alpha) and sup L(P,f,alpha) when they agree.

nodes.name: Riemann integral
nodes.description: The special case of the Riemann-Stieltjes integral when alpha(x) = x, giving the classical integral of f over [a,b].

nodes.name: Function of bounded variation
nodes.description: A function f on [a,b] has bounded variation if sup sum |f(x_i) - f(x_{i-1})| over all partitions is finite; this supremum is the total variation.

nodes.name: Rectifiable curve and arc length
nodes.description: A continuous curve gamma: [a,b] -> R^k is rectifiable if its arc length Lambda(gamma) = sup sum |gamma(t_i) - gamma(t_{i-1})| is finite.

nodes.name: Riemann-Stieltjes integrability criterion
nodes.description: f is R-S integrable with respect to alpha iff for every epsilon > 0 there exists a partition P with U(P,f,alpha) - L(P,f,alpha) < epsilon.

nodes.name: Continuous functions are R-S integrable
nodes.description: If f is continuous on [a,b] and alpha is monotonically increasing, then f is R-S integrable with respect to alpha.

nodes.name: Monotonic functions are R-S integrable
nodes.description: If f is monotonic on [a,b] and alpha is continuous and monotonically increasing, then f is R-S integrable with respect to alpha.

nodes.name: R-S integral with step function integrator
nodes.description: If alpha has a jump at s and f is continuous at s, then integral f dalpha = a * f(s).

nodes.name: R-S integral reduces to Riemann integral
nodes.description: If alpha is differentiable with alpha' Riemann integrable, then integral f dalpha = integral f(x) alpha'(x) dx.

nodes.name: Linearity of the Riemann-Stieltjes integral
nodes.description: The R-S integral is linear in both the integrand and the integrator.

nodes.name: Additivity of the integral over intervals
nodes.description: If f is integrable on [a,b] and c in (a,b), then integral_a^b f dalpha = integral_a^c f dalpha + integral_c^b f dalpha.

nodes.name: Fundamental theorem of calculus (first form)
nodes.description: If f is Riemann integrable and F(x) = integral_a^x f(t) dt, then F is continuous; if f is continuous at x_0, then F'(x_0) = f(x_0).

nodes.name: Fundamental theorem of calculus (second form)
nodes.description: If F' = f is Riemann integrable on [a,b], then integral_a^b f(x) dx = F(b) - F(a).

nodes.name: Rectifiable curves characterized via bounded variation
nodes.description: A curve gamma is rectifiable iff each component is of bounded variation; if gamma' is continuous, Lambda(gamma) = integral |gamma'(t)| dt.

nodes.name: Riemann-Stieltjes integration technique
nodes.function_signature: (Bounded f, monotone integrator alpha, partition P) -> (Approximation of integral via upper/lower sums)
nodes.description: Computes or estimates integrals by refining partitions and bounding the difference of upper and lower R-S sums.

nodes.name: Pointwise convergence of function sequence
nodes.description: A sequence {f_n} converges pointwise to f on E if for each x in E, lim f_n(x) = f(x).

nodes.name: Uniform convergence of function sequence
nodes.description: {f_n} converges uniformly to f on E if for every epsilon > 0 there exists N such that |f_n(x) - f(x)| < epsilon for all n >= N and all x in E.

nodes.name: Pointwise bounded family of functions
nodes.description: A family {f_n} on E is pointwise bounded if for each x in E there exists M(x) such that |f_n(x)| <= M(x) for all n.

nodes.name: Uniformly bounded family of functions
nodes.description: A family {f_n} on E is uniformly bounded if there exists M such that |f_n(x)| <= M for all n and all x in E.

nodes.name: Algebra of functions and subalgebra of C(X)
nodes.description: An algebra A of continuous functions on a compact set X, closed under pointwise addition, multiplication, and scalar multiplication.

nodes.name: Algebra separating points
nodes.description: An algebra A of functions on X separates points if for any distinct x,y in X there exists f in A with f(x) != f(y).

nodes.name: Self-adjoint algebra of functions
nodes.description: A complex algebra A of functions is self-adjoint if for every f in A, its complex conjugate f-bar is also in A.

nodes.name: Cauchy criterion for uniform convergence
nodes.description: {f_n} converges uniformly on E iff for every epsilon > 0 there exists N such that |f_n(x) - f_m(x)| < epsilon for all m,n >= N and all x in E.

nodes.name: Weierstrass M-test
nodes.description: If |f_n(x)| <= M_n for all x in E and sum M_n converges, then sum f_n converges uniformly and absolutely on E.

nodes.name: Uniform limit of continuous functions is continuous
nodes.description: If {f_n} are continuous and f_n -> f uniformly on E, then f is continuous on E.

nodes.name: Term-by-term integration of uniformly convergent series
nodes.description: If f_n -> f uniformly on [a,b] and each f_n is Riemann integrable, then f is integrable and integral f = lim integral f_n.

nodes.name: Uniform limit of R-S integrable functions is R-S integrable
nodes.description: If {f_n} converges uniformly and each f_n is R-S integrable, then the limit is R-S integrable with integral f dalpha = lim integral f_n dalpha.

nodes.name: Conditions for term-by-term differentiation
nodes.description: If {f_n} converges pointwise at one point and {f_n'} converges uniformly on [a,b], then {f_n} converges uniformly to a differentiable f with f' = lim f_n'.

nodes.name: Equicontinuity with pointwise convergence implies uniform convergence
nodes.description: If {f_n} is equicontinuous on compact K and converges pointwise, then f_n -> f uniformly on K.

nodes.name: Weierstrass M-test technique
nodes.function_signature: (Function series sum f_n, bounds M_n with sum M_n < infty) -> (Uniform and absolute convergence)
nodes.description: Establishes uniform convergence of a function series by bounding each term and verifying convergence of the bound series.

nodes.name: Equicontinuous approximation technique
nodes.function_signature: (Equicontinuous, pointwise bounded family on compact K) -> (Uniformly convergent subsequence)
nodes.description: Uses equicontinuity and pointwise boundedness with Arzela-Ascoli to extract uniformly convergent subsequences.

nodes.name: Stone-Weierstrass approximation technique
nodes.function_signature: (Separating subalgebra A of C(X)) -> (Density of A in C(X))
nodes.description: Approximates continuous functions uniformly by members of a separating subalgebra.

nodes.name: Power series are continuous on their disk of convergence
nodes.description: A power series sum c_n (x-a)^n defines a continuous function on its open disk of convergence.

nodes.name: Uniqueness theorem for power series
nodes.description: If two power series agree on a set with a limit point, then their coefficients are identical.

nodes.name: Term-by-term differentiation of power series
nodes.description: A power series can be differentiated term by term within its radius of convergence, and the derived series has the same radius.

nodes.name: Composition and product of power series
nodes.description: Power series can be multiplied and composed, with the resulting series converging in an appropriate disk.

nodes.name: Exponential functional equation
nodes.description: The exponential function satisfies exp(z+w) = exp(z) exp(w) for all complex z,w.

nodes.name: Gamma function recurrence relation
nodes.description: Gamma(s+1) = s * Gamma(s) for all s > 0, and Gamma(n+1) = n! for positive integers n.

nodes.name: Gamma function is analytic on the right half-plane
nodes.description: The integral Gamma(s) = integral_0^infty t^{s-1} e^{-t} dt defines an analytic function for Re(s) > 0.

nodes.name: Power series manipulation technique
nodes.function_signature: (Power series sum c_n z^n) -> (Term-by-term differentiation, integration, product, composition)
nodes.description: Manipulates power series by differentiating, integrating, multiplying, or composing term by term within the radius of convergence.

nodes.name: Fourier analysis technique
nodes.function_signature: (Periodic or L^2 function f) -> (Fourier coefficients, Parseval identity, convergence analysis)
nodes.description: Expands functions in Fourier series, computes Fourier coefficients, and applies convergence theorems.

nodes.name: Gamma function technique
nodes.function_signature: (Integral or factorial expression) -> (Evaluation via Gamma function properties)
nodes.description: Uses the Gamma function's recurrence, reflection formula, and analytic properties to evaluate integrals.

nodes.name: Total (Frechet) derivative
nodes.description: A function f: R^n -> R^m is differentiable at x if there exists a linear map A with |f(x+h) - f(x) - Ah| / |h| -> 0 as h -> 0.

nodes.name: Partial derivative
nodes.description: The derivative of f(x_1,...,x_n) with respect to x_j, holding all other variables fixed.

nodes.name: Jacobian matrix and determinant
nodes.description: For f: R^n -> R^m differentiable at x, the m x n matrix of partial derivatives; when m=n, its determinant is the Jacobian determinant.

nodes.name: C^1 mapping
nodes.description: A mapping f: E -> R^m (E open in R^n) is C^1 if all partial derivatives exist and are continuous on E.

nodes.name: Chain rule for functions of several variables
nodes.description: If f is differentiable at x and g is differentiable at f(x), then (g compose f)'(x) = g'(f(x)) f'(x), the matrix product of Jacobians.

nodes.name: C^1 implies differentiable
nodes.description: If all partial derivatives of f exist and are continuous, then f is differentiable.

nodes.name: Clairaut's theorem (symmetry of mixed partials)
nodes.description: If the mixed partial derivatives are continuous, then D_i D_j f = D_j D_i f.

nodes.name: Mean value estimate for vector-valued functions
nodes.description: If f: [a,b] -> R^k is continuous and differentiable on (a,b), then |f(b) - f(a)| <= (b-a) sup |f'(t)|.

nodes.name: Inverse function theorem
nodes.description: If f: R^n -> R^n is C^1 and f'(a) is invertible, then f is a C^1 diffeomorphism on a neighborhood of a.

nodes.name: Implicit function theorem
nodes.description: If F: R^{n+m} -> R^n is C^1 and D_x F is invertible at (a,b) with F(a,b) = 0, then near (a,b) the equation F(x,y) = 0 defines x as a C^1 function of y.

nodes.name: Rank theorem (constant rank)
nodes.description: If f: R^n -> R^m is C^1 with constant rank r near a, then there exist C^1 diffeomorphisms putting f in canonical form locally.

nodes.name: Determinant is the unique multilinear alternating form
nodes.description: The determinant is the unique function on n x n matrices that is multilinear and alternating in rows and equals 1 on the identity.

nodes.name: Contraction iteration technique
nodes.function_signature: (Contraction mapping T on complete metric space) -> (Unique fixed point via iterating T)
nodes.description: Produces a fixed point by iterating a strict contraction on a complete metric space.

nodes.name: Inverse and implicit function technique
nodes.function_signature: (C^1 map with invertible derivative) -> (Local diffeomorphism or local solution of equations)
nodes.description: Uses the contraction mapping theorem to produce local inverses or solve systems of equations.

nodes.name: Multilinear algebra technique
nodes.function_signature: (Multilinear alternating form on R^n) -> (Determinant identity or volume computation)
nodes.description: Exploits multilinearity and alternating property to compute determinants and volumes.

nodes.name: k-form on R^n
nodes.description: A k-linear alternating function on R^n; in local coordinates, sum f_I dx_{i_1} wedge ... wedge dx_{i_k}.

nodes.name: Closed differential form
nodes.description: A differential form omega is closed if d(omega) = 0.

nodes.name: Exact differential form
nodes.description: A differential form omega is exact if omega = d(lambda) for some form lambda; every exact form is closed.

nodes.name: Pullback of a differential form
nodes.description: For a C^1 map phi: R^m -> R^n, the pullback phi^* omega of a k-form omega on R^n is a k-form on R^m.

nodes.name: k-surface in R^n
nodes.description: A C^1 mapping Phi from a compact subset of R^k into R^n, serving as the domain of integration for k-forms.

nodes.name: Boundary operator for k-surfaces
nodes.description: The boundary of a k-surface Phi is a (k-1)-chain defined by oriented faces, satisfying del^2 = 0.

nodes.name: Orientation of a k-surface
nodes.description: A consistent choice of sign for the Jacobian determinant of a k-surface parametrization.

nodes.name: d^2 = 0 (exterior derivative is nilpotent)
nodes.description: The exterior derivative d satisfies d(d(omega)) = 0 for every differential form omega.

nodes.name: Pullback commutes with exterior derivative
nodes.description: For a C^1 map phi, phi^*(d omega) = d(phi^* omega).

nodes.name: Exact forms have zero integral over cycles
nodes.description: If omega = d lambda and Phi is a cycle, then integral_Phi omega = 0.

nodes.name: Closed forms are exact in simply connected domains
nodes.description: Every closed k-form on a simply connected open subset of R^n is exact.

nodes.name: Exterior calculus technique
nodes.function_signature: (k-form omega, region with boundary) -> (Integral relation via Stokes' theorem)
nodes.description: Converts integrals of forms over boundaries to integrals of exterior derivatives over interiors.

nodes.name: Pullback technique for differential forms
nodes.function_signature: (Map phi, k-form omega on target) -> (k-form phi^* omega on source)
nodes.description: Pulls back differential forms along smooth maps to transfer integration between domains.

nodes.name: Partition of unity technique
nodes.function_signature: (Open cover of manifold) -> (Subordinate smooth partition summing to 1)
nodes.description: Constructs smooth functions subordinate to an open cover to localize global problems.

nodes.name: Stokes' theorem technique
nodes.function_signature: (k-form omega, oriented k-surface Phi with boundary) -> (integral_{del Phi} omega = integral_Phi d(omega))
nodes.description: Applies generalized Stokes theorem to relate boundary integrals to interior integrals.

nodes.name: Lebesgue integral
nodes.description: For nonneg measurable f, integral f dmu = sup{integral phi dmu : phi simple, 0 <= phi <= f}; for general f, integral f+ dmu - integral f- dmu.

nodes.name: L^1 space
nodes.description: The space of measurable functions f with integral |f| dmu < infty, modulo equality a.e., with norm ||f||_1 = integral |f| dmu.

nodes.name: Set of measure zero
nodes.description: A measurable set E with mu(E) = 0; a property holds almost everywhere if the set where it fails has measure zero.

nodes.name: L^2 space
nodes.description: The space of measurable functions f with integral |f|^2 dmu < infty, forming a Hilbert space with inner product <f,g> = integral f g-bar dmu.

nodes.name: Regularity of Lebesgue measure
nodes.description: Lebesgue measure is regular: every measurable set can be approximated from outside by open sets and inside by compact sets.

nodes.name: Countable additivity of measures
nodes.description: If {E_n} is a sequence of pairwise disjoint measurable sets, then mu(union E_n) = sum mu(E_n).

nodes.name: Measurable functions form an algebra
nodes.description: Sums, products, scalar multiples, sup, inf, lim sup, lim inf of measurable functions are measurable.

nodes.name: Pointwise limit of measurable functions is measurable
nodes.description: If {f_n} is a sequence of measurable functions converging pointwise, then the limit is measurable.

nodes.name: Every measurable function is a limit of simple functions
nodes.description: Every nonneg measurable function is the pointwise limit of an increasing sequence of simple functions.

nodes.name: Comparison of Riemann and Lebesgue integrals
nodes.description: If f is Riemann integrable on [a,b], then f is Lebesgue measurable and the two integrals agree.

nodes.name: Characterization of Riemann integrability
nodes.description: A bounded function on [a,b] is Riemann integrable iff the set of its discontinuities has Lebesgue measure zero.

nodes.name: L^2 is a Hilbert space
nodes.description: L^2(mu) with inner product <f,g> = integral f g-bar dmu is complete, hence a Hilbert space.

nodes.name: Lebesgue integration technique
nodes.function_signature: (Measurable function f, measure mu) -> (Integral via simple function approximation)
nodes.description: Computes integrals by approximating measurable functions with simple functions and using monotone convergence.

nodes.name: Dominated convergence technique
nodes.function_signature: (Pointwise convergent {f_n}, dominating integrable g) -> (lim integral f_n = integral lim f_n)
nodes.description: Justifies passing limits under the integral when functions are dominated by an integrable function.

nodes.name: Monotone convergence technique
nodes.function_signature: (Increasing sequence of nonneg measurable {f_n}) -> (integral lim f_n = lim integral f_n)
nodes.description: Passes limits under the integral for increasing sequences of nonnegative measurable functions.

nodes.name: Fatou's lemma technique
nodes.function_signature: (Sequence of nonneg measurable {f_n}) -> (integral lim inf f_n <= lim inf integral f_n)
nodes.description: Provides a one-sided inequality for limits of integrals when domination is unavailable.

nodes.name: Separable metric space has a countable base
nodes.description: Every separable metric space is second-countable.

nodes.name: Measurable function
nodes.description: A function f: X -> Y between measurable spaces such that f^{-1}(E) is in M for every E in N.

nodes.name: Positive measure
nodes.description: A countably additive set function mu: M -> [0, infinity] on a sigma-algebra M with mu(emptyset) = 0.

nodes.name: Complex measure
nodes.description: A countably additive set function nu: M -> C on a sigma-algebra, necessarily of bounded total variation.

nodes.name: Vitali-Carathéodory theorem
nodes.description: Every integrable function on a locally compact Hausdorff space can be approximated in L1 norm from above by lower semicontinuous and from below by upper semicontinuous functions.

nodes.name: Completion of a measure space
nodes.description: The smallest extension of (X, M, mu) in which every subset of a null set is measurable, obtained by adding all such subsets.

nodes.name: Hardy-Littlewood maximal function
nodes.description: For f in L^1_loc(R^n), the maximal function Mf(x) = sup_{r>0} (1/|B(x,r)|) integral_{B(x,r)} |f(y)| dy, a measurable function controlling local averages.

nodes.name: Lebesgue point
nodes.description: A point x is a Lebesgue point of f in L^1_loc if lim_{r->0} (1/|B(x,r)|) integral_{B(x,r)} |f(y) - f(x)| dy = 0; almost every point is a Lebesgue point.

nodes.name: Absolutely continuous function
nodes.description: A function F on [a,b] such that for every epsilon > 0 there exists delta > 0 with sum |F(b_i) - F(a_i)| < epsilon whenever the intervals (a_i, b_i) are disjoint and sum (b_i - a_i) < delta.

nodes.name: Fundamental theorem of calculus for Lebesgue integration
nodes.description: A function F on [a,b] is absolutely continuous if and only if F' exists a.e., F' is in L^1, and F(x) - F(a) = integral_a^x F'(t) dt for all x in [a,b].

nodes.name: Rising sun lemma
nodes.description: If f is a continuous real function on R, the open set {x : there exists y > x with f(y) > f(x)} is a disjoint union of intervals (a_n, b_n) with f(a_n) <= f(b_n).

nodes.name: Cantor function (devil's staircase)
nodes.description: A continuous nondecreasing surjection from [0,1] to [0,1] that is constant on each complementary interval of the Cantor set, with derivative zero a.e. but not absolutely continuous.

nodes.name: Fourier inversion formula on R^n
nodes.description: If f and its Fourier transform f_hat are both in L^1(R^n), then f(x) = integral_{R^n} f_hat(xi) e^{2 pi i x . xi} d xi for a.e. x.

nodes.name: Fourier transform is an automorphism of Schwartz space
nodes.description: The Fourier transform is a continuous linear bijection from the Schwartz space S(R^n) onto itself, with continuous inverse given by the inverse Fourier transform.

nodes.name: Cauchy integral formula for derivatives
nodes.description: If f is holomorphic inside and on a simple closed curve gamma, then f^{(n)}(a) = (n!/(2 pi i)) integral_gamma f(z)/(z-a)^{n+1} dz for all a inside gamma.

nodes.name: Power series representation of holomorphic functions
nodes.description: Every holomorphic function on a domain has a local power series expansion f(z) = sum a_n (z-z_0)^n converging in the largest disk centered at z_0 contained in the domain.

nodes.name: Isolated zeros of holomorphic functions
nodes.description: The zeros of a nonconstant holomorphic function on a connected domain are isolated, and each zero has a finite positive order.

nodes.name: Classification of isolated singularities
nodes.description: An isolated singularity of a holomorphic function is exactly one of: removable (bounded near the point), a pole (|f(z)| -> infinity), or essential (Casorati-Weierstrass dense image).

nodes.name: Calculus of residues
nodes.function_signature: (Meromorphic function, contour) -> (Integral value)
nodes.description: Evaluation of contour integrals and real definite integrals by identifying poles, computing residues, and applying the residue theorem.

nodes.name: Cauchy estimates for derivatives
nodes.description: If f is holomorphic on |z - z_0| < R and |f| <= M there, then |f^{(n)}(z_0)| <= n! M / R^n.

nodes.name: Möbius transformation
nodes.description: A bijective holomorphic map of the Riemann sphere of the form z -> (az+b)/(cz+d) with ad-bc != 0, forming the group PSL(2,C); the automorphism group of the Riemann sphere.

nodes.name: Automorphisms of the unit disk
nodes.description: Every biholomorphic self-map of the unit disk D has the form z -> e^{i theta} (z - a)/(1 - bar{a} z) for some |a| < 1 and theta in R.

nodes.name: Normal family of holomorphic functions
nodes.description: A family F of holomorphic functions on a domain Omega such that every sequence in F has a subsequence converging uniformly on compact subsets of Omega.

nodes.name: Blaschke product
nodes.description: A product B(z) = z^m prod_n (|a_n|/a_n)(a_n - z)/(1 - bar{a_n} z) with sum (1 - |a_n|) < infinity, forming a bounded holomorphic inner function on the unit disk.

nodes.name: Blaschke condition
nodes.description: A sequence {a_n} in the unit disk is the zero set of some bounded holomorphic function if and only if sum (1 - |a_n|) < infinity.

nodes.name: Müntz-Szász theorem
nodes.description: The span of {x^{lambda_n}} is dense in C([0,1]) if and only if sum 1/lambda_n = infinity, where 0 < lambda_1 < lambda_2 < ... .

nodes.name: Hardy space H^p on the disk
nodes.description: The space of holomorphic functions f on the unit disk with sup_{0<r<1} (1/(2 pi) integral_0^{2 pi} |f(r e^{i theta})|^p d theta)^{1/p} < infinity, for 0 < p < infinity.

nodes.name: Fatou's theorem on radial limits
nodes.description: Every bounded holomorphic function on the unit disk has nontangential limits at almost every point of the boundary circle.

nodes.name: Poisson kernel for the unit disk
nodes.description: The kernel P_r(theta) = (1 - r^2)/(1 - 2r cos theta + r^2) such that the Poisson integral of an L^p boundary function is harmonic in the disk and converges nontangentially to the boundary values a.e.

nodes.name: Poisson integral representation
nodes.description: A harmonic function u in the unit disk with sup_r integral |u(r e^{i theta})| d theta < infinity is the Poisson integral of a unique finite Borel measure on the circle.

nodes.name: F. and M. Riesz theorem
nodes.description: If mu is a finite complex Borel measure on the unit circle whose negative Fourier coefficients all vanish, then mu is absolutely continuous with respect to Lebesgue measure.

nodes.name: Inner function
nodes.description: A bounded holomorphic function on the unit disk whose nontangential boundary values have modulus 1 almost everywhere; decomposes as a Blaschke product times a singular inner function.

nodes.name: Outer function
nodes.description: A function of the form F(z) = c exp((1/(2 pi)) integral (e^{i theta} + z)/(e^{i theta} - z) log psi(theta) d theta) for a positive function psi with log psi in L^1, characterized by having no inner factor.

nodes.name: Canonical factorization of H^p functions
nodes.description: Every nonzero H^p function (0 < p <= infinity) factors uniquely as f = B S F where B is a Blaschke product, S a singular inner function, and F an outer function.

nodes.name: Beurling's theorem on invariant subspaces of H^2
nodes.description: Every closed subspace of H^2 that is invariant under multiplication by z has the form phi H^2 for some inner function phi, unique up to a scalar of modulus 1.

nodes.name: Subharmonic function
nodes.description: An upper semicontinuous function u on a domain Omega in R^n (or C) satisfying the sub-mean-value property: u(x) <= (1/|partial B|) integral_{partial B} u d sigma for every ball B with closure in Omega.

nodes.name: Poisson kernel
nodes.description: The kernel P(x, y) for the unit ball in R^n reconstructing harmonic functions from boundary values: u(x) = integral_{S^{n-1}} P(x, y) f(y) d sigma(y).

nodes.name: M. Riesz conjugate function theorem
nodes.description: The Hilbert transform (conjugate function operator) is bounded on L^p(T) for 1 < p < infinity, with norm depending only on p.

nodes.name: Vitali-Carathéodory approximation technique
nodes.function_signature: (L^1 function) -> (Semicontinuous approximants)
nodes.description: Approximates an integrable function from above by lower semicontinuous and from below by upper semicontinuous functions with controlled L^1 error.

nodes.name: Nevanlinna class
nodes.description: The class N of holomorphic functions f on the unit disk satisfying sup_{0<r<1} integral_0^{2 pi} log^+ |f(r e^{i theta})| d theta < infinity, the largest class admitting canonical factorization.

nodes.name: Duality technique for L^p bounds
nodes.function_signature: (Operator bound on L^p) -> (Bound on adjoint on L^q)
nodes.description: Establishes operator bounds on L^p by proving the dual bound on L^q via the duality ||T||_{p->p} = sup {|integral Tf g| : ||f||_p = ||g||_q = 1} with 1/p + 1/q = 1.

nodes.name: Maximal function technique
nodes.function_signature: (Pointwise convergence problem) -> (Weak-type bound on maximal operator)
nodes.description: Reduces almost-everywhere convergence of operators to a weak-type (1,1) or strong-type bound on the associated maximal operator.

nodes.name: Szegő theorem
nodes.description: For a positive Borel measure mu on the unit circle with absolutely continuous part w d theta, the distance from 1 to the closed span of {e^{i n theta} : n >= 1} in L^2(mu) equals exp((1/(4 pi)) integral log w d theta).

nodes.name: Log-integrability condition for H^p
nodes.description: A nonnegative function psi on the circle is the modulus of the boundary values of some H^p function (0 < p <= infinity) if and only if log psi is integrable with respect to Lebesgue measure.

nodes.name: Conformal mapping technique
nodes.function_signature: (Problem on domain Omega) -> (Problem on canonical domain D or H)
nodes.description: Transfers function-theoretic problems to a canonical domain (disk or half-plane) via the Riemann mapping theorem, solves there, and maps back.

nodes.name: Schwarz-Christoffel formula
nodes.description: The conformal map from the upper half-plane to a polygon with interior angles alpha_k pi is f'(z) = C prod (z - x_k)^{alpha_k - 1}, where x_k are the prevertices on the real axis.

nodes.name: σ-algebra
nodes.description: A nonempty collection M of subsets of X closed under complementation and countable unions, with X in M.

nodes.name: Semifinite measure
nodes.description: A measure μ such that for every measurable set E with μ(E) = ∞, there exists a measurable subset F ⊂ E with 0 < μ(F) < ∞.

nodes.name: Counting measure
nodes.description: The measure on the power set of X defined by μ(E) = |E| if E is finite and μ(E) = ∞ if E is infinite.

nodes.name: Monotonicity of measures
nodes.description: If E ⊂ F are measurable sets, then μ(E) ≤ μ(F).

nodes.name: Subadditivity of measures
nodes.description: For any countable collection {E_j} of measurable sets, μ(⋃ E_j) ≤ Σ μ(E_j).

nodes.name: Continuity from below for measures
nodes.description: If E_1 ⊂ E_2 ⊂ ··· is an increasing sequence of measurable sets, then μ(⋃ E_j) = lim μ(E_j).

nodes.name: Continuity from above for measures
nodes.description: If E_1 ⊃ E_2 ⊃ ··· is a decreasing sequence of measurable sets with μ(E_1) < ∞, then μ(⋂ E_j) = lim μ(E_j).

nodes.name: Complete measure
nodes.description: A measure space (X, M, μ) is complete if every subset of a μ-null set belongs to M.

nodes.name: Carathéodory measurability (μ*-measurable set)
nodes.description: A set E is μ*-measurable if μ*(A) = μ*(A ∩ E) + μ*(A ∩ E^c) for all A ⊂ X, where μ* is an outer measure.

nodes.name: Carathéodory's theorem (outer measure restriction)
nodes.description: The collection of μ*-measurable sets forms a σ-algebra, and the restriction of μ* to this σ-algebra is a complete measure.

nodes.name: Algebra of sets
nodes.description: A nonempty collection A of subsets of X closed under finite unions and complementation.

nodes.name: Outer measure induced by a premeasure
nodes.type_signature: Premeasure μ₀ on algebra A → Outer measure μ* on P(X)
nodes.description: The outer measure μ*(E) = inf{Σ μ₀(A_j) : E ⊂ ⋃ A_j, each A_j ∈ A} defined from a premeasure μ₀ on an algebra A.

nodes.name: Translation invariance of Lebesgue measure
nodes.description: For any Lebesgue measurable set E ⊂ ℝⁿ and any x ∈ ℝⁿ, the translate E + x is measurable and m(E + x) = m(E).

nodes.name: Dilation property of Lebesgue measure
nodes.description: For any Lebesgue measurable set E ⊂ ℝⁿ and r > 0, m(rE) = rⁿ m(E).

nodes.name: Non-Lebesgue-measurable set (Vitali set)
nodes.type_signature: Axiom of Choice → Subset of ℝ not in Lebesgue σ-algebra
