nodes.description: A subset of [0,1] constructed via the axiom of choice by selecting one representative from each coset of ℚ in ℝ, which is not Lebesgue measurable.

nodes.name: Distribution function (Lebesgue-Stieltjes)
nodes.description: A right-continuous nondecreasing function F: ℝ → ℝ defining a Borel measure via μ_F((a,b]) = F(b) - F(a).

nodes.name: Correspondence between Borel measures and distribution functions
nodes.description: There is a bijection between finite Borel measures on ℝ and right-continuous nondecreasing bounded functions F (modulo additive constants), given by F(x) = μ((-∞, x]).

nodes.name: Cantor measure (Cantor-Lebesgue measure)
nodes.description: The Lebesgue-Stieltjes measure associated to the Cantor function, a probability measure supported on the Cantor set that assigns measure zero to every singleton.

nodes.name: Borel measurable function
nodes.type_signature: Topological spaces (X, Y) → {f: X → Y : f⁻¹(open) is Borel}
nodes.description: A function f: X → Y between topological spaces such that the preimage of every open set is a Borel set in X.

nodes.name: Lebesgue measurable function
nodes.type_signature: ℝⁿ → ℝ measurable w.r.t. Lebesgue σ-algebra
nodes.description: A function f: ℝⁿ → ℝ such that f⁻¹((a, ∞)) is Lebesgue measurable for every a ∈ ℝ.

nodes.name: Continuous functions are Borel measurable
nodes.description: Every continuous function f: X → Y between topological spaces is Borel measurable.

nodes.name: Measurability criterion via generating sets
nodes.description: A function f: X → Y is measurable if and only if f⁻¹(E) ∈ M for every E in a collection that generates the σ-algebra on Y.

nodes.name: Closure of measurable functions under limits
nodes.description: If {f_n} is a sequence of measurable functions, then sup f_n, inf f_n, lim sup f_n, and lim inf f_n are all measurable.

nodes.name: Simple function
nodes.description: A measurable function φ: X → ℂ taking only finitely many values, expressible as φ = Σ aᵢ χ_{Eᵢ} for measurable sets Eᵢ.

nodes.name: Integral of a nonnegative simple function
nodes.description: For a nonnegative simple function φ = Σ aᵢ χ_{Eᵢ}, the integral is defined as ∫φ dμ = Σ aᵢ μ(Eᵢ).

nodes.name: Integral of a nonnegative measurable function
nodes.description: For a nonnegative measurable function f, ∫f dμ = sup{∫φ dμ : 0 ≤ φ ≤ f, φ simple}.

nodes.name: Linearity of integration for nonnegative functions
nodes.description: If f, g are nonnegative measurable functions and c ≥ 0, then ∫(f + g) = ∫f + ∫g and ∫(cf) = c∫f.

nodes.name: Almost everywhere (a.e.)
nodes.description: A property P holds almost everywhere (a.e.) with respect to μ if the set {x : P(x) fails} has μ-measure zero.

nodes.name: Convergence in L¹
nodes.description: A sequence f_n converges to f in L¹ if ∫|f_n - f| dμ → 0.

nodes.name: Convergence in measure subsequence theorem
nodes.description: If f_n → f in measure, then there exists a subsequence f_{n_k} that converges to f almost everywhere.

nodes.name: Product σ-algebra
nodes.description: The σ-algebra M ⊗ N on X × Y generated by all measurable rectangles {A × B : A ∈ M, B ∈ N}.

nodes.name: Measurability of sections
nodes.description: If E ∈ M ⊗ N, then for each x ∈ X the section E_x = {y : (x,y) ∈ E} is in N, and for each y the section E^y is in M.

nodes.name: Lebesgue measure on ℝⁿ
nodes.type_signature: ℝⁿ → Complete measure extending n-fold product Lebesgue measure
nodes.description: The completion of the n-fold product of Lebesgue measure on ℝ, equivalently the measure assigning to each box its volume.

nodes.name: Polar coordinates integration formula
nodes.description: For integrable f on ℝⁿ, ∫_{ℝⁿ} f dx = ∫_0^∞ (∫_{S^{n-1}} f(rω) dσ(ω)) r^{n-1} dr, where σ is surface measure on S^{n-1}.

nodes.name: Volume of the unit ball in ℝⁿ
nodes.description: The Lebesgue measure of the unit ball B_n = {x ∈ ℝⁿ : |x| ≤ 1} is V_n = πⁿ/² / Γ(n/2 + 1).

nodes.name: Convergence in L¹ implies convergence in measure
nodes.description: If f_n → f in L¹(μ), then f_n → f in measure.

nodes.name: Positive set for a signed measure
nodes.description: A measurable set P is positive for a signed measure ν if ν(E) ≥ 0 for every measurable subset E ⊂ P.

nodes.name: Negative set for a signed measure
nodes.description: A measurable set N is negative for a signed measure ν if ν(E) ≤ 0 for every measurable subset E ⊂ N.

nodes.name: Positive variation of a signed measure
nodes.type_signature: Signed measure ν → Positive measure ν⁺
nodes.description: The positive part ν⁺ in the Jordan decomposition ν = ν⁺ - ν⁻, defined by ν⁺(E) = ν(E ∩ P) where P is the positive set in a Hahn decomposition.

nodes.name: Negative variation of a signed measure
nodes.type_signature: Signed measure ν → Positive measure ν⁻
nodes.description: The negative part ν⁻ in the Jordan decomposition ν = ν⁺ - ν⁻, defined by ν⁻(E) = -ν(E ∩ N) where N is the negative set in a Hahn decomposition.

nodes.name: Absolutely continuous measure
nodes.description: A measure ν is absolutely continuous with respect to μ (written ν ≪ μ) if μ(E) = 0 implies ν(E) = 0 for every measurable E.

nodes.name: Chain rule for Radon-Nikodym derivatives
nodes.description: If λ ≪ ν ≪ μ, then dλ/dμ = (dλ/dν)(dν/dμ) μ-a.e.

nodes.name: Total variation of a complex measure
nodes.type_signature: Complex measure ν → Positive finite measure |ν|
nodes.description: For a complex measure ν, the total variation |ν|(E) = sup Σ|ν(E_j)| over all partitions of E into countably many measurable sets.

nodes.name: Total variation of a complex measure is finite
nodes.description: For any complex measure ν on (X, M), the total variation |ν|(X) < ∞.

nodes.name: Polar decomposition of a complex measure
nodes.description: Every complex measure ν can be written as dν = h d|ν| where h is a measurable function with |h| = 1 a.e. with respect to |ν|.

nodes.name: Radon-Nikodym theorem for complex measures
nodes.description: If ν is a complex measure and μ is a σ-finite positive measure with ν ≪ μ, then dν = f dμ for some f ∈ L¹(μ).

nodes.name: Lebesgue set
nodes.type_signature: f ∈ L¹_loc(ℝⁿ) → Lebesgue set L_f ⊂ ℝⁿ
nodes.description: The set of points x where lim_{r→0} (1/m(B_r(x))) ∫_{B_r(x)} |f(y) - f(x)| dy = 0, which has full measure for any locally integrable f.

nodes.name: Differentiation of Borel measures on ℝⁿ
nodes.description: If ν and μ are Borel measures on ℝⁿ with μ the Lebesgue measure, then dν/dμ(x) = lim_{r→0} ν(B_r(x))/μ(B_r(x)) exists a.e. and equals the Radon-Nikodym derivative.

nodes.name: Total variation function
nodes.description: For f ∈ BV([a,b]), the function T_f(x) = sup{Σ|f(x_i) - f(x_{i-1})| : partitions of [a,x]}, which is nondecreasing.

nodes.name: BV functions as differences of monotone functions
nodes.description: A function f is of bounded variation on [a,b] if and only if f = g - h where g and h are nondecreasing.

nodes.name: AC functions and absolute continuity of measures
nodes.description: F is absolutely continuous on [a,b] if and only if the associated signed measure μ_F is absolutely continuous with respect to Lebesgue measure.

nodes.name: BV functions are differentiable a.e.
nodes.description: Every function of bounded variation on [a,b] is differentiable Lebesgue-almost everywhere.

nodes.name: Singular function
nodes.description: A nondecreasing continuous function F on [a,b] whose derivative F'(x) = 0 for Lebesgue-a.e. x, yet F is not constant.

nodes.name: Decomposition of BV functions
nodes.description: Every BV function on [a,b] can be uniquely decomposed as f = f_ac + f_s + f_j where f_ac is absolutely continuous, f_s is singular continuous, and f_j is a jump function.

nodes.name: Integration by parts for absolutely continuous functions
nodes.description: If F and G are absolutely continuous on [a,b], then ∫_a^b F'G dx = F(b)G(b) - F(a)G(a) - ∫_a^b FG' dx.

nodes.name: Lebesgue-Radon-Nikodym theorem on ℝ
nodes.description: Every BV function F decomposes as F = F_ac + F_s where F_ac is absolutely continuous and F_s' = 0 a.e., corresponding to the Lebesgue decomposition of μ_F.

nodes.name: Net (generalized sequence)
nodes.description: A function from a directed set (I, ≤) to a topological space X; a net (x_α) converges to x if for every open U containing x there exists α₀ with x_α ∈ U for all α ≥ α₀.

nodes.name: Subnet
nodes.description: A subnet of a net (x_α)_{α∈A} is a net (x_{φ(β)})_{β∈B} where φ: B → A is an order-preserving cofinal map between directed sets.

nodes.name: Characterization of topology by nets
nodes.description: A set F is closed if and only if it contains all limits of convergent nets in F; a function is continuous if and only if it preserves net convergence.

nodes.name: Compactness via nets
nodes.description: A topological space is compact if and only if every net has a convergent subnet.

nodes.name: Topological vector space (TVS)
nodes.description: A vector space X over ℝ or ℂ equipped with a topology making addition and scalar multiplication continuous.

nodes.name: Seminorm
nodes.description: A function p: X → [0,∞) on a vector space satisfying p(αx) = |α|p(x) and p(x+y) ≤ p(x) + p(y), but possibly p(x) = 0 for x ≠ 0.

nodes.name: Bounded linear operator
nodes.description: A linear map T: X → Y between normed spaces such that ||T|| = sup{||Tx|| : ||x|| ≤ 1} < ∞, equivalently a continuous linear map.

nodes.name: Operator norm
nodes.description: The norm ||T|| = sup{||Tx||/||x|| : x ≠ 0} on the space B(X,Y) of bounded linear operators from X to Y.

nodes.name: B(X,Y) is Banach when Y is Banach
nodes.description: If Y is a Banach space, then B(X,Y) with the operator norm is a Banach space.

nodes.name: Separation of points by continuous linear functionals
nodes.description: For any x ≠ 0 in a normed space X, there exists f ∈ X* with f(x) ≠ 0 and ||f|| = 1, ||f(x)|| = ||x||.

nodes.name: Second category set (non-meager set)
nodes.description: A subset of a topological space that is not a countable union of nowhere dense sets.

nodes.name: Banach-Steinhaus theorem (pointwise convergence corollary)
nodes.description: If T_n ∈ B(X,Y) with X Banach and T_n(x) converges for each x ∈ X, then sup_n ||T_n|| < ∞ and the pointwise limit T is in B(X,Y) with ||T|| ≤ lim inf ||T_n||.

nodes.name: Bounded inverse theorem
nodes.description: If T: X → Y is a bounded bijective linear operator between Banach spaces, then T⁻¹ is also bounded.

nodes.name: Weak topology on a normed space
nodes.description: The coarsest topology on a normed space X making every f ∈ X* continuous; x_α → x weakly iff f(x_α) → f(x) for all f ∈ X*.

nodes.name: Closest point to a closed convex set in Hilbert space
nodes.description: For every nonempty closed convex subset K of a Hilbert space H and x ∈ H, there exists a unique y ∈ K minimizing ||x - y||.

nodes.name: Separable Hilbert spaces are isomorphic to ℓ²
nodes.description: Every infinite-dimensional separable Hilbert space is unitarily isomorphic to ℓ²(ℕ).

nodes.name: Quotient normed space
nodes.type_signature: Normed space X, closed subspace M → X/M with quotient norm
nodes.description: For a closed subspace M of a normed space X, the quotient X/M with norm ||x + M|| = inf{||x + m|| : m ∈ M} is a normed space; it is Banach when X is.

nodes.name: Chebyshev-Markov inequality for Lp
nodes.description: For f ∈ Lp and α > 0, μ({x : |f(x)| > α}) ≤ α⁻ᵖ ||f||_p^p.

nodes.name: Lp inclusions under finite measure
nodes.description: If μ(X) < ∞ and 1 ≤ p ≤ q ≤ ∞, then Lq(μ) ⊂ Lp(μ) with ||f||_p ≤ μ(X)^{1/p - 1/q} ||f||_q.

nodes.name: Dual of Lp
nodes.description: For 1 ≤ p < ∞ and σ-finite μ, the dual (Lp)* is isometrically isomorphic to Lq where 1/p + 1/q = 1, via the pairing ⟨f, g⟩ = ∫fg dμ.

nodes.name: Minkowski's inequality for integrals
nodes.description: For 1 ≤ p < ∞ and nonneg measurable F on X × Y, (∫_X (∫_Y F(x,y) dν(y))^p dμ(x))^{1/p} ≤ ∫_Y (∫_X F(x,y)^p dμ(x))^{1/p} dν(y).

nodes.name: Weak Lp space
nodes.description: The space Lp,∞(μ) of measurable functions f with ||f||_{p,∞} = sup_{α>0} α·μ({|f| > α})^{1/p} < ∞, a quasi-normed space containing Lp.

nodes.name: Cc(X) — continuous functions with compact support
nodes.description: The vector space of continuous real- or complex-valued functions on a locally compact Hausdorff space X whose support is compact.

nodes.name: C₀(X) — continuous functions vanishing at infinity
nodes.description: The Banach space of continuous functions f on a locally compact Hausdorff space X such that {x : |f(x)| ≥ ε} is compact for every ε > 0, with the sup norm.

nodes.name: Lusin's theorem for Radon measures
nodes.description: If μ is a Radon measure on a LCH space X and f is measurable, then for every ε > 0 there exists a compact K with μ(K^c) < ε such that f|_K is continuous.

nodes.name: Dual of C₀(X)
nodes.description: The dual space C₀(X)* is isometrically isomorphic to the space M(X) of complex Radon measures on X, via the pairing I(f) = ∫f dμ.

nodes.name: Approximate identity on ℝⁿ
nodes.type_signature: {φ_ε}_{ε>0} family on ℝⁿ → Convolution approximation to identity
nodes.description: A family {φ_ε} ⊂ L¹(ℝⁿ) with ∫φ_ε = 1, supp(φ_ε) shrinking to {0}, and φ_ε * f → f in Lp and pointwise a.e. for f ∈ Lp.

nodes.name: Fourier transform on L² (extension from L¹ ∩ L²)
nodes.description: The Fourier transform, initially defined on L¹ ∩ L², extends uniquely to a unitary operator on L²(ℝⁿ) by the Plancherel theorem.

nodes.name: Test function space D(Ω) = C_c^∞(Ω)
nodes.description: The space of smooth functions with compact support in an open set Ω ⊂ ℝⁿ, equipped with the inductive limit topology.

nodes.name: Distribution space D'(Ω)
nodes.description: The space of continuous linear functionals on D(Ω) = C_c^∞(Ω), whose elements are called distributions on Ω.

nodes.name: Support of a distribution
nodes.description: The support of a distribution u is the complement of the largest open set on which u vanishes.

nodes.name: Distributions with compact support E'(Ω)
nodes.description: The subspace of distributions u ∈ D'(Ω) with compact support, isomorphic to the dual of C^∞(Ω).

nodes.name: Tempered distribution S'(ℝⁿ)
nodes.description: A continuous linear functional on the Schwartz space S(ℝⁿ); the space S'(ℝⁿ) of tempered distributions includes all polynomially growing functions and all Lp functions.

nodes.name: Convolution of distributions
nodes.type_signature: u ∈ E'(ℝⁿ) × v ∈ D'(ℝⁿ) → u * v ∈ D'(ℝⁿ)
nodes.description: If u has compact support and v is any distribution, their convolution extends the classical convolution to distributions.

nodes.name: Sobolev space W^{k,p}(Ω)
nodes.description: The space of functions f ∈ Lp(Ω) whose weak derivatives D^α f exist in Lp for all |α| ≤ k, with norm ||f||_{k,p} = (Σ_{|α|≤k} ||D^α f||_p^p)^{1/p}.

nodes.name: Order of a distribution
nodes.description: The smallest integer k such that |u(φ)| ≤ C sup_{|α|≤k} ||D^α φ||_∞ for all φ ∈ D(K) for each compact K ⊂ Ω.

nodes.name: Singular support of a distribution
nodes.type_signature: u ∈ D'(Ω) → sing supp(u) ⊂ Ω closed
nodes.description: The complement of the largest open set on which the distribution u agrees with a smooth function.

nodes.name: Fourier transform of tempered distributions
nodes.description: The extension of the Fourier transform to S'(ℝⁿ) defined by ⟨û, φ⟩ = ⟨u, φ̂⟩ for φ ∈ S(ℝⁿ), yielding an automorphism of S'.

nodes.name: Borel σ-algebra on ℝⁿ
nodes.description: The σ-algebra on ℝⁿ generated by the open sets in the product topology, equivalently by the open rectangles or the coordinate projections.

nodes.name: Random vector
nodes.description: A measurable function X: (Ω, F) → (ℝⁿ, B(ℝⁿ)), equivalently an n-tuple of real-valued random variables.

nodes.name: π-system
nodes.description: A nonempty collection of subsets of Ω closed under finite intersections.

nodes.name: λ-system (Dynkin system)
nodes.description: A collection of subsets containing Ω, closed under proper differences and countable increasing unions.

nodes.name: Independence of σ-algebras
nodes.description: Sub-σ-algebras (F_i)_{i∈I} of F are independent if P(A₁ ∩ ··· ∩ Aₖ) = P(A₁)···P(Aₖ) for all finite selections Aⱼ ∈ F_{iⱼ} with distinct indices.

nodes.name: Convergence in Lᵖ
nodes.description: A sequence fₙ converges to f in Lᵖ if ∫|fₙ − f|ᵖ dμ → 0, for 1 ≤ p < ∞.

nodes.name: Stopping time
nodes.description: A random variable τ: Ω → {0,1,2,…} ∪ {∞} such that {τ ≤ n} ∈ Fₙ for every n.

nodes.name: Tail σ-algebra
nodes.description: The σ-algebra T = ∩ₙ σ(Xₙ, Xₙ₊₁, …) capturing events whose occurrence is unaffected by any finite number of initial random variables.

nodes.name: Backward (reversed) martingale
nodes.description: An integrable adapted process (Xₙ)_{n≤0} with respect to a decreasing filtration (Fₙ)_{n≤0} satisfying E[Xₙ | Fₘ] = Xₘ for m ≤ n ≤ 0.

nodes.name: Regular conditional distribution
nodes.description: A function P(·|·): Ω × B(E) → [0,1] that is a probability measure in the second argument for each ω and a measurable function in ω for each Borel set.

nodes.name: Sufficient statistic
nodes.description: A statistic T(X) such that the conditional distribution of the sample X given T(X) = t does not depend on the unknown parameter θ.

nodes.name: Moment generating function
nodes.description: The function M_X(t) = E[e^{tX}] defined for real t in the domain where the expectation is finite.

nodes.name: Martingale transform
nodes.description: The discrete stochastic integral (H·M)ₙ = Σₖ₌₁ⁿ Hₖ(Mₖ − Mₖ₋₁) where H is a predictable process and M is a martingale.

nodes.name: Convergence-determining class
nodes.description: A class C of bounded continuous functions on a metric space S such that ∫f dμₙ → ∫f dμ for all f ∈ C implies μₙ →_w μ.

nodes.name: Separating class
nodes.description: A class C of bounded measurable functions such that ∫f dμ = ∫f dν for all f ∈ C implies μ = ν.

nodes.name: Properties of conditional expectation
nodes.description: Conditional expectation is linear, monotone, satisfies the tower property E[E[X|G]|H] = E[X|H] for H ⊂ G, and the taking-out-what-is-known rule E[YX|G] = YE[X|G] for G-measurable Y.

nodes.name: Relations between modes of convergence
nodes.description: Almost sure convergence implies convergence in probability which implies convergence in distribution; Lᵖ convergence implies convergence in probability; none of the reverse implications hold in general.

nodes.name: Properties of characteristic functions
nodes.description: A characteristic function φ_X(t) = E[e^{itX}] is uniformly continuous, bounded by 1 with φ(0) = 1, Hermitian (φ(−t) = φ̄(t)), and positive definite.

nodes.name: Dynkin π-λ theorem
nodes.description: If a π-system P is contained in a λ-system L, then σ(P) ⊆ L; equivalently, two measures agreeing on a π-system agree on the generated σ-algebra.

nodes.name: Monotone class theorem
nodes.description: The smallest monotone class containing an algebra of sets coincides with the σ-algebra generated by that algebra.

nodes.name: Kolmogorov's maximal inequality
nodes.description: For independent zero-mean random variables with finite variances, P(max_{1≤k≤n} |Sₖ| ≥ λ) ≤ Var(Sₙ)/λ² where Sₖ = X₁ + ··· + Xₖ.

nodes.name: Lévy's upward theorem
nodes.description: If Fₙ ↑ F∞ = σ(∪ₙ Fₙ) and X ∈ L¹, then E[X | Fₙ] → E[X | F∞] almost surely and in L¹.

nodes.name: Lévy's downward theorem
nodes.description: If Fₙ ↓ F∞ = ∩ₙ Fₙ and X ∈ L¹, then E[X | Fₙ] → E[X | F∞] almost surely and in L¹.

nodes.name: Lévy inversion formula
nodes.description: The distribution function F of a random variable X is recovered from its characteristic function φ by F(b) − F(a) = lim_{T→∞} (2π)⁻¹ ∫_{−T}^{T} (e^{−ita} − e^{−itb})/(it) φ(t) dt at continuity points a < b.

nodes.name: Uniqueness theorem for characteristic functions
nodes.description: Two probability distributions on ℝ are equal if and only if their characteristic functions are equal.

nodes.name: Cramér-Wold device
nodes.description: Random vectors Xₙ converge in distribution to X in ℝᵈ if and only if t·Xₙ →_d t·X for every t ∈ ℝᵈ.

nodes.name: Method of moments (convergence)
nodes.description: If the moment sequence E[Xₙᵏ] → E[Xᵏ] for all k ≥ 1 and the distribution of X is determined by its moments, then Xₙ →_d X.

nodes.name: Conditional Jensen's inequality
nodes.description: If φ is convex and X, φ(X) ∈ L¹, then φ(E[X | G]) ≤ E[φ(X) | G] almost surely.

nodes.name: Neyman-Fisher factorization theorem
nodes.description: A statistic T(X) is sufficient for θ if and only if the density f(x; θ) factors as g(T(x), θ) · h(x) for some nonnegative functions g and h.

nodes.name: Disintegration of measures
nodes.description: A probability measure μ on a product of Polish spaces admits a disintegration into a family of regular conditional probability measures μ_y indexed by the marginal.

nodes.name: Scheffé's lemma
nodes.description: If nonneg integrable functions fₙ → f a.e. and ∫fₙ → ∫f, then ∫|fₙ − f| → 0.

nodes.name: de la Vallée-Poussin criterion
nodes.description: A family of random variables is uniformly integrable if and only if there exists a nonneg convex function φ with φ(x)/x → ∞ such that sup E[φ(|Xᵢ|)] < ∞.

nodes.name: Truncation technique
nodes.function_signature: (Random variable X, level a) → (truncated X_a, remainder)
nodes.description: Replaces a random variable by its truncation X·1_{|X|≤a} to reduce to bounded variables, then controls the remainder separately.

nodes.name: Symmetrization technique
nodes.function_signature: (Sequence X_i) → (Symmetrized sequence X_i − X_i')
nodes.description: Introduces independent copies X_i' and studies X_i − X_i' to exploit symmetry, converting one-sided tail bounds to two-sided via Lévy's symmetrization inequalities.

nodes.name: Characteristic function method
nodes.function_signature: (Sequence of distributions) → (Convergence in distribution via pointwise φₙ(t) → φ(t))
nodes.description: Proves convergence in distribution by showing pointwise convergence of characteristic functions and applying the Lévy continuity theorem.

nodes.name: Tightness-Prokhorov method
nodes.function_signature: (Family of probability measures) → (Weak convergence of subsequence)
nodes.description: Establishes weak convergence by verifying tightness of the sequence of measures (via Prokhorov's theorem) and identifying the limit through finite-dimensional distributions.

nodes.name: Monotone class argument
nodes.function_signature: (Property on π-system) → (Property on generated σ-algebra)
nodes.description: Extends a property verified on a π-system or an algebra to the generated σ-algebra by showing the collection of sets satisfying the property is a λ-system or monotone class.

nodes.name: Dyadic approximation technique (measure theory)
nodes.function_signature: (Measurable function f) → (Sequence of simple functions 2⁻ⁿ⌊2ⁿf⌋)
nodes.description: Approximates a nonneg measurable function from below by dyadic simple functions fₙ = Σₖ (k/2ⁿ)·1_{k/2ⁿ ≤ f < (k+1)/2ⁿ}, yielding a pointwise increasing sequence converging to f.

nodes.name: Upcrossing argument (Doob)
nodes.function_signature: (Submartingale Xₙ, interval [a,b]) → (a.s. convergence via finite upcrossings)
nodes.description: Proves almost sure convergence of a submartingale by bounding the expected number of upcrossings of an interval [a,b] and applying the upcrossing inequality.

nodes.name: Martingale technique for proving convergence
nodes.function_signature: (Sequence Xₙ adapted to filtration) → (a.s. or Lᵖ limit via martingale theory)
nodes.description: Constructs a martingale or submartingale from the sequence of interest and applies Doob's convergence theorems to deduce almost sure or Lᵖ convergence.

nodes.name: G_δ set
nodes.description: A subset of a topological space that is a countable intersection of open sets.

nodes.name: F_σ set
nodes.description: A subset of a topological space that is a countable union of closed sets.

nodes.name: Positive and negative parts of a function
nodes.description: For a measurable function f, the decomposition f = f⁺ − f⁻ where f⁺ = max(f,0) and f⁻ = max(−f,0), with |f| = f⁺ + f⁻.

nodes.name: Cauchy in measure
nodes.description: A sequence {fₙ} of measurable functions is Cauchy in measure if for every ε, η > 0, there exists N such that μ({|fₙ − fₘ| ≥ η}) < ε for all n, m ≥ N.

nodes.name: Non-atomic (diffuse) measure
nodes.description: A measure with no atoms: for every measurable set A with μ(A) > 0, there exists a measurable B ⊆ A with 0 < μ(B) < μ(A).

nodes.name: Atom of a measure
nodes.description: A measurable set A with μ(A) > 0 such that for every measurable B ⊆ A, either μ(B) = 0 or μ(B) = μ(A).

nodes.name: Baire σ-algebra
nodes.description: On a compact Hausdorff space, the σ-algebra generated by the compact G_δ sets, equivalently the smallest σ-algebra making all continuous real-valued functions measurable.

nodes.name: Uniform integrability
nodes.description: A family {fₐ} of integrable functions is uniformly integrable if supₐ ∫_{|fₐ|>M} |fₐ| dμ → 0 as M → ∞ and for every ε > 0 there exists δ > 0 with μ(A) < δ implying supₐ ∫_A |fₐ| < ε.

nodes.name: Weak convergence in Lp
nodes.description: A sequence {fₙ} in Lp converges weakly to f (fₙ ⇀ f) if ∫ fₙg dμ → ∫ fg dμ for every g ∈ Lq where 1/p + 1/q = 1.

nodes.name: Modular function of a locally compact group
nodes.description: The continuous homomorphism Δ: G → (0, ∞) defined by μ(Eg) = Δ(g)μ(E), relating left Haar measure to right translation.

nodes.name: Density of rationals in ℝ
nodes.description: Between any two distinct real numbers there exists a rational number.

nodes.name: Simple approximation theorem
nodes.description: Every nonnegative measurable function is the pointwise limit of an increasing sequence of nonnegative simple functions; if bounded, the convergence is uniform.

nodes.name: Continuity of measure from below
nodes.description: If {Eₙ} is an ascending sequence of measurable sets, then μ(⋃ Eₙ) = lim μ(Eₙ).

nodes.name: Continuity of measure from above
nodes.description: If {Eₙ} is a descending sequence of measurable sets with μ(E₁) < ∞, then μ(⋂ Eₙ) = lim μ(Eₙ).

nodes.name: Regularity of Lebesgue measure
nodes.description: Lebesgue measure is regular: every measurable set can be approximated from outside by open sets and from inside by closed sets to arbitrary precision in measure.

nodes.name: Clarkson's inequalities
nodes.description: For 2 ≤ p < ∞: ‖(f+g)/2‖ₚᵖ + ‖(f−g)/2‖ₚᵖ ≤ (‖f‖ₚᵖ + ‖g‖ₚᵖ)/2, with an analogous inequality for 1 < p < 2 using the conjugate exponent.

nodes.name: Uniform convexity of Lp (1 < p < ∞)
nodes.description: For 1 < p < ∞, Lp is uniformly convex: if ‖fₙ‖ₚ ≤ 1, ‖gₙ‖ₚ ≤ 1, and ‖fₙ + gₙ‖ₚ → 2, then ‖fₙ − gₙ‖ₚ → 0.

nodes.name: Radon–Riesz theorem
nodes.description: In Lp for 1 < p < ∞, if fₙ ⇀ f weakly and ‖fₙ‖ₚ → ‖f‖ₚ, then fₙ → f strongly in Lp.

nodes.name: Banach–Saks theorem
nodes.description: If {fₙ} converges weakly to f in Lp for 1 < p < ∞, then there exists a subsequence whose Cesàro means converge strongly to f.

nodes.name: Weak lower semicontinuity of the norm
nodes.description: If xₙ ⇀ x weakly in a normed space, then ‖x‖ ≤ lim inf ‖xₙ‖.

nodes.name: Weak sequential compactness in Lp (1 < p < ∞)
nodes.description: Every bounded sequence in Lp(E) for 1 < p < ∞ has a weakly convergent subsequence.

nodes.name: Separability of Lp (1 ≤ p < ∞)
nodes.description: The space Lp(ℝ) is separable for 1 ≤ p < ∞, possessing a countable dense subset.

nodes.name: L∞ is not separable
nodes.description: The Banach space L∞ does not have a countable dense subset.

nodes.name: Inclusion of Lp spaces on finite measure sets
nodes.description: If μ(E) < ∞ and 1 ≤ p < q ≤ ∞, then Lq(E) ⊆ Lp(E) with ‖f‖ₚ ≤ μ(E)^{1/p−1/q} ‖f‖_q.

nodes.name: Interpolation of Lp norms
nodes.description: If f ∈ Lp ∩ Lr for p < r, then f ∈ Ls for all p ≤ s ≤ r with ‖f‖_s ≤ ‖f‖ₚᵅ ‖f‖ᵣᵝ for appropriate α + β = 1.

nodes.name: Schur property of ℓ¹
nodes.description: In ℓ¹, weak convergence implies strong convergence: if xₙ ⇀ x weakly then ‖xₙ − x‖₁ → 0.

nodes.name: Schauder's theorem (compact adjoint)
nodes.description: A bounded linear operator T between Banach spaces is compact if and only if its adjoint T* is compact.

nodes.name: Compact operators form a closed ideal
nodes.description: The set K(X,Y) of compact operators between Banach spaces X, Y is a closed subspace of B(X,Y) and a two-sided ideal under composition.

nodes.name: Ulam's theorem (tightness on Polish spaces)
nodes.description: Every finite Borel measure on a complete separable metric space is tight: for every ε > 0, there exists a compact K with μ(X ∖ K) < ε.

nodes.name: Intermediate value property for non-atomic measures
nodes.description: If μ is a non-atomic measure and μ(E) > 0, then for every 0 ≤ t ≤ μ(E) there exists a measurable F ⊆ E with μ(F) = t.

nodes.name: Completeness of convergence in measure
nodes.description: If {fₙ} is Cauchy in measure, then there exists a measurable function f such that fₙ → f in measure.

nodes.name: Inversion formula for Haar measure
nodes.description: For left Haar measure μ with modular function Δ: ∫ f(x⁻¹) Δ(x⁻¹) dμ(x) = ∫ f(x) dμ(x).

nodes.name: Condensation of singularities
nodes.description: If {Tₙ} are bounded linear operators on a Banach space with sup ‖Tₙ‖ = ∞, then {x : sup ‖Tₙx‖ = ∞} is residual (comeager).

nodes.name: Density of simple functions in Lp
nodes.description: Simple functions with support of finite measure are dense in Lp(X, μ) for 1 ≤ p < ∞.

nodes.name: Density of continuous functions in Lp(ℝ)
nodes.description: The continuous functions with compact support Cc(ℝ) are dense in Lp(ℝ) for 1 ≤ p < ∞.

nodes.name: Density of Cc in Lp for Radon measures
nodes.description: If μ is a Radon measure on a locally compact Hausdorff space, then Cc(X) is dense in Lp(X, μ) for 1 ≤ p < ∞.

nodes.name: Absolutely continuous functions map null sets to null sets
nodes.description: If f is absolutely continuous on [a,b] and m(E) = 0, then m(f(E)) = 0.

nodes.name: Lebesgue decomposition of BV functions
nodes.description: Every function of bounded variation on [a,b] decomposes as f = f_ac + f_s where f_ac is absolutely continuous and f_s is singular (f_s' = 0 a.e.).

nodes.name: Daniell–Stone representation theorem
nodes.description: A positive linear functional on a vector lattice of functions satisfying a monotone convergence condition can be represented as integration with respect to a measure.

nodes.name: Reflexivity of Lp (1 < p < ∞)
nodes.description: For 1 < p < ∞, the canonical embedding J: Lp → (Lp)** is surjective, so Lp is reflexive.

nodes.name: L¹ is not reflexive
nodes.description: L¹(X, μ) is not reflexive when the measure space is not purely atomic with finitely many atoms, since (L¹)* = L∞ but (L∞)* ⊋ L¹.

nodes.name: Uniqueness of Haar measure
nodes.description: The left Haar measure on a locally compact group is unique up to a positive scalar multiple.

nodes.name: L² is a Hilbert space
nodes.description: L²(X, μ) is a Hilbert space with inner product ⟨f, g⟩ = ∫ fg dμ.

nodes.name: Exhaustion technique (σ-finite decomposition)
nodes.function_signature: (Problem on σ-finite space, decomposition X = ⋃Eₙ) → (Result via finite-measure pieces)
nodes.description: Decomposes a σ-finite space into sets of finite measure, proves the result on each piece, then combines via monotone limits or countable additivity.

nodes.name: Density argument in Lp
nodes.function_signature: (Inequality on dense subclass, Lp completeness) → (Inequality on all of Lp)
nodes.description: Proves an inequality or identity for a dense subclass (simple, continuous, or Cc functions), then extends to all of Lp by continuity and approximation.

nodes.name: Duality method (functional analysis)
nodes.function_signature: (Property of X via X*) → (Characterization or identity in X)
nodes.description: Proves properties of a Banach space or Lp by studying the action of dual-space elements, e.g., showing f = 0 by verifying ∫fg = 0 for all g in the dual.

nodes.name: Uniform integrability technique
nodes.function_signature: (Uniform integrability + convergence in measure) → (Lp convergence)
nodes.description: Establishes Lp convergence by verifying uniform integrability of {|fₙ|ᵖ} and convergence in measure, bypassing dominated convergence when no single dominator exists.

nodes.name: Weak compactness argument
nodes.function_signature: (Bounded sequence in reflexive Banach space) → (Weakly convergent subsequence + limit properties)
nodes.description: Extracts weakly convergent subsequences from bounded sequences in reflexive spaces via Eberlein–Šmulian, then uses weak lower semicontinuity to pass to limits.

nodes.name: Egoroff–Lusin technique chain
nodes.function_signature: (Measurable function on finite measure space) → (Nearly continuous function on large subset)
nodes.description: Combines Egoroff's theorem (a.e. convergence → near-uniform convergence) with Lusin's theorem (measurability → near-continuity) to reduce measurable-function arguments to continuous ones.

nodes.name: Baire category method in analysis
nodes.function_signature: (Complete metric space, dense open sets) → (Existence/generic property)
nodes.description: Uses completeness and the Baire category theorem to show that a countable intersection of dense open sets is dense, proving existence or generic properties.

nodes.name: Radon–Nikodym technique
nodes.function_signature: (Absolutely continuous measure or bounded linear functional) → (Integral representation against Lp function)
nodes.description: Represents absolutely continuous measures or bounded linear functionals as integrals against an Lp function via the Radon–Nikodym theorem, central to Lp duality proofs.

nodes.name: Completeness via rapidly Cauchy subsequences
nodes.function_signature: (Cauchy sequence in normed space) → (Convergent subsequence via Σ‖xₙ₊₁ − xₙ‖ < ∞)
nodes.description: Proves completeness by showing every rapidly Cauchy sequence (with summable consecutive differences) converges, which implies every Cauchy sequence converges.

nodes.name: Tonelli–Fubini criterion
nodes.function_signature: (Measurable function on product space) → (Iterated integral computation)
nodes.description: First applies Tonelli's theorem to |f| to verify integrability via the iterated integral, then applies Fubini's theorem to compute ∫∫ f d(μ×ν).

nodes.name: Chordal metric on the Riemann sphere
nodes.description: The metric d(z,w) = |z-w|/sqrt((1+|z|^2)(1+|w|^2)) on the extended complex plane, induced by stereographic projection onto the unit sphere.

nodes.name: Stereographic projection
nodes.description: The conformal bijection from the unit sphere minus the north pole to the complex plane, extending to a homeomorphism S^2 -> C_hat.

nodes.name: Argument of a complex number
nodes.description: The angle arg(z) = theta such that z = |z|e^{i theta}, defined modulo 2pi; the principal value Arg(z) is the unique theta in (-pi, pi].

nodes.name: Polar representation of complex numbers
nodes.description: Every nonzero complex number z has a unique representation z = r e^{i theta} with r = |z| > 0 and theta = arg(z).

nodes.name: Complex conjugate
nodes.description: The involution z-bar = a - bi for z = a + bi, satisfying |z|^2 = z z-bar and fixing R pointwise.

nodes.name: Modulus of a complex number
nodes.description: The absolute value |z| = sqrt(a^2 + b^2) for z = a + bi, defining the Euclidean metric on C and satisfying |zw| = |z||w|.

nodes.name: Complex power z^alpha
nodes.description: For z != 0 and alpha in C, z^alpha = e^{alpha log z}, a multi-valued function single-valued only when alpha is an integer.

nodes.name: Complex trigonometric functions
nodes.description: The extensions sin z = (e^{iz} - e^{-iz})/(2i) and cos z = (e^{iz} + e^{-iz})/2, entire functions satisfying cos^2 z + sin^2 z = 1 on all of C.

nodes.name: Cross-ratio
nodes.description: The projective invariant (z_1,z_2,z_3,z_4) = ((z_1-z_3)(z_2-z_4))/((z_1-z_4)(z_2-z_3)), preserved by Mobius transformations and real iff the four points are concyclic.

nodes.name: Riemann surface of sqrt(z)
nodes.description: The two-sheeted branched covering of C on which w^2 = z becomes single-valued; topologically a sphere with two branch points at 0 and infinity.

nodes.name: Riemann surface of log z
nodes.description: The infinitely-sheeted unbranched covering of C \ {0} on which the logarithm is single-valued, realized as the universal cover with the map z -> e^z.

nodes.name: Simply periodic function
nodes.description: A meromorphic function f satisfying f(z + omega) = f(z) for a single fundamental period omega != 0.

nodes.name: Period lattice
nodes.description: For an elliptic function with periods omega_1, omega_2 (linearly independent over R), the lattice Lambda = Z*omega_1 + Z*omega_2 of all periods.

nodes.name: Fundamental parallelogram
nodes.description: A fundamental domain {s*omega_1 + t*omega_2 : 0 <= s,t < 1} for the lattice Lambda, on which an elliptic function's zeros and poles are counted.

nodes.name: Order of an entire function
nodes.description: The quantity rho = lim sup log log M(r) / log r where M(r) = max_{|z|=r} |f(z)|, measuring the growth rate of an entire function.

nodes.name: Genus of an entire function
nodes.description: In the Hadamard factorization, the genus is max(deg Q, p) where p is the smallest integer with sum 1/|a_n|^{p+1} convergent and Q is the polynomial in the exponential factor.

nodes.name: Schwarz triangle function
nodes.description: The conformal map from the upper half-plane onto a circular-arc triangle with angles alpha*pi, beta*pi, gamma*pi, expressible as a ratio of two hypergeometric solutions.

nodes.name: Analytic continuation along a path
nodes.description: The process of extending a germ of an analytic function along a path via overlapping disk neighborhoods, producing a (possibly different) germ at the endpoint.

nodes.name: Complete analytic function (Weierstrass)
nodes.description: The totality of all function elements obtainable by analytic continuation from a given germ, naturally organized as a sheaf of germs forming a Riemann surface.

nodes.name: Algebraic function
nodes.description: A multi-valued function w(z) defined implicitly by an irreducible polynomial P(z,w) = 0, locally holomorphic away from finitely many branch points.

nodes.name: Riemann surface of an algebraic function
nodes.description: The compact Riemann surface associated to an irreducible polynomial P(z,w) = 0 of degree n in w, an n-sheeted branched covering of the Riemann sphere.

nodes.name: Monodromy group of a linear ODE
nodes.description: The representation of pi_1 of the punctured domain in GL(n,C) obtained by analytically continuing a fundamental system of solutions around singular points.

nodes.name: Harmonic conjugate
nodes.description: For a harmonic u on a simply connected domain, the unique (up to constant) harmonic v such that u + iv is holomorphic, obtained by integrating the Cauchy-Riemann equations.

nodes.name: Residue of f at an isolated singularity
nodes.description: The coefficient c_{-1} in the Laurent expansion about an isolated singularity z_0; equivalently Res(f, z_0) = (1/2pi i) oint f(z) dz around z_0.

nodes.name: Complex line integral
nodes.description: The integral of f along a piecewise smooth curve gamma, defined as integral_gamma f(z) dz = integral_a^b f(gamma(t)) gamma'(t) dt.

nodes.name: Pole of order m
nodes.description: An isolated singularity z_0 where the Laurent series has c_{-m} != 0 and c_n = 0 for n < -m; equivalently (z-z_0)^m f(z) extends to a nonzero holomorphic value.

nodes.name: Symmetry principle for Möbius transformations
nodes.description: A Möbius transformation mapping a circle C to a circle C' sends points symmetric with respect to C to points symmetric with respect to C'.

nodes.name: Conformality of analytic functions
nodes.description: A holomorphic function f is conformal (angle- and orientation-preserving) at every point z_0 where f'(z_0) != 0.

nodes.name: Automorphisms of the upper half-plane
nodes.description: Every biholomorphic self-map of the upper half-plane H has the form z -> (az+b)/(cz+d) with a,b,c,d real and ad-bc > 0, giving Aut(H) = PSL(2,R).

nodes.name: Cauchy's theorem for multiply connected regions
nodes.description: If f is holomorphic in a region bounded by outer contour Gamma_0 and inner contours Gamma_1,...,Gamma_n, then the integral over Gamma_0 equals the sum of integrals over the Gamma_k.

nodes.name: Minimum modulus principle
nodes.description: If f is holomorphic and non-vanishing on a connected open set, then |f| has no local minimum in the interior.

nodes.name: Schwarz's theorem (Poisson integral solves Dirichlet problem for the disk)
nodes.description: The Poisson integral of a continuous function on the unit circle is harmonic in the disk and extends continuously to the given boundary values.

nodes.name: Harnack's principle
nodes.description: A monotone increasing sequence of harmonic functions on a connected domain either converges uniformly on compacta to a harmonic function or diverges to +infinity everywhere.

nodes.name: Taylor's theorem (complex analysis)
nodes.description: A holomorphic function on a domain has a convergent Taylor series f(z) = sum f^{(n)}(a)/n! (z-a)^n in every disk centered at a contained in the domain.

nodes.name: Laurent's theorem
nodes.description: A holomorphic function on an annulus r < |z-a| < R has a unique Laurent series sum_{n=-infty}^{infty} c_n (z-a)^n converging uniformly on compact subannuli.

nodes.name: Conformal mapping of rectangles to the upper half-plane
nodes.description: The Schwarz-Christoffel map for a rectangle yields an elliptic integral, and the conformal modulus (side ratio) is a complete conformal invariant.

nodes.name: Canonical conformal mapping of multiply connected regions
nodes.description: Every finitely connected region with nondegenerate boundary components is conformally equivalent to a canonical slit domain (parallel, circular, or radial slits).

nodes.name: Liouville's theorems on elliptic functions
nodes.description: An elliptic function with no poles is constant; the sum of residues in a period parallelogram is zero; an order-n elliptic function assumes every value exactly n times.

nodes.name: Differential equation for the Weierstrass p-function
nodes.description: (p'(z))^2 = 4p(z)^3 - g_2 p(z) - g_3 where g_2 = 60 G_4, g_3 = 140 G_6, identifying C/Lambda with the elliptic curve y^2 = 4x^3 - g_2 x - g_3.

nodes.name: Monodromy theorem
nodes.description: If a function element can be analytically continued along every path in a simply connected domain, then the continuation defines a single-valued holomorphic function on that domain.

nodes.name: General Cauchy theorem (homological version)
nodes.description: If f is holomorphic on U and Gamma is a cycle null-homologous in U, then integral_Gamma f(z) dz = 0 and the Cauchy integral formula holds for points with nonzero winding number.

nodes.name: Normal families method
nodes.function_signature: (Family of holomorphic functions) -> (Existence of limit function with desired properties)
nodes.description: Proves existence of extremal or limit functions by extracting convergent subsequences from a normal family via Montel's theorem.

nodes.name: Wirtinger derivatives
nodes.description: The operators ∂/∂z = (1/2)(∂/∂x − i ∂/∂y) and ∂/∂z̄ = (1/2)(∂/∂x + i ∂/∂y), so that f is holomorphic iff ∂f/∂z̄ = 0.

nodes.name: Primitive (antiderivative) of a holomorphic function
nodes.description: A holomorphic function F on a domain Ω such that F'(z) = f(z); exists on simply connected domains for every holomorphic f, and ∫_γ f dz = F(γ(1)) − F(γ(0)).

nodes.name: ML inequality (estimation lemma)
nodes.description: |∫_γ f(z) dz| ≤ M · L, where M = sup_{z ∈ γ} |f(z)| and L = length(γ), bounding contour integrals by supremum times arc length.

nodes.name: Uniform limit of holomorphic functions is holomorphic
nodes.description: If f_n are holomorphic on a domain Ω and f_n → f uniformly on compact subsets, then f is holomorphic on Ω and f_n' → f' uniformly on compacta.

nodes.name: Zero of order n
nodes.description: A point z_0 where f(z_0) = f'(z_0) = ... = f^{(n-1)}(z_0) = 0 and f^{(n)}(z_0) ≠ 0, equivalently f(z) = (z − z_0)^n g(z) with g(z_0) ≠ 0.

nodes.name: Principal part of a Laurent series
nodes.description: The sum ∑_{n=-∞}^{-1} c_n (z − z_0)^n of negative-power terms in the Laurent expansion about an isolated singularity, determining the singular behavior of f.

nodes.name: Meromorphic function
nodes.description: A function f on a domain Ω that is holomorphic except at a set of isolated points which are poles; equivalently, f is locally a ratio of holomorphic functions.

nodes.name: Branch of the logarithm
nodes.description: A continuous function log on a domain Ω ⊂ ℂ \ {0} satisfying e^{log z} = z; exists iff the winding number of every closed curve in Ω about 0 is zero.

nodes.name: Characterization of simply connected domains
nodes.description: For a connected open subset Ω of ℂ, the following are equivalent: Ω is simply connected; every holomorphic f on Ω has a primitive; ∫_γ f = 0 for all closed curves; every nonvanishing holomorphic f has a logarithm; ℂ \ Ω is connected.

nodes.name: Keyhole contour technique
nodes.function_signature: (Integrand with branch cut or multi-valued behavior) → (Definite integral evaluation via residues)
nodes.description: A contour shaped like a keyhole (large circle, slit along a ray, small circle) used to evaluate integrals involving branch cuts by exploiting the discontinuity across the cut.

nodes.name: Riemann sphere
nodes.description: The one-point compactification ℂ ∪ {∞} ≅ S², equipped with charts z and 1/z making it a compact Riemann surface; the natural domain for meromorphic functions and Möbius transformations.

nodes.name: Automorphisms of the Riemann sphere
nodes.description: Every biholomorphic self-map of the Riemann sphere ℂ ∪ {∞} is a Möbius transformation z ↦ (az+b)/(cz+d) with ad − bc ≠ 0, giving Aut(ℂ ∪ {∞}) ≅ PSL(2,ℂ).

nodes.name: Cayley transform (complex analysis)
nodes.description: The Möbius transformation z ↦ (z − i)/(z + i) mapping the upper half-plane ℍ biholomorphically onto the unit disk 𝔻, with inverse w ↦ i(1+w)/(1−w).

nodes.name: Elliptic function
nodes.description: A meromorphic function f on ℂ that is doubly periodic: f(z + ω₁) = f(z + ω₂) = f(z) for two ℝ-linearly independent periods ω₁, ω₂.

nodes.name: No nonconstant elliptic function of order one
nodes.description: There is no elliptic function with exactly one simple pole in a period parallelogram; the minimum order of a nonconstant elliptic function is 2.

nodes.name: Every elliptic function is rational in ℘ and ℘'
nodes.description: Every elliptic function with periods ω₁, ω₂ can be written as R(℘(z), ℘'(z)) for a rational function R in two variables.

nodes.name: Connection between theta functions and Weierstrass functions
nodes.description: The Weierstrass sigma function is expressible via Jacobi theta: σ(z) = (ω₁/π) exp(η₁z²/ω₁) θ₁(πz/ω₁, q) / θ₁'(0, q), and ℘(z) = −(d²/dz²) log θ₁(πz/ω₁, q) + const.

nodes.name: Representation number r₂(n) via theta functions
nodes.description: r₂(n) = #{(a,b) ∈ ℤ² : a² + b² = n} equals the n-th Fourier coefficient of θ(τ)², giving r₂(n) = 4 ∑_{d|n} χ₄(d) where χ₄ is the nontrivial character mod 4.

nodes.name: Representation number r₄(n) via theta functions
nodes.description: r₄(n) = #{(a,b,c,d) ∈ ℤ⁴ : a² + b² + c² + d² = n} equals the n-th Fourier coefficient of θ(τ)⁴, yielding Jacobi's formula r₄(n) = 8 ∑_{4∤d, d|n} d.

nodes.name: Euler's partition identity
nodes.description: The number of partitions of n into distinct parts equals the number of partitions of n into odd parts, proved via the generating function identity ∏(1+x^n) = ∏ 1/(1−x^{2n−1}).

nodes.name: Weierstrass ℘-function from theta-null values
nodes.description: ℘(z) is expressible in terms of theta functions and their values at z = 0 (theta-nulls), linking lattice invariants to modular quantities.

nodes.name: Two-square theorem via theta functions
nodes.description: An integer n ≥ 1 is a sum of two squares iff every prime p ≡ 3 (mod 4) dividing n appears to an even power, proved via the factorization of θ(τ)² using Dirichlet characters.

nodes.name: Generating function method via theta functions
nodes.function_signature: (Arithmetic counting function r_k(n)) → (Exact formula via modular form Fourier coefficients)
nodes.description: Encode r_k(n) as Fourier coefficients of θ(τ)^k, then use modular form decomposition (Eisenstein + cusp) to derive exact formulas for representation numbers.

nodes.name: Triangle inequality (complex)
nodes.description: For all z, w in C, |z + w| <= |z| + |w|, with equality iff one is a nonnegative real multiple of the other.

nodes.name: Branch of a multi-valued function
nodes.description: A single-valued continuous selection of one value of a multi-valued analytic function (such as log z or z^alpha) on a domain, obtained by introducing branch cuts.

nodes.name: Fixed-point classification of Möbius transformations
nodes.description: A non-identity Möbius transformation is classified as parabolic (one fixed point, trace ±2), elliptic (two fixed points, |multiplier| = 1), loxodromic (two fixed points, |multiplier| != 1), or hyperbolic (loxodromic with real multiplier).

nodes.name: Homotopy of curves
nodes.description: Two closed curves gamma_0, gamma_1 in a domain G are homotopic if there exists a continuous deformation H: [0,1] x [0,1] -> G with H(0,·) = gamma_0 and H(1,·) = gamma_1.

nodes.name: Cycle (complex analysis)
nodes.description: A formal integer linear combination of closed rectifiable curves in a domain, on which integration and winding numbers extend by linearity.

nodes.name: Null-homologous cycle
nodes.description: A cycle Gamma in a domain G is null-homologous (homologous to zero) if n(Gamma, a) = 0 for every point a in C \ G, where n denotes the winding number.

nodes.name: Maximum modulus theorem
nodes.description: If f is holomorphic on a bounded domain G and continuous on its closure, then |f| attains its maximum on the boundary of G.

nodes.name: Space C(G, Ω)
nodes.description: The space of continuous functions from an open set G in C to a metric space Ω, equipped with the topology of uniform convergence on compact subsets of G.

nodes.name: Germ of an analytic function
nodes.description: An equivalence class of function elements (a, sum a_n(z-a)^n) at a point a, where two elements are equivalent if they agree on a neighborhood of a.

nodes.name: Sheaf of germs of holomorphic functions
nodes.description: The étale space over a domain whose stalk at each point is the set of germs of holomorphic functions at that point, forming a Hausdorff topological space with a natural local homeomorphism to the base.

nodes.name: Riemann surface (abstract)
nodes.description: A connected one-dimensional complex manifold: a Hausdorff topological space with an atlas of charts to open subsets of C whose transition functions are biholomorphic.

nodes.name: Converse of the mean value property
nodes.description: A continuous function on a domain satisfying the mean value property over all sufficiently small circles centered at each point is harmonic.

nodes.name: Maximum principle for harmonic functions
nodes.description: A nonconstant harmonic function on a connected open set attains neither its maximum nor its minimum in the interior.

nodes.name: Dirichlet problem for the disk
nodes.description: The problem of finding a function harmonic in the open unit disk and continuous on the closed disk that agrees with a given continuous function on the boundary circle.

nodes.name: Superharmonic function
nodes.description: A lower semicontinuous function u on a domain satisfying u(z_0) >= (1/2pi) integral_0^{2pi} u(z_0 + re^{i theta}) d theta for all small r, equivalently -u is subharmonic.

nodes.name: Maximum principle for subharmonic functions
nodes.description: A nonconstant subharmonic function on a connected open set cannot attain its maximum in the interior.

nodes.name: Barrier at a boundary point
nodes.description: A superharmonic function beta on G ∩ B(zeta, r) that is positive, tends to zero as z -> zeta, and is bounded below by a positive constant on G ∩ partial B(zeta, r), certifying regularity of zeta for the Dirichlet problem.

nodes.name: Regular boundary point
nodes.description: A boundary point zeta of a domain G at which every Perron solution to the Dirichlet problem attains the prescribed boundary value, equivalently a point admitting a barrier.

nodes.name: Poisson–Jensen formula
nodes.description: For f meromorphic in |z| <= R with zeros a_k and poles b_j, log |f(z)| equals the Poisson integral of log|f| on the boundary plus logarithmic terms from the zeros and poles.

nodes.name: Type of an entire function
nodes.description: For an entire function of finite order rho, the type sigma = lim sup (log M(r)) / r^rho, classifying growth as minimal (sigma=0), normal (0 < sigma < infty), or maximal (sigma = infty).

nodes.name: Canonical product
nodes.description: The Weierstrass product P(z) = prod E_p(z/a_n) formed from the zeros {a_n} using elementary factors of genus p, representing an entire function with exactly those zeros.

nodes.name: Exponent of convergence
nodes.description: For a sequence {a_n} with |a_n| -> infty, the infimum lambda of all alpha > 0 such that sum 1/|a_n|^alpha converges, measuring the density of the sequence.

nodes.name: Landau's theorem (complex analysis)
nodes.description: There exists a universal constant L such that if f is holomorphic on the unit disk with f(0) = 0 and f'(0) = 1, then the image f(D) contains a disk of radius L.

nodes.name: Schottky's theorem
nodes.description: If f is holomorphic on the unit disk and omits the values 0 and 1, then |f(z)| is bounded by a constant depending only on |f(0)| and |z| < r < 1.

nodes.name: Montel's theorem (omitting two values)
nodes.description: A family of holomorphic functions on a domain, each omitting two fixed values in C, is a normal family.

nodes.name: Characterization of simple connectivity
nodes.description: For a domain G in C, the following are equivalent: G is simply connected; every holomorphic function on G has a primitive; C_hat \ G is connected; every nonvanishing holomorphic function on G has a holomorphic logarithm.

nodes.name: Conformal equivalence
nodes.description: Two domains are conformally equivalent if there exists a biholomorphic (bijective holomorphic with holomorphic inverse) map between them.

nodes.name: Hyperbolic distance on the disk
nodes.description: The distance d_D(z,w) = arctanh(|z-w|/|1-bar{w}z|) induced by the Poincaré metric ds = 2|dz|/(1-|z|^2), invariant under automorphisms of D.

nodes.name: Carathéodory boundary correspondence theorem
nodes.description: A conformal map from the unit disk onto a Jordan domain extends to a homeomorphism from the closed disk onto the closed Jordan domain.

nodes.name: Covering space
nodes.description: A surjective continuous map p: E -> X such that every point of X has a neighborhood U whose preimage is a disjoint union of open sets each mapped homeomorphically onto U by p.

nodes.name: Analytic covering map
nodes.description: A holomorphic covering map between Riemann surfaces: a holomorphic surjection that is a covering space map, so that each fiber is discrete and the map is a local biholomorphism.

nodes.name: Deck transformation
nodes.description: A homeomorphism phi: E -> E of a covering space satisfying p ∘ phi = p; the group of all deck transformations acts freely and properly discontinuously on E.

nodes.name: Universal covering surface
nodes.description: The simply connected covering space of a Riemann surface, unique up to isomorphism; by the uniformization theorem, biholomorphic to D, C, or C_hat.

nodes.name: Schlicht class S
nodes.description: The class of all univalent (injective holomorphic) functions f on the unit disk normalized by f(0) = 0 and f'(0) = 1, a compact family in the compact-open topology.

nodes.name: Koebe function
nodes.description: The function k(z) = z/(1-z)^2 mapping the unit disk onto C minus the ray (-infty, -1/4], extremal for the Koebe 1/4 theorem and the coefficient bound |a_n| <= n.

nodes.name: Area theorem (Gronwall)
nodes.description: If g(z) = z + sum_{n=0}^{infty} b_n z^{-n} is univalent in |z| > 1, then sum n|b_n|^2 <= 1, with equality iff g maps onto a complement of a set of area zero.

nodes.name: Bieberbach's inequality
nodes.description: For f(z) = z + a_2 z^2 + ... in class S, |a_2| <= 2, with equality only for rotations of the Koebe function.

nodes.name: Distortion theorem (Koebe)
nodes.description: For f in class S and |z| < 1, (1-|z|)/(1+|z|)^3 <= |f'(z)| <= (1+|z|)/(1-|z|)^3, with equality for rotations of the Koebe function.

nodes.name: Growth theorem (univalent functions)
nodes.description: For f in class S and |z| < 1, |z|/(1+|z|)^2 <= |f(z)| <= |z|/(1-|z|)^2, with equality for rotations of the Koebe function.

nodes.name: Loewner's method
nodes.function_signature: (Extremal problem for class S) → (Coefficient bound via ODE)
nodes.description: Embeds a univalent function in a continuously parametrized family f_t satisfying the Loewner ODE, reducing coefficient estimates to the analysis of a driving function.

nodes.name: Loewner's differential equation (radial)
nodes.description: The ODE df_t/dt = -f_t * (kappa(t) + f_t)/(kappa(t) - f_t) where |kappa(t)| = 1 is the driving function, whose solutions give a subordination chain of univalent maps.

nodes.name: Loewner chain
nodes.description: A family {f_t}_{t >= 0} of univalent functions on the disk with f_s(D) subset f_t(D) for s < t, satisfying the Loewner differential equation.

nodes.name: Robertson conjecture
nodes.description: If g(z) = z + c_3 z^3 + c_5 z^5 + ... is an odd univalent function on the disk, then sum_{k=1}^n |c_{2k-1}|^2 <= n for all n, implied by the Milin conjecture.

nodes.name: Milin conjecture
nodes.description: For f in class S with log(f(z)/z) = 2 sum gamma_k z^k, the inequality sum_{k=1}^n (n-k+1)(k|gamma_k|^2 - 1/k) <= 0 holds for all n; proved by de Branges (1984), implying the Bieberbach conjecture.

nodes.name: Boundary values of H^p functions
nodes.description: Every function in H^p(D) for 0 < p <= infty has nontangential boundary values f*(e^{i theta}) existing almost everywhere on the unit circle, with f* in L^p.

nodes.name: H^p norm and completeness
nodes.description: For 1 <= p <= infty, the Hardy space H^p(D) is a Banach space under the norm ||f||_p = sup_r (integral |f(re^{i theta})|^p d theta / 2pi)^{1/p}; for 0 < p < 1 it is a complete metric space.

nodes.name: Singular inner function
nodes.description: A function of the form S_mu(z) = exp(-integral (e^{i theta} + z)/(e^{i theta} - z) d mu(theta)) where mu is a positive singular measure on the circle, inner with no zeros in D.

nodes.name: H^p duality
nodes.description: For 1 < p < infty, (H^p)* is isometrically isomorphic to H^q (1/p + 1/q = 1); (H^1)* is isometrically isomorphic to BMO via the pairing (f, g) -> integral f g* d theta / 2pi.

nodes.name: Green's function of a domain
nodes.description: The function G(z, a) = -log|z - a| + h_a(z) where h_a is harmonic, with G vanishing on the boundary, serving as the fundamental solution for the Laplacian with Dirichlet boundary conditions.

nodes.name: Symmetry of Green's function
nodes.description: The Green's function of a domain satisfies G(z, w) = G(w, z) for all distinct points z, w in the domain.

nodes.name: Logarithmic potential
nodes.description: The function U^mu(z) = -integral log|z - w| d mu(w) associated to a compactly supported Borel measure mu, superharmonic on C and harmonic outside the support of mu.

nodes.name: Energy of a measure
nodes.description: The quantity I(mu) = integral integral -log|z - w| d mu(z) d mu(w), whose infimum over probability measures supported on a compact set K equals the Robin constant of K.

nodes.name: Equilibrium measure
nodes.description: The unique probability measure mu_K supported on a compact set K that minimizes the energy I(mu), whose potential is constant quasi-everywhere on K.

nodes.name: Logarithmic capacity
nodes.description: The quantity cap(K) = e^{-V(K)} where V(K) = inf I(mu) is the Robin constant, equivalently the transfinite diameter; K is polar iff cap(K) = 0.

nodes.name: Robin constant
nodes.description: The value V(K) = inf{I(mu) : mu probability measure on K}, equal to -log cap(K); the equilibrium potential equals V(K) quasi-everywhere on K.

nodes.name: Polar set (potential theory)
nodes.description: A set E such that there exists a subharmonic function u with E subset {z : u(z) = -infty}, equivalently a set of logarithmic capacity zero.

nodes.name: Riesz decomposition theorem (subharmonic functions)
nodes.description: Every subharmonic function u on a domain equals h - U^mu where h is harmonic and U^mu is the logarithmic potential of the Riesz measure mu = (1/2pi) Delta u.

nodes.name: Evans's theorem
nodes.description: Every compact polar set K is the minus-infinity set of some subharmonic function continuous on C \ K, so polar sets carry no positive mass for capacity-related problems.

nodes.name: Weierstrass product theorem for domains
nodes.description: On any domain G in C, given a discrete set of prescribed zeros with multiplicities, there exists a holomorphic function on G with exactly those zeros.

nodes.name: Lindelöf's theorem (boundary behavior)
nodes.description: If f is bounded and holomorphic on the unit disk and has a limit along a curve ending at e^{i theta}, then f has the same nontangential limit at e^{i theta}.

nodes.name: Corona theorem
nodes.description: If f_1, ..., f_n in H^infty(D) satisfy inf_{z in D} sum |f_k(z)| > 0, then there exist g_1, ..., g_n in H^infty(D) with sum f_k g_k = 1, equivalently the open disk is dense in the maximal ideal space of H^infty.

nodes.name: Separation properties of topological vector spaces
nodes.type_signature: TVS X Hausdorff → X is completely regular (T₃½)
nodes.description: A Hausdorff topological vector space is automatically completely regular; in particular every TVS with T₁ separation is T₃½, since translations of balanced neighborhoods of 0 separate points from closed sets via Minkowski functionals.

nodes.name: Continuity–boundedness equivalence for linear maps
nodes.type_signature: Linear map T: X → Y between TVS → (T continuous ⟺ T bounded ⟺ T continuous at 0)
nodes.description: A linear map between topological vector spaces is continuous if and only if it is bounded (maps bounded sets to bounded sets), which is equivalent to continuity at any single point.

nodes.name: Seminorm characterization of local convexity
nodes.type_signature: TVS X → (X locally convex ⟺ topology generated by a separating family of seminorms)
nodes.description: A topological vector space is locally convex if and only if its topology is generated by a family of seminorms; when the family is countable and separating, the space is metrizable.

nodes.name: Bilinear map continuity theorem (separate implies joint)
nodes.type_signature: Separately continuous bilinear B: X × Y → Z, X Fréchet, Y Fréchet → B jointly continuous
nodes.description: A separately continuous bilinear map from a product of Fréchet spaces into a TVS is jointly continuous; follows from Banach–Steinhaus applied to the family of partial maps.

nodes.name: Balanced convex hull
nodes.description: The balanced convex hull of a set A in a TVS is the smallest balanced convex set containing A; equivalently the set of all finite sums Σ λᵢxᵢ with xᵢ ∈ A, Σ|λᵢ| ≤ 1.

nodes.name: Extreme point
nodes.type_signature: x ∈ K compact convex → x extreme ⟺ K\{x} convex
nodes.description: A point x of a convex set K is an extreme point if x = ty + (1−t)z with 0 < t < 1 and y,z ∈ K implies y = z = x; equivalently, x is not an interior point of any line segment in K.

nodes.name: Milman's converse theorem
nodes.type_signature: K compact convex in locally convex TVS, S ⊂ K with closed convex hull = K → ext(K) ⊂ closure(S)
nodes.description: If K is a compact convex subset of a locally convex space and the closed convex hull of a subset S equals K, then every extreme point of K lies in the closure of S; converse to Krein–Milman.

nodes.name: Weak* convergence
nodes.type_signature: Net (f_α) in X* → f in σ(X*,X)
nodes.description: A net (f_α) in the dual X* converges weak* to f if f_α(x) → f(x) for every x ∈ X; the weak* topology σ(X*,X) is the coarsest topology making the evaluation maps x̂: X* → K continuous.

nodes.name: Schauder basis
nodes.description: A sequence (eₙ) in a Banach space X such that every x ∈ X has a unique expansion x = Σ aₙeₙ converging in the norm topology; the coordinate functionals aₙ: X → K are automatically continuous.

nodes.name: Trivial dual of Lp for 0 < p < 1
nodes.description: For 0 < p < 1 and a non-atomic measure μ, the only continuous linear functional on Lp(μ) is the zero functional; consequently Lp(μ) has no nonzero closed convex proper subsets besides ∅ and Lp itself.

nodes.name: Lyapunov's vector measure theorem
nodes.type_signature: Non-atomic vector measure μ: Σ → ℝⁿ → μ(Σ) is convex and compact
nodes.description: The range of a non-atomic vector-valued measure μ = (μ₁,…,μₙ) with each μᵢ a finite non-atomic scalar measure is a compact convex subset of ℝⁿ.

nodes.name: Space E(Ω) = C^∞(Ω)
nodes.description: The space of all infinitely differentiable functions on an open set Ω ⊂ ℝⁿ, equipped with the topology of uniform convergence of all derivatives on compact subsets; a Fréchet space whose dual is E'(Ω), the distributions with compact support.

nodes.name: Regularization of distributions by convolution
nodes.function_signature: (Distribution u ∈ D'(Ω), Mollifier φ_ε ∈ C_c^∞) → (Smooth function u * φ_ε approximating u)
nodes.description: Convolves a distribution with a smooth compactly supported mollifier to produce a smooth function that converges to the original distribution in D'; used to approximate distributions by smooth functions.

nodes.name: Completeness of distribution spaces
nodes.description: If a sequence of distributions (uₙ) in D'(Ω) satisfies uₙ(φ) → L(φ) for every test function φ, then L is a distribution; D'(Ω) is complete as a locally convex space with the weak* topology.

nodes.name: Sobolev's lemma (regularity from L² derivatives)
nodes.type_signature: u ∈ H^s(ℝⁿ), s > n/2 + k → u ∈ C^k(ℝⁿ)
nodes.description: If u ∈ L²(ℝⁿ) has all distributional derivatives up to order s in L², and s > n/2 + k, then u agrees a.e. with a Cᵏ function; proved via the Fourier transform and the integrability of (1+|ξ|²)^{-s/2}.

nodes.name: Local structure theorem for distributions
nodes.type_signature: u ∈ D'(Ω) → locally u = ∂^α f for some continuous f and multi-index α
nodes.description: Every distribution on an open set Ω ⊂ ℝⁿ is locally a finite-order distributional derivative of a continuous function; equivalently, for each compact K ⊂ Ω there exist a continuous function f and a multi-index α with u = ∂^α f on the interior of K.

nodes.name: Elliptic regularity theorem
nodes.type_signature: P elliptic, Pu = f ∈ C^∞(Ω) → u ∈ C^∞(Ω)
nodes.description: If P is an elliptic linear partial differential operator with smooth coefficients and u is a distribution satisfying Pu = f with f ∈ C^∞, then u ∈ C^∞; every elliptic operator is hypoelliptic.

nodes.name: Hypoelliptic operator
nodes.description: A linear partial differential operator P on Ω is hypoelliptic if every distribution solution u of Pu = f is smooth wherever f is smooth; equivalently, sing supp(u) ⊂ sing supp(Pu) for all distributions u.

nodes.name: Characterization of hypoelliptic operators with constant coefficients
nodes.type_signature: P(D) constant-coefficient → (P hypoelliptic ⟺ algebraic decay condition on ∂^α P/P)
nodes.description: A constant-coefficient linear partial differential operator P(D) is hypoelliptic if and only if for every multi-index α ≠ 0, |D^α P(ξ)/P(ξ)| → 0 as |ξ| → ∞ along real ξ; equivalently, the zeros of P(ζ) for complex ζ satisfy |Im ζ| → ∞ as |Re ζ| → ∞.

nodes.name: Spanning of translates in L¹(ℝⁿ)
nodes.type_signature: f ∈ L¹(ℝⁿ) → (translates of f span L¹ ⟺ f̂(ξ) ≠ 0 for all ξ)
nodes.description: The closed translation-invariant subspace of L¹(ℝⁿ) generated by f equals L¹(ℝⁿ) if and only if the Fourier transform f̂ has no real zeros; a key ingredient in Wiener's Tauberian theorem.

nodes.name: Spectral synthesis problem
nodes.description: The question of whether every closed translation-invariant subspace of L¹(G) (or equivalently every closed ideal in L¹(G)) is the intersection of the maximal ideals containing it; equivalently, whether every closed set in the Gelfand spectrum is a set of spectral synthesis.

nodes.name: Failure of spectral synthesis (Malliavin)
nodes.type_signature: G locally compact abelian, non-compact → ∃ closed sets in Ĝ that are not sets of spectral synthesis
nodes.description: Malliavin proved that spectral synthesis fails for every non-compact locally compact abelian group; there exist closed ideals in L¹(G) that are not intersections of maximal ideals, refuting the general spectral synthesis conjecture.

nodes.name: Wiener's general Tauberian theorem
nodes.type_signature: K ∈ L¹(ℝ), K̂ nowhere zero, slowly oscillating φ → asymptotic conclusion
nodes.description: If K ∈ L¹(ℝ) has Fourier transform that never vanishes, and if lim_{x→∞}∫K(x−t)φ(t)dt = A∫K for a bounded measurable φ that is slowly oscillating, then lim_{x→∞}∫f(x−t)φ(t)dt = A∫f for every f ∈ L¹(ℝ).

nodes.name: Ideals and quotient algebras in Banach algebras
nodes.type_signature: I closed ideal in Banach algebra A → A/I Banach algebra
nodes.description: A closed two-sided ideal I of a Banach algebra A makes the quotient A/I into a Banach algebra under the quotient norm; maximal ideals are automatically closed in unital Banach algebras.

nodes.name: Shilov boundary
nodes.description: The smallest closed subset S of the maximal ideal space Δ(A) of a commutative unital Banach algebra A such that max_{φ∈Δ(A)} |â(φ)| = max_{φ∈S} |â(φ)| for all a ∈ A; existence is guaranteed by a compactness argument.

nodes.name: Wiener's lemma
nodes.type_signature: f has absolutely convergent Fourier series, f(x) ≠ 0 ∀x → 1/f has absolutely convergent Fourier series
nodes.description: If f is a nowhere-vanishing continuous function on the circle with absolutely convergent Fourier series (f ∈ A(T)), then 1/f also has absolutely convergent Fourier series; a consequence of the Gelfand theory of commutative Banach algebras applied to the Wiener algebra.

nodes.name: Symbolic calculus in commutative Banach algebras
nodes.function_signature: (Element a in commutative Banach algebra A, Analytic function f on neighborhood of σ(a)) → (Element f(a) ∈ A via Cauchy integral)
nodes.description: Applies a function analytic in a neighborhood of the spectrum σ(a) to an element a of a commutative Banach algebra via the contour integral f(a) = (2πi)⁻¹∮f(λ)R(λ,a)dλ; extends the holomorphic functional calculus to compute with elements of A.

nodes.name: Toeplitz operator
nodes.description: For φ ∈ L^∞(T), the Toeplitz operator T_φ on the Hardy space H² is defined by T_φf = P₊(φf), where P₊ is the orthogonal projection onto H²; the map φ ↦ T_φ is a contractive *-linear map but not multiplicative.

nodes.name: Shift operator (unilateral and bilateral)
nodes.description: The unilateral shift S on ℓ²(ℕ) maps (x₁,x₂,…) to (0,x₁,x₂,…); it is an isometry but not unitary, with S*S = I ≠ SS*, and its spectrum is the closed unit disk; the bilateral shift on ℓ²(ℤ) is unitary with spectrum the unit circle.

nodes.name: Positive square root of a positive operator
nodes.type_signature: T ≥ 0 bounded on Hilbert space → ∃! S ≥ 0 with S² = T
nodes.description: Every bounded positive operator T on a Hilbert space has a unique positive square root S = T^{1/2}, which commutes with every operator commuting with T; constructed via the continuous functional calculus applied to f(t) = √t.

nodes.name: Unbounded operator
nodes.type_signature: T: D(T) ⊂ H → H, D(T) dense
nodes.description: A linear operator T defined on a dense linear subspace D(T) of a Hilbert space H, not required to be bounded; the domain D(T) is part of the data defining T.

nodes.name: Closable operator
nodes.type_signature: T: D(T) → H, closure of graph(T) is a graph
nodes.description: An operator T is closable if the closure of its graph in H × H is the graph of an operator (called the closure of T); equivalently, if xₙ → 0 and Txₙ → y implies y = 0.

nodes.name: Symmetric operator
nodes.description: A densely defined operator T on a Hilbert space is symmetric if ⟨Tx,y⟩ = ⟨x,Ty⟩ for all x,y ∈ D(T); equivalently T ⊂ T* (the domain of T is contained in the domain of T* and they agree on D(T)).

nodes.name: Adjoint of an unbounded operator
nodes.type_signature: T densely defined → T* with D(T*) = {y : x ↦ ⟨Tx,y⟩ bounded on D(T)}
nodes.description: For a densely defined operator T on a Hilbert space, the adjoint T* has domain D(T*) = {y ∈ H : ∃z with ⟨Tx,y⟩ = ⟨x,z⟩ ∀x ∈ D(T)}, and T*y = z; T* is always closed but need not be densely defined.

nodes.name: Essentially self-adjoint operator
nodes.description: A symmetric operator T is essentially self-adjoint if its closure T̄ is self-adjoint; equivalently, T has a unique self-adjoint extension, equivalently the deficiency indices n₊ = n₋ = 0.

nodes.name: Deficiency indices
nodes.type_signature: n₊ = dim ker(T*−iI), n₋ = dim ker(T*+iI)
nodes.description: For a closed symmetric operator T, the deficiency indices n₊ = dim ker(T* − iI) and n₋ = dim ker(T* + iI) measure the 'distance' from self-adjointness; T has self-adjoint extensions iff n₊ = n₋.

nodes.name: Von Neumann's extension theory for symmetric operators
nodes.type_signature: T closed symmetric → self-adjoint extensions classified by deficiency indices
nodes.description: A closed symmetric operator T has self-adjoint extensions if and only if its deficiency indices are equal (n₊ = n₋); when they are equal, the self-adjoint extensions are parametrized by unitary maps from ker(T*−iI) to ker(T*+iI) via the Cayley transform.

nodes.name: Nelson's theorem on analytic vectors
nodes.type_signature: T symmetric, D of analytic vectors dense → T essentially self-adjoint
nodes.description: If T is a symmetric operator on a Hilbert space and the set of analytic vectors for T (vectors v with Σ ||T^n v|| tⁿ/n! < ∞ for some t > 0) is dense, then T is essentially self-adjoint.

nodes.name: Semigroup generation by the Laplacian
nodes.type_signature: Δ on L²(ℝⁿ) or L²(Ω) with boundary conditions → generates C₀ contraction semigroup
nodes.description: The Laplacian Δ (or −Δ) on L²(ℝⁿ), or on L²(Ω) with Dirichlet/Neumann boundary conditions, is essentially self-adjoint on C_c^∞ and generates a strongly continuous contraction semigroup e^{tΔ}, the heat semigroup, via the Hille–Yosida theorem.

nodes.name: Neumann series
nodes.function_signature: (Bounded operator T with ‖T‖ < 1) → ((I − T)⁻¹ = Σₙ Tⁿ)
nodes.description: The geometric series Σₙ₌₀^∞ Tⁿ converging in operator norm to (I − T)⁻¹ whenever ‖T‖ < 1, used to construct resolvents and prove openness of the resolvent set.

nodes.name: Trace class operator
nodes.description: A compact operator T on a Hilbert space whose singular values {sₙ} satisfy Σ sₙ < ∞, forming the Banach ideal L¹(H) with trace norm ‖T‖₁ = Σ sₙ.

nodes.name: Fredholm index
nodes.description: The integer ind(T) = dim ker T − dim coker T for a Fredholm operator T, invariant under compact perturbations and continuous in the operator norm topology.

nodes.name: Spectral multiplicity theory
nodes.description: The classification of normal operators up to unitary equivalence by their spectral measure class and multiplicity function, generalizing the Jordan form to infinite dimensions.

nodes.name: Tensor product of Hilbert spaces
nodes.description: The completion of the algebraic tensor product H₁ ⊗ H₂ under the inner product ⟨φ₁⊗φ₂, ψ₁⊗ψ₂⟩ = ⟨φ₁,ψ₁⟩⟨φ₂,ψ₂⟩, fundamental for multiparticle quantum mechanics.

nodes.name: Relative bound (Kato bound)
nodes.description: The infimum of constants a such that ‖Bφ‖ ≤ a‖Aφ‖ + b‖φ‖ for all φ ∈ D(A), measuring the subordination of operator B to operator A.

nodes.name: KLMN theorem
nodes.description: If a symmetric quadratic form b is relatively form-bounded with respect to a closed semibounded form a with relative bound less than 1, then a + b is closed and semibounded on D(a).

nodes.name: Form representation theorem (Kato)
nodes.description: Every closed, densely defined, semibounded quadratic form on a Hilbert space is the form of a unique self-adjoint operator, establishing a bijection between such forms and operators.

nodes.name: Friedrichs extension
nodes.function_signature: (Semibounded symmetric operator A) → (Self-adjoint extension A_F with same lower bound)
nodes.description: Construction of the canonical self-adjoint extension of a semibounded symmetric operator by closing its associated quadratic form and applying the form representation theorem.

nodes.name: Analytic vector
nodes.description: A vector φ in the domain of all powers of an operator A such that Σ ‖Aⁿφ‖ tⁿ/n! converges for some t > 0, used in Nelson's theorem to establish essential self-adjointness.

nodes.name: Kato's inequality
nodes.description: The distributional inequality Δ|u| ≥ Re(sgn(ū)·Δu) for u ∈ L¹_loc with Δu ∈ L¹_loc, a key tool for proving self-adjointness and semigroup domination.

nodes.name: Hypercontractive semigroup
nodes.description: A semigroup e^{−tH} that maps Lᵖ to Lᵍ for q > p after sufficient time, with the optimal bound given by Nelson's best hypercontractive estimate for the Ornstein–Uhlenbeck semigroup.

nodes.name: Nelson's best hypercontractive estimate
nodes.description: The Ornstein–Uhlenbeck semigroup e^{−tN} is a contraction from Lᵖ to Lᵍ if and only if e^{−2t} ≤ (p−1)/(q−1), with sharpness attained on Gaussian functions.

nodes.name: Diamagnetic inequality
nodes.description: The pointwise bound |e^{−t(−i∇−A)²}f(x)| ≤ e^{tΔ}|f|(x) showing that magnetic fields raise the ground state energy and reduce the semigroup kernel.

nodes.name: Nelson's commutator theorem
nodes.description: If H is symmetric and N is a self-adjoint operator with D(N) ⊂ D(H) satisfying ±i[H,N] ≤ cN on D(N), then H is essentially self-adjoint on D(N).

nodes.name: Kato class
nodes.description: The class K_d of potentials V for which lim_{r→0} sup_x ∫_{|x−y|<r} |V(y)|·g_d(x−y) dy = 0 where g_d is the Green's function, ensuring −Δ+V is essentially self-adjoint and its semigroup has nice properties.

nodes.name: Cook's method
nodes.function_signature: (Perturbation V, free dynamics H₀) → (Existence of wave operators Ω±)
nodes.description: Proof of existence of wave operators by showing ∫₀^∞ ‖V e^{−iH₀t} φ‖ dt < ∞ for a dense set of φ, reducing existence to an integrability condition on the perturbation.

nodes.name: Enss method
nodes.function_signature: (Short-range potential V, phase space decomposition) → (Asymptotic completeness)
nodes.description: A geometric, time-dependent proof of asymptotic completeness using phase space decomposition into incoming and outgoing states via propagation observables.

nodes.name: Kato smoothness (H-smoothness)
nodes.description: An operator A is H-smooth if ∫_{−∞}^{∞} ‖A e^{−iHt} φ‖² dt ≤ C‖φ‖² for all φ, equivalently sup_{ε>0,λ} ‖A(H−λ−iε)⁻¹A*‖ < ∞, implying absolute continuity of H on Ran(A*).

nodes.name: Kato smoothness implies absolute continuity
nodes.description: If A is H-smooth, then the spectral measure of H restricted to Ran(A*) is absolutely continuous, providing a criterion for absence of singular spectrum.

nodes.name: Lippmann–Schwinger equation
